recipes.title: Korean Baked Chicken Wings
recipes.how: 3 pounds chicken wings, cut at joints, tips discarded 1 tablespoon toasted sesame oil 1 teaspoon minced garlic 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger 1¾ cups water, divided 3 tbsp. monk fruit allulose blend (in place of 3 tablespoons sugar) 2–3 tablespoons gochujang (adjust for heat) 1 tablespoon soy sauce 1 cup all-purpose flour 3 tablespoons cornstarch 2–3 tablespoons avocado oil (or light olive oil) – for tossing In a large bowl, combine sesame oil, garlic, and ginger. Microwave 40–60 seconds till bubbly and fragrant (not brown). Whisk in ¼ cup water, sweetener, gochujang, and soy sauce till smooth. Set aside—this is your sauce. Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil, top with a wire rack. Whisk flour and cornstarch with remaining 1½ cups water in a bowl till smooth—your batter. Pat wings dry. Toss them lightly in avocado oil (just enough to coat, maybe 2–3 tablespoons total), then dip each one in batter, let excess drip off. Place on rack—don't crowd. Bake 35–40 minutes, flipping halfway. Crank to broil last 2 minutes if you want extra snap. While they bake, warm sauce gently on stovetop if needed. Toss hot wings in sauce, let sit 2 minutes on rack to set, then plate. Same killer flavor, no oil bath. If you still crave that double-crisp, you could air-fry at 400°F for 25 minutes—flip once—but baking's dead simple. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (crisp, sugar, flour). Carb swap: replace the 3 tbsp sugar with monk fruit or erythritol blend; swap the 1 cup all-purpose flour + 3 tbsp cornstarch batter for almond flour + 1 tbsp psyllium husk (arrowroot also works as a lightener). Keep gochujang, soy, sesame, garlic, ginger as-is. Sugar swap: The sauce is tossed on after baking, so sugar is only there for sweetness and a sticky gloss; monk fruit allulose blend dissolves clear and stays glossy without crystallizing as it cools. Flour is the best for this recipe because: cornstarch makes the light, shatter-crisp coating; almond flour browns before it crisps and goes soft under sauce. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this dish. Almond flour and psyllium bake into a softer, browner coating than flour and cornstarch, so the wings lose their shatter-crisp crust and go soft faster under the sticky sauce.

recipes.title: German Pot Roast (Low carb)
recipes.how: 4-pound pot roast (chuck, rump, or similar) 1 teaspoon salt ⅛ teaspoon pepper 2 tablespoons fat (lard, tallow, ghee, or avocado oil works great) 1 cup water, ½ teaspoon monk fruit sweetener (50% mogroside) 2 slices lemon (peeled), 2 medium onions (sliced) ½ cup water ½ cup vinegar 3 cloves garlic 2 carrots (coarsely cut) 2 stalks celery with leaves (coarsely cut), 1 bay leaf ⅛ teaspoon ground cloves ⅛ teaspoon ground cinnamon ½ cup seedless raisins (reduce to 2 tablespoons or omit for lower carbs) ½ teaspoon ground ginger ¼ teaspoon glucomannan powder (Pure Konjac Gum) 1–2 tablespoons cold water (for slurry) Instructions Rub the roast with the salt and pepper. In a heavy kettle heat the 2 tablespoons fat. Brown meat on all sides. Into blender put the first group (1 cup water + ½ tsp monk fruit + lemon slices + onions). Cover and blend on high 3 seconds. Pour over meat. Into blender put the second group (½ cup water + ½ cup vinegar + garlic + carrots + celery + bay leaf). Cover and blend on high 3 seconds. Pour over meat. Add the cloves and cinnamon. Cover and cook over low heat for about 1½ hours. Add the raisins. Cover and cook 1½ hours longer, or until meat is tender. Remove roast to a platter and keep warm. Into blender put 1 cup sauce from the pot. Add the ½ teaspoon ground ginger. Cover and blend 10 seconds. Pour back into the kettle. In a small bowl whisk the ¼ teaspoon glucomannan powder with 1–2 tablespoons cold water until completely smooth. Whisk the slurry into the kettle. Heat gently 1–2 minutes while stirring. Turn off heat and let stand 2–3 minutes (it thickens more as it cools). Slice meat and spoon gravy over top. Serves 8. Carb rating (Low): Beef-forward braise with low-starch veg; named low-carb and stays in the roughly 1–10g net range without flour gravy or sugary glaze.

One cup flour (lower-carb option: 2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 2 teaspoons curry powder 1 1/2 pints of beef stock 1. cut onion the onion into small pieces and fry them in fat 2. Stirring the flour the curry powder and add the beef stock. 3. Cook for 30 minutes. 4. Refrigerate it until cool. 5. Skim off the fat off the top. 6 serve with finally chopped cauliflower Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (flour). Carb swap: swap AP flour for almond flour (psyllium helps bind baked goods). (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour structure beats arrowroot for baked flour swaps.) Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this soup. A full cup of flour gives this soup its thick, velvety body, so xanthan makes a thinner, slicker, slightly gelled soup with less toasty flavor; the curry stays the same.

recipes.title: Deviled Chicken Legs
recipes.how: For the curry paste (your exact base, scaled for 8 legs): 2 oz (55g) butter, softened to room temperature (original allowed margarine) 1 Tbsp tomato ketchup 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce 2 heaping tsp curry powder (mild to medium—Harben’s era was usually gentle; adjust heat to your taste) For the chicken: 8 chicken legs (drumsticks or whole legs), skin on Salt and freshly ground black pepper Optional extras Harben might have approved: a squeeze of lemon juice in the paste, or a pinch of sugar if you want more sweetness to balance the spice plain boiled rice or mashed potatoes, a green veg (peas, cabbage, or beans), and maybe a wedge of lemon. Or keep it light with a crisp salad. No-BS Construction Method (Oven Version) Make the paste: Mash the softened butter with a fork until creamy. Work in the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, and curry powder until you have a smooth, spreadable paste. It should smell rich and aromatic. Taste it—if it needs a lift, add a few drops of lemon juice. Set aside. (This takes 2 minutes.) Prep the chicken: Pat the legs dry with paper towel. Season all over with salt and pepper. Using your fingers or a knife tip, loosen the skin a bit without tearing it, then rub or brush a generous amount of the curry paste under and over the skin. Get it into all the nooks—this is where the flavour happens. Let the legs sit for 20–30 minutes at room temperature (or longer in the fridge) so the paste can work its magic. Oven setup: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C / Gas 6). Place the legs on a wire rack set inside a roasting tin (this lets air circulate and fat drip away, mimicking grill effect). If you don’t have a rack, just put them on a foil-lined tray and turn them halfway. Roast: Bake for 35–45 minutes, turning once or twice, until the chicken is cooked through (juices run clear, internal temp 165°F / 74°C) and the skin is starting to crisp and colour from the curry paste. Broiler finish for grill-like char: Switch the oven to broil (grill setting) on medium-high. Move the rack closer to the heat (about 4–6 inches away) and broil the legs for 3–5 minutes, watching carefully. Turn once so both sides get bubbly, golden-brown, and slightly charred spots—just like Harben’s grill would have done. Don’t walk away; it can burn fast because of the sugar in the ketchup. Rest and serve: Let the legs rest 5 minutes so the juices settle. The paste will have melted into a glossy, spiced coating with crispy bits. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (sugar, rice, potatoes, beans). Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend; swap rice for cauliflower rice; swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Chicken and Dumplings (Low-Carb Version)
recipes.how: For the Soup: 2½ lbs bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs 1 lb chicken wings 2 tablespoons butter or avocado oil 1 large onion, diced 3 carrots, sliced 3 celery stalks, sliced 4 garlic cloves, minced ¼ cup dry white wine (optional) 6 cups chicken broth 2 bay leaves 1 teaspoon dried thyme Salt and black pepper to taste For the Low-Carb Dumplings: 1½ cups almond flour 2 tablespoons coconut flour 1 teaspoon baking powder ½ teaspoon xanthan gum ½ teaspoon salt 1 large egg ⅓ cup buttermilk 2 tablespoons melted butter 1. Season chicken with salt and pepper. In a large pot, heat butter or avocado oil and brown the chicken in batches. Remove and set aside. 2.In the same pot, sauté onion, carrots, and celery until softened. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds. 3.Add white wine to deglaze, then return chicken to the pot. Add chicken broth, bay leaves, and thyme. Simmer for 45–60 minutes until chicken is tender. 4. Remove chicken, shred the meat, discard bones and skin, and return shredded meat to the pot. 5.Mix all dry dumpling ingredients together. In a separate bowl, whisk egg, buttermilk, and melted butter. Combine until a soft dough forms. Drop small spoonfuls of dough into the simmering soup. Cover and cook for 12–15 minutes until dumplings are cooked through. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Fresh Tomato Gazpacho
recipes.how: 3 lbs ripe tomatoes (about 8 medium) 1 medium cucumber, peeled and halved lengthwise 1 green bell pepper, stemmed and seeded 1 small red onion 2 garlic cloves 1 small serrano chili, stemmed and halved (remove seeds for less heat) 1½ teaspoons kosher salt 1 slice hearty white bread, crust removed, torn into pieces ½ cup extra-virgin olive oil 2 tablespoons sherry vinegar (or red wine vinegar) Pepper to taste For serving: Extra olive oil Finely diced cucumber, bell pepper, onion, and tomato Fresh herbs (parsley, chives, or basil) chopped hard boiled egg nstructions: Core the tomatoes. Roughly chop 2 pounds of the tomatoes and put them in a large bowl. Add the garlic, serrano chili, and salt. Let sit for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, finely dice the remaining 1 lb of tomatoes, half the cucumber, half the bell pepper, and a quarter of the onion. Place in a bowl and set aside in the fridge (this will be your garnish). Add the bread pieces to the large bowl with the chopped tomatoes. Let it soak for 5 minutes. Transfer everything from the large bowl (including liquid) to a blender. Add ½ cup olive oil and 2 tablespoons vinegar. Blend until very smooth, about 2 minutes. Strain the soup through a fine mesh strainer into a large bowl, pressing on the solids to extract as much liquid as possible. Discard the pulp. Chill the soup in the fridge for at least 2 hours (or overnight). Taste and adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, or vinegar if needed. Serve cold with a drizzle of olive oil, a spoonful of the diced vegetable garnish, and fresh herbs. Category: Soup / Appetizer The whole point of this recipe is that it uses raw tomatoes for maximum fresh flavor. Blanching and peeling removes some of that bright, fresh tomato taste. This recipe already strains the soup at the end, which removes all the skins and seeds anyway. So peeling them beforehand is extra work that doesn’t improve the final result. Traditional Spanish gazpacho does not peel the tomatoes. The skins and seeds are where a lot of the tomato’s insoluble fiber lives. Some people find that gazpacho is much easier to digest when those are removed. That’s actually why the original recipe has you strain the soup at the end — it’s the traditional way to remove the skins and seeds without having to blanch and peel every tomato. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (bread). Carb swap: swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Texas Steak Chili with Cocoa, Chipotle & Árbol
recipes.how: 2½ lbs beef chuck roast, cut into ¾-inch cubes 2 chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, chopped + 2 tbsp adobo sauce 2 dried chiles de árbol, stems removed (seeds optional for less heat) 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder 2 tbsp chili powder 1 tbsp ground cumin 2 tsp dried oregano 1 medium onion, diced 4 cloves garlic, minced 4 cups beef broth 2 tbsp avocado oil or lard Salt and black pepper Toast the dried chiles de árbol in a dry skillet for 30–60 seconds until fragrant. Remove stems, roughly chop or crumble, and set aside. Season beef with salt and pepper. Brown the beef cubes in batches in hot oil. Remove and set aside. In the same pot, cook onion until soft, add garlic for 30 seconds. Stir in cocoa powder, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Toast for 30–60 seconds. Add chopped chipotles + adobo sauce, the toasted chiles de árbol, and the browned beef. Pour in beef broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered on low for 2½–3 hours until beef is very tender. Uncover for the last 30 minutes if you want it thicker. The two árbol chiles add a bright, sharp heat without overpowering the dish. If you want it milder next time, just use one. Note: If you want a touch of sweetness to balance the heat, stir in ½–1 tsp monk fruit sweetener near the end of cooking. Carb rating (Moderate): Veg/fruit/dairy carbs without heavy flour/sugar (fruit, peppers, onion) — moderate.

recipes.title: West Virginia Sausage & Ramps Breakfast Skillet
recipes.how: Leeks and ramps are pretty different. Ramps are small, wild, and have a strong, pungent garlic-onion flavor — they're bold and zippy. Leeks are much bigger, milder, and sweeter, with a gentle onion taste and no real garlic kick. For a closer match in Southern California, I'd still go with scallions plus a little extra garlic — that gets you nearer to ramps' bold flavor. Serves 4, low-carb 1 lb ground pork sausage (breakfast or Italian style) 2 bunches fresh ramps (when available) — or substitute 6 scallions + 4 cloves garlic 1 small onion, sliced 2 tbsp butter or bacon grease Salt & black pepper to taste Optional: pinch of red pepper flakes Trim and clean the ramps thoroughly. Slice the white bulbs into ½ inch pieces and roughly chop the green leaves. If using substitute, slice scallions and mince the garlic. Heat butter or bacon grease in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sausage and sliced onion, breaking up the meat as it cooks. Cook until sausage is browned and onion is soft, about 8 minutes. Add the ramp bulbs (or scallions + garlic) and cook for another 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Stir in the chopped ramp greens (or scallion greens) and cook just until wilted, about 1-2 minutes. Taste and season with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes if you like heat. Serving tip: In West Virginia this is often eaten straight from the skillet with a side of cornbread. For low-carb, just eat it as-is or serve over scrambled eggs. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Skillet
recipes.how: 4 chicken breasts or 6 thighs 2 tbsp butter 4 cloves garlic, minced 1 cup heavy cream ½ cup chicken broth ½ cup grated Parmesan 2 cups fresh spinach ½ cup sun-dried tomatoes, chopped 1 tsp Italian seasoning Salt and pepper Season chicken with salt, pepper, and Italian seasoning. In your 12-inch non-stick pan over medium heat, melt 1 tbsp butter and cook chicken until golden and cooked through (about 6–7 minutes per side). Remove and set aside. In the same pan, melt remaining butter, add garlic and cook 30 seconds. Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Simmer for 2–3 minutes. Stir in Parmesan until melted and sauce thickens slightly. Add sun-dried tomatoes and spinach. Cook until spinach wilts. Return chicken to the pan and spoon sauce over it. Simmer 2 more minutes. Super easy, one-pan, and very low-carb. Perfect for your non-stick skillet. Carb rating (Moderate): Veg/fruit/dairy carbs without heavy flour/sugar (tomatoes, pepper) — moderate.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Pot Roast (Elevated Version with Red Wine)
recipes.how: 3–4 lb boneless beef chuck roast (well-marbled for best results) 2–3 tbsp high-quality avocado oil or ghee (for searing) 1 large yellow onion, thickly sliced 8–10 oz mushrooms (cremini or mixed), halved or quartered 4–6 garlic cloves, smashed 1 cup dry red wine (plus extra if you like bolder flavor) 2–3 cups high-quality beef bone broth (instead of plain water + beef base for deeper flavor) 1–2 tbsp beef base (reduced amount since broth is used) 2–3 tbsp Worcestershire sauce 2–3 tbsp tomato paste (new — adds umami and body) 2–3 bay leaves 2–3 sprigs fresh thyme or 1 tsp dried (highly recommended) 1–2 sprigs rosemary (optional but excellent) 1 tsp smoked paprika ½–1 tsp black pepper 1½–2 tsp fine sea salt (or to taste) 4–6 tbsp high-quality unsalted butter (grass-fed), divided 2–3 tbsp butter powder (for extra richness) 2–3 tbsp all-purpose flour or arrowroot (for thickening at end) (lower-carb option: 3/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) Optional veggie add-ins: 4–6 carrots in large chunks, 1 lb baby potatoes or parsnips nstructions Summary: Pat roast dry, season generously with salt, pepper, paprika. Sear in hot oil/ghee 3–4 min per side until deep brown (Maillard magic). Transfer to slow cooker. In the same pan, sauté onion, mushrooms, garlic 4–5 min. Add tomato paste, cook 1 min. Deglaze with red wine, scraping bits, simmer 2–3 min to reduce slightly. Pour over roast. Add bone broth, beef base, Worcestershire, herbs, butter powder. Nestle in carrots/potatoes if using. Dot with 2 tbsp butter. Cover and cook on LOW 8–10 hours (or HIGH 4–5 hours) until fork-tender. Remove roast and veggies. Strain liquid if desired. Mash 2–3 tbsp butter with flour into a paste (beurre manié), whisk into hot liquid on stovetop or “high” slow cooker setting until thickened (5–10 min). Taste and adjust seasoning. Shred or slice roast, return to gravy. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (flour, potatoes). Carb swap: thicken with a little arrowroot slurry instead of flour/cornstarch; swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Loaded baked potato soup
recipes.how: Prep time 35 minutes -2 large onions, chopped - 3 tablespoons butter - 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) - 2 cups water, divided - 4 cups chicken broth - 2 medium potatoes, peeled and diced - 1 and a half cups mashed potato flakes - Half a pound sliced bacon, cooked and crumbled - 3/4 teaspoon pepper - 1/2 teaspoon salt - 1/2 teaspoon dried basil - 1/8 teaspoon dried thyme - 1 cup half and half cream In a large skillet, sauté the onions and butter until they’re tender. Stir in the Flour. Gradually stir in one cup water. Bring to a boil; cook and stir for two minutes or until thickened. Transferred to a 5 quart slow cooker. 2. Add the chicken broth, potatoes, potato flakes, bacon, pepper, salt, basil, thyme, and remaining water. Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or until the potatoes are tender. Stirring and half-and-half cream; heat through garnish with cheese and green onions. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (potato, flour, potatoes). Carb swap: swap AP flour for almond flour (psyllium helps bind baked goods); swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour structure beats arrowroot for baked flour swaps.) Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this soup. Cauliflower or turnip in place of the potatoes and potato flakes makes a thinner, lighter soup that does not taste like baked potato, though the bacon and cream keep the loaded flavor.

recipes.title: Lemon chicken rice soup
recipes.how: 1. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and oregano. Sear in ghee/avocado oil until golden, then remove and set aside. 2. Sauté onion, garlic, and carrots 4–5 minutes. Add rice and toast 1 minute. Pour in bone broth, return chicken, and simmer 20–25 minutes until rice is tender and chicken is cooked. 3. Remove chicken, shred or chop, and return to pot. In a bowl, whisk eggs with lemon zest and juice. Slowly temper the egg-lemon mixture with hot broth (whisk constantly to avoid curdling), then stir back into the soup off heat. 4. Warm gently if needed (do not boil). Finish with butter if using. Adjust seasoning and lemon brightness. Chemistry Lens Chicken proteins break down and release collagen into the broth during simmering, creating natural body. Rice starches gelatinize and release amylose, lightly thickening the soup. The avgolemono technique uses egg proteins (lecithin and albumen) that emulsify with lemon acids and hot broth, forming a stable, silky suspension without curdling when properly tempered. Lemon’s citric acid brightens flavors and helps tenderize chicken slightly. Ghee provides stable fats that carry aromatics. Sensory Science (Flavor & Aroma Triggering Enjoyment) Bright lemon acidity activates sour receptors while balancing the savory umami from chicken and bone broth. Garlic, oregano, and white pepper deliver warm, herbal, and floral notes that bloom retronasally. The egg-lemon finish creates a rich, tangy creaminess that triggers strong comfort and refreshment responses — it feels both light and deeply satisfying. Dill/parsley adds fresh green volatiles that keep the palate engaged, making each spoonful craveable. Ingredients: • 1–1½ lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs (preferred for flavor and moisture) or breasts • 2 tbsp high-quality ghee or avocado oil • 1 large yellow onion, diced • 3–4 garlic cloves, minced • 2 carrots, finely diced (optional, for subtle sweetness) • ½ cup long-grain white rice (or arborio for creamier texture) • 6–7 cups high-quality chicken bone broth • Zest and juice of 2–3 large lemons (about ⅓–½ cup juice) • 2–3 eggs (for the signature silky avgolemono finish) • 1–2 tsp dried oregano • ½ tsp white pepper (or black) • 1–1½ tsp fine sea salt (to taste) • Fresh dill or parsley for garnish • Optional richness: 2–3 tbsp grass-fed butter or butter powder stirred in at the end Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (rice). Carb swap: swap rice for cauliflower rice. Grok Bot estimated cook time.

recipes.title: Toasted Cauliflower Pizza Casserole
recipes.how: 2 large heads cauliflower (about 4–5 lbs), cut into bite-sized florets 2–3 tbsp ghee or avocado oil (for roasting) 1.5–2 lbs grass-fed ground beef 1 large onion, diced 8–10 oz mushrooms (cremini or button), sliced 3–4 garlic cloves, minced 1 jar (24–28 oz) high-quality pizza sauce (no added sugar) or homemade ½–¾ cup heavy cream (or coconut cream for dairy-free) ½ cup beef bone broth 3–4 cups shredded low-moisture mozzarella (divided) 4–6 oz sliced pepperoni (nitrate-free preferred) 2 tsp dried oregano 1 tsp dried basil ½–1 tsp fennel seed (optional, for sausage-like depth) 1–1½ tsp fine sea salt + black pepper Optional: 2–3 tbsp grated Parmesan, fresh basil for garnish, red pepper flakes This transforms the original pasta-heavy pizza casserole into a flavorful, toasted cauliflower bake. Roasting the cauliflower creates crispy, caramelized edges that mimic rigatoni, absorbing all the pizza flavors. Eliminated can cream of mushroom soup. Instructions Summary: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss cauliflower florets with ghee/avocado oil, salt, pepper, and 1 tsp oregano. Spread on two baking sheets and roast 25–30 minutes until golden and toasted (edges crispy). Reduce oven to 375°F. While cauliflower roasts: Brown ground beef in a large skillet. Drain excess fat if needed, then add onion and mushrooms. Cook until softened. Add garlic and remaining spices; cook 1 min. Stir in pizza sauce, bone broth, and heavy cream. Simmer 5–7 minutes until slightly thickened. Taste and adjust seasoning. In a large baking dish: Layer half the roasted cauliflower, half the meat sauce, and half the mozzarella. Repeat layers. Top with pepperoni slices and remaining cheese. Bake at 375°F for 20–25 minutes until bubbly and pepperoni is crisp. Broil 2–3 minutes for extra toasty top if desired. Rest 5–10 minutes before serving. Carb rating (High): Name points to a starch- or sugar-heavy dish (bread/dessert/pasta family). Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend; swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Beef fajitas
recipes.how: 12–16 oz (¾–1 lb) beef top sirloin (or preferably flank/skirt steak), cut into thin strips against the grain 2 tbsp avocado oil (divided) 2 tbsp fresh lime juice 3–4 garlic cloves, minced 2 tsp ground cumin 2 tsp chili powder 1 tsp fine sea salt + ½ tsp black pepper ½–¾ tsp crushed red pepper flakes (increased for spicier profile) ¼–½ tsp cayenne pepper (optional, for extra heat) 1 large green bell pepper, julienned 1 large yellow or red onion, julienned 4–6 high-quality flour tortillas (warmed) Optional: ½ tsp smoked paprika, fresh cilantro, sliced avocado, sour cream Instructions with Pan Temperature Guidance: Marinate: Whisk together 1 tbsp avocado oil, lime juice, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt, pepper, red pepper flakes, and cayenne. Toss with beef strips. Marinate 30–60 minutes (or up to 4 hours in fridge). Prep Pan Temperature: Place your cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Use your ThermoWorks laser scanner to check surface temperature. Target 425–450°F (218–232°C) for excellent searing and char. Add 1 tbsp avocado oil when the pan reaches ~400°F — it should shimmer and lightly smoke. Cook Beef: Add beef in a single layer (work in batches if needed to avoid crowding). Sear 2–2½ minutes per side until well browned but still medium-rare inside (internal beef temp ~130–135°F / 54–57°C if you Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (flour). Carb swap: swap AP flour for almond flour (psyllium helps bind baked goods). (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour structure beats arrowroot for baked flour swaps.) Grok Bot estimated cook time.

recipes.title: Chicken Fajitas
recipes.how: Serves 2 (generous portions) This should be a hit for Peter! It pairs excellently with the refried beans or the lemon chicken rice soup we developed earlier. 12–16 oz (¾–1 lb) boneless, skinless chicken thighs (preferred) or breasts, cut into thin strips 2 tbsp avocado oil (divided) 2 tbsp fresh lime juice 3–4 garlic cloves, minced 2 tsp ground cumin 2 tsp chili powder 1 tsp fine sea salt + ½ tsp black pepper ½–¾ tsp crushed red pepper flakes ¼–½ tsp cayenne pepper (for extra heat) 1 large green bell pepper, julienned 1 large yellow or red onion, julienned 4–6 high-quality flour tortillas (warmed) Optional: ½ tsp smoked paprika, fresh cilantro, sliced avocado, sour cream Instructions with Pan Temperature Guidance: Marinate: Whisk together 1 tbsp avocado oil, lime juice, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt, pepper, red pepper flakes, and cayenne. Toss with chicken strips. Marinate 30–60 minutes (or up to 4 hours in fridge). Prep Pan Temperature: Place your cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Use your ThermoWorks laser scanner to target 400–425°F (204–218°C) for the chicken. Add 1 tbsp avocado oil when the pan reaches ~375°F — it should shimmer and lightly smoke. Cook Chicken: Add chicken strips in a single layer (in batches if needed). Sear 3–4 minutes per side until well browned and internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). Remove and set aside. (Chicken needs slightly longer and a touch lower peak temp than beef to stay juicy.) Cook Vegetables: In the same skillet (still hot, ~400°F+), add peppers and onions. Stir-fry 4–6 minutes until charred and tender-crisp. Combine: Return chicken to the skillet, toss everything for 30–60 seconds to combine flavors and reheat. Serve immediately in warm tortillas with toppings. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (beans, rice, flour). Carb swap: swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk; swap rice for cauliflower rice. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.)

recipes.title: Fresh pumpkin soup (slow cooker)
recipes.how: Pumpkin Apple Soup Recipe - 8 cups chopped fresh pumpkin (about 3 pounds) - 4 cups chicken broth - 3 small tart apples, peeled and chopped - 1 medium onion, chopped - 2 tablespoons lemon juice - 2 tablespoons minced fresh ginger root - 2 garlic cloves, minced - 1/2 teaspoon salt - Toasted pumpkin seeds - 1 teaspoon avocado oil - 1/8 teaspoon salt 1. Prepare the Soup: - In a slow cooker, combine the chopped pumpkin, chicken broth, chopped apples, chopped onion, lemon juice, minced ginger root, minced garlic cloves, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. - Cover and cook on low for about 8 to 10 hours, or until the pumpkin and apples are tender. 2. Prepare the Toasted Pumpkin Seeds: - Meanwhile, toss the pumpkin seeds with avocado oil and 1/8 teaspoon salt. - Spread the seeds onto an ungreased 15 by 10 by 1-inch baking pan. - Bake the seeds at 250 degrees Fahrenheit for 45 to 50 minutes, or until golden brown. Set aside to cool. 3. Finish the Soup: - Once the soup is cooked, cool it slightly. - Process the soup in batches in a blender until smooth. - Transfer the blended soup to a large saucepan and heat through. - Garnish with the toasted pumpkin seeds before serving. Carb rating (Moderate): Veg/fruit/dairy carbs without heavy flour/sugar (apple, onion) — moderate.

recipes.title: Kentucky Burgoo
recipes.how: ¾ lb pork shoulder, cut into 2–3 inch chunks ¾ lb beef chuck roast, cut into 2–3 inch chunks 2–3 bone-in chicken thighs 2 tbsp avocado oil or ghee 1 medium onion, chopped 1 green bell pepper, chopped 2 carrots, chopped 2 celery stalks, chopped 3 garlic cloves, minced 3 cups beef bone broth 2 cups chicken bone broth 1 (14-oz) can crushed tomatoes 1 large potato, peeled and cubed ½ cup frozen corn ½ cup frozen lima beans 2–3 tbsp Worcestershire sauce Salt and black pepper to taste Hot sauce (for serving) Instructions with Pan Temperature Guidance: Pat all meats dry and season well with salt and pepper. Heat your 12-inch wider Le Creuset Dutch oven over medium-high. Use your ThermoWorks scanner to reach 380–410°F (193–210°C). Add the avocado oil or ghee when the pan hits ~360°F. Working in batches, sear the pork, then beef, then chicken thighs until deeply browned on all sides. Remove to a plate. In the same pot, add onion, bell pepper, carrots, and celery. Cook 6–8 minutes until nicely browned. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds more. Return all meats to the pot. Add both broths, crushed tomatoes, and a bay leaf if you have one. Bring to a simmer, reduce to low, cover, and cook gently for 2 hours until the meats are very tender. Remove the meats, shred or chop (discard chicken bones and skin), and return to the pot. Add the cubed potato and cook 30–40 minutes until tender. Stir in corn, lima beans, and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer another 10–15 minutes until thick. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serving Suggestion: Ladle into bowls and serve with hot sauce on the side. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (potato, corn, beans). Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip. Grok Bot estimated cook time.

recipes.title: Carne Adovada for Two
recipes.how: 1 to 1.25 lbs boneless pork shoulder (butt), cut into 1.5–2 inch cubes 2–3 Tbsp avocado oil (divided) 1 medium yellow onion, diced (about 1.5 cups) 4 garlic cloves, minced 1–2 canned chipotle chiles in adobo, minced (start with 1 for moderate heat; sauce included) 2 Tbsp chili powder (New Mexico red if possible, or your favorite blend) 1 tsp ground cumin ½ tsp Mexican oregano ¾ cup strong brewed coffee (black, no sugar) ⅓ cup raisins (dark preferred for deeper flavor) 1 cup chicken or beef broth (low-sodium) Zest of 1 lime + juice of ½–1 lime (to taste) Salt and black pepper, to taste Fresh cilantro, chopped (for finishing) Optional: ½ tsp monk fruit baking blend if you want a tiny extra roundness (taste first) Method Prep (10 min): Pat pork dry, season generously with salt and pepper. Let it sit 15–20 minutes at room temp for better browning. Sear the pork (high-heat stage): Heat your Le Creuset Dutch oven over medium-high. Use ThermoWorks laser scanner—target 425–450°F pan surface. Add 1–2 Tbsp avocado oil; it should shimmer immediately. Work in batches: sear pork cubes 2–3 minutes per side until deep mahogany crust forms. Don’t crowd—remove to a plate. This builds fond (Maillard compounds) critical for flavor. Lower to medium if it smokes too hard. Build the sauce base: In the same pot (add a splash more avocado oil if dry), drop heat to medium (~300–350°F). Add onions, cook 5–6 minutes until softened and edges turn golden. Stir in garlic and chipotle for 1 minute until fragrant. Add chili powder, cumin, and oregano—toast 30–45 seconds to bloom oils and deepen color without burning. Deglaze and simmer: Pour in coffee and scrape up all that fond. Add raisins, broth, and seared pork with juices. Bring to a gentle simmer (surface ~200–210°F). Stir in half the lime zest. Braise: Cover and transfer to 325°F oven for 2–2.5 hours, or use your slow cooker on low for 6–8 hours. Pork should be fork-tender but not falling apart completely—stir once halfway. Sauce thickens naturally from pork collagen and raisins. Finish: Off heat, stir in lime juice and remaining zest. Taste and adjust salt/heat. Let rest 10 minutes—the sauce will cling better. Serve over cauliflower rice, refried beans (from our list), or straight up with warm tortillas if you allow occasional ones. Top generously with cilantro. Slow cooker version: Sear on stovetop first (worth it for flavor), then transfer everything to slow cooker on low. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (sugar).

recipes.title: Green Chile Cheeseburger W/  Grind option
recipes.how: For the patties: 1 lb ground beef (80/20 preferred for juiciness) or grind 1 lb beef (recommend 70% chuck + 30% brisket or short rib trimmings for optimal flavor, fat, and texture — ask your butcher or use what you have) 2 garlic cloves, minced (up from 1 for better aroma) 1 tsp kosher salt ½ tsp black pepper ½ tsp ground cumin (optional, for earthy depth) For the roasted green chile topping: 3 Anaheim chiles (or Hatch if available), roasted, skinned, seeded, and roughly chopped 1 medium yellow onion, sliced into ½-inch rounds 1–2 tbsp avocado oil or ghee Salt to taste For the Creamy Roasted Chile Crema (the star upgrade): ¼ cup sour cream 2 oz cream cheese, softened 1–2 roasted Anaheim chiles (from above), finely chopped or blended 1 garlic clove, minced 1 tsp lime juice (brightens, cuts richness) Salt & pepper to taste Optional: pinch of monk fruit baking blend if you want subtle sweetness to balance heat (minimal, chemistry impact negligible in savory) To assemble: 4–6 large butter lettuce leaves or low-carb buns (toasted in ghee for crispness) 4–6 slices sharp cheddar and/or pepper jack cheese Optional garnishes: sliced avocado, fresh cilantro, pickled jalapeños for extra pop and color Step-by-Step Instructions Roast the vegetables (builds foundational flavor via Maillard): Preheat your Le Creuset square grilling pan or All-Clad 12-inch over medium-high. Use ThermoWorks laser scanner—target 425–450°F (218–232°C) surface temp. Toss chiles and onion rounds with 1 tbsp avocado oil, salt. Grill/roast, turning occasionally, until deeply charred and softened (8–12 min). Skin chiles (steam in bag 5 min if needed), seed, chop. Set aside half for crema, half for topping. This step prevents dryness and adds smoky sweetness. Make the Creamy Chile Crema: In your All-Clad emerging blender or food processor (or by hand), blend sour cream, cream cheese, garlic, lime juice, and chopped roasted chiles until smooth. Taste and adjust salt. This emulsion provides creamy mouthfeel (fat + protein stabilization) and carries the chile heat evenly. Keep at room temp or warm gently. Form & cook patties: Gently mix beef with minced garlic, salt, pepper, cumin. Form 2 loose patties (don’t overwork—preserves tenderness). Heat Le Creuset or All-Clad frying pan to 400–425°F (scanner check). Add 1 tsp avocado oil or ghee. Sear patties 3–4 min per side for crust (Maillard again). In last 1–2 min, top with cheese slices—cover briefly if needed for perfect melt. Rest 3–5 min (juices redistribute for moist bite). Assemble for maximum appeal: On plate or toasted low-carb bun/lettuce: generous smear of crema on bottom (prevents sogginess, adds creaminess), patty with melted cheese, pile of roasted onions + chiles (nestled into cheese for integration), another drizzle of crema, top with lettuce/avocado. The visual layering—golden-brown patty, orange cheese pull, vibrant green chiles, creamy white sauce—screams restaurant quality. Total time keeps it weeknight doable. Chef Tips Juiciness hack: Higher fat beef + minimal handling + resting = no dry burgers. Fat also aids in carrying volatile chile aromas. Pan temp precision: Your ThermoWorks is gold—high heat for crust without overcooking interior. Rheology note: Crema’s viscosity holds toppings without sliding; roasting reduces water content in peppers. Make-ahead: Roast veggies and make crema up to 2 days ahead. Reheat gently. Variations Smoker boost: Use your outdoor smoker for chiles/onions at 225°F for 30–45 min before pan finish—deeper smoke aroma. Spicy upgrade: Mix in a seeded jalapeño or use hotter Hatch chiles. Casserole style (if you want hands-off): Turn into your Cauliflower Pizza Casserole vibe—layer in Le Creuset Dutch oven. Cheeseburger melt: Chop everything and make open-faced under broiler for max browning. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Peter’s Upgraded Slow Cooker Creamy Mushroom Beef Stew
recipes.how: Prep Time: 10–15 min (mostly Peter-proof) Cook Time: 6–8 hours on LOW (or 4–5 on HIGH) Servings: 2 generous (easy to double) Nutrition Notes (approx. per serving): ~550–650 cal, 35–45g fat, 8–12g net carbs (mostly onion/mushrooms), 45g+ protein. High satiety from fat + collagen in bone broth. Very low added sugar. 1.5–2 lbs stew beef (already cubed — look for chuck or similar; no extra chopping) 8–12 oz organic sliced mushrooms (pre-sliced saves him time) 1 medium yellow or white onion, roughly chopped or sliced (¼–½ onion if he wants even less) 3–4 garlic cloves, minced (or 1 tsp jarred minced garlic — zero chopping) 2–3 cups good beef bone broth (one or two packages; quality matters for flavor) 4 oz cream cheese, softened (the secret creamy upgrade — no canned soup) 1–1.5 tsp kosher salt (start low, taste at end) 1 tsp freshly ground black pepper (or to taste — we keep his pepper love but balance it) 1 tsp dried thyme (or 2–3 fresh sprigs if you have them) 1 bay leaf (optional but nice) 1–2 tbsp avocado oil or ghee (for quick sear — high smoke point, clean flavor) Optional simple add-ins for depth (if he’s game): 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce or a splash of red wine vinegar at the end for brightness Prepared for peter to replace the recipe he was using on Tuesdays June 5, 2026 Step-by-Step (Peter-Friendly) Quick sear (the flavor booster — 5 minutes, worth it): Pat beef dry. Heat your Le Creuset or All-Clad pan over medium-high to 400–425°F (ThermoWorks check). Add 1 tbsp avocado oil or ghee. Sear beef in batches 2–3 min per side until browned (not cooked through). Dump into slow cooker. This step alone makes it taste like it simmered all day with love. Dump the rest: Add sliced mushrooms, chopped onion, garlic, bone broth, thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper to the slow cooker. Stir gently. No fancy measuring — eye it. Cook low & slow: Cover and cook on LOW 6–8 hours (or HIGH 4–5). Beef should be fork-tender and falling apart. The long cook breaks down connective tissue for that melt-in-mouth texture. Creamy finish (last 10–15 min): Remove bay leaf. Stir in softened cream cheese until melted and silky. Taste and adjust salt/pepper. The cream cheese creates a rich, stable sauce that clings to the beef and mushrooms without separating. Serve: Ladle into bowls. Pairs great with the Green Chile Cheeseburgers or those Guinness onion rings we’re frying up. Visual: deep brown gravy, tender beef chunks, earthy mushrooms, creamy swirl. Chef Tips for You Two Make it even simpler for Peter: Buy everything prepped. He literally opens packages and hits “low.” The sear can be your weekend contribution or a “team” step. Rheology & texture: Cream cheese at the end prevents the grainy or broken sauce you sometimes get with canned soups. Mushrooms hold shape better than overcooked veggies. Low-carb focus: Mushrooms and onion give bulk and sweetness naturally. If you want more veg later, add zucchini or celery in the last hour. Leftovers: Even better the next day. Reheats beautifully in the slow cooker or microwave. Scaling: Easy to double for leftovers or company. Variations (Keep It Simple) Dump-and-go only: Skip sear, add everything raw. Still better than the original because of real ingredients. Slightly fancier (your days off): Add a splash of red wine with the broth or stir in fresh parsley at the end for color and brightness. Stroganoff twist: Same base, stir in sour cream instead of (or with) cream cheese at the end for classic tang. Spice nod: Keep his black pepper front and center but add a pinch of smoked paprika for warmth. This keeps Peter’s “throw it in the slow cooker” joy while delivering the depth and creaminess you were missing. He’ll still feel like the hero, and you’ll actually enjoy it. Carb rating (Moderate): ~12g net carbs noted — fits the moderate (about 11–30g) band.

recipes.title: Grilled Beef Teriyaki (Low-Carb, Real-Fat Version)
recipes.how: For the marinade/glaze (makes enough for beef + extra for brushing): ⅓ cup tamari or good soy sauce (tamari is lower carb/gluten-free option) 3–4 tbsp monk fruit baking blend (golden or classic — adjust to taste; it browns and caramelizes like sugar) 2 tbsp avocado oil or melted ghee (plus more for grilling) 2–3 garlic cloves, minced (or 1 tsp jarred) 1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated (or 1 tsp ground) 1 tsp toasted sesame oil (optional but adds that classic aroma) ½ tsp black pepper Optional: 1 tbsp rice vinegar or a splash of water to thin if needed For the beef & vegetables: 1–1.25 lbs flank steak, sirloin, or skirt steak (thinly sliced against the grain for tenderness — or buy pre-sliced if Peter’s doing it) 1 medium onion, sliced into thick rounds or wedges (caramelizes beautifully) 8–12 oz mushrooms, halved or thick-sliced (your favorite — cremini or button work great) Optional quick sides for low-carb plating: extra grilled zucchini or just the onions & mushrooms piled high Make the marinade: Whisk everything together in a bowl or zip bag. Taste — it should be savory-sweet with a good punch. Reserve ¼–⅓ cup separately for brushing/glazing later (don’t reuse the raw marinade on cooked meat for safety). Marinate the beef: Add the sliced beef to the remaining marinade. Massage it in. Let it sit 30–60 minutes at room temp or up to overnight in the fridge. The ginger, garlic, and acid help tenderize while the soy builds deep umami. Science note: The sugars (even from monk fruit) will caramelize on the grill for that signature shiny teri glaze. Prep your grill/pan: Heat your Le Creuset square grilling pan or outdoor grill to 425–450°F (use the ThermoWorks laser scanner — hot enough for good Maillard browning and char without burning the glaze). Lightly oil with avocado oil or ghee. Grill: Remove beef from marinade (let excess drip). Grill 2–4 minutes per side depending on thickness and desired doneness (medium-rare is classic for flank/skirt). In the last 1–2 minutes, brush with the reserved glaze so it caramelizes into that beautiful lacquer. At the same time, grill the onion wedges and mushrooms — they’ll pick up smoky sweetness and pair perfectly with the beef. Total cook is quick; don’t overdo it or it gets tough. Rest & serve: Let the beef rest 3–5 minutes, then slice thin against the grain. Pile with the grilled onions and mushrooms. Spoon any extra warm glaze over the top. Visual win: glossy mahogany beef with charred edges, golden onions, earthy mushrooms — restaurant-level on your own grill. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Low-Carb Silky Cheese Soup (Blender Method)
recipes.how: Prep: 15 min Cook: 15–20 min Servings: 2 generous Net carbs: ~5–8g per serving Base: 2 Tbsp butter (or ghee) 1 small shallot or ¼ small onion, finely minced (optional but adds depth with almost no carbs) 1 clove garlic, smashed (we’ll discard like original) 1½ cups good beef or chicken bone broth (low-sodium preferred) 1 cup heavy cream ½ lb good melting Cheddar (sharp or extra-sharp for flavor; or 6 oz Cheddar + 2 oz Gruyère for better stretch) 2 Tbsp cream cheese, softened (helps emulsify and thicken naturally — low-carb swap for flour) ⅛ tsp freshly grated nutmeg (fresh is noticeably better) ⅛ tsp white or black pepper (white keeps it elegant) Pinch of cayenne (optional — brightens) To finish: 2 egg yolks ¼ cup heavy cream (or crème fraîche for extra tang) 1–2 Tbsp dry white wine or sherry (optional but recommended for brightness) Grated Parmesan or aged Cheddar for topping Optional garnish: chopped chives or a few sautéed mushrooms for visual and flavor pop Step-by-Step (Modern, Precise, Still Elegant) Build the base (flavor foundation): In your Le Creuset or All-Clad saucepan, melt butter over medium-low. Add minced shallot/onion and smashed garlic. Cook gently 3–4 min until soft and fragrant (do not brown). Discard garlic clove. Add bone broth and bring to a gentle simmer. Blend the cheese mixture: While base simmers, put cubed Cheddar, cream cheese, nutmeg, pepper, and cayenne into your All-Clad emerging blender. Add ½ cup of the hot broth (careful — hot liquid). Blend on high 20–30 seconds until perfectly smooth and emulsified. The cream cheese acts as a natural stabilizer. Combine & heat gently: With blender running on low, slowly pour in the remaining hot broth + 1 cup heavy cream. Blend until silky. Pour everything back into the saucepan (or directly into a double-boiler setup if you prefer the gentlest heat). Optional wine brightness: Stir in white wine or sherry. Simmer very gently 5 min (do not boil hard). Liaison finish (the luxurious touch we keep): In a small bowl, whisk egg yolks with ¼ cup cream. Temper: add a ladle of hot soup to the yolks while whisking, then whisk the warmed yolks back into the soup. Heat gently over low heat or double boiler another 2–3 min until it thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon. Do not boil. Taste and adjust salt/pepper/nutmeg. Serve: Ladle into warm bowls. Top generously with grated Parmesan. Add chives or a few sautéed mushrooms if desired. The texture should be velvety, rich, and stable — no separation. ThermoWorks note: Keep the final heating below 180°F (82°C) after adding the liaison for perfect safety and texture. Blender note: Use your Blendtec Classic if you want the easiest, hottest, smoothest result (ideal for this). The All-Clad works fine too — just add the hot liquid very gradually on low speed and vent the lid. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Creamy Tarragon Flank Steak
recipes.how: (Works excellently with flap steak / carne asada meat) Servings: 2 For the Steak: • 1 lb flap steak or flank steak (flap steak / carne asada meat preferred — more flavorful and tender) • Salt and black pepper • 1 Tbsp avocado oil or melted beef tallow For the Creamy Tarragon Sauce: • 6 oz Philadelphia cream cheese, softened • 2 Tbsp grass-fed butter • 1 small shallot, very finely minced • 1 tsp Dijon mustard • 1 tsp white wine vinegar or tarragon vinegar • ½ tsp dried tarragon (or 1½ tsp fresh, minced) • 2–3 Tbsp heavy cream (to reach desired consistency) • Salt and pepper to taste 1. Pat steak dry and season generously with salt and pepper. Let sit at room temp while making sauce. 2. In a small saucepan over low heat, melt butter. Add minced shallot and cook 2–3 minutes until softened. 3. Add cream cheese, mustard, vinegar, and tarragon. Whisk until smooth and melted. 4. Whisk in heavy cream until sauce reaches a pourable consistency. Season to taste and keep warm. 5. Heat a grill pan or cast iron skillet over high heat. Add oil or tallow. Cook steak 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare (internal 130–135°F). Rest 5–10 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain. 6. Serve sliced steak with warm creamy tarragon sauce spooned over top. Note: Flap steak (carne asada meat) is preferred for this recipe. It has better marbling and flavor than traditional flank steak. Carb rating (Moderate): Veg/fruit/dairy carbs without heavy flour/sugar (pepper, wine) — moderate.

recipes.title: Spicy Roasted Chicken Legs for Two
recipes.how: 4–6 chicken legs (bone-in, skin-on) 2 Tbsp avocado oil or melted beef tallow 1½ tsp salt 1 tsp garlic powder 1 tsp smoked paprika ¾ tsp cayenne pepper (adjust to your heat preference) ½ tsp black pepper ½ tsp dried thyme or oregano (optional but recommended) Preheat your oven to 425°F (this high heat gives you crispy skin). Pat the chicken legs very dry with paper towels — this is important for crispy skin. Mix all the spices together with the oil to make a paste. Rub the spice mixture all over the chicken legs, getting under the skin where you can. Place them on a wire rack set over a baking sheet (this lets the fat drip away and makes the skin extra crispy). Roast for 40–45 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and crispy and the internal temperature reaches 175–180°F in the thickest part. The high heat + dry skin + good spice rub gives you crispy, spicy, flavorful chicken legs that are way better than just salt and pepper. Want me to tweak the heat level or add anything else to this before we file it? No, I think this is great. And, um, I'm going to do this for tomorrow's dinner. So I'll have a prime ribeye, $30 prime ribeye for breakfast tomorrow, and chicken legs for dinner. I'll be eating like a king.Frank here. Hell yeah, kid — that’s a damn good day of eating. Prime ribeye for breakfast and spicy roasted chicken legs for dinner? That’s eating like a king with zero guilt. Carb rating (Moderate): Veg/fruit/dairy carbs without heavy flour/sugar (pepper) — moderate.

recipes.title: Beer-Battered Fried Zucchini for Two
recipes.how: 2 medium zucchini 1–1½ tsp salt (for drawing out water) ¾ cup all-purpose flour ¼ cup cornstarch 1 tsp baking powder ½ tsp salt ½ tsp garlic powder ¼ tsp black pepper 1 cup very cold beer (or sparkling water) Beef tallow or avocado oil for frying Method — Drying (Very Important): Slice zucchini into ¼-inch rounds or sticks. Place in a colander, toss with 1–1½ tsp salt, and let sit for 30 minutes. Rinse briefly under cold water. Lay slices in a single layer between paper towels and press firmly to remove as much moisture as possible. Let them sit another 10 minutes to air dry. Batter & Frying: In a bowl, whisk together flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, garlic powder, and pepper. Just before frying, slowly whisk in the very cold beer until the batter is smooth but still has some lumps. Keep the bowl cold. Heat beef tallow or avocado oil to 375°F. Dip the dried zucchini pieces in the batter, let excess drip off, and fry in small batches for 2–3 minutes until deep golden and crispy. Drain on a wire rack and season with salt immediately. Why this works: The cold beer creates steam when it hits the hot oil, which makes the batter extra light and crispy. The cornstarch helps with crunch, and all that careful drying prevents the zucchini from steaming itself and making the batter soggy. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (flour). Carb swap: swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.) Flour is the best for this recipe because: a frying batter turns crisp because wheat starch gelatinizes and dries out in the oil; almond-flour batter soaks up oil, browns before it crisps, and slides off. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this fried zucchini. Almond flour has no starch to gelatinize and dry out in the hot oil, so the batter fries heavier and oilier, browns before it crisps, and tends to slip off the zucchini.

recipes.title: Creamy beef tomato soup
recipes.how: - 2 pounds ground beef - 1 large sweet yellow onion, diced - 3–4 garlic cloves, minced - 2 red bell peppers, roasted (instructions below) - 4 cups beef broth (or equivalent made with beef bouillon cubes dissolved in hot water; adjust salt accordingly) - 1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes - 3–4 tablespoons tomato paste - 8 ounces cream cheese, cubed and at room temperature for easier melting - Avocado oil, for brushing the peppers - Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste - Optional seasonings: dried basil, oregano, or fresh herbs for garnish 1. **Roast the red peppers**: Preheat oven to 425°F. Halve peppers, remove stems and seeds, and brush with avocado oil. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Roast for 15–20 minutes until skins are charred. Transfer to a covered bowl or paper bag to steam for 10 minutes. Peel skins, dice peppers, and set aside. 2. **Brown the beef and aromatics**: In a large pot over medium-high heat, brown ground beef, breaking it up with a spoon. Add diced sweet yellow onion and minced garlic once beef begins to brown. Cook until onion softens and beef is no longer pink (7–10 minutes). Drain excess fat. 3. **Incorporate the peppers and build the base**: Stir in diced roasted red peppers and sauté for about 1 minute. Add beef broth, crushed tomatoes, and tomato paste. Stir well. 4. **Simmer**: Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cover partially and cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. 5. **Blend for texture**: Take the pot off the heat briefly. Blend about half the soup until smooth, then mix it back with the chunky soup for a creamy texture with beef and vegetables. 6. **Add creaminess**: On low heat, gradually add cubed cream cheese, stirring until melted for a rich texture. Avoid high heat to prevent curdling. 7. **Season and serve**: Adjust salt, pepper, and herbs to taste. Serve hot in warmed bowls. This method creates a hearty soup with beefy flavors, smoky roasted peppers, and a creamy texture from cream cheese. Partial blending adds texture contrast, as advised in professional recipes. Adjust as needed during cooking. Enjoy! Carb rating (Moderate): Veg/fruit/dairy carbs without heavy flour/sugar (tomato, onion, peppers) — moderate.

recipes.title: Pulled Pork and Gravy on potatoes
recipes.how: - Two boneless pork chops - 1 cup of chicken broth - 1 cup of red wine - 1 russet potato - 1/2 package of sliced mushrooms - 1 package of brown gravy In a pressure cooker, brown to pork chops in avocado oil. Add a cup of chicken stock or broth and a couple of port wine. Pressure cook on high for 38 minutes. Peel the potatoes, Boil and mash with lots of butter and heavy cream. And pepper to taste. When the pressure cooker is finished. Quick release the steam. Remove the chops from the pressure cooker and put on a plate. While on simmer setting, Pull enough liquid out of a pot to mix it with an envelope of brown gravy. When the gravy begins to thicken you can pour in the mushrooms. When the Mushrooms have reduced you can put the pork back in and pull it apart then mix all together, poor that over the mashed potatoes on a plate. I served for this recipe to Peter around June sixth 2020. He asked me to write it down. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (potatoes, potato). Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Garlic-Salt Steak Dust
recipes.how: Ratio 4 Tbsp garlic salt 2 Tbsp smoked paprika (or 2 Tbsp dried thyme + rosemary mixed, or 1 Tbsp each paprika + herbs) Combine in a small bowl and stir until evenly mixed. Transfer to a small jar or shaker. Label it. Store in a cool, dark cupboard. That’s it. No oil, no moisture, so it stays free-flowing. Carb rating (Carnivore): Primarily meat/eggs/fat (steak) — carnivore-friendly.

recipes.title: Bean and Beef Pie
recipes.how: 1 pound lean ground beef 2 garlic cloves, minced 1 can (11½ ounces) condensed bean with bacon soup, undiluted 1 jar (16 ounces) thick and chunky picante sauce, divided ¼ cup cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 teaspoon dried parsley 1 teaspoon paprika 1 teaspoon salt ¼ teaspoon pepper 1 can (16 ounces) kidney beans, rinsed and drained 1 can (15 ounces) black beans, rinsed and drained 1 can (2¼ ounces) sliced ripe black olives, drained, divided 2 cups (8 ounces) shredded Cheddar cheese, divided ½ cup sliced green onions, divided Pastry for a double-crust pie (9-inch) 1 cup (8 ounces) sour cream 1. In a skillet, cook the ground beef and garlic until the beef is browned. Drain. 2. In a large bowl, combine the soup, 1 cup of the picante sauce, cornstarch, parsley, paprika, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Fold in the beans, half of the olives, 1¼ cups of the cheese, the green onions, and the cooked beef mixture. 3. Line a deep-dish pie plate with the bottom pastry. Fill with the bean mixture. Top with the remaining pastry; seal and flute the edges. Cut slits in the top crust. 4. Bake at 425°F for 30–35 minutes or until lightly browned. Let stand 5 minutes before cutting. 5. Garnish with sour cream and the remaining picante sauce, cheese, and olives. (Adapted from a Taste of Home Grand Prize winner) Carb rating (High): Name points to a starch- or sugar-heavy dish (bread/dessert/pasta family). Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend; swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Chicken Parmigiana
recipes.how: 6 boneless, skinless chicken breasts 1/2 cup Italian seasoned bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1/2 cup crushed pork rinds) 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese, divided 1 egg 1/4 to 1/3 cup olive oil 2 cups spaghetti sauce 1 clove garlic, minced 1 tsp oregano 1 package (8 ounces) Mozzarella cheese, cut in 6 slices 3 cups hot cooked rotini pasta 2 tbsp dried parsley 1. Preheat oven to 350°F. 2. In a large, shallow bowl, combine bread crumbs and 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese. Place egg in another shallow bowl and beat thoroughly. 3. Dip chicken into beaten egg, letting excess drip off, then dip into bread mixture turning to coat thoroughly. Shake chicken to remove excess crumbs. 4. In large skillet, heat 1/4 cup olive oil over medium-high heat until hot. Add half the chicken; cook 5 minutes on each side, until golden brown. Remove to plate. Repeat with remaining chicken, adding more olive oil if necessary. 5. In a small bowl, combine spaghetti sauce, garlic and oregano; mix well. Pour into a 13x9-inch baking dish. Arrange chicken over sauce. Cover loosely with aluminum foil. Bake 30 minutes. 6. Remove foil from dish. Top each chicken breast with one slice of Mozzarella cheese. Sprinkle with remaining Parmesan cheese. Return dish to oven and bake 10 minutes longer or until Mozzarella cheese is lightly browned and sauce is bubbly. 7. To serve, toss hot cooked pasta with 1 tbsp olive oil and parsley. Serve with chicken and sauce. I was first served Chicken Parmigiana at my sister-in-law Cher's house, and it was one of the best chicken dishes I have ever eaten. She served it with pasta, broccoli and a crisp green salad. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (pasta, crisp, bread, spaghetti). Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Chicken Tortilla Bake
recipes.how: 3 cups shredded cooked chicken 1 can (4 ounces) chopped green chilies 1 can (2-1/4 ounces) sliced black olives, divided 1 cup chicken broth 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup, undiluted 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of chicken soup, undiluted 1 small onion, finely chopped 12 corn tortillas 2 cups (8 ounces) shredded Monterey Jack cheese, divided 1. In a bowl, combine the chicken, chilies, half of the olives, broth, soups and onion; set aside. 2. Warm tortillas in the microwave according to package directions. 3. Layer half of the tortillas on the bottom of a greased 13x9-inch baking dish (they will slightly overlap). Top with half of the chicken mixture and half of the cheese. Repeat layers. 4. Bake, uncovered, at 350°F for 30 minutes. Garnish with remaining olives. I recently discovered this tasty treasure, and have already made it a few times. This is a dish everyone will love, as it has tender chicken, creamy cheese, and a little zip from the green chilies. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (tortilla, corn). Carb swap: swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Country-Fried Steak
recipes.how: 3/4 cup flour (lower-carb option: 3/4 cup blanched almond flour) 1/4 cup cornmeal 1 tsp salt 1 tsp pepper 4 beef cube steaks (about 1 pound)* 2 eggs 2 tsp milk 4 tbsp avocado oil, divided (in place of cooking oil) Gravy 1 tbsp pan drippings 2 tbsp flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1-1/2 cups milk 1 tsp beef bouillon granules 1/8 tsp pepper Dash of salt 1. Combine flour, cornmeal, salt and pepper. In shallow dish, beat eggs and 2 tsp milk. Coat steaks in flour mixture, then dip into egg mixture. Dredge in flour mixture again, and let stand 2 minutes. 2. In a skillet, over medium-high heat (about 360°F), cook two steaks in 2 tbsp oil for 5-7 minutes on each side or until crisp, lightly browned and cooked as desired. Remove steaks and keep warm. Repeat with remaining oil and steaks. 3. Drain off all but 1 tbsp of the pan drippings; whisk in flour until well blended, cooking 1 minute. Gradually add the milk; bring to a boil over medium heat. Boil for 2 minutes, stirring constantly; reduce heat to medium-low. Add bouillon, pepper and salt; simmer, uncovered, for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Serve on steaks. What a comforting dish to sit down to. This is a classic that must be served with mashed potatoes. Useful Tip: Use ground beef if you don't like the texture of cube steak. Simply shape into large, thin patties the size of cube steaks and proceed with the recipe. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (potatoes, flour). Carb swap: swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk; swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.)

recipes.title: Fettuccine Alfredo
recipes.how: 2 ounces cream cheese, cut in bits 1/2 cup butter 1 cup half and half 3/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1/4 tsp pepper 8 ounces fettuccine noodles, cooked and drained 1. In a large saucepan, combine cream cheese, butter, and half and half. Cook and stir over medium heat until smooth. Stir in Parmesan cheese and pepper and cook and stir until cheese is melted and sauce is creamy. 2. Toss pasta lightly with sauce, coating well. Serve immediately. Serve a heaping portion of this rich pasta delight along with some garlic breadsticks and steamed broccoli. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (pasta). Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Macaroni and Cheese
recipes.how: 2 cups uncooked elbow macaroni 1/2 cup butter 1/2 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1-3/4 cups milk 1 cup sour cream 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1/2 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper 1/2 tsp. dry mustard 2 cups (8 ounces) grated Sharp Cheddar cheese, divided 1. Preheat oven to 350º. 2. Cook macaroni in salted boiling water according to package directions. Drain and rinse with cold water. Pour into a 2-quart baking dish. 3. In a saucepan, melt butter and stir in flour. Cook and stir for one minute. Gradually stir in milk. Add sour cream, Parmesan cheese, salt, pepper and mustard. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until sauce bubbles and thickens. Stir in half of the Cheddar cheese until melted. 4. Toss macaroni with remaining Cheddar cheese. Pour sauce over macaroni and mix thoroughly. 5. Bake, uncovered, for 1 hour, or until bubbly and brown. The first time I made this, the boys took one look at their plates, crinkled up their noses and asked "What is this?". In between giggling, I explained it was "real macaroni and cheese", as this does not have the appearance of boxed macaroni and cheese of which they were so accustomed to. It took a few bites, but they finally approved of this "other" macaroni and cheese. This is the best version of macaroni and cheese I have eaten. Useful Tip: 8 ounces process, cubed American cheese (Velveeta) may be added in addition to the Parmesan and Cheddar cheeses. The American cheese makes it a bit more creamy and rich. I have made it both ways and both are irresistibly delicious. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (macaroni). Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Monterey Jack Casserole
recipes.how: 1 pound ground beef 1 tbsp. instant minced onion 1 package (8 ounces) corn chips, crushed (3 cups crushed) 1 can (15 ounces) mild enchilada sauce 1-1/2 cups (6 ounces) shredded Monterey Jack cheese Sour cream, optional 1. Preheat oven to 350º. 2. In skillet, brown ground beef. Add onion; reduce heat and saute 5 minutes. Drain excess fat. 3. Place 2 cups crushed corn chips in bottom of greased 1-1/2-quart dish. Layer ground beef over chips. Pour enchilada sauce over beef. Top with cheese. 4. Bake 20 to 30 minutes or until bubbly and heated through. 5. Sprinkle remaining corn chips over top of casserole. Bake an additional 5 minutes. Top individual servings with sour cream, if desired. What a delicious casserole when you need dinner in a snap. Serve with corn bread and a guacamole-topped salad, maybe a few olives for garnish, and presto, dinner is done! Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (corn, bread). Carb swap: swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Pork Chops with Scalloped Potatoes
recipes.how: 3 tbsp. butter 3 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 3/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1-1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1 can (14-1/2 ounces) chicken broth 6 rib or loin pork chops 2 tbsp. avocado oil (in place of vegetable oil) 6 cups thinly sliced peeled potatoes 1 medium onion, chopped 1. In a saucepan, melt butter; stir in flour, salt and pepper. Add chicken broth; cook and stir constantly until mixture boils. Cook for 1 minute; remove from heat and set aside. 2. In a skillet, brown pork chops in hot oil. 3. In a greased 13x9-inch baking dish, layer potatoes and onion. Pour the broth mixture over. Place pork chops on top. Cover and bake at 350º for one hour; uncover and bake 30 minutes longer or until potatoes are fork tender. These are the best scalloped potatoes, and make a wonderful meal topped with pork chops. Of course, serve applesauce on the side for dipping! Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (potatoes, flour). Carb swap: swap AP flour for almond flour (psyllium helps bind baked goods); swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour structure beats arrowroot for baked flour swaps.) Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this dish. Turnips or cauliflower bake softer and give off more water than potatoes, and xanthan lacks the starch that makes creamy, sliceable layers, so the scalloped side comes out looser and lighter.

recipes.title: Pork Cordon Bleu
recipes.how: 12 thin-sliced center-cut pork chops, boneless 6 slices Swiss cheese 6 slices smoked ham Flour (lower-carb option: same amount blanched almond flour) 1 egg, beaten 2 tbsp. water 1-1/2 cups Ritz cracker crumbs (lower-carb option: 1-1/2 cups crushed pork rinds) Lard or avocado oil for frying (in place of oil or shortening) 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed Golden Mushroom Soup, undiluted 1/3 cup heavy cream 1. Pound meat slices until very thin. Top 6 of the slices with a slice of cheese and a slice of ham cut slightly smaller than the meat. Top with remaining meat slices. Press together. 2. Dip the meat carefully into flour on both sides, then dip into egg beaten with water. Dip into crumbs, pressing firmly to make crumbs adhere. 3. Fry slowly in oil, about 45 minutes, so pork has time to cook through and is richly browned. Drain on paper towel. 4. In a saucepan, combine soup and cream; heat until bubbly. Serve pork topped with sauce. If you are looking for a spectacular dish to serve guests, or treat you family to, look no further, this is it! What a wonderful combination pork, ham and Swiss cheese make. Of course, classic Chicken Cordon Bleu is delicious, but a change once in awhile is nice, too. I usually serve this dish with Cheesy Mashed Potatoes . Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (potatoes, flour, cracker). Carb swap: thicken with a little arrowroot slurry instead of flour/cornstarch; swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Savory Pork and Vegetables
recipes.how: 2 tbsp. butter 4 boneless pork chops, 3/4-inch thick 1-1/2 cups sliced mushrooms 1/2 tsp. dried rosemary leaves, crushed 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup, undiluted 2 tbsp. water 1/2 lb. fresh green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces (or 1 package (9 ounces) frozen green beans) 4 cups hot cooked fettucine or linguine (8 ounces dry) 1. In skillet, in 1 tbsp. hot butter, cook pork chops 10 minutes or until browned on both sides. Remove. 2. In remaining hot butter, cook mushrooms with rosemary until tender and liquid is evaporated, stirring often. 3. Add soup, water and green beans. Heat to boiling. Return pork chops to skillet. Cover; cook over low heat 10 minutes or until pork chops are no longer pink and green beans are tender, stirring occasionally. Serve with hot cooked fettucine. Sometimes plain old pork chops can be boring, so here is a family pleasing recipe to turn ordinary pork chops into something extraordinary. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (beans). Carb swap: trim the highest-carb item (flour, sugar, starch, or grain) using almond flour, cauliflower, or monk fruit as fits the dish. (Chose that over arrowroot: no clear sauce-thickener role, so arrowroot was skipped.)

recipes.title: Sesame Chicken Strips
recipes.how: 1/2 cup mayonnaise 1 tsp. dried minced onion 1 tsp. dry mustard 1/2 cup crushed butter-flavor crackers 1/4 cup sesame seeds 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts SAUCE: 1/2 cup mayonnaise 2 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey (in place of 2 tbsp. honey) 1 tbsp. prepared mustard 1. In a bowl, combine 1/2 cup mayonnaise, onion and 1 tsp. mustard. In another bowl, combine crackers and sesame seeds. 2. Cut chicken lengthwise into 1/4-inch strips. Dip strips into mayonaise mixture, then into the cracker mixture. Place a single layer on a large greased baking sheet. Bake at 425º for 15 to 18 minutes or until juices run clear. 3. Combine sauce ingredients and serve with chicken strips. Yield: 5 to 6 appetizer servings. We enjoy a dinner of "just appetizers" once in awhile, and these chicken strips are always included on the menu, along with Mozzarella Cheese Sticks and Potato Skins . What a fun, family meal to eat in front of the TV...try it some night! Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (potato, honey). Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend; swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip. Sugar swap: The dipping sauce is never heated, so honey only sweetens it. Allulose honey is a 1:1 swap with the same body.

recipes.title: Sloppy Joes
recipes.how: 2 pounds ground beef 1/2 cup chopped onion 1/2 cup finely chopped green pepper 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed tomato soup, undiluted 1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce 1/3 cup golden monk fruit blend (in place of 1/3 cup packed brown sugar) 2 tbsp. ketchup 1-1/2 tbsp. Worchestershire sauce 1/2 tbsp. prepared mustard 1/2 tbsp. dry mustard 1/4 tsp. chili powder 1/4 tsp. garlic salt 10-15 hamburger buns 1. In a large saucepan or Dutch oven over medium heat, brown beef and onion. Add green pepper. Cook and stir 5 minutes; drain. Add the next 9 ingredients; bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Serve on buns. This homemade version beats the out-of-a-can type any day! And, it is so simple. Really requires little effort with rewarding results. I have modified this recipe from a much larger batch...was doubled...which makes this a perfect main dish to serve for a crowd. This size still makes more than enough for our family, but it makes great leftovers! A must try. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (brown sugar). Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend. Sugar swap: In a simmered sauce, brown sugar is for sweetness and its molasses note. Golden monk fruit blend covers both, and the ketchup and tomato soup still bring their own browning sugars.

recipes.title: Taco Pie
recipes.how: 1 pound ground beef 2 tbsp. taco seasoning mix 1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce 1-3/4 cups biscuit mix 1/2 cup milk 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese 3 cups shredded lettuce 2 tomatoes, chopped 1/2 cup sour cream 1/4 cup sliced black olives 1. Preheat oven to 400º. 2. In an 10 or 11-inch ovenproof skillet, brown ground beef; drain. Add taco seasoning mix and tomato sauce to ground beef. Simmer 5 minutes. Spread mixture evenly in skillet. Remove from heat. 3. In a mixing bowl, blend biscuit mix and milk. On a lightly floured surface, pat dough to form a circle about 1 inch smaller than the skillet. Transfer dough to top of beef mixture. 4. Bake in preheated oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until lightly browned. 5. Place a large platter or pizza pan upside down on skillet. Using pot holders, carefully turn skillet and platter over to transfer Taco Pie onto platter. 6. Assemble Taco Pie by sprinkling cheese to within 1 inch of edge of beef mixture. Distribute lettuce to within 1 inch of edge of cheese. Place tomatoes in center of cheese layer. Make 6 dallops of sour cream on pie. Garnish with olives. Cut into 6 wedges. This super delicious, super easy recipe is a perfect example of how appreciative you'll be of your cast iron skillet, as it goes from stovetop into the oven with ease. Carb rating (High): Name points to a starch- or sugar-heavy dish (bread/dessert/pasta family). Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend; swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Chicken 'n Dumplings
recipes.how: 1 large fryer chicken, cut up 2 celery stalks, sliced 4 carrots, peeled and sliced 1 medium onion, diced 1 can (14-1/2 ounces) chicken broth 2 tbsp. dried parsley 2 tsp. chicken bouillon granules 1-1/2 tsp. salt 1/2 to 1 tsp. pepper Water DUMPLINGS: 2 cups flour 4 tsp. baking powder 1 tsp. salt 3/4 cup milk 4 tbsp. avocado oil (in place of unspecified oil, usually vegetable oil) 1. Combine chicken, celery, carrots, onion, chicken broth, parsley, chicken bouillon granules, salt and pepper in a large pan or Dutch oven; add enough water to cover chicken. Bring to a boil; reduce heat, cover and simmer for 2 hours or until chicken is done. 2. Remove chicken and let stand until cool enough to handle. Remove skin from chicken and tear meat away from bones. Return meat to soup; discard skin and bones. Add more salt and pepper to taste, if desired. Return soup to a simmer. 3. In a mixing bowl, combine dumpling ingredients and mix well to form a stiff dough. Drop by tablespoonfuls into simmering soup. Cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes. Serve immediately. My mom made a similar recipe for this comforting dish, and I still remember the wonderful aroma of it cooking throughout the house. She didn't make it often, but when she did, what a treat. I especially loved the light, tender dumplings, which is still my most favorite part of this dish. (In a pinch, Bisquick dumplings are also very good). For those of you, like my good friend Cindy, who like a more Southern style of dumpling (heavier, chewier), the recipe is at the bottom (this is for you, Cindy...let's see you lose the recipe THIS time!). =) SOUTHERN STYLE DUMPLINGS (heavier and chewier) 2 cups flour 1 cup chicken broth 2 tsp. baking powder 2 eggs, beaten 1. Combine flour, broth, baking powder and eggs; mix well to form a stiff batter. Drop by tablespoonfuls into simmering soup. Cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (dumpling, flour). Carb swap: swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.) Flour is the best for this recipe because: noodles and dumplings need gluten to roll thin and hold together in boiling liquid; low-carb flours fall apart in the pot. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this dish. Almond-flour dumplings have no gluten to hold them together in simmering broth, so instead of light, tender dumplings you get dense, crumbly ones, and some will break apart in the pot.

recipes.title: Chilled Taco Salad
recipes.how: 1 pound lean ground beef 1 to 2 cloves garlic, minced 1 tbsp. chili powder 1 can (15 ounces) dark red kidney beans, undrained 1 jar (16 ounces) taco sauce 1 small can sliced black olives 1 tomato, diced 1/4 cup scallions, sliced 2 cups shredded Cheddar cheese or Monterey Jack cheese 1/2 to 1 head lettuce, shredded Crushed tortilla chips Sour cream and guacamole 1. Brown ground beef and garlic in skillet; drain. Return beef to skillet and add 1/2 jar taco sauce, chili powder and undrained kidney beans. Bring to a boil, simmer 10 minutes. 2. Pour beef mixture into a large bowl and chill in refrigerator. 3. Once chilled, add olives, tomato, scallions, cheese and lettuce. Mix well. 4. Top individual servings with crushed tortilla chips, sour cream, guacamole and remaining taco sauce, if desired. My good friend, Christina, served Don and I this wonderful chilled taco salad one day while visiting her and Travis when we were all stationed in California. We fell in love with it immediately, and it has become a regular on our menu since. I make this frequently in the warmer months, with fresh guacamole and sour cream. Sometimes I make sopapillias to go with it. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (beans, tortilla). Carb swap: swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Grilled Szechuan Chicken Salad
recipes.how: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts Seasoned pepper 1 can (8 ounces) pineapple slices 3 tbsp avocado oil (in place of vegetable oil) 2 tbsp soy sauce 2 tbsp reserved pineapple juice 1 tbsp vinegar 1 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey (in place of 1 tbsp honey) 1/4 tsp ground ginger Mixed greens (lettuce, red onion, grated carrots, red pepper and broccoli) Peanuts, optional 1. Lightly sprinkle chicken breasts with seasoned pepper. Grill; slice into strips. 2. Reserve 2 tbsp juice from pineapple.
