In a covered jar, combine avocado oil, soy sauce, pineapple juice, vinegar, sweetener and ginger. Shake well. 3. Brush pineapple slices with dressing; grill 2 to 3 minutes. 4. Arrange chicken and pineapple over lettuce and vegetables. Sprinkle with peanuts, if desired. Top with salad dressing. This main-dish salad is just as good as Red Robin’s Oriental Chicken Salad in my opinion! Team it up with cheese toast or rolls and a fruity drink for a complete meal. This screams summer! Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (pineapple, honey). Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend. Sugar swap: Here sugar only sweetens. Nothing depends on it browning or setting, so the swap is a straight 1:1.

recipes.title: Hearty Split Pea Soup
recipes.how: 1 package (16 ounces) dry green split peas 4 cups water 2 cups chicken broth 1/2 pound cooked, finely cubed ham 1 large potato, peeled and diced 3 medium carrots, peeled and sliced 1 celery stalk, sliced 1 small onion, chopped 1/2 tsp salt 1/2 tsp pepper 1/4 tsp onion powder 1/8 tsp dry thyme leaves 1 bay leaf 1. Rinse split peas in cold water. Combine all ingredients in a Dutch oven or large sauce pan; bring to a boil. Reduce heat and cover. Simmer, stirring occasionally, 1-1/2 hours. Remove bay leaf. In my quest for a hearty homemade split pea soup, I came up with this delicious recipe. I just took the basics, then added a few ingredients, and voila, a thick, satisfying meal. I team this up with homemade bread for a complete dinner. Useful Tip: If soup is too thick, add enough water until soup reaches desired consistency. Soup thickens upon standing, so leftovers will probably need more water before re-serving. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (bread, potato). Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Beef Stew
recipes.how: 1 pound lean beef stew meat 5 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed 3 large carrots, peeled and sliced 2 stalks celery, sliced 1 small onion, cut into small chunks 1/4 cup fresh chopped parsley 1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce 2 cups beef broth, red wine, or water (or a combo of the three) 3 tsp dry tapioca Salt and pepper to taste 1/2 cup frozen peas 1. Combine all ingredients except peas in a small roasting pan and cover with lid. Cook at 350°F for 3 hours. Stir in peas the last 15 minutes of cooking time. This comforting stew recipe comes from Don’s Aunt Mary (with just a couple of touch-ups by me), and has been thankfully passed around his family. Not many dinners come easier than this, since you throw all of the ingredients into a pan, bake and forget about it until it’s time to eat. I serve this with fresh bread and butter for dipping. This dish signals Fall to me, my favorite season. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (bread, potatoes). Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Shepherd’s Pie for Two
recipes.how: Meat filling ¾–1 lb ground beef (or ground lamb for true Shepherd’s Pie) 1 Tbsp avocado oil or ghee ½ medium onion, finely diced 1 small carrot, finely diced 1 celery stalk, finely diced (optional but good) 1–2 garlic cloves, minced 1 Tbsp tomato paste ½ cup beef broth 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce ½ tsp dried thyme ½ tsp dried rosemary (or 1 tsp fresh) Salt and black pepper Small handful frozen peas (optional, added at the end) Mashed potato topping 1–1¼ lb Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks 2–3 Tbsp grass-fed butter or ghee 2–3 Tbsp heavy cream or whole milk (warm) Salt and white or black pepper Optional: small pinch of garlic powder or grated Parmesan for extra flavor 1. Potatoes: Put the potatoes in cold salted water, bring to a boil, and cook until very tender (15–20 minutes). Drain well. Mash with butter/ghee, warm cream, salt, and pepper until smooth and creamy. Set aside. 2. Filling: Heat a skillet over medium-high. Use your ThermoWorks laser to confirm the pan is around 350–375°F. Add avocado oil or ghee. Brown the ground beef, breaking it up, until well browned. Drain excess fat if needed. Add onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 4–5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and tomato paste; cook 1 minute more. Stir in broth, Worcestershire, thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Simmer 5–8 minutes until the liquid reduces and the mixture is thick but still moist. Stir in peas at the end if using. Taste and adjust seasoning. 3. Assemble: Heat oven to 400°F. Spoon the meat filling into a small baking dish (or two individual ramekins). Spread the mashed potatoes evenly over the top. Use a fork to create ridges (they brown nicely). Optional: dot with a little extra butter. 4. Bake: Bake 20–25 minutes until the topping is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. For extra browning, broil the last 1–2 minutes (watch closely). 5. Rest: Let it sit 5 minutes before serving so it sets up. High carb recipe. Traditional name is for lamb; this version uses ground beef. Call it Cottage Pie if you prefer accuracy. Browning the meat properly builds the deep savory base. Reducing the broth concentrates flavor and gives the filling the right spoonable thickness. The potato ridges create more surface area for browning and a pleasant textural contrast against the soft filling. Uses avocado oil/ghee and real butter to keep the fats clean and flavorful. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Three-Cheese Chicken Enchiladas
recipes.how: 1/3 cup avocado oil (original used vegetable oil; upgraded) 8 corn tortillas (6-inch) 1 can (10 ounces) enchilada sauce 4 ounces cream cheese 3/4 cup sour cream 1/4 tsp salt 1/4 tsp ground cumin 1/4 tsp pepper 2 cups shredded chicken 2 cups (8 ounces) shredded Monterey Jack cheese, divided 1 cup (4 ounces) shredded Cheddar cheese 1/4 cup chopped green onions Sour cream and guacamole for serving 1. Heat oven to 350°F. 2. In 8-inch skillet, heat avocado oil over medium heat until hot. With tongs, dip each tortilla in hot oil, turning quickly to soften, about 3 seconds; set aside. 3. In large bowl, stir together cream cheese and sour cream until smooth. Stir in salt, cumin and pepper. Stir in chicken, 1 cup Monterey Jack cheese, Cheddar cheese and green onions. 4. Pour enchilada sauce in shallow dish (pie plate works well). Dip tortillas in enchilada sauce to lightly coat. Place 1/3 cup chicken mixture in center of tortilla; roll. Place tortillas, seam side down, in a lightly greased 13x9-inch baking dish. Cover with remaining enchilada sauce. 5. Bake for 25 minutes. Sprinkle remaining Monterey Jack cheese over enchiladas and bake 3 minutes longer. Garnish with sour cream and/or guacamole, if desired. These are undoubtably the BEST enchiladas ever (in our opinion anyway!). I created this recipe in search of something "out of this world", and well...here it is! Carb level: Moderate-carb (corn tortillas + sauce, balanced with protein and cheese) Vegetable oil replaced with avocado oil. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb.

recipes.title: French Ragout
recipes.how: 1 lb beef stew meat 2 tbsp avocado oil (original used cooking oil; upgraded) 1 medium onion, sliced 3 tbsp butter 1 beef bouillon cube 1-1/2 cups water 1 cup beef gravy 1 lemon slice 2 cups diced potatoes 1 cup sliced carrots 3/4 tsp salt 1/4 tsp pepper 1 tbsp cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1. In a large skillet, brown beef in hot avocado oil. Drain and set aside. 2. In same skillet, cook onion in butter until just tender. Add beef, bouillon, water, gravy, lemon, potatoes, carrots, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil; cover and simmer 25 minutes. 3. In a small bowl, blend 1/4 cup cold water with the cornstarch. Stir into beef mixture. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Simmer, uncovered, 5 minutes. Remove lemon slice. This dish is similar to beef stew, only cooked on the stove and much quicker. I always serve this with piping hot bread for dipping. Reminds me of Halloween as this is the perfect warm dish to serve the eager trick-or-treaters before their eve of fun. Carb level: Moderate-carb (contains potatoes and gravy) Cooking oil replaced with avocado oil. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb.

recipes.title: One-Dish Chicken and Stuffing Bake
recipes.how: 1 box (6 ounces) Chicken stuffing mix 1-1/4 cups hot water 1/4 cup butter, softened 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts Paprika Pepper 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup, undiluted 1/3 cup milk 1. In medium bowl, mix stuffing crumbs, contents of seasoning packet, water and butter until moistened; set aside. 2. Sprinkle chicken breasts lightly with paprika and pepper; place in a lightly greased 11x7-inch baking dish. 3. In a small bowl, combine soup and milk. Pour over chicken. Top with stuffing. 4. Cover and bake at 375°F for 35 minutes until chicken is no longer pink. This is adapted from a Stove Top stuffing recipe printed on the box. This is one of those simple but delicious meals you'll make over and over. Carb level: High-carb (stuffing mix based) Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: trim the highest-carb item (flour, sugar, starch, or grain) using almond flour, cauliflower, or monk fruit as fits the dish. (Chose that over arrowroot: no clear sauce-thickener role, so arrowroot was skipped.)

recipes.title: Beer Brewed Bratwurst
recipes.how: 1 can beer 1/2 cup water 1/4 cup butter 1 tbsp garlic powder 1/2 tsp salt 1/4 tsp pepper 6 bratwurst, uncooked 6 brat buns, hoagie rolls or hot dog buns 1. In a large saucepan combine beer, water, butter, garlic powder, salt and pepper. Add brats and bring to a boil, uncovered. Boil for 15 minutes. 2. Remove brats and discard cooking liquid. Grill brats directly over medium-high coals for 15 minutes, turning frequently, until brats are cooked through. Serve on buns with favorite toppings. Living in Wisconsin from '96-'99 had given us three distinctive pleasures: the Green Bay Packers, snow-filled winters, and bratwurst—simply called brats. Green Bay and brats go hand in hand, and here is a traditional way to fix them. (These are great for football parties!) Carb level: Moderate-carb (buns are the main carb source; brats themselves are low-carb) Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Spinach Lasagna Roll-Ups
recipes.how: 8 lasagna noodles, uncooked 1 package (10 ounces) frozen chopped spinach, thawed 1/3 cup finely chopped onion 2 cloves garlic, minced 1 tbsp avocado oil (original used vegetable oil; upgraded) 1 cup ricotta cheese 1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1 egg 1/2 tsp salt 1/2 tsp pepper 1 jar (15 ounces) marinara sauce, or homemade sauce 1 cup shredded Mozzarella cheese 2 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese 1. Cook lasagna noodles according to package directions until just tender (do not overcook); drain and set aside. Squeeze spinach dry; chop fine and set aside. 2. In a small skillet over medium heat, saute onion and garlic in avocado oil for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. 3. In a medium bowl, mix spinach, onion and garlic, ricotta cheese, Parmesan cheese, egg, salt and pepper. Spread mixture evenly on lasagna noodles; roll up. 4. Pour all but 3/4 cup of the marinara sauce in bottom of an ungreased 3-quart shallow baking dish. Place rolled noodles, seam side down, in sauce. Pour reserved sauce over. Sprinkle rolls with mozzarella cheese and Parmesan cheese. Cover with foil. If making ahead, refrigerate up to 24 hours. 5. Bake, covered, in a preheated 375°F oven for 40 to 50 minutes or until hot and bubbly. Want a slightly different twist on lasagna? Try this mouth-watering rolled-up pasta for a great variation from the traditional layered lasagna. The "rolls" each make one perfect-sized serving...but Don usually eats two! Carb level: High-carb (pasta based) Vegetable oil replaced with avocado oil. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Beef Jerky
recipes.how: 1-1/2 pounds beef flank steak 1/4 cup soy sauce 1/4 cup Worcestershire sauce 1-1/2 tsp garlic powder 1-1/2 tsp pepper 1 tsp liquid smoke 1 tsp onion powder 1 tsp Accent flavor enhancer 1. Trim all fat from the steak and slice 1/8-inch thick. 2. Combine remaining ingredients in a shallow dish or large, sealable plastic bag. Toss beef to coat. Marinate in refrigerator 12 hours, turning a few times. 3. Remove beef and discard marinade. Lay beef on paper towels and pat dry. Sprinkle coarse ground pepper over meat. Place aluminum foil on bottom of oven to catch drips. Lay beef strips directly on oven racks and cook on lowest oven temperature, approximately 125°F, for 8 to 10 hours, or until done. Sometimes it seems to take longer than others, depends on how thin the beef is sliced. Just as popular as Don's meatballs, this beef jerky is another of his delicious creations our family loves. Carb level: Low-carb (meat-based, minimal sugar) Yes, this is a day-long process, but most of the time you're not fussing with it. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Fresh Vegetable Pizza
recipes.how: 2 cans (8 ounces each) refrigerated crescent dinner rolls 1 package (8 ounces) cream cheese, softened 2 tbsp sour cream 1 tsp dillweed 1/2 tsp horseradish, or to taste 1/4 tsp salt 1/8 tsp pepper 1-1/2 cups small broccoli florets 1 cup fresh mushrooms, chopped 1 cup chopped, seeded tomatoes 1/2 cup chopped green, red or yellow pepper 1/2 cup chopped cucumber 1/2 cup thinly sliced green onions 1. Heat oven to 375°F. 2. Separate dough into 4 long rectangles. Place rectangles crosswise in ungreased 15x10x1-inch baking pan; press over bottom and 1 inch up sides to form crust. Seal perforations. Bake at 375°F for 14 to 19 minutes or until golden brown. Cool completely. 3. In small bowl, combine cream cheese, sour cream, dillweed, horseradish, salt and pepper; blend until smooth. Spread evenly over cooled crust. Top with remaining ingredients. Cut into appetizer-sized pieces. Store in refrigerator. Don and I first had this fantastic appetizer-pizza at a Pampered Chef party. I later discovered I had the recipe myself, and now I make it when we have friends over watching the Packer game! Carb level: High-carb (crescent roll crust) Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Asparagus Ham Rolls
recipes.how: 16 fresh or frozen asparagus spears, trimmed 3 tbsp Dijon mustard 16 thin slices cooked ham 16 thin slices Swiss cheese 2 eggs, beaten 1 cup dry bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1 cup crushed pork rinds) Avocado oil for frying (original used cooking oil; upgraded) 1. In a skillet, cook asparagus in a small amount of water until crisp-tender, about 5-6 minutes; drain well. 2. Spread about 1 teaspoon of mustard on each ham slice. Top with one slice of cheese. Place an asparagus spear at one end (trim to fit if necessary). Roll up each ham slice tightly; secure with three toothpicks. 3. Dip each ham roll in egg, then roll in bread crumbs. 4. In an electric skillet, heat 1-inch of avocado oil to 350°F. Fry rolls, a few at a time, until golden brown, about 3 to 4 minutes. Drain well on paper towels; keep warm. Cut each roll between toothpicks into three pieces. You'll be the hit of the party if you serve this heavenly appetizer! Yet another winner from Taste of Home magazine. Carb level: Moderate-carb (bread crumbs are the main carb source) Cooking oil replaced with avocado oil. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Mozzarella Sticks
recipes.how: 2 eggs 1 tbsp water 1 cup dry bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1 cup crushed pork rinds) 1-1/2 tsp Italian seasoning 1/2 tsp garlic powder 1/8 tsp pepper 12 sticks string cheese 3 tbsp flour (lower-carb option: 3/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 tbsp butter, melted 1 cup marinara or spaghetti sauce 1. In a small bowl, beat eggs and water. In a plastic bag, combine bread crumbs, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and pepper. Coat cheese sticks in flour, then dip in egg mixture and bread crumb mixture. Repeat egg and bread crumb coatings. 2. Cover and chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight (this step is very important, or the cheese will melt and flatten during baking). 3. Place on an ungreased baking sheet; drizzle with melted butter. Bake, uncovered, at 400°F for 6 to 8 minutes or until heated through. Allow to stand 3 minutes before serving. Use marinara or spaghetti sauce for dipping. These yummy finger-food appetizers make a great late night snack or fun dinnertime accompaniment. These are just like the cheese sticks served in a restaurant, with the convenience of home. Carb level: Moderate-to-high carb (bread crumbs and flour coating) Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Double Decker Tacos
recipes.how: 1 pound ground beef 1 package (1-1/4 ounces) Taco Seasoning Mix 3/4 cup water 1 can (16 ounces) refried beans 10 taco-size flour tortillas 10 hard taco shells 2-1/2 cups shredded lettuce 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese 1 tomato, diced Sour cream Taco Sauce 1. Brown ground beef in skillet, crumbling into very fine pieces; drain. Return to skillet and add water and seasoning packet. Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer 10 to 15 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. 2. Meanwhile, heat refried beans in a saucepan. Warm tortillas and taco shells according to package directions. 3. Assemble taco by spreading 3 tbsp refried beans on warm flour tortilla. Place hard taco shell on middle of flour tortilla and wrap up sides of taco. Fill with beef, lettuce, cheese and tomatoes. Top with sour cream and/or taco sauce, if desired. Move over, Taco Bell! Here is a great taco dinner you can make right at home, without being chintzy on the cheese! Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas, hard shells, and refried beans) Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: thicken with a little arrowroot slurry instead of flour/cornstarch; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Chicken Marsala for Two
recipes.how: For the chicken: 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (6–8 oz each), pounded to even ½-inch thickness 2–3 Tbsp almond flour (or light all-purpose flour if preferred) ½ tsp salt ¼ tsp black pepper ¼ tsp garlic powder (optional) 1–2 Tbsp avocado oil or ghee 1 Tbsp butter For the sauce: 8 oz cremini or button mushrooms, sliced 1 small shallot or ¼ small onion, finely minced 1–2 garlic cloves, minced ½ cup dry Marsala wine ½ cup chicken broth 1–2 tsp Dijon mustard (optional) 2–3 Tbsp heavy cream or a knob of cold butter Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish 1. Pat the chicken dry. Season both sides with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Lightly dredge in almond flour, shaking off excess. 2. Heat a skillet over medium-high. Use your ThermoWorks laser to confirm the surface is around 375–400°F. Add avocado oil or ghee. When the fat is shimmering, add the chicken. Sear 3–4 minutes per side until golden-brown and just cooked through. Remove to a plate and tent loosely. 3. In the same pan, add a little more fat if needed. Add the mushrooms and a pinch of salt. Cook 4–5 minutes until they release liquid and begin to brown. Add the shallot and cook 1–2 minutes more. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds. 4. Pour in the Marsala wine. Scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let it simmer and reduce by about half (2–3 minutes). Add the chicken broth and optional Dijon. Simmer another 3–4 minutes until the sauce is slightly thickened and glossy. 5. Reduce heat to low. Stir in the heavy cream or swirl in cold butter to finish the sauce. Taste and adjust salt and pepper. 6. Return the chicken to the pan and spoon sauce over it for 1 minute to rewarm. Garnish with fresh parsley. A classic Italian-American dish rebuilt with clean fats and a lighter dredge while keeping the rich, silky sauce and proper browned crust. Carb level: Moderate-low (mainly from mushrooms, shallot, and small amount of almond flour) Avocado oil or ghee used for searing; butter for finishing. No seed oils. Almond flour keeps the dredge lighter in carbs while still promoting browning and giving the sauce a bit of body. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (flour).

recipes.title: Pork Cutlets with Fig Pan Sauce
recipes.how: For the pork: 2 thin pork cutlets (about 4–6 oz each), or one larger cutlet pounded thin and cut in half Salt and freshly ground black pepper 1–2 Tbsp avocado oil or ghee 1 Tbsp butter For the fig pan sauce: 4–5 fresh figs, stemmed and quartered (or 3–4 soft dried figs, chopped, if fresh are unavailable) 1 small shallot, minced ¼ cup dry white wine, dry Marsala, or chicken broth ¼ cup chicken broth 1 tsp Dijon mustard (optional) 1 Tbsp cold butter (for finishing) Salt and pepper to taste Fresh thyme leaves (optional) 1. Pat the pork cutlets dry and season both sides with salt and pepper. 2. Heat a skillet over medium-high. Confirm with your ThermoWorks laser that the surface is around 375–400°F. Add avocado oil or ghee. When the fat is shimmering, add the cutlets. Sear 2–3 minutes per side until nicely browned and just cooked through. Remove to a plate and tent loosely. 3. Reduce heat to medium. Add the shallot to the same pan and cook 30–60 seconds until softened. Add the figs and cook 1–2 minutes so they begin to soften and take on a little color. 4. Pour in the wine (or Marsala) and scrape up the browned bits. Let it reduce by about half. Add the chicken broth and optional Dijon. Simmer 1–2 minutes until the sauce is lightly thickened and the figs are soft but still hold their shape. 5. Remove from heat and swirl in the cold butter. Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Add a few thyme leaves if using. 6. Return the pork to the pan for 30 seconds to coat with sauce, or simply spoon the fig sauce over the cutlets on the plate. For Two Thin, quickly seared pork cutlets finished with a simple fig pan sauce. Designed to sit alongside the Winesap Apple, Stilton & Walnut plate and a sharp endive side. Carb level: Moderate (mainly from the figs) Avocado oil or ghee for searing; butter for finishing. No seed oils. The quick pan sauce keeps the figs soft and glossy while picking up the fond from the pork. Pairs with the Winesap Apple, Stilton & Walnut plate and a sharp endive side. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (fig). Carb swap: trim the highest-carb item (flour, sugar, starch, or grain) using almond flour, cauliflower, or monk fruit as fits the dish. (Chose that over arrowroot: no clear sauce-thickener role, so arrowroot was skipped.)

recipes.title: Chicken Cordon Bleu
recipes.how: 6 boneless, skinless chicken breasts 6 slices fully cooked ham 6 slices Swiss cheese 2 eggs, beaten 2 tbsp. dry white wine or chicken broth 1/2 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 cup blanched almond flour) 1 cup fine dry bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1 cup crushed pork rinds) 1/4 cup butter 2 cups fresh, sliced mushrooms 2 cans (10-3/4 ounces each) cream of mushroom soup, undiluted 1-1/4 cups milk 1/4 cup dry white wine or chicken broth 1. Rinse chicken breasts; pat dry. Place each breast between 2 pieces of clear heavy-duty plastic wrap. Working from center to the edges, lightly pound with the flat side of a meat mallet to 1/8-inch thickness. Remove plastic wrap. 2. Place 1 slice each of ham and cheese on each chicken breast, folding to fit on chicken if necessary. 3. Starting from one short side, roll up each piece of chicken jelly-roll style, and secure with a wooden toothpick. 4. In shallow dish, stir together beaten eggs and 2 tbsp. wine or chicken broth. Roll each chicken breast in the flour, dip in the egg mixture, and coat with bread crumbs. Preheat oven to 325°F. 5. In large skillet, melt the butter. Lightly brown chicken rolls on all sides. Remove from skillet; reserve drippings. Transfer chicken to a 9x13-inch baking dish and carefully remove the toothpicks. 6. Bake at 325°F about 40 minutes or until chicken is tender and no longer pink. 7. Meanwhile, saute the mushrooms in the skillet with the reserved drippings for 5 minutes or until tender. Add the undiluted soup and milk to skillet. Stir until well combined. Remove from the heat and stir in the 1/4 cup wine or chicken broth. Serve the sauce over chicken and pasta, rice or mashed potatoes. This is a classic we'll never tire of. This is excellent served with a wild and brown rice mixture, or over a bed of egg noodles. Carb level: Moderate-carb (breading + optional pasta/rice/potatoes) The mushroom sauce adds a nice touch, but this dish is just as delicious without it if you wish to omit it. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Roast Turkey
recipes.how: 1/4 cup butter 1/2 cup sliced celery 1 large onion, chopped 1 can (14-1/2 ounces) chicken broth 1/4 cup water 2 tbsp. melted butter 1 bag (14 ounces) Herb Seasoned Stuffing 12-14 pound turkey 1/2 cup melted butter 1. Melt butter in large saucepan over medium heat. Add celery and onion; cook until tender. Add broth, water and 2 tbsp. melted butter; heat to a boil. Remove from heat and stir in stuffing. Mix lightly. 2. Remove packet of giblets and neck from cavity of turkey. Rinse turkey with cold water and pat dry. Spoon stuffing lightly into neck and body cavities (bake any remaining stuffing in covered casserole dish with turkey last 30 minutes of cooking time. For a moister stuffing, stir in some pan juices before baking.). Fold loose skin over stuffing. Place turkey, breast side up, on rack in shallow roasting pan. Brush with melted butter. Insert meat thermometer deep into thickest part of thigh next to body, not touching bone. 3. Roast at 325°F for 4-1/2 to 5 hours or until thermometer reads 180°F and drumstick moves easily, basting occasionally with pan drippings. Allow turkey to stand a few minutes before slicing. Serve with gravy. This is an absolutely stunning and delicious turkey for your Thanksgiving and Christmas dinners. Carb level: Moderate-carb (stuffing-based) Useful Tip: Stir chopped apples, cranberries and/or pecans into your stuffing for a delightful change (3/4 cup total). Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb.

recipes.title: Vegetable Beef Pot Pie
recipes.how: 2 frozen 9-inch deep-dish pie crusts 1 stalk celery, sliced 1 small onion, chopped 1–2 tbsp. butter or avocado oil (for sautéing) 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) beefy mushroom soup 2 cups cooked, finely cubed beef 1 cup diced, cooked potatoes 3/4 cup frozen sliced carrots 3/4 cup frozen green beans 1/3 cup water 1/4 tsp. pepper 1. Preheat oven to 400°F. 2. While pie crusts defrost, sauté celery and onion in butter or avocado oil until celery is crisp-tender. Add remaining ingredients (except pie crusts). Heat until bubbly. Remove from heat. 3. Line a 9-inch deep-dish pie plate with one pie crust. Pour filling into shell. Top with remaining pie crust; seal and flute edges. With a fork, poke a few holes in the top crust to allow steam to escape. 4. Bake 20 minutes or until pastry is lightly browned. Here is a quick and easy dinner that will have your family asking for seconds! It’s mmmm good! Carb level: High-carb (pie crust + potatoes) Butter or avocado oil used for the sauté—no seed oils. The canned soup provides the classic gravy base; homemade bone-broth gravy could be swapped for a cleaner version if desired. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Honey-Pineapple Glazed Ham
recipes.how: 1 fully cooked smoked ham, about 5 pounds 3/4 cup + 2 tbsp. golden monk fruit blend + 2 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 1 cup packed brown sugar) 1 tbsp. cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1/4 tsp. salt 1 can (8 ounces) crushed pineapple, undrained 1/4 cup honey 1 tsp. prepared mustard 1. Bake ham in a roasting pan at 350°F for 1-1/2 hours. 2. In a small saucepan, mix sweetener, cornstarch, and salt. Stir in pineapple, honey, and mustard. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and boils. Boil and stir 1 minute. 3. Brush sauce over ham and bake 30 minutes more, basting once or twice. Brush remaining sauce over ham before serving. Yummy!! This makes a divine ham dinner! Carb level: High-carb (brown sugar + honey + pineapple); partial monk fruit swap reduces sugar load while still allowing caramelization and glaze adhesion. Sugar swap: Cornstarch provides the classic glossy set; a small amount of real brown sugar or honey preserves Maillard notes and stickiness that pure monk fruit alone cannot fully replicate. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Extra-Easy Lasagna
recipes.how: 1/2 pound lean ground beef 1 can (27 ounces) spaghetti sauce (or homemade spaghetti sauce) 6 uncooked lasagna noodles 1 container (15 ounces) ricotta cheese 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley 1/4 cup water 1. In a 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat, cook beef until browned. Drain off fat. Add spaghetti sauce; heat through, stirring occasionally. 2. In a 2-quart oblong baking dish, spread 1-1/2 cups sauce mixture. Top with three uncooked lasagna noodles, half of the ricotta, half of the mozzarella, half of the cheddar, half of the Parmesan, and half of the parsley. Repeat layers. Top with remaining sauce mixture. Slowly pour water around the inside edges of the baking dish. Cover tightly with aluminum foil. 3. Bake at 375°F for 45 minutes. Uncover; bake 10 minutes more. Let stand 10 minutes before serving. Making lasagna does not have to be time-consuming, and this great recipe proves it. I usually whip this up with leftover spaghetti sauce, throw in some garlic bread and a salad, and dinner is as easy as one, two, three! Carb level: High-carb (lasagna noodles) No seed oils in this recipe. For a lower-carb version, zucchini or eggplant slices can replace the noodles, though the classic texture will change. The water around the edges helps the uncooked noodles soften by creating steam inside the sealed dish. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Kabobs
recipes.how: 1/2 cup ketchup 1/2 cup soy sauce 1/4 cup + 3 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tbsp. sugar (in place of 1/2 cup sugar) 1 tsp. garlic powder 1-1/2 pounds beef sirloin steak, cut into cubes 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple chunks or one fresh pineapple, cubed Assorted fresh vegetables prepared for kabobs (mushrooms, zucchini, sweet pepper, onion) 1. In a shallow dish or large plastic bag, combine ketchup, soy sauce, sweetener, and garlic powder. Add beef and toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate at least 8 hours, or overnight. 2. Alternately thread meat, pineapple, and vegetables on skewers. Bring remaining marinade to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes. 3. Grill kabobs over medium heat, turning often, until meat is done and vegetables are tender. Serve the reduced marinade over the kabobs. Because of the long marinating time, the teriyaki flavor is abundant in every bite. I gave this recipe to my Mom not too long ago, and she tells me she now marinades just about everything in this sauce 2–3 times a month! Carb level: Moderate-to-high (sugar + pineapple); monk fruit option lowers the added sugar while still allowing some caramelization on the grill. Long marination gives excellent flavor penetration; the reduced sauce becomes a glossy glaze thanks to the residual sugars. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (sugar, pineapple). Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this dish. The change is small: the long marinade still flavors the beef the same, but with less real sugar the kabobs will not char and caramelize as much on the grill.

recipes.title: Chili
recipes.how: 1 pound ground beef 1 can (15-1/2 ounces) kidney beans, undrained 1 can (15-1/2 ounces) chili beans, with sauce 1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce 1 can (15 ounces) chopped tomatoes 1 small onion, diced 1-1/2 tbsp. chili powder 2 tbsp. diced green chiles 1 tsp. cumin 1/2 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper 3/4 cup water Diced onions and shredded Cheddar cheese, optional 1. Brown the ground beef in a large pot over medium-high heat; drain. Crumble into small pieces (a pastry blender makes this job easy). 2. Return beef to the pot and add remaining ingredients except diced onions and cheese. Stir to combine well; bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat; cook, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 3 hours. Garnish with onions and cheese, if desired. Here’s a great chili recipe…you can make it hotter by upping the chili powder, and/or dropping in a sliced jalapeño pepper or two. I always serve fresh and gooey cinnamon rolls with chili…a combination Don thought strange at first, but now loves. Carb level: Moderate-to-high carb (beans are the main starch; tomatoes add a little) No added oil. The beef’s own fat is enough to brown the meat and carry the chili-powder aromatics. The long simmer reduces water, concentrates tomato acids and sugars, and lets the spices bloom. Don’t rush it if you want that “all-day” body. For a lower-carb bowl, use one can of beans (or skip beans and add extra beef and diced zucchini). Heat and salt will still carry the chili. Optional jalapeño adds capsaicin heat without extra carbs. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Chicken Stew
recipes.how: 1 can (14-1/2 ounces) chicken broth 1 can (6 ounces) tomato paste 1 lb. boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch cubes 2 cups potatoes, peeled and cubed 1 small onion, chopped 1 celery stalk, sliced 2 medium carrots, sliced 1/2 tsp. paprika 1/4 tsp. pepper 1/4 tsp. dried thyme 1-1/2 tbsp. water 1 tbsp. cornstarch (or 1 tbsp. arrowroot) (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1. In a crock pot, combine the chicken broth and tomato paste. Add the next 8 ingredients and stir to mix well. Cover and cook on high for 3-1/2 to 4 hours, or on low for 7 to 8 hours. 2. Mix water and cornstarch (or arrowroot) in a small bowl; stir until smooth. Stir into stew. Cook, covered, for 30 minutes more, or until thickened. I like this better than beef stew, and since this cooks in the crock pot, it makes the perfect dinner to whip up on busy days. I usually serve this with warm Sweet Potato Bread. Carb level: Moderate-to-high carb (potatoes + carrots + cornstarch) No added oil. Chicken and tomato paste give body; the slurry thickens the last half hour so you do not get a gluey all-day starch cook. Arrowroot thickens at a slightly lower temperature and stays clearer than cornstarch; either works. Mix the slurry into hot liquid and do not boil hard or cornstarch can thin again. For a lower-carb pot, swap cauliflower florets or turnips for the potatoes. Tomato paste still gives the stew its savory depth and color. Nice with Sweet Potato Bread (rec100). Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap AP flour for almond flour (psyllium helps bind baked goods); swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour structure beats arrowroot for baked flour swaps.) Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this stew. Cauliflower or turnips in place of the potatoes make a lighter, less hearty stew (turnip adds a peppery bite), and xanthan thickens the broth slicker than the cornstarch slurry does.

recipes.title: Spaghetti
recipes.how: For the sauce: 3/4 pound lean ground beef 1 small onion, chopped 1 can (29 ounces) crushed tomatoes 1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce 1 can (14-1/2 ounces) diced tomatoes, undrained 1 can (6 ounces) tomato paste 1 cup sliced mushrooms, optional 1 tsp. dried Italian seasoning 1 tsp. dried oregano 1 tsp. dried basil 1 tsp. garlic powder 1 bay leaf For serving: Hot cooked spaghetti 1. In a large saucepan or Dutch oven, brown beef and onion; drain. Return to the saucepan and stir in remaining sauce ingredients (not the pasta). Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and cover. 2. Cook, stirring occasionally, 2 hours. Remove bay leaf and serve over hot cooked spaghetti. I don’t actually measure the ingredients when making my spaghetti, but this is a close replica. Experiment to your own taste. For spaghetti and meatballs, see the companion recipe. Carb level: High-carb when served over pasta; the sauce itself is Moderate-low (tomatoes + optional mushrooms) No added oil. Brown the beef in its own fat so you get fond on the pot; that browned fond is where a lot of the “simmered all day” flavor starts. The two-hour simmer drives off water, concentrates tomato glutamates, and lets the dried herbs rehydrate. Tomato paste adds cooked-tomato depth (more Maillard-like notes than raw crushed tomato alone). For a lower-carb plate, serve the same sauce over zucchini noodles, cabbage ribbons, or roasted spaghetti squash. Companion recipe: Spaghetti and Meatballs. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Spaghetti and Meatballs
recipes.how: For the sauce: 1 small onion, chopped 2 cloves garlic, minced 2 tbsp. olive oil 1 can (29 ounces) crushed tomatoes 1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce 1 can (14-1/2 ounces) diced tomatoes, undrained 1 can (6 ounces) tomato paste 1 tsp. dried Italian seasoning 1 tsp. dried oregano 1 tsp. dried basil 1 bay leaf For the meatballs: 1 pound ground beef 1/2 cup Italian seasoned bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1/2 cup blanched almond flour) 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1 egg, beaten Salt and pepper to taste For serving: Hot cooked spaghetti 1. In a large saucepan or Dutch oven, sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft. Stir in remaining sauce ingredients. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and cover. Cook, stirring occasionally, 1-1/2 hours. 2. While the sauce cooks, combine beef, bread crumbs (or almond flour), Parmesan, egg, salt, and pepper. Shape into 1-1/2-inch meatballs and place on a lightly greased cookie sheet (avocado oil or olive oil). Bake at 350°F for 20 to 25 minutes or until browned. 3. Stir meatballs into the sauce and simmer 30 minutes longer. Remove bay leaf and serve over hot cooked spaghetti. The meatball version from the same original spaghetti card. Olive oil stays — it is the right fruit fat for this sauce. Carb level: High-carb over pasta; Moderate-carb meatballs if you use almond flour and skip the noodles Olive oil is the cooking fat for the soffritto — good smoke point for a gentle sauté and the classic flavor. No seed oils. Bread crumbs absorb juices and keep meatballs tender. Almond flour plus Parmesan and egg will still bind; the balls will be a little denser and less bready. Baking the meatballs instead of frying keeps the fat cleaner and still browns the surface (Maillard) before they finish in the sauce. For a lower-carb plate, serve over zucchini noodles or roasted spaghetti squash. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this dish. Almond-flour meatballs are a little denser and less bready, and zucchini noodles or spaghetti squash give a lighter, wetter plate that does not hold the sauce like real spaghetti.

recipes.title: Turkey-Mushroom Casserole
recipes.how: 1 package (12 ounces) wide egg noodles, cooked and drained 2 cups cooked, chopped turkey 1 can (4 ounces) sliced mushrooms, drained 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup, undiluted 1-1/3 cups milk 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1/2 cup crushed butter-flavor crackers 3 tbsp. butter, melted 1. In a large bowl, combine noodles, turkey, and mushrooms. Combine the soup, milk, salt, and pepper; pour over turkey mixture and mix well. 2. Pour into a greased 2-1/2-quart casserole dish. Combine crackers and melted butter; sprinkle over noodles. 3. Bake, uncovered, at 350°F for 35 to 45 minutes or until heated through. What a great way to help use up those turkey leftovers! Carb level: High-carb (egg noodles + cracker topping) Butter is tossed with the crumbs so they fry and brown on top instead of going soggy. No seed oils. The soup-and-milk mixture is a quick dairy emulsion that soaks the noodles. Don’t overbake or the sauce can break and look greasy. For a lower-carb leftover bake, use cauliflower florets or zucchini coins in place of some or all of the noodles, and skip or thin the cracker crust. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Sweet ’N Spicy Kielbasa
recipes.how: 3/4 cup + 2 tbsp. golden monk fruit blend + 2 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 1 cup packed brown sugar) 6 tbsp. spicy mustard 1 small onion, finely chopped 2 pounds smoked kielbasa, cut into 2-inch pieces 1. Combine sweetener, mustard, and onion in a crock pot; add kielbasa, stirring to evenly coat. Cover and cook on low 2-1/2 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally. This is one of those easy meals you will make over and over…also good cut into smaller chunks for a great party appetizer! Carb level: Moderate-to-high carb (brown sugar is the main source; kielbasa itself is moderate) No added oil. The sausage renders its own fat, which helps the mustard-sugar mix become a glossy glaze. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar even. Those molasses sugars caramelize in the long, moist heat and help the glaze cling. Pure monk fruit will sweeten but will not thicken or brown the same way. Spicy mustard’s vinegar brightens the sweetness so the dish does not taste flat. For a party appetizer, cut the kielbasa smaller and keep it on warm. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this dish. With less real brown sugar the mustard-sugar sauce will not thicken into a clingy, caramelized glaze, so the kielbasa ends up in a thinner, sharper sauce.

recipes.title: Swedish Meatballs
recipes.how: For the meatballs: 1-1/2 pounds ground beef 1 cup bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1 cup blanched almond flour) 1 egg 1-1/2 tbsp. instant minced onion 1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce 1/4 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper Dash garlic powder For the sauce: 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup, undiluted 1/2 cup milk 1/4 cup water 1 tsp. instant beef bouillon or one cube Dash Worcestershire sauce Dash pepper For serving: Hot cooked egg noodles 1. Combine ground beef, bread crumbs (or almond flour), egg, onion, 1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce, 1/4 tsp. salt, 1/4 tsp. pepper, and a dash of garlic powder. Mix until well combined. Shape into small meatballs. 2. Heat a skillet over medium heat with a thin film of avocado oil or ghee (in place of nonstick spray). Brown the meatballs; drain on paper towels. 3. Combine soup, milk, water, bouillon, dash of Worcestershire sauce, and dash of pepper in a crock pot; add meatballs. Cook on low 6 hours. Serve over hot cooked egg noodles. We have tried the “fancy” recipes for Swedish meatballs, but this simple one suits our taste much better. Not only is it incredibly easy, it is the tastiest (in our opinion). Carb level: High-carb over noodles; Moderate-carb meatballs if you use almond flour and skip the pasta Avocado oil or ghee replaces nonstick spray so the meatballs actually sear (Maillard) instead of steaming in a coated pan. Bread crumbs soak up juices and keep the balls soft. Almond flour binds with the egg but makes a slightly denser, less bready meatball — still very good in this creamy sauce. The long low cook lets the mushroom-soup sauce loosen and cling. If it looks too thick at the end, splash in a little more milk. Typo fixed: Worcestershire (original had “Worchestershire”). For a lower-carb plate, serve over buttered cabbage or cauliflower mash. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Baked Onion Chicken
recipes.how: 1 pouch dry onion soup mix 2/3 cup dry bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 2/3 cup crushed pork rinds) 1/2 tsp. pepper 1 egg 2 tbsp. water 6 boneless, skinless chicken breasts 2 tbsp. butter, melted 1. With a rolling pin, crush the soup mix in the pouch. On wax paper, combine soup mix, bread crumbs (or almond flour), and pepper. 2. In a shallow dish, beat together egg and water. Dip chicken into the egg mixture; coat with the crumb mixture, shaking excess crumbs off. 3. On a baking sheet, arrange chicken. Drizzle with melted butter. 4. Bake at 400°F for 20 minutes or until the chicken is no longer pink. This delicious, moist chicken is a great alternative to fried chicken as it is full of flavor without being full of fat. Carb level: Moderate-carb (bread crumbs); almond flour coating is Moderate-low Melted butter on top is what browns and crisps the coating in the oven — the same job hot oil does in a fryer. No seed oils. Almond flour works here as a dredge. It will brown a little faster than bread crumbs, so watch the last few minutes. Shake off extra coating so it does not sit in a wet clump and go soggy. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Breakfast Burritos
recipes.how: 6 large flour tortillas (10-inch) 6 eggs 6 strips bacon, cooked and crumbled 1-1/2 tbsp. milk 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1-1/2 tbsp. butter 3/4 cup salsa 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese 1. Lightly beat eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. 2. Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add eggs; cook, stirring, until set. 3. Wrap tortillas in damp paper towels. Microwave on high 30 seconds to soften. 4. Spread each tortilla with salsa. Spoon eggs on the lower half of each tortilla. Sprinkle with bacon and cheese. Roll up, tucking ends in as you roll. Place, seam side down, in a single layer in a microwave-safe dish. Cover with damp paper towels. 5. Microwave on high 1 minute. Serve with additional salsa, if desired. These delicious burritos are easy and convenient—a great change of pace on any hungry morning! Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas); the filling is Low-carb Butter is the cooking fat for the eggs. No seed oils. Soften the tortillas so they roll without cracking. The brief second microwave just melts the cheese. For a lower-carb breakfast, use low-carb tortillas or serve the same egg-bacon-cheese filling in a bowl. Don’t overcook the eggs in the skillet — they finish in the microwave. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Chicken Kiev
recipes.how: For the herb butter: 1/4 cup butter, softened 1 tbsp. chopped chives 1/2 tbsp. parsley Pinch of salt 1/8 tsp. pepper 1 garlic clove, finely minced For the chicken: 6 boneless, skinless chicken breasts 1 egg 1 tbsp. milk 1 envelope (2-3/4 ounces) seasoned chicken coating mix, or 1 cup dry bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1 cup crushed pork rinds) 1. Combine butter, chives, parsley, salt, pepper, and garlic. Shape the mixture into six pencil-thin strips about 2 inches long; place on wax paper. Freeze until firm, about 30 minutes. 2. Flatten each chicken breast to 1/4 inch. Place one butter strip in the center of each chicken breast. Fold the long sides over the butter; fold the ends up and secure with a toothpick. 3. In a bowl, beat egg and milk; place coating mix in another bowl. Dip chicken in the egg mixture, then roll in the coating. Place chicken, seam side down, in a 13x9-inch baking dish greased with butter or avocado oil. 4. Bake, uncovered, at 425°F for 35 to 40 minutes or until the chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear. Remove toothpicks before serving. A classic, mouthwatering chicken dish with a wonderful combination of buttery chicken and a crisp, flavorful crust. Definitely elegant enough to serve company when entertaining. Carb level: Moderate-carb (coating mix or bread crumbs); almond flour coating is Moderate-low Butter is the classic Kiev center — it melts into a sauce inside the chicken. Freeze the strips so they stay put while you wrap. No seed oils. High heat (425°F) crisps the crust and helps seal the seam before the butter fully melts. Useful tip from the original: one packet of regular Shake ’n Bake Chicken coating mix works well. Bread crumbs or seasoned almond flour also work. Seal the edges well or the butter will leak. Serve promptly so the burst of herb butter is still liquid. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Chicken Pot Pie
recipes.how: For the filling: 3 tbsp. butter 3 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 3/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1/2 tsp. salt 1/8 tsp. pepper 1 cup chicken broth 1 cup whipping cream 1 tsp. chicken bouillon granules 2 cups cooked cubed chicken 1 package (10 ounces) frozen peas and carrots 1 medium potato, cooked and cubed (about 1-1/2 cups) For the cheddar pie crust: 1-1/3 cups flour (lower-carb option: 1-1/3 cups blanched almond flour + 5/8 tsp. xanthan gum) 1/4 tsp. salt 1/3 cup cold butter, cut into pieces (in place of shortening) 1/4 cup cold butter, cut into pieces 1 cup grated sharp Cheddar cheese 1/2 tsp. vinegar mixed with 1/3 cup cold water 1. Melt 3 tbsp. butter in a 3-quart saucepan over low heat. Stir in flour, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture is smooth. Stir in broth, whipping cream, and bouillon. Heat to a boil, stirring constantly. Boil and stir 1 minute. Stir in chicken, peas and carrots, and potato. 2. For the crust: Combine flour and salt in a medium bowl. Cut all the cold butter into small pieces and add to the flour. Cut in with a pastry blender until crumbs begin to form. Add cheese and cut in to mix. Pour in the water mixture, 2 tbsp. at a time, and mix until the dough forms a ball. Do not add too much water. Turn onto a lightly floured surface. Specks of butter and cheese will be visible. Shape into a disk, wrap, and chill at least 2 hours. Divide into 2 pieces and roll into 11-inch circles. 3. Heat oven to 425°F. Pour the chicken mixture into a pastry-lined pie plate. Top with the other crust and trim. Seal and flute. Cut a few small slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape. 4. Bake 35 minutes, or until light golden brown. Allow the pie to sit for 15 minutes before cutting. Here is a delicious pot pie full of chicken, vegetables, and a creamy sauce in a classic pie crust. You can experiment adding different vegetables such as mushrooms, broccoli, and/or pearl onions to best suit your taste. Carb level: High-carb (pie crust + potato + peas) All butter in the crust replaces shortening. Butter gives better flavor and a tender, flaky layer because the water in the butter turns to steam. Chill well so the butter stays in pieces. The vinegar in the water limits gluten so the dough stays tender. The filling starts as a butter-and-flour roux. Almond flour can stand in for those 3 tbsp.; the sauce will be slightly less glossy. Cream keeps it rich. No seed oils. Rest 15 minutes after baking so the sauce thickens and slices hold. A store-bought crust works if you want it easier; use one made with butter if you can. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Chicken and Rice Bake
recipes.how: 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of celery soup 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of chicken soup 1 small onion, chopped 1-1/2 cups converted rice, uncooked 1-3/4 cups water 1/4 tsp. pepper 6 skinless chicken breasts 1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a 13x9-inch baking dish with avocado oil or butter (in place of cooking spray). 2. Mix together soups, onion, rice, water, and pepper. Spoon half of the rice mixture on the bottom of the greased baking dish. Arrange chicken over top and spoon remaining rice mixture on top. 3. Cover and bake for 1 hour and 45 minutes. My Step-Mother, Diane, made this absolutely wonderful dish one night Don and I were visiting. This is the ultimate chicken and rice dish. Carb level: High-carb (converted rice + condensed soups) Avocado oil or butter replaces cooking spray so the rice does not stick and you are not using seed-oil spray. Converted (parboiled) rice holds its shape in a long covered bake. Regular long-grain can go mushy in 1 hour 45 minutes. Keep the dish covered so steam cooks the rice through. Uncovering late will dry the top layer. The original card suggested reduced-fat soups to cut fat and salt. Full-fat soups give a creamier sauce; use whichever you prefer. For a lower-carb version, cauliflower rice will not behave the same in this long bake — better as a separate side than a 1:1 swap here. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Corn Chowder
recipes.how: 2 tbsp. butter 1 small onion, finely chopped 1 clove garlic, minced 3 cups peeled potatoes, diced 1-1/2 cups hot water 1 heaping tsp. chicken bouillon 2 cups milk 1 cup half-and-half 3 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 3/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1/2 tbsp. minced dried parsley 1 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend (in place of 1 tbsp. sugar) 1 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. white pepper 1 package (10 ounces) frozen sweet corn 1. Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat; sauté onion and garlic until onion is soft. Add potatoes, hot water, and bouillon. Bring to a boil; cover and reduce heat. Simmer until the potatoes are tender. 2. Combine milk and half-and-half; gradually whisk in flour, parsley, sweetener, salt, and pepper. Stir into the potato mixture along with corn. Bring to a gentle boil; reduce heat. Stirring occasionally, simmer about 10 minutes. This is just plain GOOD soup! You can use canned or fresh corn and even adjust the amounts to suit your taste. Carb level: High-carb (potatoes + corn + flour) Butter is the sauté fat. It softens the onion and carries the corn sweetness. No seed oils. Whisk flour (or almond flour) into cold dairy first so the starch/protein hydrates without lumps. Simmer gently after it goes in — a hard boil can scorch the milk. Almond flour thickens a little less glossily than wheat flour but works at 3 tbsp. Useful tip: Add diced smoked ham if desired. For a lower-carb pot, swap cauliflower for some of the potatoes. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Cottage Pie
recipes.how: 1-1/2 lbs. ground beef 1 small onion, chopped 1/4 tsp. salt 1/8 tsp. pepper 1/8 tsp. marjoram 2 cups brown gravy 2 cups mashed potatoes 1/2 cup Cheddar cheese 2 tsp. butter 1. Brown ground beef and onion in a skillet; drain. Stir in spices and gravy and heat until bubbling. Pour into a 2-quart casserole dish. 2. Stir cheese into the mashed potatoes and spread atop the meat mixture. Dot with butter. 3. Bake, uncovered, at 400°F for 30 minutes or until the potatoes are lightly browned. This comes from a warm, friendly lady (Lorie) from a cooking board I frequent (What’s For Dinner?) and has been slightly modified to suit our taste. It has a likeness of Shepherd’s Pie only with a gravy-based sauce instead of tomato. This is the only way we enjoy this dish, with Don savoring seconds! Carb level: High-carb (mashed potatoes) No added cooking oil for the beef. Dotting butter on the potato top helps it brown and crisp in the 400°F oven. Cottage pie is the beef version; shepherd’s pie is traditionally lamb. This one uses brown gravy instead of a tomato base, as Lorie wrote it. The cheese in the potatoes helps them set and brown. Don’t pack the mash too tight or it sits like a lid and the gravy can bubble over. For a lower-carb top, use cauliflower mash; it will brown less but still tastes good with the gravy. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Creamy Turkey-Vegetable Soup
recipes.how: 1 small onion, diced 2 tbsp. butter 2 cups water 2 chicken bouillon cubes 2 cups diced cooked turkey 1/2 cup chopped celery 1-1/2 cups diced potatoes 1 cup diced carrots 2-1/2 cups milk 2 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper 1. Sauté onion in butter until translucent. Add water, bouillon cubes, turkey, and vegetables. Cover and boil gently until vegetables are tender. 2. Add a small amount of milk to the flour, stirring until the mixture is smooth. Add remaining milk, salt, and pepper. 3. Stir milk mixture into soup. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until soup thickens slightly. Remove from heat and serve. This is a great, satisfying soup, perfect for a chilly night. This also makes the best of leftover turkey! Chicken can be substituted for the turkey for an equally delicious soup. Carb level: Moderate-to-high carb (potatoes + carrots + flour); almond flour option lightens the thickener Butter is the sauté fat. It softens the onion and carries the bouillon aroma. No seed oils. Make a smooth slurry first so the starch (or almond flour) does not lump in the hot pot. Simmer gently after adding milk — a hard boil can curdle the dairy. Almond flour thickens a bit less glossily than wheat flour but still works at 2 tbsp. For a lower-carb pot, swap cauliflower for the potatoes. Chicken works in place of turkey. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Goulash
recipes.how: 1 pound lean ground beef 1 small onion, chopped 8 ounces elbow macaroni, cooked 1 cup frozen corn or peas 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed tomato soup, undiluted 1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce 1/4 cup water Salt and pepper to taste 1. In a skillet, brown ground beef and onion; drain. 2. Combine all ingredients in a 2-quart casserole dish or small roasting pan; cover and bake in a 350°F oven for 30 minutes or until thoroughly warmed. Here is one of those simple, throw-it-together dishes, and it remains one of Don’s favorites. Carb level: High-carb (elbow macaroni + corn) No added oil. Brown the beef in its own fat so you get a little fond before it goes into the casserole. Cover the dish so the pasta stays moist while the tomato soup and sauce heat through and cling. For a lower-carb version, use zucchini coins or cauliflower florets in place of some or all of the macaroni. Typo fixed: Don’s (original had “Dons”). Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Honey-Barbecued Ribs
recipes.how: 4 pounds pork baby back ribs 1 pouch dry onion soup mix 3/4 cup ketchup 1/2 cup water 3 tbsp. + 1 tsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 2 tbsp. honey (in place of 1/3 cup honey) 1/2 tsp. pepper 1/4 tsp. garlic powder 1. Cut ribs into 2- or 3-rib portions. 2. In a 6-quart Dutch oven, place ribs in enough cold water to cover. Heat to boiling over high heat. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 35 minutes; drain. 3. Meanwhile, in a 1-quart saucepan, combine soup mix, ketchup, water, sweetener, pepper, and garlic powder. Heat to boiling over high heat. Reduce heat to low; cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. 4. On a preheated grill rack, arrange ribs directly above medium coals. Grill, uncovered, 30 minutes, turning often and basting with barbecue sauce. Does finger-lickin’ good mean anything? Around here it means “Mom has made those yummy ribs again.” These are the best ribs in town…tender and covered in a rich, tangy barbecue sauce. Baked beans and corn on the cob always round out these fantastic ribs in our house. Carb level: Moderate-to-high carb (honey + ketchup) No added cooking oil. The pre-simmer renders fat and starts breaking down collagen so the grill time can be about glaze, not toughness. Honey is kept. It browns and sticks on the grill in a way monk fruit cannot. If you want it less sweet, drop the honey to 3–4 tbsp. and do not replace all of it. Turn often and baste late as well as often — sugar burns if it sits in one spot over the coals. Nice with baked beans and corn on the cob, as in the original house meal. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Sugar swap: This is a glaze that lacquers on the ribs. A quarter stays real honey, and allulose browns even faster than sugar, so baste late and watch it.

recipes.title: Meatloaf with Onion Gravy
recipes.how: For the meatloaf: 1-1/2 pounds lean ground beef 1 cup bread crumbs or crushed crackers (lower-carb option: 1 cup blanched almond flour) 1 small onion, chopped 1 egg 1/2 cup milk 1/2 cup ketchup 1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce 1 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper For the onion gravy: 2 cups water 1 envelope dry onion soup mix 4 to 6 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 3/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 cup water 1. In a large bowl, combine beef, bread crumbs (or almond flour), onion, egg, milk, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper; mix thoroughly. In a shallow baking pan, shape into a loaf. Bake at 350°F for 1 hour, draining off fat halfway through cooking. 2. In a medium saucepan, bring 2 cups water to a boil; stir in soup mix. Simmer, covered, for 10 minutes. Combine flour with 1 cup water and gradually stir into soup. Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer, stirring frequently, until gravy thickens, about 5 minutes. Serve with meatloaf. When we’re hungry for a change from my traditional meatloaf, I make this gravy-covered meatloaf and baked potatoes. I serve it with Baked Brown Sugar Squash, just like with my traditional meatloaf. The three make for a hearty, homestyle dinner. Carb level: Moderate-carb (bread crumbs + gravy flour); almond flour options bring it down No added cooking oil. Drain the loaf halfway so the crust can brown instead of sitting in fat. Bread crumbs (or crackers) hold moisture. Almond flour still binds with the egg and milk; the loaf will be a little denser and less bready. Whisk the flour slurry in gradually so the starch gelatinizes smoothly. Almond flour thickens via protein and fat, so that gravy will be slightly less glossy. Pairs with Baked Brown Sugar Squash (rec114) and baked potatoes. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Parmesan Chicken Shells
recipes.how: For the filling: 1-1/2 cups ricotta cheese 1 egg 1/2 tsp. parsley 1/4 tsp. garlic powder 1/8 tsp. oregano 1/8 tsp. pepper 3/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese, divided 2 cups cooked, shredded chicken For the bake: 16 jumbo pasta shells, cooked and drained 2–3 cups spaghetti sauce 1. In a medium mixing bowl, combine ricotta cheese, egg, parsley, garlic powder, oregano, and pepper; mix well. Stir in Parmesan cheese, 1-1/4 cups mozzarella, and chicken. 2. Preheat oven to 350°F. 3. Pour half of the spaghetti sauce in the bottom of an 11x7-inch baking dish. Evenly fill shells with chicken mixture and place in the dish. Pour remaining sauce over shells; sprinkle with remaining mozzarella. 4. Cover the dish with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes. Uncover and let stand 5 minutes before serving. I came up with this pasta delight one night when I wanted to use up chicken, spaghetti sauce, and pasta shells. It was a big success, and a great way to use up some key ingredients you may have on hand! Carb level: High-carb (jumbo pasta shells) No added cooking oil. Cheese and sauce supply the fat. The egg sets the ricotta so the filling doesn’t leak when the shells bake. Don’t overcook the shells before stuffing or they tear. Keep the pan covered so the pasta steams and finishes tender without drying the cheese. For a lower-carb version, stuff the same filling into zucchini boats or large mushroom caps and bake until hot. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Salisbury Steak with Onion Mushroom Gravy
recipes.how: For the patties: 1-1/2 pounds lean ground beef 1 jar (12 ounces) beef gravy, divided* 1 egg 1/2 cup bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1/2 cup blanched almond flour) 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1/4 tsp. onion powder For the gravy: 1 small onion, thinly sliced 1/2 pound fresh mushrooms, sliced, or 1 jar (4 ounces) sliced mushrooms Remaining gravy from the jar 1/4 cup water 1. Combine beef, 1/4 cup gravy, egg, bread crumbs (or almond flour), salt, pepper, and onion powder; mix well. Shape into 6 oval patties. 2. Heat a large skillet over medium heat with a thin film of avocado oil or ghee (in place of nonstick spray). Brown patties 4 to 5 minutes per side. Remove from the skillet and keep warm. 3. In the same skillet, sauté onions and mushrooms until tender. Stir in the remaining gravy and water and simmer for 1 minute. Return beef to the skillet; cover and cook another 10 minutes, or until the beef is cooked to desired doneness. This is a great comfort meal that can turn an ordinary day into something special. Teamed with mashed potatoes and Cream Peas, you’ll have your family asking for seconds! Carb level: Moderate-carb (bread crumbs + jarred gravy); almond flour option is Moderate-low Avocado oil or ghee replaces cooking spray so the patties actually sear (Maillard) instead of steaming. Bread crumbs (or almond flour) plus a little gravy in the meat keep the steaks tender. Almond flour makes a slightly denser patty that still holds. *Useful tip: If you like more gravy with steak and mashed potatoes, add an extra 1 to 2 cups of gravy. Nice with Cream Peas. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this dish. The change is small: almond flour makes a slightly denser, richer patty that still holds, so the flavor stays close.

recipes.title: Sunshine Barbecue Chicken
recipes.how: 1 Reynolds Oven Bag, large size 2 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 2 tbsp. blanched almond flour) 1 cup barbecue sauce 1/4 cup orange juice 8 skinless chicken pieces 1. Preheat oven to 350°F. 2. Shake flour in the oven bag; place in a 13x9-inch baking dish. Add barbecue sauce and orange juice to the bag. Squeeze the bag to blend ingredients. Add chicken to the bag. Turn the bag to coat the chicken with sauce. Arrange chicken in an even layer. 3. Close the bag with the nylon tie; cut 6 half-inch slits in the top. 4. Bake until chicken is tender, 45 to 50 minutes. To serve, stir the sauce and spoon over the chicken. This comes from the “Reynolds kitchen” and is a tried-and-true recipe in my house. One reason is because it’s so easy. Another, because it is tender, juicy, and full of barbecue flavor. You can also cook this in a crock pot by omitting the oven bag and flour. Cook on low for 6 to 8 hours. Carb level: Moderate-carb (barbecue sauce + orange juice) No added cooking oil. The bag traps steam so the chicken stays juicy. The flour (or almond flour) is what Reynolds wants shaken into the bag — it blends with the juices and keeps the bag from bursting. Don’t skip it for the oven-bag method. Typo fixed: omitting (original had “ommiting”). Crock-pot path: skip the bag and flour; cook on low 6 to 8 hours. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb.

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Chicken
recipes.how: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts 2 cups water 2 chicken bouillon cubes 1/4 cup + 2 tbsp. golden monk fruit blend + 2 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 1/2 cup brown sugar) 4 tbsp. cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1/2 cup white vinegar 2 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple chunks 1 can (15 ounces) sliced carrots 1 green pepper, diced 1 small onion, diced Hot cooked rice 1. Bake chicken at 375°F for 20 minutes or until the chicken is no longer pink; cool. 2. Cut chicken into small cubes and add to a skillet. Add water and bouillon cubes. Cover and simmer while making the sauce. 3. Drain pineapple and reserve the juice. Combine sweetener and cornstarch in a saucepan. Add vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, and pineapple juice. Cook and stir over medium heat until thick and bubbly. 4. Add sauce to the chicken. Stir in pineapple, carrots, green pepper, and onion. Cook over low heat until heated through and the green pepper is crisp-tender. Serve over hot cooked rice. Here is my Mom’s wonderful sweet and sour chicken recipe. This version is much lower in fat than its “battered and deep-fat-fried chicken” counterpart. I enjoy both versions, but make this one more often. Carb level: High-carb (brown sugar + pineapple + rice) No added frying oil. Baking the chicken first keeps this lighter than the battered restaurant version. Sugar swap: Keep some real brown sugar. Those molasses sugars help the sauce gloss and caramelize; cornstarch does the thickening either way. Cornstarch needs a full bubble to set. Stir constantly so it does not scorch. For a lower-carb plate, serve over cauliflower rice and use the monk fruit option. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Chicken
recipes.how: 1-1/2 lbs. boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut in thin pieces 3/4 cup water 1/2 cup soy sauce* 3/4 to 1 cup brown sugar (or ⅓–½ cup monk fruit baking blend + 2–3 tbsp. brown sugar) 1/4 tsp. garlic powder 1/8 tsp. ground ginger 1/2 tbsp. cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 tbsp. avocado oil (in place of vegetable oil) Hot cooked rice 1. Combine water, soy sauce, sweetener, garlic, and ginger; whisk to mix well. 2. Marinate chicken in half of the sauce 2 to 3 hours, turning once. Stir cornstarch into the remaining sauce and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture boils and thickens slightly. Cool to room temperature. 3. Drain marinade off the chicken and reserve 2 tbsp. of the marinade; discard remaining marinade. Stir-fry chicken in avocado oil until the chicken is almost done. Stir in the reserved 2 tbsp. of marinade and continue stir-frying until the chicken is done and glazed. Serve over hot rice with the cooled teriyaki sauce. It took a lot of experimenting, but I finally came up with a sweet teriyaki sauce we enjoy as much as the one served in our favorite teriyaki restaurant. Beef and pork would also work well with this sauce. Carb level: High-carb with rice (brown sugar + soy); the chicken itself is Moderate-carb Avocado oil replaces vegetable oil for the stir-fry. It handles the heat and stays neutral so the teriyaki can shine. No seed oils. Sugar swap: Keep some real brown sugar. Those molasses sugars are what glaze and caramelize in the pan; cornstarch thickens the table sauce either way. Boil the unused half of the sauce (the cornstarch half) so it is safe to serve. Discard the leftover raw marinade except the 2 tbsp. you cook onto the chicken. *Useful tip: Lite soy sauce has less sodium. Beef or pork works in this same sauce. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Vegetable Beef Soup
recipes.how: 1 pound stew meat 1 can (15 ounces) crushed tomatoes 3 cups water 2 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed 2 carrots, peeled and sliced 2 celery ribs, sliced 3 beef bouillon cubes 1 large onion, diced 1 tsp. dried parsley 1/2 tsp. dried basil 1/2 tsp. dried oregano 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1-1/2 cups frozen mixed vegetables 1. In a crock pot, combine the first 13 ingredients. Cover and cook on high for 5 hours. Add the frozen vegetables; cover and cook on high 2 hours longer, or until the meat and vegetables are tender. Another great, hearty soup that warms the soul. Paired with sweet cornbread and maybe a salad, this is a delicious way to top off a wintery night and chase the chill away. Carb level: Moderate-to-high carb (potatoes + mixed vegetables) No added oil. The long cook renders the stew meat and builds body from collagen. Add the frozen vegetables at the end so they stay bright instead of turning to mush in a 7-hour cook. For a lower-carb pot, swap turnips or cauliflower for the potatoes. Nice with Sweet Cornbread. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Chili Mac
recipes.how: 1 pound lean ground beef 1 medium onion, chopped 1 clove garlic, minced 1 can (14-1/4 ounces) tomatoes, cut up 2 cups water 1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce 1 tbsp. chili powder 1/2 tsp. oregano 8 ounces uncooked elbow macaroni 1 can (15-1/4 ounces) dark red kidney beans, undrained 1. Brown the ground beef, onion, and garlic in a 3-quart saucepan; drain. 2. Return the beef mixture to the saucepan. Add tomatoes, water, tomato sauce, chili powder, and oregano; bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer 10 minutes. 3. Stir in the uncooked macaroni and kidney beans. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium. Simmer 9 to 10 minutes or until the macaroni is tender, stirring occasionally. This great dish is a cross between chili and goulash, and is so satisfying. Not to mention, very simple to prepare. Don loves this stuff! Carb level: High-carb (elbow macaroni plus kidney beans) No added oil needed. The beef renders its own fat for browning; those browned bits (Maillard) are the flavor base before the tomatoes go in. Cooking the macaroni in the chili instead of a separate pot lets the pasta starch thicken the sauce and pull tomato and chili flavor into the noodles. Keep the wheat pasta as the backbone of the dish. A full almond-flour or zucchini-noodle swap will not give you chili mac. For a lower-carb bowl, use half the macaroni and extra beef, or serve a scoop over sautéed zucchini. Leave the beans undrained. That canning liquid adds body and a little extra starch so the stew is spoonable, not soupy. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Parmesan Carbonara
recipes.how: 12 ounces linguine 4 eggs, beaten 1/4 cup butter, melted 1/4 cup milk 3/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 4 slices bacon, crisply cooked and crumbled 1 tbsp. chopped parsley, optional 1/2 tsp. pepper Additional Parmesan, for serving 1. Cook the linguine according to package directions. Drain; do not rinse. 2. Return the hot pasta to the pan. Toss with the eggs, butter, and milk so the residual heat thickens the eggs into a sauce. Add the Parmesan, bacon, parsley, and pepper; heat thoroughly, stirring often, until the sauce is creamy and steaming. Serve with additional Parmesan. When you're not in the mood for spaghetti or fettuccine Alfredo, turn to this delicious pasta alternative. The Parmesan and bacon blend nicely together in this classic pasta dish. I am aware of the dangers of eating raw eggs, but I heat mine enough to “cook” the eggs until I feel they're safe. Carb level: High-carb (linguine is the base) Butter stays. It emulsifies with the egg, milk, and cheese into a glossy sauce and carries the bacon fat. No seed oils. Do not rinse the pasta. Surface starch helps the egg-cheese mixture cling instead of sliding off. Steph’s instinct is right: the eggs need heat. Off the boil, toss continuously so the proteins set into a custard, not scrambled curds. The sauce is safe when it is steaming hot and thick, not runny-raw. If you want extra insurance, pull a little pasta water and whisk it into the beaten eggs first to start the temper. Wheat pasta stays primary. Zucchini noodles will not make this sauce behave the same way; they shed water and dilute the emulsion. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Apple Stuffed Pork Chops
recipes.how: For the chops: 4 pork chops, 1 to 1-1/2 inches thick Salt and pepper, to taste For the stuffing: 1 box (6 ounces) cornbread stuffing mix 1-1/2 cups hot chicken broth 1 cup chopped apple 1/4 cup chopped onion 2 tbsp. chopped parsley 1. Heat the oven to 350°F. Season each pork chop with salt and pepper. Make a pocket in each chop by cutting between the rib bones. 2. Combine the stuffing mix, chicken broth, apple, onion, and parsley; mix well. 3. Stuff each chop with 1/2 cup stuffing. Place in an 11x7-inch baking dish. Spoon the remaining stuffing around the chops. 4. Bake, uncovered, for 1 hour and 15 minutes, turning once halfway through baking, until the pork is cooked through. Pork and apples pair so nicely together, and this delicious dish will have everyone wanting seconds. Carb level: High-carb with the stuffing (cornbread mix); the pork itself is low-carb No seed oils in the original. The stuffing mix and broth supply the fat and moisture; the apple and onion steam inside the pocket and perfume the meat. Wheat cornbread stuffing stays primary so the dish still reads as stuffed pork chops. A full almond-flour stuffing will not bind the same way. For a lower-carb plate, stuff more lightly and serve extra sautéed apple and onion on the side. Pork is done at 145°F in the thickest part, then rest a few minutes. The original hour-plus bake was written for well-done chops; start checking around 50–55 minutes if your chops are closer to 1 inch. Unstuffed method: layer half the stuffing in a greased 11x7-inch dish, top with 3/4-inch chops, spoon the remaining stuffing over, cover, and bake about 45 minutes. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Sweet Onion Burgers
recipes.how: For the onions: 1 large sweet onion, sliced 1 tbsp. butter, melted 1 tsp. dry mustard 1 tsp. honey For the burgers: 1-1/2 pounds lean ground beef 1/4 cup Worcestershire sauce 1/4 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper For serving: 6 hamburger buns, onion rolls, or Kaiser rolls (or lettuce leaves for a lower-carb wrap) 6 lettuce leaves 6 tomato slices 1. For the onions, tear a large piece (36x18 inches) of heavy-duty foil. Fold in half to make a double thickness (18x18 inches). Place the onions in the center.
