Combine the melted butter, mustard, and honey; drizzle over the onions. Bring up two opposite ends of the foil and seal with a double fold. Fold the remaining ends to enclose the onions, leaving space for steam to build. Place the packet on an uncovered grill directly over medium heat for 15 minutes. 2. Meanwhile, combine the ground beef, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper; mix well. Shape into 6 patties. Add the patties to the grill. Grill the patties and onions for 5 minutes. Turn the patties and grill 8 to 10 minutes more, until no pink remains and the onions are tender. 3. Lightly toast the buns or rolls on the grill. Top with desired condiments, then add a lettuce leaf, tomato slice, burger, grilled onions, and the top bun. Try these one grilling day for a scrumptious twist on the ol' hamburger! Carb level: High-carb on a bun; Moderate-low as a lettuce-wrap burger (honey is a teaspoon for the whole onion packet) Butter stays on the onions. Combined with honey and dry mustard it glazes the slices as they steam in the foil. No seed oils. Keep the teaspoon of honey. It is doing real work: a little reducing sugar helps the onions brown and gives the mustard something to cling to. Monk fruit will not glaze the same way here. Worcestershire is the burger’s umami. Mix it in gently so the patties stay tender; overworking the beef squeezes out fat and water and makes them tight. The beef, onions, lettuce, and tomato are a solid low-carb plate. Use lettuce wraps when you want the flavor without the roll. Carb rating (Low): ~6g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Turkey & Cranberry on Cinnamon Bread
recipes.how: For the herbed spread: 4 oz cream cheese, softened 2 tbsp avocado oil mayonnaise (in place of regular mayonnaise) 1 tsp Dijon mustard 1 tbsp finely chopped fresh chives or parsley Pinch of salt and black pepper For the cranberry relish (quick version): 1 cup leftover cranberry sauce (or whole-berry) 1–2 tsp monk fruit sweetener (only if the sauce is very tart) 1 tsp orange zest (optional but excellent) Pinch of cinnamon For the sandwich: 4 thick slices cinnamon swirl bread (or cinnamon raisin) 8–10 oz leftover roasted turkey, thinly sliced Soft butter or ghee, for toasting Optional: thin slices of sharp white cheddar or Brie 1. Make the herbed spread: mix cream cheese, avocado oil mayonnaise, Dijon, chives, salt, and pepper until smooth. Set aside. 2. Stir the cranberry sauce with a little monk fruit and orange zest if using. Taste and adjust. 3. Lightly butter the outer sides of the cinnamon bread slices. 4. Spread the herbed mixture generously on the inner sides of two slices. Layer turkey, a spoonful of cranberry relish, and optional cheese. Top with the remaining bread. 5. Toast in a skillet over medium heat (or in a panini press) 2–3 minutes per side until the bread is golden and fragrant and the cheese (if using) begins to melt. 6. Slice on the diagonal and serve warm. For Peter A post-Thanksgiving favorite rebuilt for better flavor, texture, and balance. Soft cinnamon swirl bread meets savory roasted turkey, a bright low-sugar cranberry relish, and a creamy herbed spread. Warm, slightly sweet, and deeply satisfying. Yield: 2 generous sandwiches Carb level: Moderate-carb (cinnamon bread is the main source; turkey, cheese, and the spread are protein and fat) Avocado oil mayonnaise replaces regular mayo so the spread is seed-oil-free. Cream cheese plus mayo is a stable cold emulsion: the extra fat keeps the sandwich moist, and Dijon’s acid stops the cinnamon-cranberry sweetness from taking over. Butter or ghee on the outside of the bread is what browns and perfumes the crust (Maillard). Do not use seed oil in the pan. Orange zest brightens leftover cranberry without more sugar. Monk fruit is only if the sauce is harsh — you want the relish tart enough to cut the rich spread. Cinnamon swirl bread stays; it is the sandwich. For a lower-carb plate, use the same turkey, spread, and relish in lettuce wraps or on a thin slice of toasted low-carb bread. Medium heat only. Too hot and the sugar in the swirl bread scorches before the cheese melts. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Cap'n Crunch Chicken
recipes.how: For the chicken: 2-1/2 cups Cap’n Crunch cereal 1 cup cornflakes 1 egg 1/2 cup milk 1/2 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 cup blanched almond flour) 1 tsp. onion powder 1 tsp. garlic powder 1/2 tsp. black pepper 2 pounds chicken breast, cut into 1-oz. tenders Avocado oil or lard, for frying (in place of vegetable oil) For the honey-mustard sauce: 1/2 cup avocado oil mayonnaise (in place of regular mayonnaise) 1 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 1 tbsp. honey (in place of 2 tbsp. honey) 1 tbsp. prepared mustard 1. Coarsely grind or crush the two cereals and set aside. Beat the egg with the milk and set aside. 2. Stir together the flour, onion powder, garlic powder, and black pepper. 3. Dip the chicken pieces in the seasoned flour and coat well; shake off the excess. Dip in the egg wash, coating well, then dip in the cereal mixture, coating well. 4. Heat avocado oil or lard in a large heavy skillet to 325°F. Drop the coated tenders carefully into the hot fat and cook until golden brown and fully cooked, 3 to 5 minutes depending on size. Drain and serve immediately with the sauce. 5. For the sauce, combine the avocado oil mayonnaise, honey, and mustard and mix well. This is a copycat of Planet Hollywood’s Cap’n Crunch Chicken. The first time I made it, I burned it, and we could barely eat it. The second time it came out perfect, and boy is it good! We enjoy ours with my homemade honey-mustard sauce. They make the best combo! Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: High-carb (Cap’n Crunch and cornflake crust); the chicken itself is low-carb Avocado oil or lard replaces vegetable oil for frying. Both handle 325°F without seed oils. Steph’s first batch burned — stay at 325°F, not hotter. The cereal is already full of sugar and will scorch before the chicken cooks if the fat is too hot. Sugar swap: Avocado oil mayonnaise replaces regular mayo in the honey-mustard so the sauce is seed-oil-free. Keep some real honey; it gives the sauce body and gloss that monk fruit alone will not. The flour dredge can be almond flour. It is only there so the egg wash sticks. The cereal coating is the dish — do not swap that for almond flour or you lose the copycat crunch. Three-step breading (flour → egg → cereal) is food science, not fuss. Dry flour gives the egg proteins something to grab; the egg glues the crumbs. Press the cereal on firmly and rest the tenders a minute before they hit the fat so less coating sheds. Serve at once. The sugar in the cereal stays crisp for only a short window, then it softens. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Cheesy Eggs Benedict
recipes.how: For the eggs: 12 eggs, beaten 1/4 cup milk Dash of salt and pepper 1-1/2 tbsp. butter, for scrambling For the cheese sauce: 1/4 cup butter 1/4 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 2 cups milk Dash of salt and pepper 2 cups shredded Cheddar cheese For serving: 12 thick slices cooked ham 6 toasted English muffins (12 halves) 1. Warm the ham in the oven or microwave; keep warm. 2. Combine the beaten eggs, 1/4 cup milk, and a dash of salt and pepper. Melt 1½ tbsp. butter in a frying pan or electric skillet and scramble the eggs until just set; keep warm. 3. Melt 1/4 cup butter in a medium saucepan. Stir in the flour and cook until smooth, about 1 minute. Whisk in 2 cups milk and a dash of salt and pepper; cook and stir until thick and smooth. Add the cheese and remove from the heat. Stir until the cheese is melted and blended. 4. Place one slice of ham on each muffin half. Top with scrambled eggs and cheese sauce. My family loves this brunch dish, and it’s so easy to make! This is a traditional after-Easter breakfast for us to use up the leftover ham. This is one of my Mom’s specialties! Carb level: Moderate-carb (English muffins plus a flour roux); the eggs, ham, and cheese are low-carb Butter is the fat for both the eggs and the sauce. No seed oils. The roux (butter + flour) gelatinizes in the milk into a stable white sauce; Cheddar then melts into that starch network so the sauce stays smooth instead of breaking. Almond flour can stand in for the wheat in the roux if you want a lighter sauce. Cook it the same minute in the butter so it loses its raw taste, then whisk the milk in slowly. Wheat still gives the silkier classic texture. Keep this as Mom’s cheesy Benedict, not a hollandaise swap. The cheddar sauce is the dish. English muffins stay. They are the platform. For a lower-carb plate, skip the muffins and spoon ham, eggs, and sauce over sautéed spinach or roasted tomato halves. Do not boil the sauce after the cheese goes in. High heat squeezes fat out of the Cheddar and the sauce looks greasy. Off heat, residual warmth is enough to melt it. Soft-set the scramble. The hot sauce will cook the eggs a little more on the plate. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Chicken-Vegetable Linguine
recipes.how: 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms 2 tbsp. butter 1 cup cooked chicken, cut into thin strips 1 can (19 ounces) ready-to-serve cream of chicken soup 1/4 cup milk 1 cup frozen peas 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1/8 tsp. pepper 4 cups cooked linguine Additional Parmesan, for garnish 1. In a 4-quart saucepan over medium heat, cook the mushrooms and chicken in the butter until the mushrooms are tender and most of the liquid has evaporated, stirring often. 2. Add the soup, milk, peas, Parmesan, pepper, and linguine. Heat through, stirring often. Garnish with additional Parmesan, if desired. This dish is so quick and easy, perfect when you need dinner in a hurry. Carb level: High-carb (linguine is the base) Butter stays. It browns the mushrooms (Maillard) and carries the Parmesan. No seed oils. Cook the mushrooms until their liquid is gone before the soup goes in. Water left in the pan thins the cream sauce and tastes steamed instead of savory. Wheat linguine stays primary. This is a pasta supper; zucchini noodles will shed water and turn the soup sauce watery. For a lower-carb bowl, use half the pasta and extra chicken and mushrooms. The canned cream soup is the weeknight shortcut that makes this dinner-in-a-hurry. If you want a from-scratch version, swap in 2 cups warm chicken broth whisked with 1/2 cup heavy cream and a pinch of extra Parmesan, and simmer until it coats a spoon. Frozen peas go in at the end so they stay bright. Long heat turns them gray and dulls the sweetness. Do not rinse the pasta. Starch on the noodles helps the sauce cling. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Honey Mustard Pork Scallopine
recipes.how: 4 thin-cut boneless pork chops 1 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 1 tbsp. honey (in place of 2 tbsp. honey) 2 tbsp. spicy mustard 1/4 cup fine dry bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1/4 cup crushed pork rinds) 1/4 cup finely crushed buttery crackers 2 tbsp. butter 1. Pound the pork chops to about 1/8-inch thickness between sheets of waxed paper. 2. In a small bowl, combine the honey and mustard; mix well. In a shallow dish, combine the bread crumbs and cracker crumbs. 3. With a pastry brush, generously coat both sides of the pork slices with the honey-mustard sauce. Coat in the crumbs. 4. Melt the butter in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pork 4 minutes per side until crisp and lightly browned. This has to be one of the quickest main dish entrees I have...and one of the most delicious! We love honey mustard, and when paired with this crispy pork it's even a more mouth-watering blend. It's nice to have something so tasty to turn to when time is short. This recipe humbly earned me a 4th place win in a 1998 Taste of Home Quick Cooking magazine contest. =) Carb level: Moderate-carb (honey plus bread-crumb and cracker dredge); the pork itself is low-carb Butter is the frying fat. It browns the crumbs and carries the honey-mustard aroma. No seed oils. Sugar swap: Keep at least a tablespoon of real honey. Honey is both flavor and glue — it helps the crumbs stick and gives the crust a little Maillard color in the skillet. Monk fruit will not do that on its own. Almond flour can stand in for the dry bread crumbs in the dredge; keep the crushed buttery crackers if you want Steph’s original crunch and flavor. For a lower-carb plate, use all almond flour (or finely crushed pork rinds) and the same honey-mustard brush. 1/8 inch is the point. Thin cutlets cook through in 4 minutes a side without drying, and the crust stays crisp instead of steaming. Do not crowd the skillet or the crumbs will soak instead of fry. This is the same honey-mustard idea as the dipping sauce, cooked onto the meat. A 1998 Taste of Home Quick Cooking contest 4th-place recipe — leave the method recognizable. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Hearty Scrambled Eggs
recipes.how: 12 eggs 1/3 cup milk 1-1/2 cups diced fully cooked ham 1 cup shredded Colby Jack cheese 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms 3 green onions, thinly sliced (green part included) 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 3 tbsp. butter 1. In a bowl, beat the eggs and milk together. Stir in the ham, cheese, mushrooms, green onions, salt, and pepper. 2. Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the egg mixture. Cook and stir until the eggs are completely set and the cheese is melted. Serve these for a filling breakfast or part of your fancy brunch feast. Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: Low-carb (eggs, ham, cheese, and mushrooms; milk is a few tablespoons for the whole skillet) Butter is the cooking fat. It browns the ham bits and keeps the curds tender. No seed oils. Medium heat, not high. Egg proteins set around 160–180°F; a ripping-hot pan squeezes out water and makes rubbery curds before the cheese melts. Mushrooms shed water as they cook. Keep stirring until that moisture cooks off and the eggs look set, not wet. If you want a drier skillet, sauté the mushrooms in the butter for 2 minutes before adding the egg mixture. Twelve eggs plus ham and cheese is a brunch platter, not a two-person scramble. It stretches to 6 plates next to toast, or 4 very full ones. Carb rating (Carnivore): Eggs and dairy fat only — no flour, sugar, starch, or sweet mix-ins, so digestible carbs stay near zero.

recipes.title: Mushroom Beef over Pasta
recipes.how: 1 pound beef stew meat 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup, undiluted 1 envelope dry onion soup mix 2 cups sliced fresh mushrooms 1/4 tsp. pepper Hot cooked pasta, for serving 1. Combine the beef, soup, soup mix, mushrooms, and pepper in a crock pot. 2. Cover and cook on low 8 to 10 hours. 3. Serve over pasta. This is a fantastic crock pot dish which is just as delicious as easy! Carb level: High-carb over pasta; Moderate-low if you serve the same gravy over zucchini noodles or cauliflower No added cooking oil. The stew meat and canned soup supply the fat. If you brown the cubes in a little butter or avocado oil first, you get extra Maillard flavor, but the original dump-and-go method still works. Eight to ten hours on low is collagen turning into gelatin. That is what makes cheap stew meat spoon-tender and gives the gravy body. High for 4 hours will cook the meat but will not give you the same silky sauce. The onion soup mix is salt, onion, and a little starch — it seasons the pot and helps the mushroom soup cling. Taste before adding extra salt. Wheat pasta stays the classic plate. The beef and mushroom gravy are the dish; use zucchini ribbons or mashed cauliflower when you want the same supper without the noodles. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Chicken and Rice Quesadillas
recipes.how: For the chicken: 1/4 cup water 2 tbsp. vinegar 2 tbsp. avocado oil (in place of vegetable oil) 1 package (1 ounce) fajita marinade 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into thin strips For the Mexican rice: 1 can (14 ounces) tomatoes 1-1/2 cups chicken broth 2 tbsp. butter (in place of margarine) 1 cup long-grain white rice 1 small onion, chopped 1 clove garlic, minced 2 tbsp. diced green chiles 1/4 cup water Salt and pepper 2 tbsp. chopped cilantro leaves For the quesadillas: 3 cups shredded Monterey Jack and Colby cheeses 8 large flour tortillas Salsa, sour cream, and guacamole, optional 1. Combine the water, vinegar, avocado oil, and fajita marinade in a large plastic bag or glass dish. Add the chicken and let stand while you prepare the Mexican rice. 2. Drain the liquid from the tomatoes into a glass measuring cup. Add enough chicken broth to make 2 cups liquid. Set aside. 3. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the rice and cook, stirring, until it begins to turn opaque, about 3 minutes. Add the onion, garlic, chiles, and 1/4 cup water; continue to cook and stir for 5 minutes. Add more water, 1 tablespoon at a time, if needed. 4. Add the tomatoes and the broth mixture (break up the tomatoes with a spoon). Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover and simmer until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender, about 25 minutes. Season with salt and pepper and stir in the cilantro. 5. Remove the chicken from the marinade; discard the marinade. In a large skillet over medium-high heat, sauté the chicken 5 minutes or until done. 6. Heat the oven to 350°F. Evenly layer the chicken strips among 4 flour tortillas. Spread a generous amount of rice over the top (serve leftover rice on the side). Sprinkle each with 1/2 cup of the combined cheeses. Top with another tortilla and sprinkle with the remaining cheese. 7. Place on foil-lined baking sheets. Cover loosely with foil and bake 10 minutes, or until the cheese is melted. Cut into wedges. Serve with salsa, sour cream, and guacamole if desired. These are awesome! Combined with my good friend Trish's Mexican Rice and delicious, tender chicken, this is a great Mexican meal in itself. The rice is halved from Trish's Bloomin' Good Recipes. Yield: 4 servings (4 large quesadillas) Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas plus a full cup of rice in the filling) Avocado oil replaces vegetable oil in the marinade. Butter replaces margarine for toasting the rice. No seed oils. Toasting the raw rice in butter until it turns opaque is a pilaf step: each grain gets a thin fat coat so it stays separate after the tomato broth goes in, and the butter toasts a little flavor onto the starch. Discard the used marinade. The acid and salt have done their work on the raw chicken; boiling it into a sauce is not worth the food-safety hassle on a weeknight. Wheat flour tortillas stay — they are the quesadilla. Low-carb tortillas work if you want a lighter plate; skip the rice inside and serve a spoon of it on the side, or use cauliflower rice in the filling. Cover the pan loosely with foil so the top cheese melts without the tortillas scorching. Ten minutes at 350°F is a melt, not a crisp-up; use a skillet with a little butter if you want browned edges. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Beef Burgundy
recipes.how: 2 pounds round steak, cut into 1-inch cubes 2 tbsp. avocado oil 1/4 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1 cup beef broth 3/4 cup Burgundy wine 1 tsp. beef bouillon granules 1 clove garlic, minced 1/2 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. seasoned salt 1/4 tsp. dried marjoram 1/4 tsp. dried thyme 1/4 tsp. pepper 1 tbsp. cornstarch dissolved in 1 tbsp. water (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1. Combine the flour, 1/2 tsp. salt, and 1/4 tsp. pepper; coat the beef in the flour mixture. 2. Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet; brown the beef on all sides, working in batches if necessary. Transfer the beef to a crock pot, leaving excess fat behind. 3. Add the beef broth, wine, bouillon, garlic, remaining salt, seasoned salt, marjoram, thyme, and remaining pepper. Cover and cook on low 6 to 8 hours, until the meat is tender. 4. Turn the cooker to high and stir in the cornstarch mixture. Cook 15 minutes, until the sauce is glossy and slightly thickened. Serve over mashed potatoes, or over rice or pasta if you want a starchier plate. This is a delicious recipe inspired by one of my "great-Chef-loopie-buddies," Cheryl, on AOL. This aromatic dish will have you drooling during cooking time! Carb level: Moderate-low for the stew itself (a light flour dredge and a cornstarch finish); Moderate-carb to High-carb if you pour it over potatoes, rice, or pasta Avocado oil replaces vegetable oil for the sear. It handles skillet heat without seed oils and stays neutral so the wine and herbs can lead. The flour dredge is not just coating — it browns (Maillard) and later melts into the sauce. A full almond-flour swap will not thicken the same way; leave this small amount of wheat flour. Low-and-slow in the crock pot turns collagen in the round steak into gelatin, which is why cheap stew beef goes silky after 6 to 8 hours. High heat at the end lets the cornstarch slurry swell and gloss the sauce without a long boil. Burgundy (or another dry Pinot Noir) adds acid and fruit; most of the alcohol cooks off. Do not skip the wine — water will not give the same depth. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap rice for cauliflower rice; swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Grilled Pizza
recipes.how: For the dough: 1 cup flat beer 2 tbsp. butter 1 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tbsp. sugar (in place of 2 tbsp. sugar) 1 tsp. salt 2-1/2 cups all-purpose flour 1 package (2-1/4 tsp.) active dry yeast For the toppings: Olive oil, for brushing Pizza sauce or barbecue sauce Finely chopped garlic and fresh or dried herbs Any combination of ham, pepperoni, sausage, chicken, grilled vegetables (mushrooms, bell peppers, tomatoes, onions, yellow squash, zucchini), olives, pineapple Cheese: shredded mozzarella, Monterey Jack, Cheddar, provolone, or grated Parmesan 1. For the dough, use a bread machine on the dough setting, adding the ingredients to the pan in the order listed. Or dissolve the yeast in warm beer (105°F to 115°F). Add the butter, sugar, salt, and flour. Mix until the dough forms a ball and cleans the sides of the bowl. Turn onto a floured surface and knead 2 minutes. Place in a greased bowl, turning to grease the top. Cover; let rise in a warm place, free from draft, until doubled, about 1 hour. Punch down. 2. Divide the dough into 4 balls. On a cornmeal-coated or lightly floured surface, roll and pat each ball to 1/4-inch thickness. Brush each circle with olive oil. 3. Oil the hot grill grate with olive oil or avocado oil to help prevent sticking. Vegetables such as mushrooms, bell peppers, yellow squash, and zucchini need to be grilled until tender before using them as toppings. 4. Place the circles directly over medium coals. Grill uncovered until the dough starts to bubble on top and the bottom is lightly browned. Turn with tongs. Grill until the second side is lightly browned, then remove the crusts from the heat. 5. Brush each crust lightly with sauce. Top with herbs, meats, vegetables, and cheese. Grill, covered, about 5 minutes, until the cheese melts, the bottom is crisp, and the pizza looks done. Tired of grilling the same ol' stuff? Try these delicious pizzas for a great change of pace! This awesome dough recipe comes from a wonderful lady, Pam, on an AOL cooking board I frequent. I can't rave enough about it! Yield: 4 individual pizzas Carb level: High-carb (wheat pizza dough; sauce and toppings are secondary) Butter replaces margarine in the dough. Olive oil is already the right fat for brushing and the grate. No seed oils. Wheat flour stays primary. This is structural yeast dough; a full almond-flour swap will not stretch, blister, or hold toppings on the grill. Sugar swap: Keep some real sugar. Yeast feeds on sucrose, and those few grams help the crust brown over the coals. Beer adds malt flavor and extra food for the yeast — flat beer is fine; you are not chasing carbonation. Grill the first side before saucing. A dry, set crust will not stick or go soggy when the toppings go on. Medium heat is the goal: too hot and the sugar and cheese burn before the crumb cooks. One loaf of frozen bread dough can stand in for extra convenience. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour is the best for this recipe because: the gluten network is what traps the yeast's gas and gives the rise and chew; almond and coconut flour have no gluten, so the dough cannot rise or stretch.

recipes.title: Almond Chicken Salad
recipes.how: For the salad: 4 cups cubed cooked chicken 1 can (11 ounces) mandarin oranges, drained 1-1/2 cups seedless green grapes, halved 1 cup chopped celery 1/2 cup minced onion 1/2 cup slivered almonds For the dressing: 3/4 cup avocado oil mayonnaise 1/4 cup sour cream 1 tsp. prepared mustard 1 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper 1/2 tsp. poppy seeds 1/8 tsp. paprika 1. In a large bowl, combine the chicken, oranges, grapes, celery, and onion. 2. In another bowl, whisk the avocado oil mayonnaise, sour cream, mustard, salt, pepper, poppy seeds, and paprika until creamy. 3. Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture and toss gently. Stir in the almonds. Serve immediately, or refrigerate just until serving. 4. Serve over large lettuce leaves if desired. It also makes a great pita stuffing. This is a very tasty salad to serve and perfect for guests (especially a ladies' luncheon or tea)! Yield: 6 to 8 servings Carb level: Moderate-carb (fruit and a little dressing sugar; the chicken, almonds, and mayo are protein and fat) Avocado oil mayonnaise replaces regular mayo so the dressing is seed-oil-free. Sour cream adds lactic tang and body so the dressing clings instead of sliding off the chicken. Drain the mandarin oranges well. Extra syrup thins the emulsion and makes the salad watery by the time guests sit down. Add the almonds last, just before serving, so they stay crisp. Poppy seeds and paprika are more than garnish — the seeds add a faint nuttiness and the paprika a little color and warmth. This is a meal salad (chicken is the main). Pile it on lettuce for a plate, or stuff a pita if you want it handheld. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb.

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Kebabs
recipes.how: For the glaze: 3 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tbsp. sugar (in place of 1/4 cup sugar) 1 tbsp. cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 3/4 cup cranberry juice 2 tbsp. cider vinegar 2 tsp. soy sauce For the kebabs: 1 pound kielbasa or smoked sausage, cut into 1-1/2-inch chunks 1 red pepper, cut into squares 2 medium red cooking apples, cut into 8 wedges each 1. Prepare the grill for barbecuing. 2. In a small saucepan, combine the sugar and cornstarch. Stir in the cranberry juice, vinegar, and soy sauce. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens; boil 1 minute. Remove from heat. 3. On long metal skewers, thread the kielbasa, red pepper, and apples. 4. Grill the skewers 6 inches above low-heat coals until the sausage is lightly browned. Brush with glaze, turning occasionally. Serve the kebabs with leftover glaze. I first made these tangy, grilled kebabs this past summer and what a hit they instantly became. We all enjoyed the wonderful glaze on the kielbasa, red peppers and apples...well, Don didn't like the apples, but the rest of us did (they must be too healthy for him)! Carb level: Moderate-carb (sugar glaze plus apples; kielbasa and peppers are low) Kielbasa is already cooked, so you are heating and glazing, not cooking raw meat through. Low coals keep the apples from scorching before the sausage browns. Cornstarch needs a full 1-minute boil to set. Stir constantly so the cranberry juice does not scorch. The gloss on the kebabs is that starch gel plus a little leftover sugar. Sugar swap: Keep some real sugar. Those few grams help the glaze caramelize on the grill; monk fruit alone will thicken but will not brown the same way. Red cooking apples (Rome, Jonathan, or Cortland) hold their shape. Eating apples turn to mush over the coals. Skip the apples if you are cooking for Don, and add extra pepper. If you use wooden skewers, soak them 30 minutes so they do not burn. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb.

recipes.title: Oriental Chicken Salad
recipes.how: For the salad: 1 package (3 ounces) chicken-flavor Top Ramen 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cooked and cubed 1/2 head lettuce, shredded 2 green onions, thinly sliced, green tops included 2 tbsp. toasted sesame seeds 1/4 cup slivered almonds, toasted For the dressing: 2 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend (in place of 2 tbsp. sugar) 2 tbsp. vinegar 1/2 tbsp. sherry 1/2 tbsp. soy sauce 1/4 tsp. pepper 1/8 tsp. salt 2-1/2 tbsp. avocado oil (in place of vegetable oil) 1. Cook the Top Ramen according to package directions; drain and set aside to cool. (Save the seasoning packet for another use, or whisk a pinch into the dressing if you want extra chicken-soup savor.) 2. In a large bowl, combine the chicken, lettuce, onions, sesame seeds, almonds, and cooled noodles. 3. In a small saucepan, combine the sugar, vinegar, sherry, soy sauce, pepper, and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer until the sugar is dissolved, about 5 minutes. Cool. 4. When the dressing is cool, whisk in the avocado oil. Pour over the salad and toss well. Chill, or serve immediately. Don's Aunt Judy made this delicious salad for a family gathering several years ago. I just had to have the recipe. The scrumptious dressing has Oriental flair with a slightly sweet hue. I have cut the recipe in half to suit our family's needs, which can easily be doubled again. Carb level: Moderate-carb (ramen noodles and dressing sugar); chicken, lettuce, and nuts are low Avocado oil replaces the generic oil. It goes in after the dressing cools so the emulsion stays smooth. No seed oils. Sugar swap: Boiling the sugar with the vinegar and soy dissolves the crystals and slightly reduces the dressing so it clings. Monk fruit can replace the 2 tbsp. sugar here — you are sweetening a cold vinaigrette, not baking — but simmer just until blended. Toasting the almonds (and the sesame seeds) wakes up their oils. Raw nuts taste flat next to the warm dressing spices. Cooked, cooled ramen is Aunt Judy’s version — softer, more of a pasta salad. For crunch, break the raw noodles and toss them in just before serving instead. Double the recipe for a crowd; this write-up is already the family half-batch. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this salad. Monk fruit sweetens the dressing just as well, so the bigger change is cutting the ramen, which takes away the noodle body and crunch that make Aunt Judy's salad.

recipes.title: Beef Rice-A-Roni
recipes.how: 2 tbsp. butter 1/2 cup spaghetti, broken into 3/4-inch pieces 1/2 cup long grain rice 2 cups beef broth 1/2 envelope Lipton Golden Onion Soup Mix 1 tbsp. dried parsley 1/2 tsp. salt 1/8 tsp. pepper 1. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir in the spaghetti and rice and sauté until lightly browned. 2. Stir in the beef broth, onion soup mix, parsley, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. A similar recipe was posted on a cooking message board I frequent by a wonderful lady, Nancy, but I didn't have all of the ingredients on hand, so I modified it to suit my on-hand needs. This is fantastic. You'll never have to buy boxed Rice-A-Roni again. Carb level: High-carb (rice plus broken spaghetti) Butter replaces margarine. Toasting the pasta and rice in it is the whole boxed-mix trick: the noodles brown (Maillard), the rice gets a nutty coat, and the grains stay separate once the broth goes in. No seed oils. Keep the heat high enough to color the pasta, and stir so the butter does not burn. Pale rice tastes like plain steamed rice with onion powder; browned rice tastes like Rice-A-Roni. Half an envelope of Golden Onion Soup Mix is the seasoning base. If you are out, use 1 tbsp. dried onion flakes, a pinch of onion powder, and a little extra salt. Covered simmer, then leave it alone. Lifting the lid dumps steam and stretches the cook time. If the pot looks wet at 20 minutes, give it 5 minutes off the heat, still covered. Leftover roast beef or browned ground beef stirred in at the end makes this more of a plate than a side. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap rice for cauliflower rice.

recipes.title: Reuben Sandwiches
recipes.how: 8 slices rye or sourdough bread 3/4 pound sliced corned beef 1 can (14 ounces) sauerkraut, well drained 4 large slices Swiss cheese 1/2 cup Thousand Island dressing (homemade with avocado oil mayonnaise, or a seed-oil-free brand) Soft butter, for grilling 1. For each sandwich, spread 1 tablespoon dressing on one bread slice. Layer 1-1/2 ounces corned beef, about 1/4 cup sauerkraut, another 1-1/2 ounces corned beef, a slice of Swiss, another 1 tablespoon dressing, and the second bread slice. 2. Butter the outsides of the sandwich. Grill over medium heat until lightly browned on both sides and the cheese is melted. These are very tasty and hearty. They make a filling lunch or dinner paired with soup or salad, and are a great way to use up leftover corned beef! Yield: 4 sandwiches Carb level: Moderate-carb (rye or sourdough is the main source; corned beef, Swiss, and sauerkraut are low) Butter replaces margarine on the outside of the bread. That is what browns and crisps the crust (Maillard). No seed oils in the pan. Squeeze the sauerkraut dry. Water left in the kraut steams the bread and keeps the Swiss from melting into a sealed layer. Double-meat around the kraut (as written) keeps the filling from sliding and puts fat and salt on both sides of the acid. Shaved deli corned beef stacks more evenly than thick leftover slices if that is what you prefer. Thousand Island is a mayo dressing. Use avocado oil mayonnaise if you make it, or a brand without seed oils. The dressing’s sugar and pickle relish are the sweet-sour foil for the corned beef. Medium heat only. Too hot and the rye scorches before the cheese melts. Cover the skillet for a minute if the Swiss needs help. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb.

recipes.title: Homemade Pizza
recipes.how: For the crust: 1 cup flat beer or water (use the beer!) 2 tbsp. butter 1 tbsp. + 2 tsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tsp. sugar (in place of 2 tbsp. sugar) 1 tsp. salt 2-1/2 cups all-purpose flour 1 package active dry yeast (2-1/4 tsp.) Cornmeal, for the pan Olive oil, for brushing For the sauce: 1 can (15 ounces) tomato puree 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1/4 tsp. garlic powder 1/4 tsp. dried basil 1/4 tsp. dried oregano 1/4 tsp. ground thyme For the toppings: 2 cups shredded pizza cheese (mixture of mozzarella and Cheddar) Desired toppings: pepperoni, ham, sausage, peppers, onions, mushrooms, pineapple, Parmesan cheese, red pepper flakes, etc. 1. For the crust, use a bread machine set on the dough setting, adding the ingredients to the pan in the order listed. Or, dissolve the yeast in warm beer (105°F to 115°F). Add the butter, sugar, salt, and flour. Mix until the dough forms a ball and cleans the sides of the bowl. Turn onto a floured surface and knead for 2 minutes. Place in a greased bowl, turning to grease the top. Cover; let rise in a warm place, free from draft, until doubled in bulk, about 1 hour. Punch down the dough. 2. For the sauce, combine all sauce ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat. When the sauce begins to bubble, reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring often. Remove the sauce from the heat and let cool until ready to use on the pizza. Store leftover sauce in the refrigerator. 3. Sprinkle a 14-inch pizza pan with cornmeal. Turn the dough out on a floured surface. Roll or press into the prepared pan, forming a collar around the edge. Brush lightly with olive oil. Cover the dough; let stand 15 minutes. 4. Spread sauce on the dough. Sprinkle three-quarters of the cheeses evenly over the top. Add the desired toppings. Sprinkle the remaining cheeses over the top. 5. Bake at 400°F for 25 minutes or until done and the crust is crispy on the outside. If there was one food I could not give up, I think pizza would have to be it. I LOVE homemade pizza! This crust recipe comes from a fabulous lady, Pam, on a cooking board I frequent and is by far the absolute best crust recipe ever. Thank you for letting me share this fabulous recipe with the cyber world, Pam! Yield: 1 (14-inch) pizza (about 8 slices) Carb level: High-carb (yeast wheat crust; sauce is moderate-low) Wheat flour stays primary. This is a real pizza crust; a full almond-flour swap will not stretch, rise, or crisp the same way. Use the beer. Flat beer feeds the yeast, adds malt flavor, and the leftover carbonation helps the dough stay light. Warm it only to 105°F–115°F so you do not kill the yeast. Butter in the dough and olive oil on the shaped crust are the fats. No seed oils. The oil keeps the surface from drying during the 15-minute rest and helps the edge brown. Sugar swap: Keep a little real sugar. Yeast uses some of it, and those few grams help the crust color. Cornmeal on the pan is not garnish — it acts like tiny ball bearings so the crust does not glue itself down and the bottom can dry and crisp at 400°F. A 30-minute simmer is the whole sauce. Water cooks off, acidity mellows, and the dried herbs rehydrate. Cool the sauce before spreading so it does not start melting the cheese in the bowl. Useful tip: Or try Honey Wheat Pizza Dough. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour is the best for this recipe because: the gluten network is what traps the yeast's gas and gives the rise and chew; almond and coconut flour have no gluten, so the dough cannot rise or stretch.

recipes.title: Chinese Roast Pork Buns
recipes.how: For the pork: 3 tbsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 1/4 cup firmly packed brown sugar) 1/4 cup ketchup 2 tbsp. soy sauce 2 tbsp. hoisin sauce 1 tbsp. water 1 garlic clove, minced 1-1/2 lbs. pork chops (1/2 inch thick) For the filling: 1 tbsp. cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 tbsp. water 1 tbsp. avocado oil 1/2 cup chopped onion 1/2 cup chopped water chestnuts 1 tbsp. soy sauce 1 tbsp. hoisin sauce 2 tbsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 3 tbsp. brown sugar) 1/2 cup chicken broth For the buns: 1 can (17.3 ounces) Pillsbury Grands refrigerated biscuits (not butter flavor) For the glaze: 1 tsp. sugar 1 tsp. water 1 egg white 1. Heat the oven to 375°F. Line a broiler pan with foil. 2. In a blender or food processor, combine 1/4 cup brown sugar, ketchup, 2 tbsp. soy sauce, 2 tbsp. hoisin sauce, 1 tbsp. water, and garlic; blend until smooth. Generously brush both sides of the pork chops, reserving the remaining basting sauce. Place the pork on the foil-lined broiler pan. 3. Bake for 30 minutes. Remove the pork from the oven. Brush both sides with the remaining basting sauce. Bake an additional 10 to 20 minutes or until tender. Remove from the oven; cool. Remove the meat from the bone; finely chop. Set aside. 4. In a small bowl, combine the cornstarch and 1 tbsp. water; blend well. Heat the avocado oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add the onion and water chestnuts; cook and stir 2 to 3 minutes or until the onion begins to brown. Add 1 tbsp. soy sauce, 1 tbsp. hoisin sauce, and 3 tbsp. brown sugar; stir to coat. Add the chicken broth. Stir in the cornstarch mixture; cook and stir until the mixture begins to thicken. Remove from the heat; stir in the pork. 5. Separate the dough into 8 biscuits. On a lightly floured surface, press or roll each biscuit into a 5-inch circle. Place about 1/3 cup pork mixture in the center of each biscuit. Gathering up the edges, twist and pinch to seal. Place, seam side down, on an ungreased baking sheet. In a small bowl, beat the glaze ingredients until well blended; brush over the buns. 6. Bake at 375°F for 14 to 18 minutes or until golden brown. These are absolutely delicious! Very filling when paired with a stir-fry or fried rice. Yield: 8 buns Carb level: High-carb (refrigerated biscuit dough + sugary hoisin filling) Avocado oil is the stir-fry fat. No seed oils. High heat on the onion and water chestnuts is what gives the filling a little wok browning before the sauce goes in. The cornstarch slurry is what keeps the buns from leaking. A loose, brothy filling will blow out the seal in the oven; cook until it thickens and clings to the pork. Sugar swap: Keep some real brown sugar. Hoisin and ketchup already bring sugar; the extra brown sugar is for gloss and caramel notes on the roasted pork. Wheat biscuit dough stays. These are bao-style stuffed biscuits, not almond-flour pastries. A full flour swap will not puff or seal the same way. Twist and pinch firmly, then bake seam side down. The egg-white glaze is a thin protein wash — it browns and shines without making the tops greasy. Cool the roasted pork before chopping so the juices stay in the meat instead of watering down the filling. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: New England Style Clam Chowder
recipes.how: For the vegetables: 2 tbsp. butter 1 cup chopped onion 1/2 cup chopped leeks 1/2 cup chopped celery 3 cups diced, peeled potatoes 2 cans (6-1/2 ounces each) minced clams, drained and juice reserved 1 cup clam juice 1 cup water 1-1/2 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper 1/2 tsp. dried thyme For the cream base: 1/2 cup butter 1/2 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 tsp. monk fruit baking blend (in place of 1 tsp. sugar) 2 cups half-and-half 2 cups milk 2 slices bacon, crisply cooked and crumbled 2 tbsp. finely chopped fresh parsley Salt and pepper to taste For serving: Oyster crackers 1. Melt 2 tbsp. butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the onion, leeks, and celery; sauté until the vegetables begin to soften. Stir in the potatoes, reserved clam juice, 1 cup clam juice, water, salt, pepper, and thyme. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat; simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes. 2. Meanwhile, melt 1/2 cup butter in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Whisk in the flour and sugar and cook and stir for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the half-and-half and milk; cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and begins to boil. 3. Add the milk mixture to the vegetables. Stir in the clams and bacon. Heat through over medium-low heat; do not boil. 4. Stir in the parsley and salt and pepper to taste. Serve topped with oyster crackers. This is a rich and hearty chowder, one of Don’s favorites! Don’t let the long list of ingredients scare you…this is easy and not too time consuming. Carb level: High-carb (potatoes + flour roux + oyster crackers) Butter is the sauté fat and the roux fat. No seed oils. The first 2 tablespoons soften the onion, leek, and celery; the 1/2 cup builds a blond roux that thickens the dairy. Two pots is the point. Potatoes cook in clam juice so they taste like the ocean; the roux cooks the raw-flour taste out of the cream so the finished chowder is silky, not pasty. Do not boil after the clams go in. A hard boil can break the dairy and turn the clams rubbery. Medium-low just to heat through is enough. Wheat flour stays in the roux. A full almond-flour swap will thicken less glossily; if you want a lower-carb bowl, keep the roux and swap cauliflower for some of the potatoes, and skip the crackers. Sugar swap: The teaspoon of sugar (or a pinch of monk fruit) is not dessert — it rounds the clam brine the way a pinch of sugar rounds tomato sauce. Bacon is a finish, not the cooking fat. Crumble it in at the end so it stays smoky instead of dissolving into the pot. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Turkey Tetrazzini
recipes.how: 1 package (7 ounces) spaghetti 2 cups turkey or chicken broth 2 cups half-and-half or milk 1/2 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1/4 cup butter 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1 tsp. chicken bouillon granules 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, divided 2 cups cooked, cubed turkey 3/4 cup frozen peas and carrots 1/4 cup sliced almonds 1. Cook the spaghetti as directed on the package. Rinse with cold water and drain; set aside. 2. Preheat the oven to 350°F. 3. Mix the broth, half-and-half, flour, butter, salt, pepper, and chicken bouillon granules in a 3-quart saucepan. Heat to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly. Boil and stir 1 minute. Stir in the Parmesan cheese and 1/2 cup Cheddar cheese. 4. Stir in the spaghetti, turkey, peas and carrots, and almonds. Spread in an ungreased 2-quart casserole dish. Sprinkle with the remaining Cheddar cheese. 5. Bake, uncovered, 25 to 30 minutes or until hot and bubbly. A real “turkey” of a homemade treat! This is fabulous! Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: High-carb (spaghetti + flour-thickened sauce) Butter is the sauce fat. Combined with flour it makes a quick roux right in the pot with the broth and dairy. No seed oils. Wheat spaghetti stays primary. This is tetrazzini — leftover turkey bound in a cheese sauce on pasta. A full almond-flour or zucchini-noodle swap will not give you the same bake. For a lower-carb casserole, use half the pasta and extra turkey, or fold the same sauce through cauliflower florets. Stir constantly until the sauce boils for a full minute. That cooks the raw-flour taste out and lets the starch gel so the casserole slices instead of running. Rinse the spaghetti. You want the noodles cool and separate so they do not keep cooking in the sauce before the pan even hits the oven. Half-and-half makes a richer sauce than milk; either works. Do not use a higher heat than medium or the dairy can scorch. The almonds toast in the oven and keep a little crunch against the creamy pasta. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Chicken Noodle Stir Fry
recipes.how: 1 package (3 ounces) chicken-flavored ramen noodles* 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into strips 1 tbsp. avocado oil 1 cup broccoli florets 1 cup cauliflower florets 1 cup sliced celery 1 cup coarsely chopped cabbage 2 medium carrots, thinly sliced 1 medium onion, cut into thin wedges 1/2 cup fresh or canned bean sprouts 1/2 cup teriyaki sauce, divided 1/4 cup cashews or peanuts 1. Cook the noodles according to package directions; discard the seasoning packet or reserve for another use. 2. Meanwhile, in a large skillet or wok, stir-fry the chicken in hot oil for 5 to 6 minutes, or until no longer pink. Stir in 2 tbsp. teriyaki sauce during the last couple of minutes to glaze the chicken. Add the vegetables; stir-fry 4 to 6 minutes, or until crisp-tender. 3. Drain the noodles; add to the chicken and vegetables with the remaining teriyaki sauce and the cashews. Stir well. Serve immediately. Not only fast and easy, but so delicious. You can use frozen vegetables for extra convenience, too. Don't forget the chopsticks! Carb level: High-carb (ramen noodles plus teriyaki sauce) Avocado oil replaces the unnamed frying fat. It handles wok heat and stays seed-oil-free. No vegetable oil. Discard the ramen seasoning packet. It is mostly salt; the teriyaki is the sauce. Glaze the chicken with 2 tbsp. teriyaki near the end of its cook so the sugars caramelize on the meat (Maillard) instead of steaming under the vegetables. High heat, constant motion, crisp-tender vegetables. If the pan crowds, cook the vegetables in two batches so they sear instead of stew. Cashews or peanuts go in last so they stay crunchy. *Useful tip: This is also good served over hot, cooked rice. Simply omit the ramen noodles and serve the chicken-and-vegetable stir-fry over a bed of steamed rice. For a lower-carb plate, use cauliflower rice or skip the starch and pile the stir-fry into bowls. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Sausage and Potato Skillet
recipes.how: 1 tbsp. butter or avocado oil 4 large potatoes, peeled and cubed 1 pound smoked kielbasa, cut into small chunks 1 medium onion, chopped 1 can (7 ounces) mushroom pieces and stems, drained 1 tbsp. chopped fresh parsley Salt and pepper to taste 1. Heat the butter or avocado oil in a large skillet (cast iron if you have it) over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes, kielbasa, onion, mushrooms, parsley, salt, and pepper. 2. Cook, stirring frequently, until the potatoes are tender. Re-season with salt and pepper as needed. I came up with this one evening while camping, and it was a huge success. Beat our normal camping fare of hot dogs and hamburgers, and required very little work. This is an excellent way to put your cast iron skillet to use, at the campsite or at home! Carb level: High-carb (potatoes are the starch; kielbasa is fat and protein) Butter or avocado oil replaces nonstick spray so the skillet is seed-oil-free. You need that fat for the potatoes to brown instead of glue themselves to the pan. Smoked kielbasa is already cooked. The potatoes are the clock — cubes need 15 to 20 minutes over medium-high heat to go tender and pick up color. Stir often enough that they do not scorch, but not so often that they never sit and brown (Maillard). Cast iron holds heat, which is why this works on a camp stove as well as a home burner. If the pan crowds, the potatoes steam; give them room or cook in two batches and combine at the end. Drain the canned mushrooms well. Extra liquid cools the skillet and keeps the potatoes pale. No wheat in this one. For a lower-carb skillet, swap half or all of the potatoes for cauliflower florets and shorten the cook. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Italian Grilled Cheese Sandwiches
recipes.how: 4 slices French bread (1-inch thick) 4 slices mozzarella or provolone cheese 1/4 cup marinara or pizza sauce 3 eggs 1/2 cup milk 3/4 tsp. Italian seasoning 1/2 tsp. garlic powder 2/3 cup Italian-seasoned bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 2/3 cup crushed pork rinds) Butter, for the griddle 1. Cut a 3-inch pocket in each slice of bread. Place a slice of cheese in each pocket. Spoon 1 tbsp. sauce into each pocket. 2. In a bowl, beat the eggs, milk, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder. Soak the bread for 2 minutes on each side. Coat with the bread crumbs. 3. Heat a griddle over medium heat and grease with butter. Cook until golden brown on both sides. This little beauty originally came from Taste of Home magazine, but I have modified it a tad to suit our taste. This makes the perfect accompaniment to a bowl of soup! Carb level: High-carb (French bread, bread crumbs, and a spoon of sauce) Butter on the griddle. No seed-oil spray. The egg-milk soak is a French-toast batter; butter is what fries the crumb crust gold. Wheat stays primary — this is stuffed French bread with a bread-crumb shell. An almond-flour crumb will not cling or crisp the same way. Two minutes per side is long enough for the custard to wet the crumb without turning the slice to mush. Press the pocket closed so the cheese and sauce stay inside when you flip. Medium heat, not ripping hot. The bread crumbs brown fast; the cheese in the pocket needs time to melt before the outside scorches. Useful tip: Try a variety of cheeses in these delicious sandwiches. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.) Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this sandwich. Pork rinds fry up richer than bread crumbs and almond-flour bread is more fragile, so you lose the classic toasty crumb shell and the sandwich is harder to flip in one piece.

recipes.title: Tomato-Basil Pizza
recipes.how: 1 (12-inch) thin-crust uncooked pizza dough 1/2 tsp. garlic salt 1-1/2 tbsp. butter, melted 1-1/2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese 2 tbsp. coarsely chopped fresh basil 2 small Roma tomatoes, chopped 1 tsp. olive oil 2 tbsp. grated fresh Parmesan cheese 1. Preheat the oven to 475°F. 2. Roll out the dough to a 12-inch diameter, 1/8-inch thick (you want a very thin crust, almost like a flour tortilla). Place on an ungreased pizza pan or cookie sheet. 3. Mix the garlic salt with the melted butter. Use a pastry brush to coat the entire crust with garlic butter. 4. Sprinkle the mozzarella over the crust. Toss the basil and tomato with the olive oil. Sprinkle over the cheese. 5. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, or until the cheese melts and the tomatoes are slightly soft. 6. Remove the pizza from the oven and sprinkle the fresh Parmesan over it. Slice into 8 pieces and serve warm. This is a marvelous summertime dinner choice when basil and tomatoes are abundant in your garden! Carb level: High-carb (wheat pizza crust; toppings are moderate-low) Wheat flour stays primary. This is a real thin pizza crust; a full almond-flour swap will not stretch, crisp, or bake in 8 to 10 minutes at 475°F. Homemade Pizza dough from the box works if you roll it very thin. Butter on the crust and a teaspoon of olive oil on the tomatoes are the fats. No seed oils. The garlic butter takes the place of a cooked red sauce so the crust can stay cracker-thin and still taste seasoned. 475°F is the point. A 1/8-inch crust needs blast heat so the bottom dries and the cheese melts before the tomatoes waterlog the dough. Do not pile on extra tomato. Tossing chopped Roma tomatoes and basil with olive oil is just enough fat to keep the basil from scorching and to help the tomatoes slump. Romas are meatier and less watery than a slicing tomato. Parmesan goes on after the bake so it stays nutty instead of disappearing into the mozzarella. Slice into 8 and eat while the crust is still crisp. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.)

recipes.title: Sausage Gravy over Biscuits
recipes.how: For the gravy: 1 pound pork sausage 4 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 3 cups milk 1/4 tsp. pepper 1/8 tsp. salt 6 biscuits (recipe below) For the biscuits: 1 cup flour (lower-carb option: 3/4 cup + 2 tbsp. blanched almond flour + 1 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 1-1/2 tsp. baking powder 1-1/2 tsp. monk fruit baking blend (in place of 1-1/2 tsp. sugar) 1/4 tsp. cream of tartar 1/8 tsp. salt 1/4 cup butter 1/3 cup milk or buttermilk 1. Preheat the oven to 450°F. For the biscuits, stir together the flour, baking powder, sweetener, cream of tartar, and salt. Cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Make a well and stir in the milk. Knead on a floured surface a few times. Roll or pat the dough to 1/2-inch thickness. Cut with a 2-1/2-inch cutter. Transfer to an ungreased baking sheet. Bake 10 to 12 minutes. 2. Slice the pork sausage into 1/2-inch thick slices and cook in a hot skillet until done. Drain off all but 2 tbsp. fat. Crumble half of the sausage into tiny pieces. 3. Whisk the flour into the fat in the skillet until well blended, cooking 1 minute. Gradually add the milk; bring to a boil over medium heat. Boil for 2 minutes, stirring constantly; reduce heat to low. Add pepper, salt, and the crumbled sausage; simmer, uncovered, for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally. 4. Serve the gravy on split biscuits with the remaining sausage slices on the side. This is a true Country comfort meal! Yield: 4 to 6 servings (6 biscuits) Carb level: High-carb (biscuits plus a flour-thickened milk gravy) Sausage fat is the cooking fat and the roux fat. Those 2 tablespoons left in the skillet are what thicken the milk. No seed oils, no margarine. Wheat flour stays primary in the biscuits and the gravy. This is a gluten dough that needs a short knead and a 2-1/2-inch cut, plus a blond roux. Almond flour will not rise into a biscuit or gel into sausage gravy. Baking powder plus cream of tartar is old-fashioned double-acting lift: the tartaric acid gives an extra burst of CO2 when the wet dough hits 450°F. Do not over-knead or you tighten the gluten and get hockey pucks. Cook the flour in the fat a full minute before the milk goes in. That cooks off the raw-flour taste so the gravy is peppery and silky, not pasty. Boil 2 minutes so the starch fully gels, then simmer with the crumbled sausage. Sugar swap: Keep the biscuit sugar tiny (or use monk fruit). A teaspoon and a half is just enough for browning, not dessert. Buttermilk in place of milk adds acid that helps the cream of tartar and baking powder. Slice half the sausage and crumble the rest. You get gravy meat plus a side of browned patties — that is the country-breakfast plate. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Tomato-Basil Tortellini
recipes.how: 1 package (16 ounces) cheese-filled tortellini* 1 small onion, finely diced 1 clove garlic, minced 1 tbsp. olive oil 1 can (28 ounces) crushed tomatoes, undrained 1 plum tomato, chopped 5 tbsp. tomato paste 3 tbsp. chopped fresh basil leaves 1/4 tsp. Italian seasoning Dash pepper 1. Sauté the onion and garlic in hot olive oil in a small saucepan until the onions become soft. Stir in the undrained crushed tomatoes, plum tomato, tomato paste, basil, Italian seasoning, and pepper. Simmer over low heat for 45 minutes. 2. Cook the tortellini according to package directions; drain. Toss with the sauce and serve immediately. This makes a great pasta (and vegetarian) alternative! Very filling and delicious. Carb level: High-carb (cheese tortellini is the base) Olive oil is the sauté fat. It softens the onion and garlic and carries the tomato. No seed oils. Wheat tortellini stays primary. This is a pasta supper; zucchini “tortellini” will shed water and thin the sauce. For a lower-carb bowl, use half the pasta and extra sauce, or spoon the same tomato-basil over roasted vegetables. Forty-five minutes on low is the point. Tomato paste starts sharp and metallic; a long simmer cooks out that raw taste, concentrates the crushed tomatoes, and lets the fresh plum tomato melt in. Fresh basil can fade in a long simmer. Stir most of it in as written, then tear a little extra over the plates if you want a brighter finish. *Useful tip: I use 2 (9 ounces each) packages of fresh DiGiorno Mozzarella Garlic tortellini. You can use frozen or dry tortellini if desired. Do not rinse — starch on the pasta helps the sauce cling. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Ham and Cheese Bow Ties
recipes.how: 2 cups (8 ounces) uncooked bow tie pasta 1/4 cup butter (in place of margarine) 1 clove garlic, minced 1/4 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1/2 tsp. salt 1/8 tsp. pepper 2 cups milk 1/2 tsp. prepared mustard 2-1/2 cups shredded Colby cheese 4 ounces sliced cooked ham, cut into strips 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1. Heat oven to 350°F. Cook and drain the pasta as directed on the package. 2. While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in a 3-quart saucepan over low heat. Sauté the garlic in the butter for 30 seconds. Whisk in the flour, salt, and pepper. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture is smooth and bubbly. Gradually stir in the milk. Heat to a boil, stirring constantly. Boil and stir for 1 minute. Stir in the mustard and Colby cheese. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the cheese is melted. Stir the pasta and ham into the cheese sauce. 3. Pour into an ungreased 2-quart baking dish. Sprinkle with the Parmesan. Bake uncovered 20 to 25 minutes, or until bubbly. This is like homemade macaroni and cheese but with the fun bow tie pasta and hearty ham. Serve this with a steamed vegetable and Waldorf Salad for a delicious and quick dinner. There usually aren't any leftovers when I serve this! Carb level: High-carb (bow ties plus a flour-thickened cheese sauce) Butter replaces margarine. Margarine is a seed-oil spread; butter is the roux fat and carries the garlic and Colby. No seed oils. Wheat bow ties stay primary. This is baked mac and cheese with ham. A full almond-flour or zucchini-noodle swap will not bake the same. For a lower-carb casserole, use half the pasta and extra ham and cheese. Garlic only gets 30 seconds in the butter. Longer and it burns before the flour goes in. Then cook the roux until smooth and bubbly, add the milk, and boil 1 minute so the starch gels and the raw-flour taste is gone. Mustard is not a condiment here — a half teaspoon brightens the Colby the way it does in a classic Mornay. Parmesan on top browns in the oven (milk solids) so you get a savory crust over the creamy pasta. Do not rinse the pasta. Starch on the noodles helps the sauce cling. There usually aren't leftovers. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.how: 1 small fryer chicken, cut up (about 2 pounds) 1 small onion, finely diced 1/2 cup diced carrots 2 stalks celery, sliced (leaves included) 3 garlic cloves, minced 3 chicken bouillon cubes 1 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper 8 cups water 1/2 cup sliced fresh mushrooms 2 tbsp. chopped fresh parsley 1-1/2 cups uncooked egg noodles 1. In a large saucepan or Dutch oven, combine the chicken, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, bouillon cubes, salt, pepper, and water. Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer for one hour, stirring occasionally. 2. Remove the chicken from the soup and allow to cool enough to handle. Remove the meat; discard the skin and bones. Dice the meat into small pieces. 3. Return the meat to the soup. Add the mushrooms and parsley, and re-season with salt and pepper if desired. Bring the soup back to a boil. Stir in the noodles and cook over medium-high heat for 20 minutes, or until the noodles are tender, stirring occasionally. Just like Mom makes...soothing and satisfying homemade Chicken Noodle Soup. Show your family just how much you love them by serving them this delicious, hearty soup for dinner one night soon. Carb level: High-carb (egg noodles; the broth itself is low) No added frying fat and no seed oils. The chicken simmers in water and its own juices; any fat that rises is from the bird. Wheat egg noodles stay primary. This is chicken noodle soup. Zucchini ribbons will go limp in a 20-minute boil. For a lower-carb bowl, use half the noodles and extra chicken and vegetables, or skip the pasta and add more celery and mushrooms. The hour simmer is the broth. Bones, skin, and meat give you gelatin and flavor the bouillon cubes cannot make alone. Pull the chicken, strip it, and send only the meat back so the bowl is not full of bones. Noodles go in at the end, after the meat is back. They cook in the finished broth so they taste like soup, not water. Twenty minutes is right for sturdy egg noodles; thinner ones will need less. Do not add them at the start or they turn to mush. Celery leaves and parsley are the fresh finish. Mushrooms go in with the meat so they stay tender, not gray from a full hour in the pot. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: BLT Wraps
recipes.how: 6 cups lettuce leaves, coarsely chopped 1 large tomato, diced Avocado oil mayonnaise, for spreading (in place of regular mayonnaise) 8 large flour tortillas 1 pound bacon, cooked and crumbled 1 small avocado, diced (optional) 1. Combine the lettuce and tomato; toss to mix together. 2. Lightly spread avocado oil mayonnaise on the flour tortillas. Top with the lettuce mixture. Sprinkle the bacon over the top (and the avocado, if using) and roll up. A simple yet delicious recipe which complements a bowl of soup or salad nicely. Yield: 8 wraps Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas). Lettuce, tomato, bacon, and mayo are low. Avocado oil mayonnaise replaces regular mayo so the spread is seed-oil-free. A thin smear is a moisture barrier — it keeps tomato juice from turning the tortilla soggy. Wheat flour tortillas stay primary. That is the wrap. For a lower-carb lunch, use the same filling in large lettuce leaves, or choose a low-carb wheat-style tortilla; do not swap the whole meal to almond-flour wraps if you want this to taste like a BLT. Crisp the bacon first and crumble it so every bite gets smoky crunch. Soft bacon disappears into the lettuce. *Useful tip: Add a small, diced avocado for a delightful "California" twist. Roll tight and serve soon; leftover wraps wilt as the tomato weeps. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Tortilla Club Wrap
recipes.how: 1/3 cup avocado oil mayonnaise (in place of regular mayonnaise) 2 tbsp. mustard* 1 tsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 1 tsp. honey (in place of 2 tsp. honey) 6 large flour tortillas 6 ounces fully cooked ham 6 ounces fully cooked turkey 6 slices bacon, crisply cooked and crumbled 6 slices cheese (Swiss, Cheddar, American, or Provolone) 1 cup shredded lettuce 1 tomato, chopped (optional) 1/2 cup alfalfa sprouts 1. Combine the mayonnaise, mustard, and honey; spread over the tortillas. 2. Layer with the ham, turkey, bacon, cheese, lettuce, tomato (if using), and sprouts. Roll up and cut in half. This is a delightful change of pace from the traditional club sandwich; one you'll win raves over! These keep nicely in a lunch box, too. Yield: 6 wraps Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas plus a little honey). Monk fruit in the spread drops the sugar; the tortillas are still the carb. Avocado oil mayonnaise replaces regular mayo so the spread is seed-oil-free. Honey and mustard turn it into a sweet-sharp club sauce. Wheat flour tortillas stay primary. This is a club sandwich in a wrap. For a lower-carb lunch, use the same filling on lettuce leaves or a low-carb wheat-style tortilla. Sugar swap: Keep at least a teaspoon of real honey. Honey is the body of the sauce; all-monk-fruit mustard-mayo tastes thin. Two teaspoons in six wraps is already a light sweetening. Crisp bacon and a tight roll are what make it travel. These keep nicely in a lunch box; wrap each one so the tomato does not weep into the tortilla. *Useful tip: Try Dijon mustard for an equally delicious blend (or half and half). Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Breakfast English Muffins
recipes.how: 4 toasted English muffins (8 halves) 1 package (3 ounces) cream cheese, softened 2 tbsp. peanut butter 2 tbsp. sliced almonds 2 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 2 tbsp. honey (in place of 1/4 cup honey) 1. Combine the cream cheese and peanut butter. Spread onto the toasted English muffin halves. 2. Sprinkle on the almonds; drizzle honey over the top. An extraordinary breakfast treat! Carb level: High-carb (English muffins plus honey). Mixing monk fruit into the cream cheese and using less honey drops the sugar; the muffins are still the carb. Cream cheese and peanut butter are the fat. No seed oils. Softened, they mash into a spread that sits on the nooks instead of soaking through. Wheat English muffins stay primary. Toast them first so the cut faces dry and brown (Maillard) and the spread does not turn them gummy. Almond-flour “muffins” will not give you the same fork-split texture. Sugar swap: Keep some real honey for the drizzle. Honey is the gloss and the flavor; monk fruit will not pour. If you want it less sweet, use 2 tablespoons of honey on top and stir 1–2 teaspoons monk fruit into the cream-cheese mixture. Sliced almonds go on before the honey so they stick. Serve right away while the muffins are still warm. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Maple Brown Sugar Oatmeal
recipes.how: 2 cups water 1-1/2 cups milk 2 cups quick oats 1/4 cup + 2 tbsp. golden monk fruit blend + 2 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 1/2 cup packed brown sugar) 1/4 cup maple syrup 1/8 tsp. ground cinnamon 1. Bring the water and milk to a boil in a medium saucepan. Stir in the oats; cook 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally. 2. Remove from the heat and stir in the sweetener, maple syrup, and cinnamon. Here is an easy, warm breakfast you can make for your family in practically no time at all. Very yummy for us oatmeal lovers. Carb level: High-carb (oats + brown sugar + maple) No added oil here. Milk and water together give a creamy bowl without being as heavy as all milk, and they keep the oats from scorching the way water alone can. Quick oats are rolled thinner and cut smaller than old-fashioned, so they hydrate in 2 to 3 minutes. That extra surface area is why this is a weeknight breakfast instead of a 15-minute simmer. Old-fashioned oats work if you give them closer to 5 minutes. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar. The molasses is part of the maple-brown-sugar smell; monk fruit sweetens but does not perfume the pot the same way. Keep the maple syrup. Those few tablespoons are flavor and gloss, not just sweetness. If you want it less sweet, cut the brown sugar first and leave the maple. Stir after you take it off the heat. Residual heat finishes the oats and melts the sugar without turning the pot gluey. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Country Chicken Casserole
recipes.how: For the filling: 1/4 cup butter 1/3 cup flour (lower-carb option: 5/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. white pepper 2 cups half-and-half 2 tsp. chicken bouillon granules 2 cups cubed cooked chicken 1 package (1 pound) frozen mixed vegetables, thawed For the topping: 1 cup flour (lower-carb option: 3/4 cup + 2 tbsp. blanched almond flour + 1 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 1/4 tsp. baking powder 1/3 cup butter, softened 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1 egg 1. Heat the oven to 400°F. Melt 1/4 cup butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in 1/3 cup flour, salt, and pepper until smooth. Stir in the half-and-half and bouillon granules. Cook until thickened and the mixture comes to a boil, stirring constantly. Stir in the chicken and vegetables; cook until thoroughly heated. Pour the filling into an ungreased 2-quart casserole dish. 2. In a small bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, butter, cheese, and egg; mix with a fork or pastry blender until crumbly. Crumble the topping over the chicken mixture. 3. Bake at 400°F for 20 to 30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling bubbles around the edges. This is a comforting and filling casserole perfect for chicken leftovers. Carb level: High-carb (flour-thickened sauce + biscuit-style crumb topping) Butter is the fat in both the filling and the topping. Combined with flour it makes a quick roux; in the topping it fries the crumbs gold. No seed oils. Wheat flour stays primary. The 1/3 cup in the pot is the thickener (starch gels as it boils) and the cup on top is a pastry crumb. A full almond-flour swap will not set the sauce or crumble the same way. Stir the sauce constantly until it boils. That cooks the raw-flour taste out and lets the starch gel so the casserole slices instead of running. Thaw and drain the mixed vegetables first. Extra ice water thins the sauce you just thickened. The topping is a quick biscuit dough without milk — flour, butter, egg, Parmesan, and a pinch of baking powder. Mix only until crumbly so it bakes into a craggy lid instead of a paste. 400°F is hot on purpose so the top browns before the leftover chicken dries out. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: thicken with a little arrowroot slurry instead of flour/cornstarch; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Country Scramble Skillet
recipes.how: For the skillet: 8 eggs 1/4 cup milk 1/4 cup green pepper, finely diced 1/4 cup onion, finely chopped 1 cup frozen shredded hash browns, thawed and patted dry 1/4 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1 tbsp. butter 3/4 cup shredded Cheddar cheese 1 cup country gravy (recipe below) For the country gravy: 1 tbsp. butter 1 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 1/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 cup milk 1/2 tsp. beef bouillon granules 1/8 tsp. pepper Dash of salt 1. For the country gravy, melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour until well blended and cook 1 minute. Gradually add the milk; bring to a boil. Boil 1 minute, stirring constantly; reduce heat to medium-low. Add the bouillon, pepper, and salt; simmer 2 to 3 minutes, stirring occasionally. Keep warm. 2. For the skillet, beat the eggs and milk together in a large bowl. Stir in the onion, green pepper, hash browns, salt, and pepper. 3. Heat the butter in a large skillet. Pour in the egg mixture and cook over medium heat until the eggs are cooked through, stirring occasionally to scramble. Re-season with salt and pepper if desired. Stir in the cheese and heat until almost melted. 4. Top with the gravy. Serve immediately. I ate "this" at Denny's and picked at my food so I could try to re-create this dish at home. This is my version. It's soooo good!! Carb level: High-carb (hash browns plus a flour gravy); the eggs and cheese are low-carb Butter is the fat in both the skillet and the gravy. No seed oils. Pat the thawed hash browns very dry. Surface water steams the shreds instead of letting them fry in the butter, and wet potatoes make watery eggs. The gravy is a classic 1:1 butter-and-flour roux. Cooking it a full minute knocks out the raw-flour taste; boiling the milk 1 minute lets the starch gel so the gravy coats a spoon. Beef bouillon is the diner trick that makes a breakfast gravy taste like sawmill gravy without sausage drippings. Almond flour can stand in for the tablespoon of wheat in the gravy. It will thicken, but the sauce will be a little less glossy. Stir the cheddar in off a hard boil and stop when it is almost melted. Extra heat splits the cheese into oil and grainy protein. Have the gravy ready before you start the eggs. This is a plate that wants to be eaten hot. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Ham and Potatoes Au Gratin
recipes.how: For the casserole: 1/3 cup butter 1/4 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 2-1/2 cups milk 2 cups shredded Cheddar cheese 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. white pepper 6 cups sliced potatoes, cooked 1-1/2 cups cubed, cooked ham 1-1/2 cups small broccoli florets, cooked 1/4 cup chopped onion For the topping: 3 tbsp. butter, melted 1/2 cup cracker crumbs (lower-carb option: 1/2 cup crushed pork rinds) 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar cheese 1 tbsp. dried parsley 1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Butter a 2-quart casserole dish. 2. In a saucepan, melt the 1/3 cup butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour until smooth and cook 1 minute. Gradually add the milk; cook and stir until thickened and bubbly. Add the 2 cups cheese, salt, and white pepper; stir until the cheese melts. Remove from heat. 3. Divide the potatoes, ham, broccoli, and onion into thirds. In the prepared dish, layer one-third of the potatoes, ham, broccoli, and onion; pour on one-third of the cheese sauce. Repeat the layers two more times, ending with sauce. 4. Combine the topping ingredients and sprinkle over the casserole. 5. Bake at 350°F for 35 to 40 minutes, until hot and the topping is golden. This has been adapted to feed a family of six from a smaller recipe. This can be a great meatless meal without the ham. Carb level: High-carb (potatoes, a flour-thickened sauce, and cracker crumbs) Butter is the fat in the sauce and the topping. In the pan it makes a roux with the flour; on the crumbs it fries them into a crisp lid. No seed oils. The sauce is a cheddar Mornay. Cook the roux a full minute so the flour does not taste raw, then add the milk gradually and let it bubble before the cheese goes in. White pepper seasons without leaving black specks in a pale sauce. Potatoes and broccoli are already cooked, so 35 to 40 minutes is just to heat through and brown the top. Raw potatoes would need a longer covered bake and would thin the sauce as they give off water. Wheat flour in the roux can be almond flour if you want a slightly lower-carb sauce. The potatoes are still the starch of the dish. Leave the ham out for a meatless bake. Butter the dish, not a spray. The first potato layer picks up that fat and browns instead of sticking. Carb rating (Low): ~2g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Country Wine Chicken
recipes.how: 4 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts Salt and pepper 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) cream of mushroom soup, undiluted 1/4 cup dry white wine 1 small carrot, peeled, julienned and cut into 1/2-inch pieces 1/4 cup sliced mushrooms 1 tsp. dried parsley 1/8 tsp. pepper 1. Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Place in a crockpot. 2. Combine the soup, wine, carrots, mushrooms, parsley, and pepper. Pour over the chicken. 3. Cover and cook on low for 5 to 6 hours, stirring quickly a couple of times during cooking. Serve with cooked pasta, rice, or mashed potatoes. So simple yet tastes so elegant! Carb level: Moderate-low on its own (canned cream soup is the main starch); High-carb if you serve it over pasta, rice, or mashed potatoes No added oils in this pot. The soup and chicken supply the fat. No seed oils. Dry white wine is there for acid. It cuts the canned-soup richness and smells like a much fancier sauce after a long low cook. The alcohol cooks off over 5 to 6 hours. Chicken breasts on low for 5 to 6 hours is the window. Much longer and the lean meat dries and shreds. Thighs will stay juicier if you want a more forgiving pot. The canned cream of mushroom is the weeknight shortcut.
