For a from-scratch pot, sauté the mushrooms in 1 tbsp. butter, then whisk in 1 cup chicken broth and 1/2 cup heavy cream and simmer until it coats a spoon; use that in place of the soup. Stir only a couple of times, and quickly, so you do not dump the heat. The sauce should stay around the chicken, not get beaten into shreds. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki; swap rice for cauliflower rice; swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: French Toast Sticks
recipes.how: 4 eggs, beaten 1/3 cup milk 1 tsp. ground cinnamon 1/2 tsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1/2 tsp. brown sugar (in place of 1 tsp. brown sugar) 8 slices white bread Butter, for the griddle Powdered monk fruit, for serving (in place of maple syrup and/or confectioners' sugar) 1. Combine the beaten eggs, milk, cinnamon, and brown sugar; set aside. 2. Heat a griddle over medium heat and butter it well. 3. Cut each piece of bread into four strips. Dip the strips into the egg mixture, turning to coat both sides. 4. Cook on the hot buttered griddle until golden brown; turn and cook the second side. Sprinkle with confectioners' sugar and serve with syrup, if desired. Let the kids help you prepare these for a simple, delicious and fun breakfast. Carb level: High-carb (white bread, plus syrup or confectioners' sugar) Butter is the griddle fat. It browns the custard-soaked bread (Maillard) and keeps the sticks from sticking. No seed oils, no spray. Wheat bread stays primary. This is French toast — the crumb has to soak up egg and still hold a stick shape. A full almond-flour loaf will crumble in the dip. Day-old or slightly stale white bread soaks without falling apart; very fresh bread turns soggy. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar in the custard. Those molasses sugars help the sticks spot gold on the griddle. Do not soak the strips. A quick dip on both sides is enough. Sitting in the bowl makes the centers wet and the outsides pale. Medium heat is the window. Too hot and the sugar scorches before the egg sets; too cool and the sticks steam and never crisp. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Cream of Chicken Soup
recipes.how: 6 tbsp. butter 6 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 3/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1/2 cup milk 1/2 cup light cream or half-and-half 3 cups chicken broth 1 envelope Cup-a-Soup Cream of Chicken soup mix 1/4 tsp. white pepper Pinch of salt 1 cup cooked chicken, finely chopped 1/2 cup croutons, slightly crushed 1. In a saucepan, melt the butter. Blend in the flour; cook and stir for 1 minute. 2. Stir in the milk, cream, chicken broth, soup mix, pepper, and salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and comes to a boil. 3. Reduce the heat and stir in the chicken. Gently return the soup to a boil. 4. Top individual servings with croutons and serve immediately. Move over Campbell’s! If you like cream of chicken soup, you will love this. Carb level: Moderate-carb (butter-flour roux + soup mix + croutons); the chicken and dairy are the body Butter is the roux fat. Cook it with the flour for a full minute so the raw-flour taste cooks off and the starch swells before the liquid goes in. No seed oils. Wheat flour stays in the roux. That 6-tablespoon paste is what turns broth and cream into soup; almond flour will not thicken the same way. For a lighter bowl, keep the roux and skip the croutons. Stir constantly once the dairy is in. A blond roux plus cold milk and cream will lump if you walk away; constant heat gelatinizes the starch into a smooth, glossy base. The Cup-a-Soup packet is a flavor concentrate — extra chicken, onion, and a little starch. If you do not have it, use 1 tsp. chicken base or bouillon and a pinch more salt, and simmer a minute longer. Do not hard-boil after the chicken goes in. A gentle return to a simmer heats the meat without tightening it or breaking the cream. Useful tip: Swap the Cream of Chicken packet for Cup-a-Soup Chicken Noodle for a Cream of Chicken Noodle Soup. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb.

recipes.title: French Bread Pizza
recipes.how: For the sauce: 1 can (15 ounces) tomato puree 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 1/4 tsp. garlic powder 1/4 tsp. dried basil 1/4 tsp. dried oregano 1/4 tsp. ground thyme For the bread and toppings: 1 loaf (16 ounces) French bread, cut in half (or two 8-ounce loaves) 2 cups shredded pizza cheese (mixture of mozzarella and Cheddar) Desired toppings: pepperoni, ham, sausage, peppers, onions, mushrooms, pineapple, Parmesan cheese, red pepper flakes, etc. 1. For the sauce, combine all sauce ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat. When the sauce begins to bubble, reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring often. Remove from the heat and let cool until ready to use. Store leftover sauce in the refrigerator. 2. Heat the oven to 400°F. Place the French bread cut-side up on a large baking sheet and toast lightly. 3. Spread sauce on the toasted bread. Sprinkle three-quarters of the cheeses evenly over the top. Add the desired toppings. Sprinkle the remaining cheeses over the top. 4. Bake for 15 minutes or until the cheese is melted and the edges are golden. We are a pizza-lovin’ family, any which way — thick crust, thin crust, French bread, English muffin, bagel. Next to traditional homemade pizza, this is our favorite pizza variety! Carb level: High-carb (French bread); the sauce is moderate-low No seed oils. Cheese and any sausage or pepperoni fat are enough; the bread toasts in a dry oven. Toast the cut faces first. A dry surface is what keeps the 30-minute sauce from soaking the crumb into soggy bread pizza. The second bake is only to melt cheese and finish the toppings. A 30-minute simmer is the whole sauce. Water cooks off, acidity mellows, and the dried herbs rehydrate. Cool it before spreading so it does not start melting the cheese on the counter. Three-quarters of the cheese under the toppings, the rest on top — the bottom layer glues the toppings down; the top layer browns. Same layering as the homemade pizza. Leftover sauce keeps in the refrigerator and is the same puree-and-herb mix as the pizza sauce. Use it on breadsticks or another loaf later in the week. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Breakfast Casserole
recipes.how: 8 frozen hash brown patties 3 cups shredded sharp Cheddar cheese 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese 1 cup fully cooked ham, diced 1 scallion, thinly sliced 7 eggs 1 cup milk 1/2 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. dry mustard 1/4 tsp. pepper Butter, for the dish 1. Place the hash brown patties in a single layer in a buttered 13x9-inch baking dish. Sprinkle with the cheeses, ham, and scallion. 2. In a bowl, beat the eggs, milk, salt, dry mustard, and pepper until well combined. Pour over the hash browns. 3. Cover and bake at 350°F for 1 hour. Uncover and bake 15 minutes longer, or until the edges are golden brown and a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. This is a great choice for company and holiday brunches. Carb level: High-carb (hash brown patties are the base); the egg-and-cheese custard is moderate Butter the dish. No seed oils. The patties fry a little against the buttered pan while the custard sets above them. Leave the hash brown patties frozen and in a single layer. They are the “crust.” Thawed or broken-up potatoes weep water and turn the bottom soggy. Seven eggs plus 1 cup milk is a classic breakfast-strata custard. Dry mustard does not taste like mustard in the finished bake — it sharpens the cheddar the way a pinch of mustard does in a cheese sauce. Cover for the first hour so the eggs set without the top drying out; uncover for the last 15 minutes so the cheese browns and the knife test can go clean in the center. This can be assembled, covered, and refrigerated overnight. Bake as directed — cold from the fridge may need an extra 5 to 10 minutes. Swap bacon or sausage for the ham, and add diced green pepper, mushrooms, or another favorite vegetable if you like. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Chicken Parmesan Scallopine
recipes.how: 4 chicken breasts, pounded to 1/4-inch thick 1/4 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 cup blanched almond flour) 1/8 tsp. salt 1/8 tsp. pepper 1 egg 2 tbsp. water 1 cup dry bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1 cup crushed pork rinds) 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1 tsp. dried parsley 1/4 tsp. dried basil 2 tbsp. butter 2 tbsp. olive oil (in place of olive or vegetable oil) 1. Stir together the flour, salt, and pepper in a shallow bowl. Beat together the egg and water in another shallow bowl. Combine the bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, parsley, and basil in a third shallow bowl. 2. Coat each chicken breast first in the flour mixture, shaking off the excess, then in the egg mixture, and finally in the bread-crumb mixture, coating well. 3. In a large skillet over medium-high heat, heat the butter and olive oil until the butter melts. Add the coated chicken and cook for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, or until no pink remains. Drain on paper towels. Here’s a quick and easy main dish my family really enjoys! Carb level: Moderate-carb (flour dredge + bread-crumb crust); the chicken itself is low-carb Butter plus olive oil is the frying fat. Butter browns the crumbs and carries the Parmesan aroma; olive oil raises the smoke point so the butter does not burn in 3 to 4 minutes a side. No seed oils, and no margarine. Flour, then egg, then crumbs is the point. The thin flour coat dries the surface so the egg sticks; the egg is glue for the Parmesan crumbs. Skip a station and the crust slides off in the pan. Almond flour can stand in for the 1/4 cup dredge flour. The cup of bread crumbs is the crust — keep them for Steph’s original crunch, or use finely crushed pork rinds for a lower-carb plate. 1/4 inch is the thickness. Thin cutlets cook through in 3 to 4 minutes a side without drying, and the crust stays crisp instead of steaming. Do not crowd the skillet. This is breaded Parmesan scallopine, not a baked marinara chicken Parmesan. Serve with lemon, a simple tomato salad, or pasta if you want a fuller plate. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Strawberry Stuffed French Toast
recipes.how: 8 slices (1-inch thick) French bread 1/2 cup no-sugar-added strawberry jam (in place of strawberry jam) 3 eggs 1/3 cup milk 1/8 tsp. ground cinnamon Butter, for the griddle 1. Make a pocket in each bread slice; fill with strawberry jam. 2. Whisk together the eggs, milk, and cinnamon. Pour over the bread slices, turning to coat evenly. 3. Heat a griddle over medium heat and butter it generously. Fry the bread slices on both sides until golden brown. Here's a quick and easy breakfast dish that's nice enough for company as well as a leisurely Saturday morning breakfast with the family. This would be great with strawberry syrup and a few whole strawberries for garnish! Carb level: High-carb (thick French bread + jam) Butter on the griddle replaces nonstick spray. The milk-fat browns the custard (Maillard) and keeps the toast from sticking. No seed oils. Wheat bread stays. This is stuffed French toast; the 1-inch slices have to hold a jam pocket and soak without falling apart. Almond-flour bread will shred in the egg bath. Sugar swap: The jam is the sugar load. No-sugar-added or monk-fruit jam drops the carbs without changing the soak. A little real sugar in the jam still helps the cut faces caramelize on the griddle. Cut the pocket from the crust side so the slice stays hinged. Do not soak until floppy — a quick turn in the custard coats the crumb; a long soak turns the jam into a leak. Medium heat, not screaming hot. The egg needs time to set through the thick slice before the outside burns. Serve with strawberry syrup and whole berries if you want it company-pretty. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend; swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.)

recipes.title: Ravioli Lasagna
recipes.how: 1 cup small-curd cottage cheese 1 cup ricotta cheese 1 garlic clove, minced 1 jar (20 ounces) spaghetti sauce or homemade sauce 1 package (25 ounces) cheese ravioli, uncooked 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese Chopped fresh parsley, optional 1. Combine the cottage cheese, ricotta cheese, and garlic. 2. Spread 1/2 cup of the spaghetti sauce in an ungreased 13x9-inch baking dish. Layer with half of the ravioli, half of the remaining sauce, half of the cottage cheese mixture, and half of the cheeses. Repeat the layers. Sprinkle with parsley if desired. 3. Bake, uncovered, at 350°F for 30 to 40 minutes or until bubbly. Let stand for 5 to 10 minutes before serving. If you like lasagna and cheese ravioli, you'll love this dish! This was modified from a Quick Cooking recipe and definitely wins raves in my house. Yield: 6 to 8 servings Carb level: High-carb (ravioli pasta + sauce) No seed oils in this bake. The fat is cheese — cottage and ricotta in the middle, mozzarella, cheddar, and Parmesan on the layers. The ravioli stay uncooked. Sauce moisture plus the uncovered 350°F bake is what softens the pasta; if you boil them first the casserole goes slack. Use homemade spaghetti sauce when you have it (Easy Marinara Sauce works) or a jar. A 20-ounce jar is tight for two full layers in a 13x9. If the top ravioli look dry, spoon on extra sauce or use a 24- to 26-ounce jar so they stay covered. Let it stand 5 to 10 minutes. The starches set as it cools a little, so the squares slice instead of sliding into a cheesy puddle. Cheese ravioli is the point. Meat ravioli will work, but then you have two rich fillings stacked — taste before you salt. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Baked Ravioli
recipes.how: 1 package (25 ounces) frozen ravioli 1/2 cup melted butter 1 cup Italian seasoned dry bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1 cup crushed pork rinds) 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1/4 tsp. ground pepper 3 tbsp. chopped fresh parsley Jarred or homemade marinara sauce, warmed, for serving 1. Heat the oven to 400°F. Lightly grease a 13x9-inch baking dish with butter. 2. Cook the ravioli as directed on the package; drain well. Toss the ravioli with the melted butter in the prepared dish. Mix the bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and pepper; toss with the ravioli. Sprinkle with the parsley. 3. Bake, uncovered, for 15 minutes or until the ravioli is hot and the mixture is golden brown. Serve with warmed marinara sauce dribbled over the top. This wonderful pasta entree was shared with me by a wonderful friend, Janis, and my family just loves it. And because it uses prepared ravioli and pantry ingredients it makes the perfect quick dinner. Carb level: High-carb (ravioli + bread crumbs) Butter is the coating fat — half a cup tossed with hot, drained ravioli so the crumbs have something to cling to. Grease the pan with butter instead of spray. No seed oils. Wheat pasta and wheat crumbs stay. This is a toasted bread-crumb bake, not a low-carb casserole. Easy Marinara Sauce is a good homemade pour-over if you do not want a jar. Drain the ravioli well. Water left on the pasta slides the butter off and leaves wet spots that will not brown at 400°F. Toss the crumbs on while the ravioli is still hot from the pot. Warm buttered pasta grabs the coating; cold pasta leaves a sandy layer in the bottom of the dish. Fifteen minutes is a toast, not a long bake. Pull it when the top is golden. Useful tip: fresh ravioli totaling 25 ounces works the same way — still boil it first so the crumb coat is not sitting on raw pasta. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Asparagus Quiche
recipes.how: 1 cup buttermilk baking mix (lower-carb option: same amount almond-flour baking mix) 3/4 cup milk 3 eggs 1 bunch fresh asparagus, cut into bite-size pieces (about 3 cups) 1/2 cup sliced fresh mushrooms 1 cup shredded Swiss cheese 1 cup shredded white cheddar cheese 1/2 cup onion, diced 1/4 tsp. ground pepper 1/8 tsp. salt Dash cayenne pepper 1/2 cup cooked cubed ham or cooked crumbled bacon, optional 1. Preheat the oven to 375°F. Grease a 9-inch pie plate with butter. 2. Combine the baking mix, milk, and eggs. Stir in the remaining ingredients. Pour into the prepared pie plate. 3. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes or until a knife inserted near the middle comes out clean. This is a wonderful brunch dish for asparagus lovers! You can make it a bit more hearty by adding some cooked, cubed ham or cooked, crumbled bacon. Carb level: Moderate-carb (1 cup baking mix; eggs, cheese, and vegetables carry the rest) Butter on the pie plate replaces spray. No seed oils. The fat in the custard is cheese and egg yolk. Wheat baking mix stays. This is a crustless dump quiche — the mix, milk, and eggs set into a savory cake around the asparagus. A full almond-flour swap will not gel the same way. If you want it lower-carb, skip the mix and use 4 eggs plus 1 cup cream in a buttered plate, knowing it will be a custard, not this biscuit-tender slice. Do not overmix once the vegetables and cheese go in. You want the asparagus distributed, not a beaten batter with no lift left. 375°F for 30 to 35 minutes is enough for a 9-inch plate. The knife test is doneness — wet egg in the center will weep as it sits. A handful of ham or bacon makes it a full brunch plate; pat the meat dry so it does not water the custard. Fresh asparagus should be tender-crisp pieces, not woody ends. The mushrooms and onion cook in the custard, so dice the onion small. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Club Sandwiches
recipes.how: 8 large slices wheat bread Avocado oil mayonnaise, for spreading (in place of regular mayonnaise) 3/4 pound cooked turkey breast, thinly sliced 8 slices bacon, crisply cooked 8 slices tomato 4 large slices Provolone cheese 4 lettuce leaves 1/2 cup alfalfa sprouts 2-1/2 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 1-1/2 tsp. honey (in place of 3 tbsp. yellow mustard mixed with 1 tbsp. honey) 1. Lightly toast the bread. 2. For each sandwich, spread one slice of bread with avocado oil mayonnaise. Top with turkey, 2 slices of bacon, 2 slices of tomato, 1 slice of cheese, 1 lettuce leaf, and 1 tbsp. alfalfa sprouts. 3. Spread honey-mustard on the second bread slice and top off the sandwich. Cut in quarters. Serve immediately. These are so adaptable...add what you like on a sandwich. Make a really big sandwich by adding a third bread slice in the middle, too! Carb level: High-carb (wheat bread plus a little honey). Monk fruit in the mustard drops the sugar; the toast is still the carb. Avocado oil mayonnaise replaces regular mayo so the spread is seed-oil-free. A thin smear is a moisture barrier — it keeps tomato juice from turning the toast soggy. Bacon fat and Provolone are the rest of the richness. No seed oils. Wheat bread stays primary. This is a club sandwich; the toast has to hold turkey, bacon, tomato, and cheese in quarters. A full almond-flour loaf will crumble when you cut it. Add a third slice in the middle if you want a really big sandwich. Sugar swap: Keep at least a teaspoon of real honey. Honey is the body of the mustard sauce; all-monk-fruit mustard tastes thin and sharp. Toast the bread and crisp the bacon. Soft bread and limp bacon make a wet club. Cut in quarters and serve immediately so the tomato does not weep. Useful tip: one of my favorite club sandwiches is on cranberry-walnut bread from the bakery. The combination is just wonderful! Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this sandwich. Lettuce wraps or almond-flour bread cannot toast crisp or hold a stacked club in quarters, so you lose the crunch, the tomato makes it wetter, and it eats more like a wrap.

recipes.title: Wheat Germ Pancakes
recipes.how: For the pancakes: 1 cup flour (lower-carb option: 3/4 cup + 2 tbsp. blanched almond flour + 1 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 1/2 cup wheat germ 2 tsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tsp. sugar (in place of 1 tbsp. sugar) 1 tbsp. baking powder 1 tsp. baking soda 1/2 tsp. salt 3/4 cup orange juice 3/4 cup plain whole-milk yogurt (in place of nonfat) 3 tbsp. avocado oil (in place of vegetable oil) 1 egg, lightly beaten Butter, for the griddle For the topping: 1 cup raspberry jam 1/2 cup fresh or frozen (thawed) raspberries Whipped cream, optional 1. In a medium bowl, combine the flour, wheat germ, sweetener, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; mix well. 2. In a small bowl, combine the orange juice, yogurt, avocado oil, and egg; blend well. Add to the dry ingredients, stirring just until the dry ingredients are moistened. 3. Heat a griddle or skillet over medium-high heat and butter it well. For each pancake, pour 1/4 cup batter onto the hot griddle. Turn the pancakes when the tops are covered with bubbles and the edges look cooked. 4. In a microwave-safe bowl, heat the jam and raspberries until warm. Spoon over the pancakes. Top with whipped cream, if desired. With a light citrus flavor in every scrumptious bite, these are excellent topped with raspberries. This treasure comes from Kretschmer, the wheat germ people. =) Carb level: High-carb (flour, wheat germ, orange juice, and raspberry jam) Avocado oil replaces vegetable oil in the batter. Butter is the griddle fat — it browns the cakes (Maillard) and keeps them from sticking. Whole-milk yogurt replaces the original nonfat so the batter stays tender and the pancakes do not taste chalky. No seed oils. Wheat stays primary — 1 cup all-purpose plus 1/2 cup wheat germ. The white flour’s gluten is the structure; the wheat germ adds nuttiness and a little crunch. A full almond-flour swap will not rise or flip the same way. Sugar swap: Keep a little real sugar in the batter. Those grams help the cakes spot gold on the griddle. Monk fruit will not replace the sugar already in the jam — this is a treat breakfast. Stop stirring the moment the dry streaks disappear. Extra mixing develops gluten and makes the pancakes tough, especially with wheat germ in the bowl. Lumps are fine. Medium-high heat is the window. Too hot and the sugar scorches before the centers set; too cool and the cakes steam and never brown. Flip when the tops are bubbled and the edges look dry — one flip. Real whipped cream if you want a dollop. Frozen whipped topping is built on seed oils. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Stromboli
recipes.how: For the honey wheat pizza dough: 1-1/2 tsp. yeast 3/4 cup warm water (105°F to 110°F) 1-1/2 cups all-purpose flour 3/4 cup whole wheat flour 1 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 2 tbsp. honey (in place of 3 tbsp. honey) 1-1/2 tbsp. olive oil 1-1/4 tsp. salt For the marinara sauce: 1 can (14-1/2 ounces) crushed tomatoes 1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce 1/2 tsp. dried basil 0.38 tsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1/8 tsp. sugar (in place of 1/2 tsp. sugar) 1/4 tsp. dried Italian seasoning Pinch of salt Dash of pepper For the filling: Cornmeal, for the pan Sliced pepperoni Sliced salami 1 small onion, cut into thin wedges and separated 2 plum tomatoes, sliced 6 large slices Provolone cheese 1 tsp. olive oil 1/4 tsp. dried oregano 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1 tbsp. olive oil 1 tbsp. sesame seeds 1. For the dough, dissolve the yeast in the warm water. Add the remaining dough ingredients and mix well. Knead for several minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic. Place the dough in a greased bowl, turning to coat. Cover and let rise in a warm, draft-free space for 1 to 2 hours, or until double in bulk. Punch the dough down. 2. For the sauce, combine all sauce ingredients in a small saucepan. Heat over medium heat until bubbly. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 30 to 45 minutes, stirring occasionally. 3. Lightly grease a 15x10x1-inch baking sheet with olive oil; sprinkle with cornmeal. Pat the dough into a 15x10-inch rectangle on the baking sheet. Spread 1/2 cup marinara sauce over the crust to within 1 inch of the edges. Arrange the pepperoni and salami over the sauce; top with the onion wedges and tomatoes. Lay the Provolone slices over the top; drizzle with 1 tsp. olive oil and the oregano. Sprinkle the mozzarella and Parmesan evenly over the top. 4. Moisten the edges of the dough with water. Fold the long edges to the center; pinch to seal all edges so the filling is completely enclosed. Smooth the dough out. Brush with 1 tbsp. olive oil and sprinkle on the sesame seeds. 5. Bake at 375°F for 20 to 25 minutes, or until golden brown. Cut into 1-1/2-inch strips and serve with the leftover marinara sauce. This makes a delicious, hearty meal. Don loves it! Carb level: High-carb (honey-wheat yeast dough); sauce and filling are moderate Wheat stays primary — 1-1/2 cups all-purpose plus 3/4 cup whole wheat. This dough has to rise, stretch to 15x10 inches, and seal around meat and cheese. A full almond-flour swap will not develop the gluten sheet you need. Olive oil is the fat in the dough, on the filling, and on the loaf. Grease the bowl and the sheet with olive oil too. No seed oils. Cornmeal on the pan is not garnish — it keeps the bottom from gluing down so it can crisp. Sugar swap: Water at 105°F to 110°F wakes the yeast without killing it. Keep most of the honey; yeast uses some of it as food, and those grams help the crust brown. Do not swap the entire 3 tbsp. for monk fruit. A 30- to 45-minute simmer is the whole sauce. Water cooks off, acidity mellows, and the dried herbs rehydrate. Cool it a little before you spread so it does not start melting the cheese on the counter. Leftover sauce is the dip. Easy Marinara Sauce from the box is the same pot if you already have it made. Leave a 1-inch border and pinch every seam. Gaps leak cheese and pepperoni oil onto the sheet. The teaspoon of oil and oregano on the Provolone seasons the middle; the sesame seeds toast on the olive-oil brush. 375°F is hot enough to brown the loaf and melt the cheeses before the tomatoes waterlog the dough. Rest a few minutes before you cut 1-1/2-inch strips so the cheese sets. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour is the best for this recipe because: the gluten network is what traps the yeast's gas and gives the rise and chew; almond and coconut flour have no gluten, so the dough cannot rise or stretch.

recipes.title: Honey Wheat Pizza Dough
recipes.how: 1-1/2 tsp. yeast 3/4 cup warm water (105°F to 110°F) 1-1/2 cups all-purpose flour 3/4 cup whole wheat flour 1 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 2 tbsp. honey (in place of 3 tbsp. honey) 1-1/2 tbsp. olive oil 1-1/4 tsp. salt 1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water. Add the remaining ingredients and mix well. 2. Knead for several minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic. Place the dough in a greased bowl, turning to coat. Cover and let rise in a warm, draft-free space for 1 to 2 hours, or until double in bulk. 3. Punch the dough down and roll to shape. I was looking for a good honey wheat pizza dough recipe, and a few fellow recipe-lovers came to my rescue with the California Pizza Kitchen recipe. I made it as listed, and it was indeed good. But one day not too long afterwards, I wanted a honey-wheat pizza crust for dinner and didn't have the time to follow the original recipe (which requires an overnight refrigeration). So, I didn't, and the results of my modifications are just as good with a lot less time involved. This is the modified version of California Pizza Kitchen's Honey Wheat Pizza Dough. Yield: dough for one 15-inch pizza (8 servings) Carb level: High-carb (two wheat flours + honey) Wheat stays primary — 1-1/2 cups all-purpose plus 3/4 cup whole wheat. This is a real pizza crust; a full almond-flour swap will not stretch, rise, or crisp the same way. The white flour’s gluten is the stretch; the whole wheat is the flavor and a little chew. Olive oil is the fat in the dough. Grease the bowl with olive oil too. No seed oils. Water at 105°F to 110°F wakes the yeast without killing it. Cooler water and the rise stalls; hotter water kills the yeast and you get a dense disc. Sugar swap: Keep most of the honey. Yeast uses some of it as food, it is hygroscopic (it holds water) so the crumb stays tender, and those grams help the crust brown (Maillard). Do not swap the entire 3 tbsp. for monk fruit. Knead until the dough is smooth and springs back. Under-kneaded dough tears when you roll it; a few minutes is enough for this small batch. The 1- to 2-hour rise is a same-day shortcut — the original CPK dough refrigerates overnight, which builds more flavor if you have the time. Punch down and roll to a 15-inch round, or pat into the 15x10-inch rectangle for Stromboli. Cornmeal on the pan keeps the bottom from gluing down. This is the crust Homemade Pizza points to when you want honey-wheat instead of the beer dough. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour is the best for this recipe because: the gluten network is what traps the yeast's gas and gives the rise and chew; almond and coconut flour have no gluten, so the dough cannot rise or stretch.

recipes.title: Savory Grilled Ham and Cheese Sandwiches
recipes.how: 1/2 cup butter, softened (in place of margarine) Golden monk fruit blend (in place of pinch brown sugar) Pinch ground red pepper (cayenne) 8 large slices sourdough bread 8 slices American cheese 1/2 pound sliced, cooked ham 8 thin tomato slices, patted dry 1. Mix the butter, brown sugar, and red pepper. Top 4 bread slices with 1 cheese slice, ham, tomatoes, a second cheese slice, and the second bread slice. Spread the outsides of the sandwiches with the butter mixture. 2. Grill on a griddle or skillet over medium heat until lightly browned on both sides and the cheese is melted. Serve these delicious and hearty sandwiches with a salad and fruit smoothie for a quick and fun meal! Carb level: High-carb (sourdough is the base); ham, cheese, and tomato are low-carb Butter replaces margarine on the outside of the bread. That is what browns and crisps the crust (Maillard). No seed oils. Sugar swap: The pinch of brown sugar and cayenne in the butter is the “savory” twist — a thin sweet-heat film that caramelizes on the griddle. Monk fruit can take the pinch of sugar; you only need a few real brown-sugar granules if you want that molasses note. American cheese is here on purpose. The emulsifying salts keep it molten instead of splitting into oil and string, so you get a sealed, diner-style melt. Cheddar or Colby Jack work if you prefer a sharper sandwich; they need slightly gentler heat. Pat the tomato slices dry. Water left on the fruit steams the bread and keeps the cheese from gluing the filling shut. Cheese on both sides of the ham and tomato is the seal. Medium heat only. Too hot and the sugar in the butter scorches before the middle is hot. Cover the skillet for a minute if the cheese needs help. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Chicken and Asparagus Fettucine
recipes.how: For the pasta: 12 ounces uncooked fettucine 2 cups fresh asparagus, cut in 2-inch pieces For the sauce: 1/2 cup butter 2 cups heavy cream (or half-and-half) 3/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1/4 tsp. garlic powder 1/4 tsp. pepper Dash cayenne pepper 1/2 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cooked and cubed Additional grated Parmesan, for serving 1. Start cooking the fettucine according to package directions, adding the asparagus the last 5 minutes of cooking time. 2. While the pasta cooks, heat the butter and cream over medium heat until the butter is melted and the mixture begins to bubble. Stir in the Parmesan, garlic powder, pepper, and cayenne. Continue cooking over medium heat until the mixture is thickened and creamy, stirring occasionally. Stir in the chicken. 3. Drain the pasta and asparagus. Toss with the sauce to evenly coat. Serve immediately. Sprinkle on additional grated Parmesan, if desired. This is a rich and tasty way to enjoy fettucine. One serving goes a long way! Carb level: High-carb (fettucine is the base); the cream sauce, chicken, and asparagus are moderate-low Butter plus heavy cream is the sauce fat. No seed oils. This is an Alfredo-style emulsion — butter, cream, and Parmesan — not a flour roux. Medium heat until it bubbles, then stir until it coats a spoon. A hard boil can split the cream and turn the cheese grainy. Wheat fettucine stays primary. This is a pasta supper. Zucchini noodles will shed water and thin the sauce you just thickened. For a lower-carb plate, use half the pasta and extra chicken and asparagus. Drop the asparagus into the pasta water for the last 5 minutes. One pot, and the stems cook tender-crisp in already-salted water. Do not rinse the pasta; surface starch helps the sauce cling. Heavy cream is richer and more stable than half-and-half. If you use half-and-half, keep the heat gentler and pull it as soon as it thickens. The chicken is already cooked, so it only needs to heat through in the sauce. Leftover roast or poached chicken is the weeknight path; if you are starting from raw, sauté the cubes in a little of the butter first, then build the cream sauce in the same pan. Serve immediately. Cream sauces tighten as they sit, and the pasta keeps drinking them. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap pasta/noodles for zucchini noodles or shirataki.

recipes.title: Asparagus Swiss Omelet
recipes.how: 2 eggs 2 tbsp. milk 1 tbsp. butter (in place of nonstick spray) 1/2 cup fresh asparagus, cut in 2-inch pieces 1/4 cup shredded Swiss cheese Salt and pepper to taste 1. Beat together the eggs and milk. 2. Melt the butter in an 8-inch pan over medium heat. Add the asparagus and cook 1 to 2 minutes, until bright green and just tender-crisp. 3. Pour the egg mixture into the hot pan. Sprinkle on the cheese and salt and pepper to taste. Cook until the edges begin to lightly brown and the eggs appear almost fully cooked. Fold in half, creating the omelet shape. Continue cooking until the eggs are completely set, another minute or two. Asparagus lovers will delight in every bite of this hearty omelet. Serve this for breakfast, lunch or dinner! Carb level: Low-carb (eggs, asparagus, Swiss, and a splash of milk) Butter replaces nonstick spray. It browns the asparagus, keeps the eggs tender, and is what gives the outside those lightly browned edges. No seed oils. A brief sauté first is the upgrade. Two-inch pieces of raw asparagus will stay woody in a 2-egg omelet that only cooks a few minutes; 1 to 2 minutes in the butter takes the raw snap off and seasons the spears before the eggs go in. The 2 tablespoons of milk dilute the egg proteins just enough for a softer set. Medium heat, not high — egg proteins set around 160–180°F; a ripping-hot pan browns the bottom before the center cooks and the Swiss melts. Fold when the top still looks a little wet. Residual heat finishes the inside so you do not dry it out waiting for a fully set surface. One hearty omelet. Scale the pan, not just the eggs, if you are cooking for two — an overcrowded 8-inch skillet steams instead of browning. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Peanut Chicken-Vegetable Lo Mein
recipes.how: 2 large chicken breasts, thinly sliced for stir-frying 1 tbsp. avocado oil (plus 1 tsp. toasted sesame oil, optional) 1 cup bean sprouts 1 cup thinly julienne-cut carrots 1 cup sugar snap peas 2 cups shredded green cabbage 1/2 cup sliced scallions 1 cup chicken broth 1/4 cup creamy peanut butter 2 tbsp. teriyaki sauce or hoisin sauce 1/2 tsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1/2 tsp. brown sugar (in place of 1 tsp. brown sugar) 1 tsp. cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) Dash cayenne pepper 8 ounces spaghetti, cooked until just al dente and drained 1/4 cup coarsely chopped roasted peanuts 1. Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and stir-fry about 3 minutes, until no longer pink. Remove from the skillet; cover to keep warm. 2. In the same skillet, sauté the bean sprouts, carrots, and peas for 2 minutes. Add the cabbage and scallions; stir-fry another minute or two, until the carrots are crisp-tender. 3. Whisk together the broth, peanut butter, teriyaki or hoisin sauce, sweetener, cornstarch, and cayenne. Stir into the vegetable mixture. Add the chicken and stir to combine. Reduce the heat to medium and cook until the mixture thickens, about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. 4. Add the spaghetti and peanuts and toss to combine. Drizzle with the toasted sesame oil if using. Serve immediately. This is a nice change of pace from traditional lo meins and stir fries. Carb level: High-carb (wheat spaghetti plus a peanut-teriyaki sauce) Avocado oil replaces a lone tablespoon of sesame oil for the stir-fry. It handles wok heat and stays off the seed-oil list. A teaspoon of toasted sesame oil at the end is flavor only — toasted sesame smokes if you fry in it. No vegetable oil. Wheat spaghetti stays primary. This is lo mein; the noodles have to take a thick peanut sauce without falling apart. A full almond-flour pasta will not. For a lower-carb plate, toss the chicken and vegetables with zucchini noodles or skip the starch and serve in bowls. Sugar swap: Keep the 1/2 tsp. of real brown sugar. Those molasses grams help the sauce glaze and brown (Maillard) instead of tasting like sweetened broth. Cornstarch needs a minute on medium heat to swell and turn the peanut-broth mix glossy — do not boil it hard or the emulsion can break. High heat, constant motion, crisp-tender vegetables. If the pan crowds, cook the vegetables in two batches so they sear instead of stew. Cook the spaghetti just to al dente and drain well. Wet noodles thin the sauce. The original step called for soy sauce; the ingredient list is teriyaki or hoisin, and that is the sauce. Useful tip: or use chunky peanut butter and omit the chopped peanuts. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Hula Ham Sandwiches
recipes.how: 5 Kaiser rolls, split in half 5 tsp. Dijon mustard 5 lettuce leaves 10 slices Swiss cheese 1 pound deli-sliced smoked ham 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple slices, drained and patted dry 5 tsp. avocado oil mayonnaise (in place of regular mayonnaise) 1. Spread Dijon mustard over the bottom halves of the rolls. 2. Layer on each bottom: one lettuce leaf, two slices of Swiss, about 3 ounces ham, and 2 pineapple slices. 3. Spread the top halves of the rolls with avocado oil mayonnaise and place on the sandwiches. Serve immediately. These quick and easy sandwiches from Dole are so delicious! The pineapple is a wonderful addition. Carb level: High-carb (Kaiser rolls plus canned pineapple) Avocado oil mayonnaise replaces regular mayo so the spread is seed-oil-free. A thin smear on the top bun is a moisture barrier — it keeps pineapple juice from turning the crumb soggy. Dijon on the bottom is the sharp counter to the ham and fruit. No seed oils. Wheat Kaiser rolls stay primary. This is a stacked deli sandwich; the roll has to hold ham, Swiss, and two pineapple rings. A full almond-flour bun will crumble. Drain the pineapple well and pat the slices dry. Water left on the fruit soaks the roll and slides the cheese. Swiss against the ham is the seal and the melt if you want to warm them. Build and serve right away so the lettuce stays crisp. If you want them hot, toast the split rolls and warm the ham and pineapple in a skillet before stacking. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.)

recipes.title: Grilled Peppered Steak
recipes.how: 2 tsp. coarse black pepper 1 tsp. onion salt 1 tsp. garlic salt 4 strip steaks (New York strip), about 8 ounces each 1. Combine the pepper, onion salt, and garlic salt. Pat the steaks dry, then rub the spice mix on both sides. Let stand in the refrigerator while preparing the grill, about 15 minutes. 2. Grill over medium-hot coals, 5 to 9 minutes per side, depending on desired doneness. Rest 5 minutes before slicing. I knew I wanted some sort of peppered steak for dinner one night, so I just tossed some spices together and voilà, a meal my family thoroughly enjoyed. Don complimented dinner that night at least four times! Serve this with a baked potato and salad or veggie for a scrumptious, hearty meal. Carb level: Low-carb (steak and spices only) No added fat is required — the steaks bring their own. If they stick, brush the grates with avocado oil or a little melted ghee, not vegetable oil. No seed oils. Pat the steaks dry before the rub. Surface water steams and keeps the pepper from toasting. Coarse black pepper is the crust — the oils in the cracked pepper bloom on the hot grate (Maillard) and taste round instead of dusty. Fifteen minutes in the fridge is just long enough for the onion salt and garlic salt to dissolve and season the surface. Much longer and the salt starts to cure the outside. Bring the steaks off the cold plate for a few minutes while the grill heats if they are fridge-cold through the middle. Medium-hot coals, not a raging fire. Five to 9 minutes per side covers rare to well for an 8-ounce strip. Pull them a few degrees early and rest 5 minutes so the juices settle instead of running onto the cutting board. Useful tip: strip steak is also known as New York strip steak. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Grilled Italian Sub Sandwich
recipes.how: 2 loaves (8 ounces each) French or sourdough bread 4 tbsp. mustard 8 ounces pastrami, thinly sliced 8 ounces smoked ham, thinly sliced 2 roma tomatoes, thinly sliced Red onion rings 4 large slices Provolone cheese 4 tbsp. avocado oil Italian dressing (in place of regular Italian dressing) 1. Slice the bread in half lengthwise. Scoop out the bread in the bottom halves, leaving a 1/2-inch-thick shell. Evenly layer the ingredients in the order listed in both bottom halves; replace the bread tops. Wrap the sandwiches in foil. 2. Grill over medium coals for 15 minutes, or until warmed and the cheese is melted. Or bake at 350°F until warmed and the cheese is melted. Unwrap the sandwiches and slice into serving-size pieces. This makes a nice and hearty dinner, not to mention delicious! Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: High-carb (French or sourdough loaves); the meats, cheese, and vegetables are low-carb Avocado oil Italian dressing replaces regular bottled dressing so the drizzle is seed-oil-free. Mustard, pastrami, ham, and Provolone carry the rest of the fat. No seed oils. Wheat bread stays. This is a grilled sub; the 1/2-inch shell has to hold meat and melt without collapsing. Scooping the bottoms is not just for room — it cuts some of the crumb so the sandwich is meat-forward instead of a bread brick. Foil is a steam jacket. It heats the stack through and melts the Provolone without drying the ham. Open the foil for the last couple of minutes if you want a crisper top. Layer in the order listed so the cheese sits near the top and the dressing soaks the meat, not the bottom crust. Medium coals (or 350°F) — too hot and the bread scorches before the middle is warm. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: BBQ Chicken Burritos
recipes.how: For the chicken: 4 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts 1/2 cup no-sugar-added barbecue sauce (in place of barbecue sauce) For the burritos: 6 large flour tortillas 3 cups shredded lettuce 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese 1 small tomato, diced 1 small avocado, diced 1/2 cup diced purple onion For the sauce: 1/4 cup no-sugar-added barbecue sauce (in place of barbecue sauce) 2 tbsp. sour cream 1 tbsp. avocado oil ranch dressing (in place of regular ranch) 1. Heat the grill over medium-hot coals. Oil the grates with avocado oil. Grill the chicken breasts for 7 minutes; turn over and grill 5 minutes longer. Brush the chicken with barbecue sauce. Grill about 3 minutes and turn the chicken over. Brush with more barbecue sauce and continue grilling and turning until the chicken is done and generously coated with barbecue sauce. 2. Let the chicken cool enough to handle. Slice into thin, short strips. 3. Warm the flour tortillas according to package directions. Evenly divide the chicken among the tortillas. Top with lettuce, cheeses, tomato, avocado, and onion. Combine the remaining barbecue sauce, sour cream, and avocado oil ranch dressing; dollop on the burritos. Roll up. Not your traditional burrito. These are awesome!! Serve with a mixed salad of some sort and fresh fruit for a delicious and filling dinner. Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas + barbecue sauce); the chicken, cheese, avocado, and ranch are protein and fat Avocado oil ranch replaces regular ranch so the drizzle is seed-oil-free. Oil the grill grates with avocado oil so the breasts do not stick. No seed oils. Wheat flour tortillas stay primary. That is the burrito. For a lower-carb plate, use the same filling in large lettuce leaves or a low-carb wheat-style tortilla. Keep some real sugar in the barbecue sauce if you want that lacquered grill crust (Maillard plus caramelization). No-sugar-added sauce still browns from the chicken juices; it just will not glaze as hard. Brush late so the sugars do not burn. The sour cream–ranch–barbecue dollop is the “not your traditional burrito” move — cool, tangy, and a little sweet against the smoky chicken. Mix it just before serving so it stays thick. Slice the chicken short so it does not pull out when you bite. Warm the tortillas so they roll without cracking. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Peaches and Cream French Toast
recipes.how: For the toast: 1 loaf (8 ounces) unsliced French bread Butter, for the griddle For the filling: 1 package (3 ounces) cream cheese, softened 3 tbsp. no-sugar-added peach preserves (in place of peach preserves) 1/2 tsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1/2 tsp. brown sugar (in place of 1 tsp. brown sugar) For the custard: 3 eggs 1/2 cup milk 1/2 tsp. vanilla extract 1/4 tsp. ground cinnamon For serving: Powdered monk fruit (in place of confectioners' sugar) Sugar-free monk fruit maple syrup (in place of maple syrup) 1. Cut the French bread into 8 slices (slices should be about 1-inch thick). Cut a pocket in each slice, cutting from the top-crust side almost to the bottom-side crust. 2. In a small bowl, combine the cream cheese, peach preserves, and brown sugar. Spoon about 1 tablespoon of the mixture into each pocket. 3. In another small bowl, beat the eggs, milk, vanilla, and cinnamon until well combined. Dip the stuffed bread slices into the egg mixture, letting the excess drip off. 4. Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat and butter it well. Cook the bread slices until golden brown, turning once, about 2 minutes per side. Lightly sprinkle each serving with confectioners' sugar and serve with maple syrup. This is absolutely delicious and makes a great breakfast for company (the recipe can easily be doubled)! Yield: 8 slices Carb level: High-carb (French bread + preserves + syrup) Butter on the griddle replaces nonstick spray. The milk-fat browns the custard (Maillard) and keeps the toast from sticking. No seed oils. Wheat bread stays. This is stuffed French toast; the 1-inch slices have to hold a cream-cheese pocket and soak without falling apart. Almond-flour bread will shred in the egg bath. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar in the filling, and keep some real sugar in the preserves if you want the cut faces to caramelize. Powdered monk fruit and monk-fruit maple can stand in at the table. Cut the pocket from the crust side so the slice stays hinged. Do not soak until floppy — a quick dip coats the crumb; a long soak turns the filling into a leak. Medium heat, not screaming hot. The egg needs time to set through the thick slice before the outside burns. Softened cream cheese is what lets you spoon a full tablespoon into each pocket. The recipe doubles easily for company. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Peach Oatmeal
recipes.how: 3 cups old-fashioned oats 1/3 cup dried cranberries (or unsweetened dried cranberries) 1/4 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. ground cinnamon 5 cups water 1 can (16 ounces) sliced peaches, drained and chopped 1/4 cup golden monk fruit blend + 2 tbsp. brown sugar, or to taste (in place of 6 tbsp. brown sugar) Milk, for serving 1. Combine the oats, cranberries, salt, and cinnamon. 2. Bring the water to a boil in a 2-quart saucepan. Stir in the oat mixture. Cook over medium heat about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and creamy. 3. Stir in the peaches and sweetener. Serve with milk if desired. This is a delicious fruity alternative to regular oatmeal. One my family loves. Carb level: High-carb (oats + peaches + brown sugar + cranberries) No added oil here. Water plus old-fashioned oats is a classic simmer; the milk at the table is creaminess you control, not fat cooked into the pot. Old-fashioned oats are rolled thicker than quick oats, so they need about 5 minutes to hydrate. That extra time is why the bowl turns creamy instead of pasty. Quick oats will cook faster and get gluey if you leave them the full 5 minutes. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar. The molasses is part of the peach-cinnamon smell; monk fruit sweetens but does not perfume the pot the same way. Drain the peaches well so the syrup does not thin the oatmeal into soup. Stir the fruit in off the hard boil so the pieces stay intact. Unsweetened dried cranberries plus the monk fruit blend drop the extra sugar if the canned peaches are already sweet. Salt is not optional garnish — a pinch makes the peaches taste riper. Leftovers thicken in the fridge; loosen with a splash of milk when you reheat. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Cheddar Pie Crust
recipes.how: 1-1/3 cups flour (lower-carb option: 1-1/3 cups blanched almond flour + 5/8 tsp. xanthan gum) 1/4 tsp. salt 1/3 cup cold butter, cut into pieces (in place of shortening) 1/4 cup cold butter, cut into pieces 1 cup grated sharp Cheddar cheese 1/2 tsp. vinegar mixed with 1/3 cup cold water 1. Combine the flour and salt in a medium bowl. Cut all the cold butter into small pieces and add to the flour. Cut in with a pastry blender until crumbs begin to form. Add the cheese and cut in to mix. Pour in the water mixture, 2 tbsp. at a time, and mix until the dough forms a ball. Do not add too much water. 2. Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface. Specks of butter and cheese will be visible in the dough. Shape into a disk, wrap in plastic wrap, and chill at least 2 hours. 3. Divide the dough into 2 pieces and roll into 11-inch circles. Use for pot pie, or for apple or pear pie. This is a wonderful pie crust in meat and dinner pies as well as apple and pear pies. Yield: double-crust pie dough (8 servings) Carb level: High-carb (flour crust) All butter replaces the original shortening-and-butter mix. Butter gives better flavor and a tender, flaky layer because the water in the butter turns to steam. Chill well so the butter stays in pieces. No seed oils. Wheat flour stays primary. This dough has to roll into two 11-inch circles and hold a pot-pie filling or fruit juices; a full almond-flour swap will crack and will not flake. Do not rebuild this crust in almond flour. The vinegar in the water limits gluten so the dough stays tender instead of turning into cardboard. Add the water 2 tablespoons at a time — too much and you get paste; too little and it will not gather. Visible specks of butter and cheese are the goal, not a smooth ball. Two hours cold is not optional. Warm butter smears and the crust bakes greasy instead of layered. Sharp Cheddar is salt and fat in the dough; it browns the crust and tastes like a dinner pie even under apples. Same dough lives in Chicken Pot Pie if you want the filling too. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Mom's Meatloaf
recipes.how: 1-1/2 pounds lean ground beef 1 cup crushed crackers (Ritz) (lower-carb option: 1 cup blanched almond flour) 1 small onion, chopped 1 egg 1/2 cup milk 1/2 cup ketchup, divided 1 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce 1 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper 1. Heat the oven to 350°F. In a large bowl, combine the beef, cracker crumbs (or almond flour), onion, egg, milk, 1/4 cup ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper; mix thoroughly. In a shallow baking pan, shape into a loaf. Spread the remaining ketchup over the top. 2. Cover and bake for 30 minutes. Drain off the fat and continue baking, uncovered, 30 minutes longer. This is my mom’s meatloaf recipe and still my favorite. I still remember her serving this with Scalloped Potatoes and Baked Brown Sugar Squash and what true soul food it is. Carb level: Moderate-carb (crackers + ketchup); almond flour brings the loaf down No added cooking oil. Drain the loaf at 30 minutes so the crust can brown instead of sitting in fat. No seed oils. Crackers hold moisture and give that diner-loaf tenderness. Almond flour still binds with the egg and milk; the loaf will be a little denser and less bready. Mix thoroughly but do not knead — overworked beef squeezes out fat and bakes tight. Covered first, then uncovered. The first half steams the loaf through; the second half lets the ketchup glaze take color (sugars in the ketchup caramelize and Maillard on the meat). That is why you drain before the last 30 minutes. Half the ketchup goes in the mix for moisture and tang; the rest is the glaze. Worcestershire is glutamate and a little sweetness — do not skip it. Pairs with Scalloped Potatoes and Baked Brown Sugar Squash, just like Mom served it. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Crockpot Pot Roast
recipes.how: 1 beef roast (3 to 5 pounds) 4 large potatoes, peeled and quartered 6 large carrots, peeled and cut into chunks 1 large onion, peeled and quartered 5 cloves garlic, minced 3/4 cup beef broth or red wine 1 tbsp. dried parsley Pinch dried thyme Salt and pepper to taste 1–2 tbsp. cornstarch mixed with cold water, optional, to thicken the juices (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1. Trim most of the fat off the roast. Season lightly with salt and pepper. 2. Place the potatoes, carrots, and onion in the crockpot. Stir in the garlic. Place the roast on top. 3. Stir together the broth or wine, parsley, thyme, and salt and pepper. Pour over and around the roast. Cover and cook on low for 8 to 9 hours until the roast and vegetables are tender. 4. Remove the meat and vegetables. If you want gravy, whisk the cornstarch slurry into the hot liquid and cook until it thickens. Good old-fashioned pot roast with all of the trimmings really signifies down-home cooking. Mmmm good! Carb level: High-carb with the potatoes; Moderate-low if you skip the potatoes and thicken only a cup of the juices No added cooking oil. The roast supplies the fat as it renders. If you brown the roast in a little butter or avocado oil first, you get extra Maillard flavor, but the original dump-and-go method still works. No seed oils. Eight to nine hours on low is collagen turning into gelatin. That is what makes a cheap roast spoon-tender and gives the juices body. High for 4 to 5 hours will cook the meat but will not give you the same silky sauce. Vegetables go under the roast so they cook in the drippings instead of drying out on top. Red wine adds acid, which helps the connective tissue break down; broth keeps it classic Sunday-supper. Either is 3/4 cup — this is a braise, not a stew, so do not flood the pot. A cornstarch slurry is optional. The gelatin-rich juices are already a light gravy once you skim the fat. For a lower-carb plate, skip the potatoes, keep the carrots and onion, and serve the beef with the juices over cauliflower mash. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: thicken with a little arrowroot slurry instead of flour/cornstarch; swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this pot roast. Turnips or cauliflower in place of the potatoes do not soak up the beefy juices the same way, and cauliflower turns mushy over 8 hours (add it near the end), so the plate is lighter; the beef and juices stay the same.

recipes.title: Hot Rice Cereal
recipes.how: 1-1/2 cups cooked white rice 1/2 cup milk 1 tsp. vanilla 3 tbsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 1/4 cup packed brown sugar) 1/4 tsp. ground cinnamon 1/4 cup raisins or other dried fruit, optional Additional milk and brown sugar or monk fruit, for serving 1. Combine the rice, milk, vanilla, sweetener, cinnamon, and raisins in a small saucepan. 2. Heat over medium-high heat until thick and creamy, stirring often. Serve with additional milk and sweetener to taste if desired. I came up with this one morning when I had leftover cooked rice from the night before to use up. Delicious and soothes the soul. Don't throw away leftover rice, and start cooking extra to save for this cereal in the morning. Carb level: High-carb (rice + brown sugar + optional raisins) No added oil here. Milk plus leftover rice is the whole bowl. The starch that cooled and retrograded overnight swells again in the milk and turns creamy instead of watery. No seed oils. Day-old rice is the point. Fresh-hot rice is too wet and will go gluey; cold grains stay separate long enough to drink the milk. If you only have freshly cooked rice, spread it on a plate to steam off for 10 minutes first. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar. The molasses is part of the cinnamon-rice smell; monk fruit sweetens but does not perfume the pot the same way. Stir often so the milk does not scorch on the bottom. Raisins plump in the hot milk and add little bursts of sweetness. Dried cherries or chopped dates work the same way. For a lower-carb bowl, skip the dried fruit and use cauliflower rice with the same milk, vanilla, cinnamon, and a monk fruit blend — it will not be as starchy-creamy, but it still soothes. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: German Apple Pancake (Puff Pancake)
recipes.how: 2 large cooking apples 1/4 cup butter, divided 1 cup flour 1 cup milk 6 eggs 1 tsp. vanilla 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. grated nutmeg Powdered monk fruit, for dusting (in place of confectioners’ sugar) Maple syrup, for serving 1. Preheat the oven to 475°F. 2. Peel, core, and very thinly slice the apples; you should have approximately 1-1/2 cups. Melt 2 tbsp. of the butter over medium-low heat in a small fry pan and sauté the apples until they are just tender, about 3 minutes. Keep warm while preparing the batter. 3. Place a 9- or 10-inch cast-iron skillet or very heavy ovenproof pan in the oven to heat for at least 5 minutes. When it is well heated, add the remaining 2 tbsp. butter to melt and put the skillet back in the oven; the butter should be very hot but not brown when you add the apples and the batter. 4. While the skillet is heating, place the flour, milk, eggs, vanilla, salt, and nutmeg in a blender and whiz until smooth (or beat with a rotary beater). Remove the skillet from the oven, quickly arrange the warm sautéed apple slices over the melted butter, and pour the batter evenly over all. 5. Bake for 15 minutes, reduce heat to 375°F, and bake 10 minutes longer. The pancake will puff and climb up the sides of the pan. Sprinkle with powdered sweetener, then cut into wedges and serve warm with maple syrup. I am always on the lookout for delicious and filling meatless meals, and this treasure from Marcia Adams' Cooking from Quilt Country fits the bill perfectly. I prefer to finely chop my apples instead of slice, and sometimes omit the apples completely. Try this with other fruit like peaches, pears, or berries, too. Carb level: High-carb (flour batter plus apples and maple) Butter is the only fat — 2 tbsp. to sauté the apples, 2 tbsp. in the screaming-hot skillet. That hot fat is what the batter hits so it puffs instead of sticking. No seed oils. If you opt for a plain puff pancake with no fruit, put the full 1/4 cup butter in the hot skillet. Wheat flour stays primary. This is a Dutch baby / popover: gluten plus egg protein trap steam so the pancake climbs the pan. A full almond-flour swap will not puff or hold. Do not swap the flour. 475°F then 375°F is the science. The blast of heat turns the milk to steam and sets the walls as they climb; the lower finish cooks the center without burning the edges. A cold skillet will give you a flat omelet. The butter should shimmer, not brown. Six eggs are the structure. Blend the batter smooth — unlike muffins, you want this gluten developed enough to stretch. Work fast once the skillet is out so the butter stays hot. Sugar swap: Keep a light dusting of real confectioners’ sugar if you use powdered monk fruit; those few grams help the top look glazed. The maple is serving syrup, not batter sugar. Finely chopped apples (as I prefer) melt into the custard more than slices do; peaches, pears, or berries work the same way. Pat wet fruit dry so it does not steam the puff flat. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour is the best for this recipe because: steam-puffed batters (popovers, puff pancakes, cream puffs, crepes) need wheat starch and gluten to stretch and set into a thin shell; almond flour is too heavy and oily to puff.

recipes.title: Banana Pancakes
recipes.how: 1 cup flour (lower-carb option: 3/4 cup + 2 tbsp. blanched almond flour + 1 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 1 tbsp. baking powder 2 tsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tsp. sugar (in place of 1 tbsp. sugar) 1/2 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. ground cinnamon 1 egg 1 large ripe banana, mashed 1 cup milk Butter, for the griddle 1. Combine the flour, baking powder, sweetener, salt, and cinnamon in a medium bowl. Add the egg, mashed banana, and milk; whisk until just smooth. 2. Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat and butter it well. Pour small circles of batter onto the hot griddle. Cook until the batter begins to bubble, 2 to 3 minutes; flip. Cook an additional 2 to 3 minutes until the other side is lightly browned. These are a nice change of pace from regular pancakes, and make great use of ripe bananas. Yield: 10 medium-sized pancakes Carb level: High-carb (flour batter plus banana) Butter is the griddle fat. It browns the cakes (Maillard) and keeps them from sticking. No seed oils. Wheat flour stays primary. This is a thin chemical-leavened batter; the gluten and starch hold the banana and the bubbles from the baking powder. A full almond-flour swap will not rise or flip the same way. If you want a lower-carb stack, start by swapping only 1/4 cup of the flour for almond flour. Sugar swap: Keep a little real sugar. Those few grams help the cakes spot gold on the griddle. Ripe banana already brings reducing sugar and moisture; the tablespoon of sugar is for color, not sweetness. Use a banana that is spotted and soft. Starch has converted to sugar and it mashes smooth, so the batter stays pourable. Underripe fruit leaves lumps and a starchier pancake. Stop whisking once the dry streaks disappear. Extra mixing develops gluten and makes the cakes tough, especially with mashed banana in the bowl. Lumps are fine. Medium heat is the window. Too hot and the banana sugars scorch before the centers set; too cool and the cakes steam and never brown. Flip when the tops are bubbled and the edges look set — one flip. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Swiss Dip Sandwiches
recipes.how: 2 loaves (8 ounces each) French or Italian bread, sliced in half horizontally 1/4 cup butter 2 pounds thinly sliced cooked roast beef 8 ounces thinly sliced Swiss cheese 1 envelope Lipton Beefy Onion soup mix 2 cups water 1. Heat the oven to 375°F. 2. Spread the butter evenly on the top halves of the bread. On the bottom bread halves, layer the roast beef and top with the cheese; top with the buttered bread halves. Wrap each loaf securely in aluminum foil. Bake 25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, then slice each loaf in quarters. 3. Meanwhile, combine the soup mix and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Pour into 4 individual cups and serve with the sandwiches for dipping. These are better than regular French dip sandwiches and the soup mix makes the best "au jus." Carb level: High-carb (French or Italian bread is the base); beef, Swiss, and jus are low-carb Butter on the cut top halves is the richness and what helps the crust stay tender in the foil instead of drying out. No seed oils. Wheat bread stays primary. These are dip sandwiches; the loaves have to hold two pounds of beef and a melt of Swiss, then stand up to a cup of jus. A full almond-flour loaf will crumble when you quarter it and dissolve in the dip. Foil is the method. Twenty-five minutes at 375°F steams the interior just enough for the Swiss to melt through the beef without toasting the crust hard. Open the packets if you want a drier, crisper top for the last few minutes. Beefy Onion soup mix plus water is the au jus — onion, salt, and beef flavor in ten minutes. Simmer so the powder dissolves and the onion hydrates; a raw boil tastes dusty. Homemade beef broth simmered with a sliced onion and a pinch of salt is the from-scratch stand-in if you do not want the packet. Thin-sliced roast beef and Swiss are the upgrade on a classic French dip (which is usually provolone or nothing). Swiss melts milder and nuttier than cheddar and does not fight the onion jus. Two 8-ounce loaves, quartered, is 8 sandwich pieces for 4 people. Serve the jus in cups on the side so the bread stays intact until you dip. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Meatball Stew
recipes.how: For the meatballs: 1 pound ground beef 1/2 cup dry bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1/2 cup blanched almond flour) 1 egg 1/4 tsp. salt 1/8 tsp. pepper 1 tbsp. butter or avocado oil, for browning For the stew: 5 medium potatoes, peeled and cubed 3 large carrots, peeled and sliced 2 stalks celery, sliced 1 small onion, cut into small chunks 1 tbsp. dried parsley 1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce 2 cups beef broth or water 3 tsp. dry tapioca Salt and pepper to taste 1/4 cup frozen peas 1. Combine the beef, bread crumbs, egg, salt, and pepper; shape into small meatballs. Heat the butter or avocado oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the meatballs; drain. 2. Combine the meatballs and the remaining ingredients except the peas in a small roasting pan and cover with a lid. Cook at 350°F for 3 hours. Stir in the peas the last 10 minutes of cooking time. The meatballs in this stew are a very tasty change of pace from regular beef stew (and more economical). My family just loves it. Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: Moderate-to-high carb (potatoes + bread crumbs + tapioca); meatballs and broth are protein Butter or avocado oil replaces a dry or sprayed skillet so the meatballs actually sear (Maillard) instead of steaming. Drain the fat after browning. No seed oils. Bread crumbs soak up juices and keep the balls soft. For a lower-carb meatball, swap the crumbs for 1/2 cup almond flour — denser, still good in this tomato broth. Wheat crumbs stay if you want the original bready bite. Dry tapioca (not a cornstarch slurry) is the thickener. The granules hydrate over the 3-hour covered bake and give the tomato-broth a light body without a gluey last-minute starch cook. Three teaspoons is a gentle set, not gravy. Three hours at 350°F under a lid is a low oven stew. The potatoes, carrots, and celery go completely tender and the meatballs finish in the sauce. Uncover only to add the peas — ten minutes is enough to heat them through so they stay green instead of turning army drab. Beef broth tastes beefier than water; water works if the tomato sauce and browned drippings are doing the seasoning. Taste for salt at the end — broth and tomato sauce vary. For a lower-carb pot, swap cauliflower florets or turnips for the potatoes and use almond flour in the meatballs. The tomato sauce, onion, and parsley still make it stew. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Beef Barley Stew
recipes.how: 1-1/2 pounds beef stew meat, cut into 1-inch pieces 1 medium onion, chopped 3 medium carrots, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces 2 large potatoes, peeled and cut into small chunks 1 celery rib, thinly sliced 4 cups beef broth 1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce 1 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper 1/2 tsp. dried oregano 1/4 tsp. paprika 1 cup fresh or frozen green beans 1 cup fresh or frozen corn 3/4 cup medium pearl barley 1. Add the beef, onion, carrots, potatoes, celery, broth, tomato sauce, salt, pepper, oregano, and paprika to a 5-quart slow cooker; mix well. Cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours. Add the beans, corn, and barley; cover and cook on low 2 hours longer, or until the barley, beef, and vegetables are tender. 2. To cook this in the oven, add the beef, onion, carrots, potatoes, celery, broth, tomato sauce, and spices to a Dutch oven or roasting pan; mix well. Cover and cook at 325°F for 2-1/2 hours. Stir in the beans, corn, and barley and cook 30 minutes longer, or until the barley, beef, and vegetables are tender. This hearty beef stew recipe has been adapted from a Taste of Home recipe and quickly became a family favorite. The barley is an excellent addition. Yield: 6 to 8 servings Carb level: High-carb (potatoes + pearl barley + corn) No added oil. The long, moist cook renders the stew meat and turns collagen into gelatin, which is the body of the broth. Tomato sauce adds glutamate depth and a little acidity. Pearl barley is the extra starch. It goes in late on purpose — 2 hours in the slow cooker (or 30 minutes in the oven) is enough to swell the grains without turning them to mush. If you add it at the start it will drink the pot dry. Green beans and corn go in with the barley so they stay bright. Frozen is fine; do not thaw first or they go limp. 325°F covered is a pot-roast oven — gentle enough that the beef stays in cubes instead of shredding. The slow-cooker low setting is the same idea over a longer clock. For a lower-carb pot, skip the potatoes, corn, and barley and add extra beef, celery, and green beans (or cauliflower). You will lose the stew’s classic thickness; a spoon of tomato paste helps the broth still feel hearty. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Cashew Chicken Stir-Fry
recipes.how: 2 tbsp. avocado oil 2 cups chicken broth 1/4 cup cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 3 tbsp. soy sauce 1 tbsp. + 2 tsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1 tsp. brown sugar (in place of 2 tbsp. brown sugar) 1/8 tsp. ground ginger 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1/2-inch strips 2 garlic cloves, minced 1/2 cup thinly sliced carrots 1/2 cup sliced celery 3 cups broccoli florets 1 cup fresh or frozen snow peas 1 can (8 ounces) sliced water chestnuts, drained 1-1/2 cups cashews Hot cooked rice, for serving 1. Heat 1 tablespoon of the avocado oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Meanwhile, whisk the cornstarch, soy sauce, sweetener, ginger, and broth until smooth; set aside. 2. Add the chicken to the skillet; stir-fry until no longer pink, about 3 to 5 minutes. Remove and keep warm. 3. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon avocado oil. Add the garlic, carrots, and celery; stir-fry for 3 minutes. Add the broccoli and peas; stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes, or until crisp-tender. Stir the broth mixture; add to the skillet with the chicken and water chestnuts. Cook and stir for 2 minutes, until the sauce thickens and turns glossy. Stir in the cashews. Serve over rice if desired. If you love cashews and Chinese cuisine, you will enjoy this tasty stir-fry dish (modified from Taste of Home). It's very filling and great with rice or noodles. Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: High-carb with rice (sauce plus vegetables are moderate-carb) Avocado oil replaces the original “heat 3 tbsp. of broth” stir-fry, which steamed the chicken instead of searing it. Two tablespoons of oil is enough for a proper wok sear (Maillard) without seed oils. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar. Those molasses grams gloss the sauce and help it cling; cornstarch does the thickening either way. Whisk the slurry until smooth and stir it again before it hits the pan so the starch is not sitting on the bottom. Cornstarch needs a full bubble to set. Two minutes of stirring is enough; longer and the vegetables go soft. High heat, constant motion, crisp-tender vegetables. If the pan crowds, cook the vegetables in two batches so they sear instead of stew. Frozen snow peas can go in still frozen. Cashews go in last so they stay crunchy. Water chestnuts are the snap; drain them well or they dilute the sauce. For a lower-carb plate, serve over cauliflower rice or skip the starch and pile the stir-fry into bowls. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Barbecue Chicken Pizza
recipes.how: For the crust: 3/4 cup warm water (105°F to 115°F) 2 tbsp. butter 1 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 1 tbsp. honey (in place of 2 tbsp. honey) 1 tsp. salt 2 cups all-purpose flour 1-1/2 tsp. active dry yeast Cornmeal, for the pan For the pizza: 2 cups cooked, shredded chicken breast 1/2 cup honey barbecue sauce, divided 2 tbsp. butter 1 medium red or purple onion, cut in half and sliced into thin pieces 1 clove garlic, minced 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese 1/2 cup shredded Gouda cheese 1. For the crust, use a bread machine set on the dough setting, adding the ingredients to the pan in the order listed. Or, dissolve the yeast in the warm water (105°F to 115°F). Add the butter, honey, salt, and flour. Mix until the dough forms a ball. Turn onto a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic. Place in a greased bowl, turning to grease the top. Cover; let rise in a warm place, free from draft, until doubled in bulk, about 1 hour. Punch down the dough and roll or pat into a 12- or 14-inch circle. Place on a cornmeal-dusted pizza pan. 2. Heat the oven to 450°F. Coat the chicken with 2 tablespoons of the barbecue sauce; set aside. 3. Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a sauté pan over medium heat. Sauté the onions and garlic in the butter, stirring occasionally, until the onions are brown and caramelized, about 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the chicken. 4. Spread the remaining barbecue sauce over the pizza dough. Top with half of the cheeses. Spread on the chicken mixture. Top with the remaining cheeses. 5. Bake in the heated oven for 15 to 18 minutes, until the crust is lightly browned and the cheese is completely melted. Let the pizza sit for 5 minutes before slicing. Now you can make a delicious barbecue chicken pizza like a gourmet pizzeria would serve in the convenience of your own home for a fraction of the cost. The caramelized onions are definitely the crowning touch. Yield: 1 (12- or 14-inch) pizza Carb level: High-carb (yeast wheat crust + honey barbecue sauce) Wheat flour stays primary. This is a real pizza crust; a full almond-flour swap will not stretch, rise, or crisp at 450°F. Butter is the fat in the dough and in the onion pan. Grease the rise bowl with butter or olive oil. No seed oils. Sugar swap: Keep most of the honey in the crust. Yeast uses some of it as food, it is hygroscopic (it holds water) so the crumb stays tender, and those grams help the edge brown (Maillard). Do not swap the entire 2 tablespoons for monk fruit. Water at 105°F to 115°F wakes the yeast without killing it. Cooler water and the rise stalls; hotter water kills the yeast and you get a dense disc. The 15-minute onion cook is the point of the pizza. Medium heat and butter slowly brown the onion sugars; rush it and you get fried onion, not caramel. Stir the sauced chicken in off the heat so it does not dry out. Cornmeal on the pan keeps the bottom from gluing down so it can dry and crisp. 450°F is hot on purpose — 15 to 18 minutes browns the crust before the barbecue sauce waters it. Rest 5 minutes so the cheese sets and the slices come out clean. Honey barbecue sauce already carries sugar; monk fruit will not replace that. Cheese goes half under and half over the chicken so the topping does not slide. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour is the best for this recipe because: the gluten network is what traps the yeast's gas and gives the rise and chew; almond and coconut flour have no gluten, so the dough cannot rise or stretch.

recipes.title: Cinnamon-Nutmeg French Toast
recipes.how: 5 eggs 1/2 cup milk 1/2 tsp. vanilla extract 1/2 tsp. ground cinnamon 1/4 tsp. ground nutmeg 1 loaf (16 ounces) sliced Italian or French bread (1/4 to 1/2-inch thick) Butter, for the griddle (in place of nonstick spray) Sugar-free monk fruit maple syrup (in place of maple syrup, for serving) 1. In a shallow dish, beat the eggs with the milk, vanilla, cinnamon, and nutmeg. 2. Dip the bread slices into the egg mixture to coat both sides, letting the excess drip off. 3. Heat a griddle over medium heat and butter it well. Cook the slices until golden brown on both sides. 4. Serve warm with syrup. This is a simple but absolutely delicious French toast recipe. The nutmeg adds the perfect touch! Yield: 6 to 8 servings Carb level: High-carb (French or Italian bread, plus syrup) Butter replaces nonstick spray on the griddle. The milk-fat browns the custard (Maillard) and keeps the toast from sticking. No seed oils. Wheat bread stays primary. This is French toast — the crumb has to soak up egg and still hold a slice. A full almond-flour loaf will crumble in the dip. Day-old or slightly stale bread soaks without falling apart; very fresh bread turns soggy. Do not soak the slices. A quick dip on both sides is enough. Sitting in the bowl makes the centers wet and the outsides pale. Medium heat is the window.
