Too hot and the spices scorch before the egg sets; too cool and the toast steams and never crisps. Sugar swap: Nutmeg is the difference here — a little goes a long way and reads as “bakery” next to the cinnamon. Real maple syrup if you want the classic plate; monk fruit or sugar-free syrup drops the sugar without changing the toast. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this French toast. Low-carb or almond-flour bread is more fragile and less absorbent than a French loaf, so the slices tear in the egg dip and cook up denser and eggier instead of crisp-edged with a custardy middle.

recipes.title: Ham and Beans
recipes.how: 1 bag (16 ounces) great northern beans 1/2 pound diced cooked ham 1 small onion, diced 1/3 cup packed brown sugar (a large handful; or 3 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tbsp. brown sugar) Salt and pepper to taste Dash cayenne pepper 1 tbsp. dried parsley Water 1. Rinse and sort the beans in a large pot. Add 8 cups cold water. Let stand overnight, or at least 8 hours. Drain and rinse the beans. 2. Return the beans to the pot and add the ham, onion, brown sugar, salt, pepper, cayenne, and parsley. Generously cover with water. 3. Bring to a boil; reduce the heat and simmer 1-1/2 to 2 hours, until the beans are tender. Add more water if needed during cooking, and reseason with salt, pepper, and brown sugar to taste. This is my Mom's recipe and it's soooo good! One might think water makes it bland, but this dish is far from bland. The ham, brown sugar and spices add just the right seasoning. Yield: 6 to 8 servings Carb level: High-carb (a full pound of beans plus brown sugar); ham and onion are not the carb No added oil. The ham’s fat is enough to carry the brown sugar and spices. No seed oils. Soaking hydrates the beans so they cook evenly and shortens the simmer. A quick-soak works if you forgot overnight: cover with water, boil 2 minutes, take off the heat, and stand 1 hour; drain and continue. Keep a little real brown sugar if you use monk fruit. The molasses is the flavor next to the ham — monk fruit sweetens but will not give that same round, smoky-sweet pot-liquor. A large handful is about 1/3 cup packed. The long simmer lets starches thicken the broth and gives the ham time to season the beans. Water is not bland here; it is the medium that pulls salt, smoke, and sugar through every bean. A leftover ham bone in the pot adds even more body. Taste at the end — beans drink salt, so you often need another pinch plus a little more brown sugar. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Almond Pork Stir-Fry with Couscous
recipes.how: For the sauce: 2 cups chicken broth 1/4 cup cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 3 tbsp. soy sauce 2 tbsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 3 tbsp. packed brown sugar) 1/8 tsp. ground ginger For the stir-fry: 2 tbsp. avocado oil, divided (in place of vegetable oil) 1 pound pork tenderloin, cut into 1/2-inch strips 2 garlic cloves, minced 1 bag (16 ounces) fresh broccoli and cauliflower florets 1 large carrot, bias-sliced in 1/2-inch pieces 1 can (8 ounces) sliced water chestnuts, drained 1/2 cup sliced almonds For serving: Hot cooked couscous 1. Whisk the broth, cornstarch, soy sauce, brown sugar, and ginger until smooth; set aside. 2. In a large sauté pan or wok, heat 1 tablespoon of the oil over medium-high heat. Add the pork and stir-fry until no longer pink, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove and keep warm. 3. Heat the remaining oil. Add the garlic, broccoli, cauliflower, and carrot; stir-fry 7 to 8 minutes, until crisp-tender (add a splash of water if the pan gets too dry). 4. Stir the broth mixture and add it to the skillet with the pork and water chestnuts. Cook and stir 2 minutes, until the sauce thickens and turns glossy. Stir in the almonds. Serve over couscous. Couscous is a nice twist with stir-fry. Cashews would also be delicious with this dish. Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: High-carb (couscous plus a cornstarch-thickened, brown-sugar sauce) Avocado oil replaces vegetable oil. It handles wok heat and stays seed-oil-free. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar. Those molasses sugars help the sauce glaze and caramelize on the pork (Maillard). Monk fruit sweetens but will not brown. Cornstarch needs a full boil to thicken and turn clear — two minutes of stirring after it hits the pan is the set. Whisk the slurry again just before it goes in; starch settles. High heat, constant motion, crisp-tender vegetables. If the pan crowds, cook the vegetables in two batches so they sear instead of stew. Almonds go in last so they stay crunchy. Cashews are excellent here too. For a lower-carb plate, serve the stir-fry over cauliflower rice or in bowls without couscous. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Bacon, Egg & Potato Casserole
recipes.how: 1/2 pound bacon 1 small onion, diced 1/4 cup diced green pepper 12 eggs 1 cup milk 1 package (16 ounces) frozen hash brown potatoes, thawed 1 cup shredded sharp Cheddar cheese 1 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. pepper Pinch paprika Butter, for the dish 1. Cook the bacon until crisp; crumble and set aside. Pour off all but about 1 tablespoon of the drippings. 2. In the reserved drippings, sauté the onion and green pepper until tender; remove with a slotted spoon. 3. Beat the eggs and milk in a large bowl. Stir in the hash browns, cheese, salt, pepper, paprika, onion, green pepper, and bacon. Transfer to a buttered 13x9-inch baking dish. 4. Bake, uncovered, at 350°F for 40 to 45 minutes, or until the center is set and the top is golden. This makes a terrific breakfast, brunch or dinner dish. We enjoy breakfast dinners a couple of times a month and this filling casserole fits the bill just perfectly! Yield: 6 to 8 servings Carb level: High-carb (hash browns are the starch); the egg-and-cheese custard is moderate Bacon drippings sauté the onion and pepper, and butter greases the dish. That is the fat — no seed oils, no spray. Thaw the hash browns so they do not ice the custard. Twelve eggs plus 1 cup milk is a classic breakfast-casserole set; the potatoes and cheese give it body so it slices. Paprika is mostly color on top, with a little sweetness. Sharp cheddar stands up to the bacon. The casserole is done when the center no longer jiggles and a knife near the middle comes out clean. Rest 5 to 10 minutes so it cuts in squares instead of slumping. This can be assembled, covered, and refrigerated overnight. Bake as directed — cold from the fridge may need an extra 5 to 10 minutes. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Blueberry Sour Cream Pancakes
recipes.how: 2 cups flour (lower-carb option: 1-3/4 cups blanched almond flour + 2 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 1 tbsp. + 1/2 tsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tsp. sugar (in place of 1-1/2 tbsp. sugar) 1 tbsp. baking powder 1/4 tsp. salt 2 eggs 1-1/2 cups milk 1/3 cup sour cream 3 tbsp. melted butter 3/4 cup fresh or frozen blueberries Butter, for the griddle (in place of nonstick spray) Golden monk fruit blend and vanilla, for serving (in place of blueberry syrup and/or sour cream sweetened with brown sugar) 1. Combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Stir in the eggs, milk, sour cream, and melted butter just until combined, then fold in the blueberries last. 2. Heat a griddle over medium heat and butter it well. Ladle the batter onto the hot griddle. Cook until the underside is brown and the top begins to bubble. Turn and cook until done. This recipe makes wonderful blueberry pancakes, especially served with blueberry syrup and/or sour cream sweetened with brown sugar and vanilla. My kids, however, continue to prefer plain pancakes and upon request would only eat the plain variety. They don't know what they're missing! Yield: 12 to 14 large pancakes (about 6 servings) Carb level: High-carb (flour pancakes, plus syrup if you use it) Melted butter is in the batter; more butter is the griddle fat. It browns the cakes (Maillard) and keeps them from sticking. No seed oils, no spray. Wheat flour stays primary. These are real pancakes — gluten plus baking powder is the lift. A full almond-flour swap will not rise or flip the same way. A spoon of almond flour can stand in for a spoon of wheat if you want a nuttier crumb. Sugar swap: Keep a little real sugar in the batter. Those grams help the cakes spot gold on the griddle. Sour cream is the tenderness: fat plus acid, which also wakes up the baking powder. Stop stirring the moment the dry streaks disappear, then fold the berries. Extra mixing develops gluten and makes the pancakes tough. Frozen blueberries go in frozen so they do not bleed purple through the batter. Medium heat is the window. Too hot and the sugar scorches before the centers set; too cool and the cakes steam and never brown. Flip once, when the tops are bubbled and the edges look dry. The kids’ plain version is the same batter without berries. The brown-sugar sour cream on top is worth making — keep a little real brown sugar in it for flavor even if you sweeten the rest with monk fruit. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Chicken Wild Rice Casserole
recipes.how: 1 small onion, diced 1 stalk celery, sliced 1 large clove garlic, minced 3 tbsp. butter 3 cups cooked wild rice 2 cups cooked, diced chicken 1 can (4 ounces) sliced mushrooms, drained 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup, undiluted 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed cream of chicken soup, undiluted 1 cup water 1 tsp. chicken bouillon granules 1/4 tsp. pepper 1/4 cup sliced almonds Butter, for the dish 1. Sauté the onion, celery, and garlic in the butter over medium heat until the onion and celery are soft. Heat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a 2-quart casserole dish with butter. 2. Combine the rice, chicken, mushrooms, sautéed onion mixture, soups, water, bouillon, pepper, and almonds; pour into the prepared casserole dish. 3. Cover the dish; bake for 45 minutes. Uncover and bake 15 minutes longer. This is a super tasty casserole and a great way to use up leftover chicken or turkey. Carb level: High-carb (wild rice + condensed soups) Butter is the sauté fat and the dish grease. No seed oils. Many canned cream soups are built on seed oils — use a brand without them, or swap each can for about 1-1/4 cups homemade cream-of-chicken or cream-of-mushroom (butter, flour, broth, and a splash of cream). Wild rice is the starch. It is already cooked, so the hour in the oven is only to heat the casserole through and let the soup sauce soak the grains. Turkey stands in for the chicken with no other change. Drain the canned mushrooms. Their packing liquid thins the sauce you just built. The 1 cup water plus bouillon loosens the undiluted soups so the bake is creamy, not paste. Cover for the first 45 minutes so the top does not dry before the center is hot. Uncover the last 15 so the almonds toast and the surface loses its steam. Sauté the onion, celery, and garlic first. Raw onion in a soup-sauce bake stays sharp; the butter sauté sweetens it and is the aroma of the dish. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: thicken with a little arrowroot slurry instead of flour/cornstarch; swap rice for cauliflower rice.

recipes.title: Vanilla French Toast
recipes.how: 5 eggs 1/2 cup milk 2 tbsp. vanilla extract 1/4 tsp. ground cinnamon 1 loaf (16 ounces) sliced Italian or French bread (1/4 to 1/2-inch thick) Butter, for the griddle Sugar-free monk fruit maple syrup, for serving (in place of maple syrup) Fresh berries, optional 1. In a shallow dish, beat the eggs with the milk, vanilla, and cinnamon. Dip the bread slices into the egg mixture to coat both sides, letting the excess drip off. 2. Cook on a hot griddle buttered generously until the French toast is golden brown on both sides. Serve warm with sugar-free maple syrup and berries, if you like. This is just as yummy as the title indicates. Superb with butter flavored syrup and/or fresh berries. Yield: 6 to 8 servings Carb level: High-carb (a whole loaf of bread; the custard is eggs and milk) Butter on the griddle replaces nonstick spray. The milk-fat browns the custard (Maillard) and keeps the toast from sticking. No seed oils. Real maple syrup replaces butter-flavored pancake syrup, which is usually corn syrup and seed oil. Wheat bread stays. Italian or French loaf is the structure — 1/4- to 1/2-inch slices soak without falling apart. Almond-flour bread will shred in the egg bath. Two tablespoons of vanilla is the point of the title, not a typo. That much extract is the flavor; cinnamon is just a background note. Do not cut it back or you will have plain French toast. A quick dip, both sides, then drip. A long soak turns thin bakery slices to mush and they tear on the flip. Medium-hot griddle: the egg needs time to set through the slice before the outside burns. One loaf feeds a table. Leftover slices reheat in a toaster or a hot buttered skillet better than the microwave, which steams the crust soft. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend; swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.) Sugar swap: The sugar-free version sets with the same gelatin or starch, so it is a 1:1 package swap. Heads up: the lower-carb swaps will change the character of this French toast. Low-carb or almond-flour bread is more fragile and less absorbent than a French loaf, so the slices tear in the egg dip and cook up denser and eggier instead of crisp-edged with a custardy middle.

recipes.title: Hamburger Stroganoff
recipes.how: 1 to 1-1/2 pounds lean ground beef 1 small onion, chopped 2 cloves garlic, minced 1-1/2 cups beef broth 1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms 1/2 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. pepper 2/3 cup sour cream 2 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) Hot cooked egg noodles 1. Brown the meat, onion, and garlic in a large skillet; drain off the fat. Stir in the broth, mushrooms, salt, and pepper. Cook over medium-low heat until the mushrooms are tender. 2. Combine the sour cream and flour; whisk into the skillet and heat until the sauce is thickened, about 5 minutes. Do not boil. Serve over egg noodles. When time is of the essence, or we just want a change of pace, I'll fix this delicious stroganoff instead of traditional Beef Stroganoff. It's quite delicious and takes less than 30 minutes to prepare! Carb level: High-carb on the plate (egg noodles); the stroganoff itself is Moderate-carb (a little flour plus sour cream) The ground beef is the fat and the browning. Drain the extra so the sauce is silky, not greasy. No seed oils. Butter the noodles if you want a little gloss. Wheat flour stays in the 2 tablespoons that thicken the sauce, and in the egg noodles. The flour is whisked into cold sour cream first so it does not lump when it hits the hot skillet. A full almond-flour swap will not gel the same way; if you want a lower-carb plate, keep the sauce and serve it over zucchini ribbons or cauliflower instead of noodles. Do not boil after the sour cream goes in. Sour cream is a dairy emulsion; a hard boil curdles the proteins and the sauce looks grainy. Medium-low, about 5 minutes, just until it coats a spoon. This is weeknight stroganoff — ground beef instead of strips of steak — so it is on the table in under 30 minutes. The mushrooms cook in the broth after the meat is browned; they do not need a separate pan. Taste the salt after the broth reduces. Bouillon-style broths vary; you may not need the full 1/2 teaspoon. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Oven Buttermilk Fried Chicken
recipes.how: For the chicken: 8 to 9 chicken pieces, legs, thighs, and breasts 1 cup buttermilk For the pan: 1/3 cup avocado oil (in place of vegetable oil) 1/3 cup butter For the coating: 1 cup flour (lower-carb option: 3/4 cup + 2 tbsp. blanched almond flour + 1 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 2 tsp. pepper 1 tsp. salt 1 tsp. garlic salt 1/2 tsp. paprika 1. Place the chicken pieces in a large, shallow pan; pour the buttermilk over and turn the pieces to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for two hours. 2. Place the avocado oil and butter in a shallow pan (a jelly-roll pan is perfect) and put in a heated 375°F oven to melt. Set aside. 3. In a large paper sack or plastic bag, combine the flour and seasonings. Drain the chicken and pat dry. Roll the chicken pieces, 3 at a time, in the melted oil-butter mixture, then drop them into the sack and shake to cover. Place on a dish or wax paper. 4. Place the coated chicken in the pan, skin side down. Bake for 45 minutes. With a spatula, turn the chicken over and bake 5 to 10 minutes longer, or until the top crust begins to bubble. This is one of the best fried chicken recipes I have tried. It comes slightly altered from one of my very favorite cookbooks, Cooking From Quilt Country by Marcia Adams. I highly recommend her books. Yield: 4 to 5 servings Carb level: Moderate-carb (a flour crust on bone-in pieces); the chicken itself is low-carb Avocado oil plus butter replace vegetable oil and butter in the pan. Both handle 375°F without seed oils. The melted fat is the “fry” — you roll the chicken in it before the flour, then bake it in the same pan so the coating fries in the oven instead of a skillet. Wheat flour stays in the cup of dredge. It is what crisps. A full almond-flour swap will brown faster and can taste pasty; if you want a lower-carb crust, start by swapping only 1/4 to 1/2 cup of the flour for almond flour and watch the last 10 minutes. Buttermilk is the marinade, not a wash. Two hours in the fridge lets the lactic acid tenderize the meat and gives the flour something to grab once you pat the pieces dry. Skip the soak and the crust sheds. Three at a time in the bag so the pieces coat instead of steaming in a wad of flour. Skin side down first renders fat into the pan; the flip for the last 5 to 10 minutes is when the top crust bubbles and finishes. Do not crowd — use a jelly-roll pan so the pieces sit in one layer. This is Marcia Adams’s Quilt Country method, slightly altered. Bone-in legs, thighs, and breasts stay juicier than tenders in a 45-minute oven fry. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Apple-Nut Hot Cakes
recipes.how: 1-1/2 cups flour (lower-carb option: 1-1/4 cups + 1 tbsp. blanched almond flour + 1-1/2 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 1/3 cup ground pecans 2 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tbsp. sugar (in place of 3 tbsp. sugar) 1 tbsp. baking powder 3/4 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. ground cinnamon 1-1/2 cups milk 5 tbsp. melted butter 2 egg whites 1/2 cup shredded, peeled apple Butter, for the griddle Maple syrup, for serving 1. In a large bowl, combine the flour, pecans, sweetener, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon. Stir in the milk and melted butter until just combined. Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form; fold into the batter with the apple. 2. Pour the batter by 1/4 cupfuls onto a hot, buttered griddle. Cook until bubbles form on top and the underside is golden brown. Flip and cook until the second side is golden. Serve warm with maple syrup. These apple beauties are so light and tender and full of good, downhome flavor. Treat the apple of your eye with this delicious breakfast treat sometime! =) Yield: 18 pancakes Carb level: High-carb (flour batter + apple + syrup) Melted butter is the fat in the batter; more butter on the griddle browns the cakes (Maillard) and keeps them from sticking. No seed oils. Pecans are the nut, not a frying oil. Wheat flour stays primary. This is a chemical-leavened hot-cake batter lifted further by stiff egg whites; a full almond-flour swap will not hold that foam or flip the same way. If you want a lower-carb stack, start by swapping only 1/4 to 1/2 cup of the flour for almond flour. Sugar swap: Keep a little real sugar. Those grams help the cakes spot gold on the griddle. Monk fruit will not replace the maple syrup on top. The whites are why these are light. Beat them to stiff peaks and fold — do not stir — so the air stays in the batter. Stop mixing the milk and butter the moment the dry streaks disappear; extra gluten makes the cakes tough and knocks the whites down. Shredded apple (not chunks) cooks through in the time it takes the cakes to brown. Squeeze it lightly if it is very juicy so the batter does not thin. Medium heat: too hot and the sugar and nuts scorch before the centers set. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Oatmeal Pancakes
recipes.how: For the overnight soak: 2 cups old-fashioned rolled oats 2 cups buttermilk For the batter: 1/2 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 cup + 3 tbsp. blanched almond flour + 1/2 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 1/2 cup whole wheat flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 cup + 3 tbsp. blanched almond flour + 1/2 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 2 tsp. monk fruit baking blend (in place of 2 tsp. sugar) 1-1/2 tsp. baking powder 1-1/2 tsp. baking soda 1 tsp. salt 2 eggs 2 tbsp. butter, melted and cooled 2 to 4 tbsp. additional buttermilk, as needed Butter, for the griddle Maple syrup, for serving 1. Partially prepare the batter the night before. In a small bowl, combine the oatmeal and 2 cups of the buttermilk. Cover and refrigerate overnight. 2. The next morning, sift together the flours, sweetener, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; set aside (you can also do this the night before to save time in the morning). 3. In a large mixer bowl, beat the eggs until frothy. Add the butter and blend, then add the oatmeal mixture. Quickly blend in the flour mixture. The batter will be very thick; add 2 to 4 more tablespoons of buttermilk if needed, but not more than that. 4. Heat a buttered griddle to 350°F. Drop a large spoonful of batter on the hot griddle and pat it down a bit. The pancakes will be about 3/4 inch thick, and will puff up when turned over. Serve with warmed maple syrup. These hearty pancakes are a tasty change of pace and perfect for Saturday morning breakfast. They're excellent served with maple syrup. These come from one of my favorite cookbooks, Cooking from Quilt Country by Marcia Adams and I highly recommend her books. Note: You must start the batter the night before serving. Yield: 16 pancakes Carb level: High-carb (oats + two flours + buttermilk + syrup) Butter in the batter and butter on the griddle replace nonstick spray. The milk-fat browns the cakes (Maillard) and keeps them from sticking. No seed oils. Wheat stays primary — 1/2 cup all-purpose plus 1/2 cup whole wheat, with oats as the body. This is a Quilt Country griddle cake, not an almond-flour flapjack. A full almond-flour swap will not hold a 3/4-inch cake or puff on the flip. If you want a slightly lower-carb batch, swap only the 1/2 cup all-purpose for almond flour and keep the whole wheat and oats. Sugar swap: Keep a little real sugar. Those few grams help the crust color. Monk fruit will not replace the maple syrup. The overnight soak is not optional. Oats drink the buttermilk while you sleep so the cakes cook tender instead of dry and grainy. Baking soda plus the acid in the buttermilk is the lift — mix the dry in quickly in the morning so the bubbles do not spend themselves in the bowl. The batter is supposed to be thick. Two to 4 extra tablespoons of buttermilk is the most you should add; more and the cakes will not stand 3/4 inch tall. Pat each spoonful down on a 350°F griddle. They puff on the turn. This is another Marcia Adams keeper. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Grilled Apricot Chicken
recipes.how: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts 1/2 cup apricot jam (or 1/4 cup apricot jam + 2 tbsp. monk fruit sweetener) 1 tbsp. white wine* 1/8 tsp. coarse ground pepper Pinch salt Salt and pepper, for the chicken 1. Lightly sprinkle the chicken breasts with salt and pepper; set aside. 2. Heat the grill over medium-hot coals. In a small saucepan, melt the jam, breaking up any large chunks of fruit. Stir in the wine, pepper, and salt until the mixture is smooth. 3. Grill the chicken over the prepared coals until cooked through, brushing with the apricot glaze during the last half of cooking. Serve extra glaze on the side. This simple yet elegant recipe will surely become a dinnertime staple come summer. It takes less than 30 minutes to prepare and the taste is superior. Carb level: Moderate-carb (apricot jam is the sugar; the chicken is protein). Using half jam and monk fruit drops it toward Moderate-low. No seed oils. The glaze is jam thinned with wine; if the chicken sticks, brush the grates with avocado oil or melted butter, not vegetable oil. Keep at least 1/4 cup real jam if you use monk fruit. Jam is pectin plus sugar — that is the body and the gloss of the glaze. Monk fruit sweetens but will not reduce into a coat that clings. Sugar-free apricot preserves can stand in for the full 1/2 cup if you want it leaner; expect a thinner glaze. Brush only during the last half of cooking. Fruit sugar burns on a hot grate if it sits there the whole time. The last minutes are enough for the glaze to set and spot gold (Maillard) without turning bitter. Medium-hot coals, not a raging fire. Boneless breasts cook through in about 6 to 8 minutes per side, depending on thickness. Pull them at 165°F in the thickest part and rest a few minutes so the juices settle. *Useful tip: or use any liquid such as water, broth, soy sauce, or melted butter in place of the wine. A tablespoon is just enough to loosen the jam so it brushes. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb. Pairs with: Carrot Soup

recipes.title: Hearty Chicken and Noodles
recipes.how: 3 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts 2 cups chicken broth 2 cups water 1/3 cup chopped celery leaves 1 medium onion, chopped 2 tbsp. snipped parsley (or 1 tbsp. dried) 1 bay leaf 1 tsp. salt 1/2 tsp. dried thyme 1/2 tsp. garlic powder 1/4 tsp. poultry seasoning 1/4 tsp. pepper 2 cups sliced, peeled carrots 1 cup sliced celery 3 cups packaged dried wide noodles 2 cups milk, divided 1 cup frozen peas 4 tbsp. flour 1. In a 4-1/2-quart Dutch oven, place the chicken, broth, water, celery leaves, onion, parsley, bay leaf, salt, thyme, garlic powder, poultry seasoning, and pepper. Bring to a boil; reduce the heat. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes. Add the carrots and sliced celery. Cover and simmer about 20 minutes more, or until the chicken and vegetables are tender. Remove from the heat. Remove the chicken; cool slightly. Chop the chicken and set aside. Discard the bay leaf. 2. Bring the vegetable mixture back to a boil. Add the noodles; cook for 5 minutes. Stir in 1-1/2 cups of the milk and the peas. Whisk together the remaining 1/2 cup milk and the flour. Stir into the noodle mixture. Cook and stir until thickened and bubbly. Stir in the chicken. Cook 1 to 2 minutes more, or until heated through. This is soooo good! Serve it with bread or rolls for a complete meal. Carb level: High-carb (wide noodles + a flour-thickened milk sauce) No frying fat and no seed oils. The chicken simmers in broth and water; the richness is milk and the bird. Butter the bread or rolls on the side if you serve them. Wheat egg noodles stay primary. This is chicken and noodles. Zucchini ribbons will go limp in the boil and will not give you the same stew. For a lower-carb bowl, use half the noodles and extra chicken and vegetables. The flour slurry is the gravy. Cold milk plus flour, whisked smooth, then cooked to a full bubble so the starch gelatinizes and the sauce turns glossy. Do not dump dry flour into the hot pot or it lumps. Almond flour will not thicken this; keep the 4 tablespoons of wheat. Simmer the chicken first so the broth tastes like chicken, then the carrots and celery so they stay tender, not mush. Pull the bay leaf before the noodles go in. Frozen peas go in with the milk so they heat through without turning army green. Noodles cook in the finished broth so they taste like stew, not water. Five minutes is right for wide dried noodles; thinner ones will need less. Stir in the chopped chicken at the end so it does not shred to bits. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour is the best for this recipe because: noodles and dumplings need gluten to roll thin and hold together in boiling liquid; low-carb flours fall apart in the pot.

recipes.title: Barbecue Ham Pizza
recipes.how: For the crust: 3/4 cup warm water (105°F to 115°F) 2 tbsp. butter 1 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 1 tbsp. honey (in place of 2 tbsp. honey) 1 tsp. salt 2 cups all-purpose flour 1-1/2 tsp. active dry yeast Cornmeal, for the pan For the pizza: 2 cups cooked, diced ham 1/2 cup honey barbecue sauce, divided 2 tbsp. butter 1 medium red or purple onion, cut in half and sliced into thin pieces 1 clove garlic, minced 1 can (8-1/4 ounces) pineapple tidbits, drained 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese 1/2 cup shredded Gouda cheese Dried parsley 1. For the crust, use a bread machine set on the dough setting, adding the ingredients to the pan in the order listed. Or, dissolve the yeast in the warm water (105°F to 115°F). Add the butter, honey, salt, and flour. Mix until the dough forms a ball. Turn onto a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic. Place in a greased bowl, turning to grease the top. Cover; let rise in a warm place, free from draft, until doubled in bulk, about 1 hour. Punch down the dough and roll or pat into a 12- or 14-inch circle. Place on a cornmeal-dusted pizza pan. 2. Heat the oven to 450°F. Coat the ham with 2 tablespoons of the barbecue sauce; set aside. 3. Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a sauté pan over medium heat. Sauté the onions and garlic in the butter, stirring occasionally, until the onions are brown and caramelized, about 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the ham and pineapple. 4. Spread the remaining barbecue sauce over the pizza dough. Top with half of the cheeses. Spread on the ham mixture. Top with the remaining cheeses. Sprinkle with dried parsley. 5. Bake in the heated oven for 15 to 18 minutes, until the crust is lightly browned and the cheese is completely melted. Let the pizza sit for 5 minutes before slicing. Turn that leftover ham into a delicious pizza! Yield: 1 (12- or 14-inch) pizza Carb level: High-carb (yeast wheat crust + honey barbecue sauce + pineapple) Wheat flour stays primary. This is a real pizza crust; a full almond-flour swap will not stretch, rise, or crisp at 450°F. Butter is the fat in the dough and in the onion pan. Grease the rise bowl with butter or olive oil. No seed oils. Sugar swap: Keep most of the honey in the crust. Yeast uses some of it as food, it is hygroscopic (it holds water) so the crumb stays tender, and those grams help the edge brown (Maillard). Do not swap the entire 2 tablespoons for monk fruit. Water at 105°F to 115°F wakes the yeast without killing it. Cooler water and the rise stalls; hotter water kills the yeast and you get a dense disc. The 15-minute onion cook is the point of the pizza. Medium heat and butter slowly brown the onion sugars; rush it and you get fried onion, not caramel. Stir the sauced ham and drained pineapple in off the heat so the ham does not dry out and the pineapple does not water the pan. Drain the pineapple well. Extra juice soaks the crust. Cornmeal on the pan keeps the bottom from gluing down so it can dry and crisp. 450°F is hot on purpose — 15 to 18 minutes browns the crust before the barbecue sauce waters it. Rest 5 minutes so the cheese sets and the slices come out clean. Honey barbecue sauce already carries sugar; monk fruit will not replace that. Cheese goes half under and half over the ham so the topping does not slide. Gouda is the smoky note next to the ham. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour is the best for this recipe because: the gluten network is what traps the yeast's gas and gives the rise and chew; almond and coconut flour have no gluten, so the dough cannot rise or stretch.

recipes.title: Grilled Sausages with Apricot Mustard
recipes.how: For the apricot mustard: 1/2 cup apricot preserves (or 1/4 cup apricot preserves + 2 tbsp. monk fruit sweetener) 1/3 cup Dijon mustard Pinch salt and pepper For the sausages: 1 pound Italian sausages (such as Johnsonville)* 1. Prepare the grill for direct grilling. Combine the preserves, mustard, salt, and pepper in a small bowl; mix well. 2. Grill the sausages over medium-hot coals for 20 minutes, turning once. Baste with the preserve mixture and continue grilling 3 minutes more, turning once, or until the sausage is lightly browned and cooked through. Serve with the remaining preserve mixture for dipping. This is just soooo good! Perfect when you want a change of pace on the grill. Carb level: Moderate-carb (apricot preserves are the sugar; sausage and mustard are protein and fat). Using half preserves and monk fruit drops it toward Moderate-low. No seed oils. If the sausages stick, brush the grates with avocado oil or a little melted butter, not vegetable oil. Keep at least 1/4 cup real preserves if you use monk fruit. Preserves are fruit, pectin, and sugar — that is the body of the dip and the glaze. Monk fruit sweetens but will not cling or gloss the same way. Sugar-free apricot preserves can stand in for the full 1/2 cup; expect a thinner sauce. Dijon’s acid and mustard seed cut the sweet so the glaze is not candy. Mix the mustard and preserves until smooth before they hit the grill. Baste only for the last 3 minutes. Fruit sugar burns on a hot grate if it sits there the whole 20. The last pass is enough for the glaze to set and spot gold (Maillard) without turning bitter. Serve the rest as a cold dip. Medium-hot coals, not a raging fire. Twenty minutes, turning once, cooks a raw Italian sausage through; pull them at 160°F in the center. *Useful tip: or use smoked sausage cut into desired sizes and cut the grilling time in half — it is already cooked, so you are just heating and glazing. Carb rating (Moderate): Notes mark this as moderate-carb.

recipes.title: Chicken Pecan Pitas
recipes.how: For the filling: 3 cups cubed, cooked chicken 1 can (8-1/4 ounces) crushed pineapple, drained 1/2 cup chopped pecans 1/2 cup finely chopped celery 1/4 cup minced onion For the dressing: 1/2 cup avocado oil mayonnaise (in place of regular mayonnaise) 2 tbsp. sour cream 1/2 tsp. Dijon mustard 1/2 tsp. salt 1/8 tsp. cayenne pepper 1/8 tsp. paprika For serving: 4 whole pitas, cut in half Large lettuce leaves 1. In a medium bowl, combine the chicken, pineapple, pecans, celery, and onion. 2. In another bowl, combine the avocado oil mayonnaise, sour cream, mustard, salt, cayenne, and paprika until creamy. Pour over the chicken mixture and toss gently. 3. Line each pita pocket with a large lettuce leaf. Gently stuff about 1/2 cup of the chicken mixture into each pita pocket half. These are great when you have leftover chicken to use up. Perfect in the summer when you don't want to fuss with a hot kitchen, too! Yield: 4 whole pitas (8 halves) Carb level: High-carb with the pitas (the chicken salad itself is Moderate-carb from pineapple). Lettuce wraps drop the plate to Moderate-low. Avocado oil mayonnaise replaces regular mayo so the dressing is seed-oil-free. Sour cream adds lactic tang and body so the dressing clings instead of sliding off the chicken. Drain the crushed pineapple well. Extra juice thins the emulsion and makes the pitas soggy by the time you sit down. Cayenne and paprika are the warmth — a little heat next to the sweet pineapple. Dijon is the acid that keeps the dressing from tasting flat. The original step said “pepper”; the ingredient list is cayenne, and that is what belongs here. Add the pecans with the chicken so they get a light coat of dressing, but do not make this hours ahead or they soften. Toast them first if you want more roast flavor. The lettuce leaf is not just garnish. It is a moisture barrier so the pita does not turn to paste. Wheat pitas stay primary if you want the sandwich; for a lower-carb plate, pile the salad on extra lettuce and skip the bread. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread.

recipes.title: Steak in Pepper Cream
recipes.how: 1/4 tsp. salt 2 (12-ounce) New York strip steaks (3/4-inch thick) 2 tbsp. green peppercorns (brined, drained) 2 tbsp. steak sauce (seed-oil-free) 2 tbsp. water 1 cup whipping cream 1/4 tsp. ground pepper 1. Place a 10-inch cast-iron skillet over medium heat until hot; sprinkle the salt in the skillet. Place the steaks over the salt; cook 4 minutes on each side or until browned. Remove from the skillet. 2. Combine the peppercorns, steak sauce, and water in the hot skillet; cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, to loosen any browned bits in the bottom of the skillet. Stir in the whipping cream and pepper. 3. Bring to a boil; reduce the heat and simmer, stirring constantly, 3 to 4 minutes or until slightly thickened. Add the steaks; simmer 5 minutes or to desired doneness, stirring occasionally. If you feel like grilling, simply make the pepper cream on the stove and grill the steaks outside. Yield: 2 to 4 servings Carb level: Low-carb (steak and cream; a little steak sauce) No added cooking oil. Salt in a hot dry cast-iron skillet seasons the meat and helps the surface contact the pan so it browns (Maillard). The fat that renders from the strips is the frying fat. No seed oils. Green peppercorns (soft, brined) are the pepper in the cream — milder and fruitier than cracked black. Drain them if they sit in brine so you are not watering down the sauce. Ground pepper at the end is a second, sharper hit. Whipping cream is the body. After the fond is deglazed with steak sauce and water, the cream reduces 3 to 4 minutes until it coats a spoon. Stir constantly so the dairy does not scorch. A hard boil for too long can break the emulsion; once it thickens, nest the steaks back in and simmer gently to the doneness you want. Use a seed-oil-free steak sauce (or a splash of Worcestershire plus a pinch of tomato paste). Many bottled sauces hide soybean oil. The sauce is there for Worcestershire-style tang and a little sugar to gloss the cream, not to taste like a bottle. If you grill the steaks instead, make the pepper cream in the skillet the same way (use a spoon of the steak drippings or a pat of butter to start the fond) and spoon it over the grilled strips. Two 12-ounce steaks serve 2 hungry people, or 4 if you slice them. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Apple Pancakes
recipes.how: 2 cups flour (lower-carb option: 1-3/4 cups blanched almond flour + 2 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 1 tsp. baking soda 2 tsp. baking powder 2 tsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1 tsp. brown sugar (in place of 1 tbsp. brown sugar) 1 tsp. salt 1 tsp. ground cinnamon 2 eggs 1-1/2 cups buttermilk 1/2 cup sour cream 1/4 cup butter, melted 1 large apple, peeled, cored, and grated Butter, for the griddle Maple syrup, for serving 1. In a large bowl, mix together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, sweetener, salt, and cinnamon. In another bowl, mix the eggs, buttermilk, sour cream, and melted butter; add to the flour mixture. Fold in the grated apple. 2. Using 1/4 cup batter per pancake, pour onto a hot, buttered griddle. Cook, turning once, until golden brown and cooked through. These puff up light and airy and are full of naturally great taste. Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: High-carb (flour batter + apple + syrup) Melted butter is the fat in the batter; more butter on the griddle browns the cakes (Maillard) and keeps them from sticking. Butter replaces margarine. No seed oils. Wheat flour stays primary. This is a chemical-leavened pancake batter lifted by baking powder plus baking soda; a full almond-flour swap will not rise or flip the same way. If you want a lower-carb stack, start by swapping only 1/4 to 1/2 cup of the flour for almond flour. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar. Those grams, plus the molasses in the brown sugar, help the cakes spot gold on the griddle. Monk fruit will not replace the maple syrup on top. Buttermilk and sour cream are the tenderness: fat plus acid, which also wakes the baking soda. Stop stirring the moment the dry streaks disappear, then fold the apple. Extra mixing develops gluten and makes the cakes tough. Grated apple (not chunks) cooks through in the time it takes the cakes to brown. Squeeze it lightly if it is very juicy so the batter does not thin. Medium heat: too hot and the cinnamon-sugar scorches before the centers set; too cool and the cakes steam and never brown. Flip once, when the tops are bubbled and the edges look set. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: BBQ Joes
recipes.how: 2 pounds ground beef 1/2 cup chopped onion 1/2 cup finely chopped green pepper 1 can (10-3/4 ounces) condensed tomato soup, undiluted (seed-oil-free, or 1-1/4 cups tomato sauce) 1 cup barbecue sauce (seed-oil-free) 1/4 cup + 1 tsp. golden monk fruit blend + 1 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 1/3 cup packed brown sugar) 1-1/2 tbsp. Worcestershire sauce 3/4 tbsp. dry mustard 1/4 tsp. chili powder 1/4 tsp. garlic salt 10 to 15 hamburger buns 1. In a large saucepan or Dutch oven over medium heat, brown the beef and onion. Add the green pepper. Cook and stir 5 minutes; drain. Add the tomato soup, barbecue sauce, sweetener, Worcestershire, dry mustard, chili powder, and garlic salt; bring to a boil. Reduce the heat; cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Serve on the buns. This twist on the Sloppy Joe is perfect when you're craving BBQ flavor. These are a huge hit in our house! Yield: 10 to 15 servings Carb level: High-carb on the bun (hamburger buns + tomato soup + barbecue sauce + brown sugar); the meat mixture alone is Moderate-carb The ground beef is the fat and the browning. Drain the extra so the sauce is sloppy, not greasy. No seed oils in the pot. Wheat buns stay primary. These are Joes — the bun has to hold a scoop of saucy beef. A lettuce wrap works if you want a lower-carb plate; keep the filling. Use a seed-oil-free barbecue sauce and a tomato soup without soybean oil (or swap the soup for 1-1/4 cups tomato sauce). Many canned soups and bottled sauces hide seed oil and corn syrup. The soup is the body; the BBQ sauce is the smoke and tang. Sugar swap: Keep a little real brown sugar so the sauce still glosses and caramelizes in the hour-long simmer (Maillard). Monk fruit sweetens but will not reduce into the same sticky Joe coating. Worcestershire, dry mustard, chili powder, and garlic salt are the rest of the BBQ — do not skip the mustard. Cover and simmer 1 hour, stirring occasionally. That hour is not just heating — the onion and pepper melt, the tomato and brown sugar reduce, and the beef drinks the sauce. A 15-minute shortcut tastes like meat in ketchup. Taste the salt after it reduces; soup and BBQ sauce vary. Two pounds of beef on 10 to 15 buns is a party pot. Keep it warm on low and toast the buns in butter if you want them to stand up to the sauce. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Waffles
recipes.how: 2 cups flour (lower-carb option: 1-3/4 cups blanched almond flour + 2 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 3 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tbsp. sugar (in place of 1/4 cup sugar) 4 tsp. baking powder 1 tsp. salt 1 tsp. ground cinnamon 1/2 tsp. ground nutmeg 1/2 tsp. ground cloves 1-1/2 cups milk 1 cup canned pumpkin 3/4 cup butter, melted 1 tsp. vanilla 4 eggs, separated Butter, for the waffle iron 1. Mix together the dry ingredients; stir in the milk, pumpkin, melted butter, vanilla, and egg yolks. 2. In a separate bowl, beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form. Fold into the waffle batter. 3. Butter a preheated waffle iron if it needs it. Cook the waffles to the desired doneness. Serve warm with maple syrup or cinnamon syrup. Mmmmm! Boy do these warm up the house with a delicious cinnamony aroma on a chilly morning. This winning recipe comes from a wonderful poster on a cooking board I frequent, Nancy, and I am forever grateful for her sharing what has become a family favorite! Thanks Nancy! Carb level: High-carb (flour batter plus pumpkin and syrup at the table) Melted butter is the fat in the batter; a little more butter on the iron if it sticks. That 3/4 cup is why these brown and taste rich instead of like pumpkin bread. No seed oils. Wheat flour stays primary. This is a thick chemical-leavened waffle batter; the gluten and starch have to hold a cup of pumpkin and four eggs so the grids stay crisp. A full almond-flour swap will be dense and greasy and will not release from the iron. If you want a lower-carb batch, start by swapping only 1/4 to 1/2 cup of the flour for almond flour. Sugar swap: Keep a little real sugar. Those grams help the grids spot gold (Maillard). Pumpkin already brings moisture and a little reducing sugar; the 1/4 cup is for color and a hint of sweetness, not dessert. Separated eggs are the lift. Yolks go in with the wet mix for richness; stiff whites folded in last trap air so the waffles stay light around all that pumpkin and butter. Stop folding when the white streaks disappear — extra stirring knocks the air back out. Useful tip: for pumpkin pancakes, use whole eggs instead of beaten egg whites and cook on a buttered griddle. Medium heat on the iron; too hot and the pumpkin sugars scorch before the centers set. Serve right away — these soften as they sit. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken Noodle Casserole
recipes.how: 8 ounces garden rotini pasta 1/2 cup butter 1/2 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 2 cups chicken broth 1 cup milk 1/2 tsp. salt Pepper to taste 2 cups cooked chicken, cut up 1 cup frozen peas and carrots 3 tbsp. grated Parmesan cheese Butter, for the dish 1. Cook the pasta according to package directions and drain. Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter a 2-quart casserole dish. 2. Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour; cook and stir for 1 minute. Gradually add the broth, milk, salt, and pepper, stirring constantly until the sauce is thickened. Remove from the heat and stir in the chicken and the peas and carrots. Combine the chicken mixture with the pasta in the prepared casserole dish. Sprinkle with the Parmesan. 3. Cover and bake 20 to 30 minutes, until heated through. I had some leftover chicken and noodles to use up one night and wanted to make something along the lines of a chicken noodle casserole. A wonderful lady, Nancy, on a cooking board I frequent shared a recipe for Amish Chicken Casserole which came very close to what I was looking for. The original recipe calls for egg noodles, mushrooms and pimento — none of which I had — so I modified the recipe a bit to suit what was on hand. This reminds me of cream of chicken soup with oodles of noodles baked in a casserole dish. It's very tasty! Thanks for sharing, Nancy! Carb level: High-carb (pasta + a flour-thickened sauce) Butter is the roux fat and the dish grease. No seed oils, no spray. This is a from-scratch cream-of-chicken sauce — no canned soup — so you control the fat. Wheat flour stays in the roux. Equal parts butter and flour (1/2 cup each) cooked one minute is a blond roux; it thickens 3 cups of liquid (2 cups broth + 1 cup milk) into a casserole sauce that will not go watery in the oven. Almond flour will not gelatinize the same way and the bake will be thin. The pasta and chicken are already cooked. Twenty to 30 minutes at 350°F is only to heat the center and melt the Parmesan. Cover so the top does not dry before the middle is hot. Frozen peas and carrots go in from the freezer. They thaw in the hot sauce and stay bright; pre-cooking them turns them mushy. Garden rotini is what was on hand — egg noodles are the Amish original and work the same way. Whisk constantly as the liquid goes into the roux so you do not get lumps. Pull the pot off the heat before the chicken goes in so the sauce does not keep reducing to paste. Leftover turkey stands in for the chicken with no other change. A handful of sautéed mushrooms or a spoon of chopped pimento brings it closer to Nancy's original if you have them. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Apple Breakfast Sandwiches
recipes.how: For the spread: 1/2 cup cream cheese, softened (in place of light cream cheese) 2 tbsp. peanut butter 1-1/2 tbsp. apple butter 1/8 tsp. ground cinnamon 1/3 cup grated or finely chopped peeled apple For the sandwiches: 12 slices raisin bread, toasted 1. Beat the cream cheese until light and fluffy. Beat in the peanut butter, apple butter, and cinnamon. Stir in the apple. Spread on toasted raisin bread and top with a second toasted slice. My friend, Karen, shared this wonderful breakfast recipe with me and it was a huge hit in my house. And since the spread is so quick and easy to prepare they have become a breakfast staple. Carb level: High-carb (raisin bread + apple butter); the spread itself is moderate-carb Full-fat cream cheese replaces light. It beats fluffier, tastes richer, and skips the fillers. Peanut butter is the second fat. No seed oils. Wheat raisin bread stays primary. These are breakfast sandwiches; the toast has to hold a creamy apple-peanut spread without dissolving. A full almond-flour loaf will crumble when you bite it. English muffins, bagels, or your favorite bread work the same way. Apple butter is concentrated cooked apple — a little goes a long way for flavor. If you are out of it, use all peanut butter. The fresh grated apple is crunch and juice; peel it so the spread stays smooth, and stir it in last so it does not weep into the cream cheese while you beat. Cinnamon ties the apple and raisin bread together. Toast the bread so the spread sits on a dry surface instead of soaking in. Use this spread on English muffins, bagels, muffins, and your favorite bread too. Try topping open-face sandwiches with chopped nuts, dried fruit, or sliced bananas. The spread keeps a couple of days in the refrigerator; stir before you use it. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap AP flour for almond flour (psyllium helps bind baked goods); swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour structure beats arrowroot for baked flour swaps.)

recipes.title: Applesauce Sausage Bites
recipes.how: 2 pounds smoked sausage or kielbasa 1 cup applesauce 1/2 cup + 2 tsp. golden monk fruit blend + 2 tbsp. brown sugar (in place of 2/3 cup packed brown sugar) 1 small white onion, finely chopped 1. Cut the sausage into desired-size pieces. In a large baking dish, combine the applesauce, sweetener, and onion. Stir in the sausage and toss to coat. 2. Bake, uncovered, at 325°F for 40 minutes, stirring once during cooking. Serve with toothpicks if making appetizers. Serve this in larger chunks as an entree or in smaller pieces for an appetizer. People will rave over this quick and easy dish! If desired, this can be made in the crockpot on low heat for 3 hours. Carb level: Moderate-carb (applesauce and brown-sugar glaze; the sausage itself is low-carb) No seed oils. The fat is already in the smoked sausage; it renders into the applesauce as the pan bakes and is what makes the glaze glossy. Sugar swap: Keep some real brown sugar. Those molasses sugars caramelize at 325°F and give the onion a sticky coat (Maillard). Monk fruit alone will sweeten but will not brown or thicken the same way. Stir once so every piece gets a turn in the glaze. Skip that and the top pieces dry while the bottom sits in syrup. The crockpot version is the same toss, cooked on low for 3 hours. Larger chunks make an entree; bite-size pieces are the toothpick tray. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Creamed Dried Beef
recipes.how: 1/4 pound dried beef 1/4 cup butter 1/4 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 cup hot milk 1 cup half-and-half 1/4 tsp. pepper 1. Separate the slices of beef; chop into small pieces. 2. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for one minute. Stir in the milk and half-and-half and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the sauce has thickened. Stir in the pepper and beef and stir until heated through. Serve over biscuits or toast. True comfort food! From good ol' Fannie Farmer. Carb level: Moderate-carb (flour roux and milk; the beef is low-carb). Biscuits or toast push it high. Butter is the fat in the roux. No seed oils. Cooking the flour in the butter for one minute toasts the raw-flour taste without taking the roux to brown, so the sauce stays pale and creamy. Wheat flour stays in the quarter-cup. That starch is what thickens the milk and half-and-half into gravy. A full almond-flour swap will not gel the same way; if you want it lighter, start by using 3 tbsp. flour and cook a minute longer. Hot milk plus half-and-half go in together so the roux does not seize into lumps. Stir constantly over medium heat — boiling hard can break the emulsion and leave a greasy skin. Separate and chop the dried beef first. The slices stick in a wad and will not distribute if you dump the pack in whole. This is Fannie Farmer's creamed chipped beef (SOS) — pepper only; the beef is already salty, so do not add salt until you taste. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Cheese Quesadillas
recipes.how: 8 (10-inch) flour tortillas 1/4 cup butter 1 package (3 ounces) cream cheese 1/4 cup finely chopped green onions 1 medium tomato, finely chopped Dash salt 3 cups shredded Colby Jack cheese 1 can (4 ounces) diced jalapeño, optional Sour cream, guacamole, and/or salsa, for serving 1. Lightly spread one side of each tortilla with butter; place four tortillas buttered side down on a large skillet or griddle (you may have to cook in batches). 2. Whip the cream cheese until fluffy; stir in the onions, tomato, and salt. Spread on the tortillas in the skillet to within 1/2 inch of the edge; sprinkle on the Colby Jack cheese and jalapeño. Top with the remaining tortillas, buttered side up. 3. Cook on medium heat until the bottom is lightly browned, about 2 minutes. Carefully flip the quesadillas over to brown the other side. Remove from the heat and cut into 4 or 6 wedges. Serve with sour cream, guacamole, and/or salsa. These are the best cheese quesadillas! They make a terrific meatless entree paired with beans and rice or an excellent appetizer cut into thinner wedges. Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: Moderate-high (flour tortillas). Cheese, cream cheese, and sour cream are low-carb; beans and rice on the side push it higher. Butter on the outside of the tortillas is the browning fat (Maillard). No seed oils. It fries the flour skin crisp the way a dry pan never will. Whip the cream cheese first so it spreads in a thin, even layer and acts as glue for the tomato and onion. Cold cream cheese tears the tortilla. Stay 1/2 inch off the edge or the filling leaks and burns. Medium heat is the cook. Hotter and the tortilla scorches before the Colby Jack melts; cooler and it dries out. Flip once, carefully — two 10-inch tortillas full of cheese are heavy. Cut into 4 wedges for an entree or 6 thinner wedges for an appetizer. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Hot Wings
recipes.how: 2 pounds chicken wings 1/4 cup hot sauce (such as Tabasco) 1/4 cup melted butter Blue cheese or ranch dressing, optional Celery sticks, optional 1. Arrange the wings on a large baking sheet. Bake at 425°F for 1 hour. 2. Combine the hot sauce and melted butter. Pour over the wings and toss to coat. Serve with dressing and celery sticks on the side. These are very good Buffalo wings. For extra convenience with flavor just as good, buy frozen hot wings and bake according to the package directions. When done, toss in the hot sauce mixture to give them the from-scratch taste. Delicious! Carb level: Low-carb (chicken, butter, and hot sauce; dressing and celery on the side) Melted butter is the Buffalo fat. No seed oils. The hour at 425°F renders the skin and crisps it so the sauce clings instead of sliding off wet meat. Equal parts hot sauce and butter is the classic emulsified Buffalo coat. Whisk them together while the butter is still warm so the sauce stays one glossy mixture; if it splits, another brief whisk brings it back. Tabasco is thinner and hotter than a cayenne-vinegar wing sauce. If you like them hotter, use more hot sauce. If you like them really hot, add cayenne too. Toss the wings the second they come out of the oven. Hot skin takes the sauce; cooled skin beads it. The frozen-wing shortcut works the same way — bake them crisp, then toss in this butter-hot-sauce mix for the from-scratch taste. Store-bought ranch and blue cheese often hide seed oils. Homemade ranch with avocado oil mayonnaise, or a real blue-cheese dressing of crumbled cheese, sour cream, and mayo, keeps the plate clean. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Baked Blueberry French Toast
recipes.how: For the casserole: 1 loaf (14 ounces) French or Italian bread 1 package (8 ounces) cream cheese (in place of light), cut in small bits 1 cup fresh or frozen blueberries Butter, for the pan For the custard: 12 eggs 2 cups whole milk 1/3 cup sugar-free monk fruit maple syrup (in place of 1/3 cup maple syrup) 1/2 tsp. ground cinnamon 1. Cut or tear the bread into 1-inch cubes. Generously butter a 13x9-inch baking pan. 2. Place half of the bread cubes in the prepared pan. Evenly distribute the cream cheese bits over the bread. Sprinkle on the blueberries. Place the remaining bread cubes over the top. 3. Beat together the eggs, milk, syrup, and cinnamon; pour over the bread cubes. Cover with aluminum foil and refrigerate overnight (8 hours). 4. Remove from the refrigerator. Heat the oven to 350°F. Bake, covered, for 30 minutes. Uncover and bake an additional 30 minutes, or until lightly browned on top and the center is set. Cut into squares and serve with blueberry or maple syrup. Boy oh boy is this ever good! This comes from the Moms Online Recipe Box and has been raved about from several people who have made it. Prepare it before going to bed and allow an hour in the morning for baking. It's superb! (This would also be good with raspberries or banana chunks.) Carb level: High-carb (a loaf of bread plus maple in the custard and at the table) Butter greases the pan. Full-fat cream cheese replaces light. Whole milk replaces unspecified milk so the custard stays rich. No seed oils. Wheat bread stays. This is baked French toast — the crumb has to soak overnight and still hold cubes. Almond-flour bread will dissolve in 12 eggs and 2 cups of milk. Day-old or slightly stale French or Italian loaf soaks without turning to mush. The overnight rest is the method. Cold custard has time to move all the way into the cubes so the middle bakes set instead of wet. Covered for the first 30 minutes steams the center through; uncovered the last 30 lets the top brown (Maillard) and the cream cheese spots gold. Frozen blueberries go in frozen. Thawed berries bleed a gray streak through the custard. Raspberries or banana chunks stand in the same way. Sugar swap: Keep real maple in the custard if you want it to brown and taste like syrup baked in; monk-fruit maple can take the table pour. Useful tip: Halve this and bake it in an 11x7-inch dish to feed a smaller crowd. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap sugar/honey for monk fruit or erythritol blend; swap AP flour for almond flour (psyllium helps bind baked goods); swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour structure beats arrowroot for baked flour swaps.)

recipes.title: Tamale Pie
recipes.how: For the filling: 1/2 pound lean ground beef 1 small onion, chopped 1/2 cup green pepper, chopped 1 clove garlic, minced 1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce 1 cup frozen corn 1 can (4 ounces) sliced black olives, drained 1 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend (in place of 1 tbsp. sugar) 1 tbsp. chili powder 1 tsp. salt 1/4 tsp. white pepper 2 cups shredded sharp Cheddar cheese, divided For the topping: 3/4 cup cornmeal 1 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend (in place of 1 tbsp. sugar) 1/2 tsp. salt Pinch white pepper 2 cups cold water 1 tbsp. butter 1. In a 10-inch cast-iron skillet, brown the beef with the onion, green pepper, and garlic; drain. Stir in the tomato sauce, corn, olives, sweetener, and spices. Simmer 20 minutes. Stir in 1-1/2 cups of the cheese. 2. Whisk together the cornmeal, sweetener, salt, pepper, and water in a small saucepan. Cook and stir over medium-high heat until thick. Stir in the butter and remaining cheese. Spoon over the hot meat mixture. 3. Bake at 375°F for 40 minutes. This is our favorite Tamale Pie recipe. Serve it dolloped with sour cream and a lettuce, tomato, avocado, and black olive salad on the side. Carb level: High-carb (corn, tomato sauce, and a cornmeal topping) Butter goes into the topping. The beef browns in its own fat in the skillet — no extra oil. No seed oils. Wheat stays out of this topping on purpose. The coating is cornmeal cooked in cold water until thick — a spoonable mush, like a fast polenta. That is the tamale. Almond flour will not hydrate and set the same way; do not swap it. Start the cornmeal in cold water and whisk as it heats. Dumping cornmeal into hot liquid makes lumps that never cook out. The starch gelatinizes as it boils and turns from grit to a spreadable coat; stir in the butter and remaining cheese off the heat so the topping stays glossy. Simmer the filling 20 minutes before the cheese goes in. That reduces the tomato sauce so the pie is meaty, not soupy, under the topping. Drain the olives or their brine thins what you just reduced. Cast iron goes from burner to 375°F oven. Forty minutes sets the cornmeal and browns the cheese spots on top. Sour cream on the square cools the chili heat. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Minnesota Wild Rice Soup
recipes.how: 1 box long-grain and wild rice mix with herb seasoning (such as Uncle Ben's), prepared according to package directions 4 tbsp. butter 2 tbsp. minced onion 1 cup finely chopped celery 1/2 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 6 cups chicken stock 1-1/2 cups light cream or half-and-half White pepper, to taste Parsley, to taste 2 tbsp. sherry Minced chives, for garnish 1. Melt the butter, add the onion and celery, and sauté until tender. Blend in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring to blend well. 2. Add the stock, pepper, and parsley, stirring constantly until the mixture thickens. Stir in the prepared rice. 3. Blend in the cream and sherry. Heat to serving temperature, but do not boil. Garnish each serving with chives. This delicious and satisfying soup comes from my friend, Linda. It's a terrific meatless choice. Thanks so much for sharing, Linda! Carb level: High-carb (wild-rice mix plus a 1/2-cup flour roux) Butter is the sauté fat and the roux fat. Keep it — the original's "omit the butter" tip is a diet-era skip, not an improvement. No seed oils. Real light cream or half-and-half stays; evaporated skim and fat-free half-and-half are not the house version. Wheat flour stays in the roux. That 1/2-cup paste is what turns stock into soup; almond flour will not thicken the same way. Cook the flour in the butter for a full 2 minutes so the raw-flour taste cooks off and the starch swells before the stock goes in. Stir constantly once the stock is in. A blond roux plus cold stock will lump if you walk away; constant heat gelatinizes the starch into a smooth, glossy base. The seasoned rice mix is already cooked and salted. Stir it in after the soup has thickened so the grains stay whole instead of breaking into the roux. Do not boil after the cream and sherry go in — a hard boil can break the cream and cooks the sherry's aroma off. Sherry is a finish, not a braise. Two tablespoons at the end lifts the wild rice and cream. Chives on top are the fresh bite. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Crispy Buffalo Chicken Strips
recipes.how: For the dredge: 1/2 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 cup blanched almond flour) 1/4 tsp. cayenne pepper 1/8 tsp. salt For the wash: 1/4 cup buttermilk (in place of lowfat) 1/4 cup whole milk 1 egg, beaten 3 tsp. hot pepper sauce For the coating: 2 cups fine cornflake crumbs 1/2 tsp. cayenne pepper 1-1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut in 1-inch strips Butter or avocado oil, for the pan For serving: Ranch or blue cheese dressing 1. Combine the flour, cayenne, and salt in a small bowl. Combine the buttermilk, milk, egg, and hot pepper sauce in another small bowl. Combine the cornflakes and cayenne in a third small bowl. 2. Dip the chicken strips into the flour mixture, then into the egg mixture, and finally into the cornflake mixture. Place the chicken on a baking sheet greased with butter or avocado oil. Lightly brush or drizzle more butter or avocado oil over the chicken. 3. Bake at 400°F for 15 minutes, or until crispy and the chicken is done. (Or fry in hot 375°F avocado oil for a few minutes on each side until done.) Serve with ranch or blue cheese dressing, if desired. I came up with this delicious chicken strip recipe by combining a few different recipes that weren't quite what I was looking for. Delicious results! Kick it up a notch or two by adding more cayenne and pepper sauce if desired. Yield: 5 to 6 servings Carb level: High-carb (cornflake crust); the chicken itself is low-carb. Almond-flour dredge drops the flour a little; the crumbs are still the dish. Butter or avocado oil replaces cooking spray on the sheet and over the strips. Both handle 400°F without seed oils. If you fry instead, avocado oil at 375°F is the shallow-fry fat. Wheat flour is only the first dredge so the egg wash sticks — almond flour can take that job. The cornflake crumbs are the coating; do not swap those for almond flour or you lose the crunch. Three-step breading (flour → egg → crumbs) is food science, not fuss. Dry flour gives the egg proteins something to grab; the buttermilk-egg wash (lactic acid plus protein) glues the crumbs. Full-fat buttermilk and whole milk replace the lowfat originals so the wash is richer and browns better (Maillard). Press the crumbs on firmly and give the strips a minute on the pan before they go in the oven so less coating sheds. The butter on top is what fries the crumbs in the oven. More cayenne and hot sauce if you want them hotter. Store-bought ranch and blue cheese often hide seed oils. Homemade ranch with avocado oil mayonnaise, or a real blue-cheese dressing, keeps the plate clean. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Potato Cheese Quesadillas
recipes.how: 2 flour tortillas 2 tbsp. cream cheese (regular or flavored) 1 small baked potato, sliced into 1/4-inch slices 2 ounces shredded Monterey Jack cheese 1 green onion, thinly sliced (green tops included) Butter, for the skillet Salsa, optional 1. Spread cream cheese over the bottom half of both tortillas. Lay the sliced potatoes over the cream cheese. Sprinkle on the cheese and onion; fold the top over the filling. 2. Heat a skillet or griddle over medium heat and butter it well. Brown the tortillas on both sides until crispy and the cheese is melted. Cut each quesadilla into 3 wedges. Serve with salsa if desired. Make an extra baked potato for dinner to have this yummy lunch the following day. Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas plus a baked potato) Butter on the skillet replaces nonstick spray. The milk-fat browns the tortilla (Maillard) and keeps it from sticking. No seed oils. Wheat flour tortillas stay — they are the quesadilla. Low-carb tortillas work if you want a lighter plate; the potato is still the starch inside. Cream cheese is the glue. A thin smear on the bottom half holds the potato slices so they do not slide when you fold. Regular or flavored cream cheese both work; a chive or garden-veg flavor echoes the green onion. 1/4-inch potato slices heat through in the time the Jack melts. Thicker slabs stay cold in the middle; mashed leftover potato also works if you spread it thin. Medium heat, not screaming hot — the tortilla needs time to crisp before the cheese burns. Leftover baked potato is the point of the recipe. A fridge-cold potato slices cleaner than a fresh-hot one. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Smoked Turkey & Mango Wraps
recipes.how: 4 flour tortillas (8 inches) 4 tsp. avocado oil mayonnaise (in place of lite mayonnaise) 4 tsp. Dijon mustard 1 tsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 1 tsp. honey (in place of 2 tsp. honey) 8 ounces smoked turkey or chicken breast, thinly sliced 2 mangoes, peeled and diced Lettuce leaves 1. In a small bowl, combine the mayonnaise, mustard, and honey. Spread on the tortillas. 2. Top each with turkey, mango, and lettuce. Roll up; cut in half. These are SO good. Hard to believe the original card sold them as a low-fat wrap — they taste even better with real mayo and regular tortillas. Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas plus mango and a little honey); turkey, mayo, Dijon, and lettuce are low Avocado oil mayonnaise replaces lite mayo so the spread is seed-oil-free and actually tastes like a sandwich. A thin smear is a moisture barrier — it keeps mango juice from turning the tortilla soggy. No seed oils. Wheat flour tortillas stay primary. This is a wrap; the tortilla has to hold turkey, diced mango, and lettuce and still slice cleanly. A full almond-flour wrap will crack when you roll it. For a lower-carb lunch, use the same filling in large lettuce leaves, or a low-carb wheat-style tortilla. Sugar swap: Keep at least a teaspoon of real honey. Honey is the body of the Dijon-mayo sauce; all-monk-fruit mustard tastes thin and sharp against the mango. Ripe mango should give slightly and smell floral at the stem. Dice it small so the wrap rolls tight. Roll and cut soon so the lettuce stays crisp; leftover wraps wilt as the fruit weeps. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Aloha Burgers
recipes.how: 8 pineapple slices 1 cup teriyaki sauce, divided 1-1/4 pounds ground beef 1 small sweet onion, sliced 1 tbsp. butter, for the onions (in place of cooking spray) 4 lettuce leaves 4 slices Swiss cheese 4 sesame seed buns 1. Place the pineapple and 3 tbsp. teriyaki sauce in a resealable plastic bag; turn to coat and set aside to marinate. 2. Shape the beef into four patties. Place in a resealable plastic bag or shallow dish and pour 1/2 cup teriyaki sauce over the patties; marinate for 15 minutes, turning once. 3. Meanwhile, melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and saute the onion until tender. 4. Grill or broil the burgers until cooked through and no longer pink. Grill or broil the pineapple to heat through. 5. Layer lettuce and onion on the bottom of the buns. Top with the burgers, cheese, and pineapple and drizzle with the remaining teriyaki sauce; top with the top buns. These are so tasty and similar to a popular Red Robin burger! Carb level: High-carb (sesame seed buns plus pineapple and teriyaki); beef, Swiss, onion, and lettuce are low Butter replaces cooking spray for the onions so they soften and pick up a little browning (Maillard) instead of steaming dry in a dry nonstick pan. No seed oils. Wheat sesame seed buns stay primary. This is a stacked burger with pineapple and Swiss; an almond-flour bun will crumble under the juice. Toast the cut faces if you want a moisture barrier. Fifteen minutes in teriyaki is a surface marinade, not a brine. Longer and the salt starts to cure the outside and the patties cook up dense. 80/20 beef stays juicier than extra-lean — fat is what keeps a grilled burger from tasting like a hockey puck. Pat the pineapple dry after it marinates so it marks on the grill instead of steaming. Swiss goes on the hot burger so it melts into the meat before the pineapple goes on. The last drizzle of teriyaki is the glaze — do not dump the raw marinade from the beef bag back onto the plate. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Carb swap: swap flour/starch dredge for almond flour + a pinch of psyllium husk; swap bread/tortilla for lettuce wraps or almond-flour flatbread. (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour gives better crunch than arrowroot alone for coatings.)

recipes.title: Monte Cristo Sandwich
recipes.how: 4 slices firm bread 4 tsp. sugar-free raspberry preserves (in place of raspberry preserves) 2 ounces very thinly sliced smoked ham 2 slices Swiss cheese (2 ounces) 1/4 cup milk 1 egg 1 tbsp. butter, for the pan (in place of cooking spray) 1/2 tsp. powdered monk fruit + 1/2 tsp. confectioners' sugar (in place of 1 tsp. sifted powdered sugar) 1. Spread one side of each slice of bread with preserves. Layer the ham and cheese between the spread sides of the bread. In a shallow bowl or pie plate, beat together the milk and egg. Melt the butter in a skillet or on a griddle over medium heat. 2. Dip each sandwich in the milk mixture, turning to coat. Place in the pan; cook 2 minutes per side, or until golden brown and the cheese is melted. Sprinkle with powdered sugar. Yummy!! Carb level: High-carb (firm bread plus preserves and a dusting of sugar); ham, Swiss, egg, and butter are low A whole egg plus whole milk replaces the original egg-white-and-1% dip. Yolk lecithin helps the custard cling, and the fat browns instead of steaming. Butter in the pan replaces cooking spray so the crust actually fries (Maillard). Regular smoked ham and Swiss replace the low-fat versions so the sandwich tastes like a Monte Cristo. No seed oils. Wheat bread stays primary. This is a French-toast sandwich; the slices have to soak, flip, and hold ham and a melt of Swiss. A full almond-flour loaf will fall apart in the custard. Use a firm sandwich bread, not a soft sandwich white that turns to mush. Sugar swap: Keep a little real powdered sugar on top — it is only a teaspoon, and it is the classic finish. Sugar-free raspberry preserves drop the filling sugar without changing the method. The sweet-savory contrast is the whole sandwich; do not skip the jam. Medium heat only. Too hot and the bread scorches before the Swiss melts. Two minutes a side is the usual window. Serve right away so the crust stays crisp. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter & Banana Quesadillas
recipes.how: 4 flour tortillas 4 tbsp. peanut butter 2 small bananas, diced Butter, for the griddle (in place of cooking spray) 1. Spread 1 tablespoon peanut butter on each tortilla. Place the diced banana over half of each tortilla; fold the other half over the banana. 2. Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat and butter it well. Brown the quesadillas on one side, about 2 minutes. Flip and brown the other side. Cut each into three wedges. This is a really nummy lunch or after-school snack! Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas plus banana); the peanut butter is mostly fat and protein Butter replaces cooking spray on the griddle. It browns the tortillas (Maillard) and keeps them from sticking. No seed oils. Wheat flour tortillas stay — they are the quesadilla. A low-carb tortilla works if you want a lighter plate; the filling is the same. There is no added sugar. Ripe banana is the sweetness; peanut butter is the fat that keeps the fruit from turning the tortilla soggy. A natural peanut butter that needs stirring is fine — warm it a few seconds if it is too stiff to spread. Dice the banana so it stays put when you fold. Slices slide. Medium heat is the window: too hot and the tortilla scorches before the peanut butter warms; too cool and it steams instead of browning. Flip once. Three wedges per quesadilla is the snack cut. Serve right away — banana browns if they sit. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Fruit 'N Cream Roll Ups
recipes.how: 4 flour tortillas 4 tbsp. cream cheese, softened (in place of light or fat-free cream cheese) 4 tsp. sugar-free preserves, any flavor (in place of fruit preserves) Fresh sliced fruit (peaches or strawberries are favorites) 1 tsp. monk fruit baking blend (in place of 1 tsp. cinnamon sugar) 1. Warm the flour tortillas until pliable. 2. Spread 1 tablespoon cream cheese and 1 teaspoon preserves on each tortilla. Place sliced fruit on top and sprinkle with cinnamon sweetener. Roll up. Whip these up for a healthy breakfast or snack. They're so delicious and versatile (peaches 'n cream and strawberries 'n cream are my favorites). Carb level: High-carb (flour tortillas plus preserves and fruit) Full-fat cream cheese replaces the light or fat-free kind. The fat is a moisture barrier so the fruit juice and preserves do not soak the tortilla. No seed oils — there is no frying fat here unless you want to warm the tortillas in a little butter. Wheat flour tortillas stay. Warm them in a dry skillet or a few seconds in the microwave so they roll without cracking. Low-carb tortillas work if you want a lighter roll. Sugar swap: Keep the preserves even in the cinnamon sprinkle — that teaspoon is glue and flavor, not just sugar. Sugar-free preserves are the cleanest swap if you want less sugar; monk fruit will not spread like jam. Soften the cream cheese so it spreads in a thin coat instead of tearing the tortilla. Peaches 'n cream and strawberries 'n cream are Steph’s favorites; any ripe sliced fruit works. Serve right away so the roll stays snappy. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Blueberry Buttermilk Pancakes
recipes.how: 1-1/2 cups flour (lower-carb option: 1-1/4 cups + 1 tbsp. blanched almond flour + 1-1/2 tsp. psyllium husk powder) 1 tbsp. + 2 tsp. monk fruit baking blend + 1 tsp. sugar (in place of 2 tbsp. sugar) 1 tsp. baking powder 1/2 tsp. baking soda 1/2 tsp. salt 1-3/4 cups buttermilk 1/4 cup water 1 egg, beaten 2 tbsp. butter, melted (in place of reduced-calorie margarine) 1/4 tsp. vanilla extract 1 cup fresh or frozen blueberries Butter, for the griddle (in place of cooking spray) 1. Whisk the flour, sweetener, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. 2. In a separate bowl, beat the buttermilk, water, egg, melted butter, and vanilla. Add to the dry ingredients, stirring just until combined. Stir in the blueberries. 3. Heat a griddle to 350°F and butter it well. Pour 1/4 cup batter onto the hot griddle for each pancake. Cook until the edges look set; flip and cook the other side. These are so tasty! I love the buttermilk and blueberry combo.
