Yield: 14 pancakes Carb level: High-carb (flour pancakes plus blueberries) Melted butter replaces reduced-calorie margarine in the batter; more butter is the griddle fat. It browns the cakes (Maillard) and keeps them from sticking. No seed oils, no spray. Wheat flour stays primary. These are real buttermilk pancakes — gluten plus baking powder and soda is the lift. A full almond-flour swap will not rise or flip the same way. If you want a lower-carb stack, start by swapping only 1/4 cup of the flour for almond flour. Sugar swap: Keep a little real sugar. Those grams help the cakes spot gold on the griddle. Buttermilk is the tenderness: fat plus lactic acid, which also wakes up the baking soda. Do not swap in sweet milk without dropping the soda and adding a little extra powder. Stop stirring the moment the dry streaks disappear, then fold the berries. Extra mixing develops gluten and makes the pancakes tough. Frozen blueberries go in frozen so they do not bleed purple through the batter. 350°F is the window. Too hot and the sugar scorches before the centers set; too cool and the cakes steam and never brown. Flip once, when the edges look done and the tops are just starting to bubble. 1/4 cup batter makes 14 cakes. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Sesame Chicken with Peanut Sauce
recipes.how: 1 cup basmati rice 2 tbsp. creamy peanut butter 2 tbsp. sugar-free allulose honey + 2 tbsp. honey (in place of 1/4 cup honey) 3/4 cup chicken broth 2 tbsp. soy sauce 1/4 tsp. ground ginger 1/8 tsp. cayenne pepper 2 cloves garlic, minced 1 tbsp. cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 tbsp. avocado oil (in place of cooking spray) 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, diced 1 tbsp. sesame seeds 2 green onions, sliced 1. Cook the rice according to package directions. Whisk the peanut butter, sweetener, broth, soy sauce, ginger, cayenne, garlic, and cornstarch until smooth; set aside. 2. Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add the chicken and stir-fry until cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes. Add the sesame seeds and stir-fry 30 seconds more. 3. Reduce the heat to medium-high. Pour in the peanut sauce and the green onions and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes, until the sauce thickens and turns glossy. Serve over the rice. This is SO good, and it's good for you, too! Carb level: High-carb with rice (sauce is moderate-carb from honey and peanut butter); the chicken itself is low-carb Avocado oil replaces cooking spray so the chicken can actually sear (Maillard) instead of steaming in a dry nonstick pan. No seed oils. Sugar swap: Keep at least 2 tablespoons of real honey. Honey is the gloss and some of the body next to the peanut butter; cornstarch does the thickening either way. Whisk the slurry until smooth and stir it again before it hits the pan so the starch is not sitting on the bottom. Cornstarch needs a full bubble to set. Two minutes of stirring is enough. High heat for the chicken, then drop to medium-high when the sauce goes in so the honey does not scorch. Sesame seeds go in for the last 30 seconds so they toast in the fat without burning. Green onions go in with the sauce so they soften just enough. Regular soy sauce replaces the original lite soy — you want the salt and the savor. For a lower-carb plate, serve over cauliflower rice or skip the starch and pile the chicken into bowls. Basmati (not “basmatti”) stays fluffy next to a thick peanut sauce. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Asparagus-Turkey Au Gratin
recipes.how: 1 tbsp. butter 2 tbsp. flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 cup milk 1 cup grated Cheddar cheese 4 slices bread, toasted and buttered 1 package (10 ounces) frozen asparagus spears, cooked and drained (or an equal amount of fresh asparagus, trimmed and cooked until just tender) 8 slices cooked turkey 4 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled 1. Preheat the broiler. 2. Melt the butter in a small saucepan; stir in the flour. Add the milk gradually and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the sauce is thickened. Add the cheese and stir until melted. 3. Place the toast on a baking sheet. Top with the asparagus spears, then with the turkey slices. Spoon on the cheese sauce. Broil 3 to 5 minutes, or until golden. Sprinkle with the bacon. Use fresh asparagus if it's in season. Either way, this is delicious! Carb level: High-carb with the buttered toast (the cheese sauce is moderate-carb); skip the bread and the plate drops toward Moderate-low Butter is the roux fat. No seed oils. Cook the flour in the butter for a minute before the milk goes in so the sauce does not taste pasty; then add the milk slowly and keep stirring so the starch gelatinizes without lumps. Wheat flour is the classic thickener in a 2-tablespoon roux. Almond flour can stand in for a lower-carb sauce — it will be a little grainier and will not thicken quite as hard. Either way, the Cheddar is what turns a white sauce into au gratin. Wheat bread stays if you want Steph’s open-face plate. Toast it and butter it so the asparagus juice does not soak the crumb. For a lower-carb supper, skip the toast and build the asparagus, turkey, and sauce in a shallow broiler-safe dish. Fresh asparagus in season is better than the frozen box — cook it just tender so it still has snap after the broiler. Frozen spears need to be drained well or they water the sauce. Broil only until the cheese is golden (Maillard on the cheddar fat). Three to 5 minutes is plenty. Bacon goes on after the broiler so it stays crisp instead of steaming under the sauce. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Spicy Pecan Pork
recipes.how: 12 ounces boneless pork loin 1 egg, beaten 1/2 cup milk 1/3 cup finely crushed cornflakes 1/3 cup ground pecans 1/2 tsp. ground red pepper 1/3 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/3 cup blanched almond flour) 1/8 tsp. salt 1/8 tsp. pepper 2 tbsp. avocado oil (in place of vegetable oil) 1. Slice the pork loin crosswise into 4 equal slices. Place the meat between 2 sheets of wax paper; pound with the flat side of a meat mallet to 1/4-inch thickness. 2. In a shallow bowl, combine the egg and milk. In another bowl, combine the cornflakes, pecans, and ground red pepper. Season the flour with the salt and pepper. Coat the pork in the seasoned flour. Dip the slices, one at a time, into the egg mixture, then coat with the crumb mixture. 3. Heat the avocado oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pork slices 6 to 8 minutes, or until tender and just slightly pink, turning once. I adapted this recipe from Better Homes and Gardens to suit our taste. It's a terrific way to use pork loin. Carb level: Moderate-carb (flour dredge plus cornflake crust); the pork itself is low-carb. Almond flour in the dredge and a pecan-only coat drops it toward Moderate-low. Avocado oil replaces vegetable oil. It handles medium-high heat without seed oils and lets the pecan crust brown instead of burn. Pecans are rich in their own oil — do not go hotter than medium-high or the nuts scorch before the pork is done. Three-stage breading is the crust: flour dries the surface, egg wash is the glue, pecan-cornflake is the crunch. Almond flour can stand in for the wheat dredge. For a lower-carb plate, skip the cornflakes and use all ground pecans (watch the heat — no cereal buffer). 1/4 inch is the point. Thin cutlets cook through in 6 to 8 minutes without drying, and the crust stays crisp instead of steaming. Do not crowd the skillet. Pork is done at 145°F in the thickest part and should still be just slightly pink; rest a minute on the plate. Ground red pepper is the “spicy.” Half a teaspoon in the crumbs is a warm kick, not a dare — add more if you want it hotter. A Better Homes and Gardens idea, adapted — leave the pecan crust recognizable. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Strawberry Filled Crepes
recipes.how: For the strawberry sauce: 1/4 cup + 2 tbsp. monk fruit baking blend + 2 tbsp. sugar (in place of 1/2 cup sugar) 1 pint strawberries, sliced 1-1/2 tbsp. cornstarch dissolved in 1/4 cup cold water (lower-carb option: 3/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) For the crepes: 3/4 cup flour 1/2 tsp. salt 1 tsp. baking powder 1 tbsp. + 2 tsp. powdered monk fruit + 1 tsp. confectioners' sugar (in place of 2 tbsp. powdered sugar) 2 eggs 2/3 cup milk 1/3 cup water 1/4 tsp. vanilla Butter, for the skillet (in place of oil) For serving: Fresh whipped cream, sweetened with sugar or monk fruit 1. Make the strawberry sauce first. Place the sweetener and strawberries in a saucepan and stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves. Add the cornstarch mixture and cook until thickened and bubbly. Cool to room temperature. 2. For the crepes, sift together the flour, salt, baking powder, and powdered sugar. Beat the eggs and stir in the milk, water, and vanilla. Make a well in the sifted ingredients. Pour in the liquid and stir quickly to combine. A few small lumps are fine. 3. Heat an 8-inch skillet over moderate heat and butter it with a few drops of melted butter. Add a small quantity of batter. Tip the skillet and let the batter spread over the bottom. Cook until the crepe is brown underneath; flip and brown the other side. Butter the skillet with a few drops for each crepe. 4. Spoon strawberry sauce down the center of each crepe, roll or fold, and top with sweetened whipped cream. Go out of the ordinary one breakfast...or dinner...and treat your family to this rich and incredibly scrumptious crepe delight. Yield: 12 crepes (6 servings) Carb level: High-carb (wheat crepes plus a sugar-thickened strawberry sauce) Butter replaces oil in the skillet. A few drops per crepe brown the surface (Maillard) and keep the thin batter from sticking. No seed oils. Wheat flour stays primary. Crepes have to stretch, flip, and roll without tearing; that is gluten. A full almond-flour swap will be fragile and will not make a dozen thin 8-inch rounds. If you want a lower-carb plate, make fewer, slightly thicker crepes with up to 1/4 cup of the flour swapped for almond flour — they will not be as elastic. Sugar swap: Keep some real sugar in the sauce so the strawberries still gloss and the cornstarch has a little dissolved solid to set around. Monk fruit sweetens but will not give the same shiny coat. Keep a pinch of real powdered sugar in the batter for color. The sauce first, then cool it. Hot filling will steam the crepes limp. Sugar pulls juice from the berries (maceration); the cornstarch slurry thickens that juice into a spoonable sauce. Dissolve the starch in cold water or it lumps. A few lumps in the batter are fine — overmixing develops gluten and makes the crepes rubbery. Rest the batter 15 to 20 minutes if you have time so the flour hydrates and the bubbles settle; you will get fewer holes. Moderate heat, one thin pour, tip the pan, flip once. Real whipped cream, sweetened to taste, is the topping. Frozen whipped topping is built on seed oils; skip it. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent. Flour is the best for this recipe because: steam-puffed batters (popovers, puff pancakes, cream puffs, crepes) need wheat starch and gluten to stretch and set into a thin shell; almond flour is too heavy and oily to puff.

recipes.title: Turkey Divan
recipes.how: 1 bunch broccoli, or 2 packages (10 ounces each) frozen broccoli spears 1/4 cup butter 1/4 cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 2 cups milk 2 tsp. chicken bouillon granules 3/4 pound sliced turkey or chicken 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1. Cook the broccoli until just tender; drain and arrange on the bottom of an 11x7-inch baking dish. 2. Melt the butter in a saucepan; stir in the flour. Add the milk and cook, stirring, until the sauce is thickened and smooth. Add the bouillon granules; stir to dissolve. 3. Pour half of the sauce over the broccoli. Top with the sliced turkey and cover with the remaining sauce. Sprinkle with the Parmesan cheese. 4. Broil until the cheese is light golden and the sauce is bubbling hot. Don't we all enjoy a quick, delicious, home-cooked meal? This dish tastes like so much more work went into it than actually did. The flavors blend together so perfectly, making for a perfect dish! For extra convenience, buy your turkey or chicken from the deli case (sliced, not shaved). Yield: 4 to 6 servings Carb level: Moderate-carb (a 1/4-cup flour roux over broccoli and turkey); almond flour in the sauce drops it toward Moderate-low Butter is the roux fat. No seed oils. Cook the flour in the butter for a minute before the milk goes in so the sauce does not taste pasty; then keep stirring so the starch gelatinizes without lumps. Wheat flour is the classic thickener. Almond flour can stand in for a lower-carb sauce — it will be a little grainier and will not set quite as firm. Either way, two cups of milk and a spoon of bouillon make the “divan” gravy; Parmesan on top is the brown crust. Broccoli goes on the bottom so it stays under the sauce instead of drying out under the broiler. Cook it just tender — it will soften more in the hot sauce. Drain it well or the extra water will thin the gravy. Frozen spears work; fresh bunch broccoli is nicer if you have it. Deli turkey or chicken, sliced not shaved, is the weeknight shortcut. Shaved meat disappears into the sauce; slices stay in layers. Broil only until the Parmesan is light gold (Maillard) and the sauce bubbles. Do not walk away — cheese goes from gold to bitter fast. This is the same idea as Asparagus-Turkey Au Gratin, built as a casserole instead of open-face toast. Four to 6 servings, depending on how hungry the table is. Carb rating (Low): ~1g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: 70/30 Short Rib & Brisket Burger
recipes.how: - 1 lb 5 oz boneless short rib, well-trimmed of excess exterior fat - 9 oz beef brisket (point preferred for extra marbling) - 1½ tsp kosher salt - ¾ tsp freshly ground black pepper - Optional: ½ tsp garlic powder For cooking: - 1–2 Tbsp butter or avocado oil - Salt and pepper for finishing (if needed) Instructions 1. Cut the short rib and brisket into 1-inch cubes. Keep very cold — ideally near freezing. 2. Grind once through a coarse plate (¼-inch or 6 mm). If you want a finer texture, grind a second time through a medium plate. Work quickly so the fat does not smear. 3. Gently mix the ground meat with salt, pepper, and optional garlic powder. Do not overwork. Form into 4 loose, thick patties about ¾–1 inch thick. Make a slight dimple in the center of each. 4. Refrigerate the patties 20–30 minutes to firm up. 5. Heat a cast-iron skillet or griddle over medium-high until very hot. Add butter or avocado oil. 6. Season the outside of the patties lightly with extra salt if desired. Place in the pan. Do not press down. 7. Cook 3–4 minutes on the first side until a deep brown crust forms. Flip once and cook another 2–4 minutes for medium-rare to medium, depending on thickness. 8. Rest 3–4 minutes before serving. A rich, steakhouse-style burger made from a custom grind of short rib and brisket. Pure beef, high fat, deep flavor. Built for a hard sear and a juicy center. - Carb level: Low-carb (pure beef and fat; zero added starch or sugar) - The 70/30 ratio (short rib dominant) gives rich marbling and beefy depth while the brisket keeps the patty juicy and cohesive. - Keep the meat and equipment cold during grinding. Warm fat smears and produces a greasy, dense texture. - Cast iron + high heat = best crust. Butter adds flavor; avocado oil handles higher heat without smoking as quickly. - No seed oils. No fillers. Just beef. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Bacon Corn Chowde
recipes.how: 6 slices thick-cut bacon, chopped 1 medium yellow onion, diced 2 cloves garlic, minced 3 medium Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and diced (or 1 small head cauliflower for lower carb) 3 cups chicken or pork stock 2 cups corn kernels (fresh or frozen) 1 cup heavy cream ½ tsp dried thyme Salt and black pepper to taste Optional: 2 tbsp butter Optional: chopped chives or green onion for serving In a heavy pot, cook the chopped bacon over medium heat until crisp. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the fat in the pot. Add the onion to the bacon fat and cook until soft, about 5–6 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds more. Stir in the potatoes (or cauliflower) and stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the potatoes are tender, 12–15 minutes. Add the corn, heavy cream, thyme, and most of the cooked bacon. Simmer gently another 5 minutes. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Stir in butter if you want extra richness. Serve topped with the remaining bacon and chives Carb level: Moderate (mainly from potatoes and corn). Use cauliflower instead of potatoes for a lower-carb version. Bacon fat replaces any need for seed oils. The rendered fat carries the flavor through the whole pot. Heavy cream gives body without flour. If you want it thicker, mash a few potato pieces against the side of the pot. Carb rating (Low): ~3g net carbs noted — fits the low-carb (about 1–10g) band.

recipes.title: Ham & Potato Chowder
recipes.how: 2 tbsp butter 1 medium yellow onion, diced 2 cloves garlic, minced 3 medium potatoes, peeled and diced (or cauliflower) 3 cups chicken or pork stock 1½–2 cups diced cooked ham 1 cup heavy cream ½ tsp dried thyme or a pinch of smoked paprika Salt and black pepper to taste Optional: ½ cup shredded cheddar Optional: chopped green onion for serving Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until soft, about 5–6 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds. Add the potatoes and stock. Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer until potatoes are tender, 12–15 minutes. Stir in the diced ham, heavy cream, and thyme. Simmer gently 5 more minutes. Taste and season. Stir in cheddar if using until melted. Serve with green onion on top. Carb level: Moderate (potatoes). Swap to cauliflower for lower carb. Butter is the only fat used — clean and flavorful. This is very forgiving. Leftover holiday ham works especially well. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (potato, potatoes). Carb swap: swap potatoes for cauliflower or turnip.

recipes.title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Rosemary Caramelized Pears, Gorgonzola & Toasted Walnuts
recipes.how: For the Arugula & Pear Salad: 4–5 cups baby arugula ½ ripe but firm pear, thinly sliced (same variety as the main) 1 small shallot, very thinly sliced 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice 3 Tbsp avocado oil Salt and black pepper to taste Optional: small handful toasted walnuts For the Pork Chops: 2 thick-cut pork chops (bone-in preferred) Salt and black pepper 1 Tbsp avocado oil or beef tallow 2 Tbsp grass-fed butter (divided) For the Caramelized Pears & Sauce: 2 firm ripe pears, peeled, halved, cored, and cut into wedges 2 Tbsp monk fruit baking blend ½ cup dry white wine 1 tsp fresh lemon juice 1–1½ tsp fresh rosemary, finely minced (plus 1–2 sprigs for basting) Pinch salt 2–3 Tbsp crumbled Gorgonzola ¼ cup toasted walnuts, roughly chopped 1. Make the salad dressing: Whisk lemon juice, salt, pepper, and avocado oil. Set aside. Do not dress the salad until just before serving. 2. Pat pork chops dry and season generously with salt and black pepper. Let sit at room temperature while you prepare the pears. 3. Caramelize the pears: In a skillet over medium heat, melt 1 Tbsp butter. Add pear wedges and cook until they begin to soften and take on color. Stir in monk fruit baking blend, minced rosemary, and a pinch of salt. Deglaze with white wine and lemon juice. Reduce 4–6 minutes until the liquid becomes a glossy sauce. Keep warm. 4. Sear the pork chops: Heat avocado oil or tallow in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear chops 4–5 minutes per side. In the last 2 minutes, add the remaining 1 Tbsp butter and a rosemary sprig; tilt the pan and baste the chops. Cook to 145°F internal temperature. Rest 5–10 minutes. 5. Assemble the salad: Toss arugula, pear slices, and shallot with the dressing. Top with a few toasted walnuts if desired. 6. Plate the main: Place a rested pork chop on each plate. Spoon caramelized pears and sauce over the top. Scatter Gorgonzola and toasted walnuts. Garnish with a rosemary sprig. 7. Serve the salad first or alongside. (with Arugula & Pear Salad) A composed dinner for two. Light, peppery arugula salad with fresh pear leads into rich pan-seared pork chops finished with caramelized pears, Gorgonzola, and toasted walnuts. Pear appears in both courses for cohesion; lemon acidity in the salad cuts the richness of the main. Carb level: Moderate-low (pears and a small amount of wine are the main sources; the rest is protein, greens, and fat) Key upgrades: Avocado oil and grass-fed butter replace any seed oils. Monk fruit is already used in place of sugar for the caramelized pears, preserving gloss and browning while keeping sweetness. No flour or dredge is needed. Food science: Reducing the wine with monk fruit creates a glossy, lightly sweet sauce that clings to the pears without the crystallization risk of regular sugar. Basting with butter and rosemary in the final minutes builds a flavorful fond and keeps the chops juicy. The fresh lemon in the salad provides bright acidity that cuts the richness of the Gorgonzola and pork. Cohesion: Fresh pear in the starter mirrors the caramelized pear on the main. Walnuts and rosemary appear in both components, tying the courses together. Make-ahead tip: Toast the walnuts and mince the rosemary earlier in the day. The salad dressing can be made ahead; dress only at the last moment so the arugula stays crisp. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (sugar, flour, crisp).

recipes.title: Eggplant, Swiss Chard & Egg Bake
recipes.how: For the vegetables: 1 medium eggplant (about 1 lb), cut into ½-inch rounds or half-moons 1 large bunch Swiss chard, stems and leaves separated 3–4 Tbsp grass-fed butter, divided Salt and black pepper For the egg custard: 6–7 large eggs ⅓ cup heavy cream ¾ cup grated Gruyère or Swiss cheese (divided) 2 Tbsp grated Parmesan (optional but good) Pinch of nutmeg or ½ tsp fresh thyme leaves Salt and black pepper 1. Preheat oven to 375°F. Butter a small baking dish (about 8×8 or similar size for 2–3 people). 2. Season the eggplant slices lightly with salt. In a large skillet over medium heat, melt 2 Tbsp butter. Fry the eggplant in batches until golden and tender on both sides, adding more butter as needed. Transfer to a plate. 3. In the same skillet, add a little more butter if the pan is dry. Sauté the chopped chard stems for 2–3 minutes until they begin to soften. Add the chard leaves and a pinch of salt; cook until just wilted. Remove from heat. 4. Whisk the eggs, heavy cream, most of the Gruyère (reserve some for the top), Parmesan if using, nutmeg or thyme, salt, and pepper until well combined. 5. Layer the fried eggplant and wilted chard in the prepared baking dish. Pour the egg mixture evenly over the vegetables. Sprinkle the remaining cheese on top. 6. Bake 25–30 minutes, until the center is just set and the top is lightly golden. Let rest 5 minutes before serving. A soft, savory casserole that sits between a frittata and a strata. Golden butter-fried eggplant and wilted Swiss chard are set in a gentle egg custard with melted cheese. No bread, no toast — the eggs do all the binding. Yield: 2–3 servings Carb level: Low-carb (mainly from the eggplant and a small amount of cream; no flour or bread) Key technique: Frying the eggplant in butter first develops deep flavor and soft texture that carries through the bake. The eggs set gently around the vegetables rather than being scrambled, giving a soft custard-like texture. Cheese note: Gruyère melts beautifully and adds a nutty depth that pairs well with both eggplant and chard. Swiss cheese works as a direct substitute. Make-ahead: You can fry the eggplant and wilt the chard earlier in the day. Assemble and bake just before serving. Leftovers reheat well in a low oven or covered in a skillet with a lid. Carb rating (Low): Notes/title mark this as low-carb or keto.

recipes.title: Baked Eggs Florentine (cream + Parmesan)
recipes.how: Makes 2 ramekins Ingredients • 1 Tbsp butter or ghee • 2 big handfuls fresh spinach (or ~1 cup cooked, squeezed dry) • Salt and pepper • Pinch nutmeg (optional) • ¼ cup heavy cream • ⅓ cup freshly grated Parmesan, divided • 2–4 eggs (1 or 2 per dish) Method 1. Heat oven to 375°F. Butter the ramekins. 2. Wilt spinach in the butter. Salt. Squeeze out the water hard. Divide into the dishes. 3. Mix cream with most of the Parmesan. Pour over the spinach. 4. Crack eggs on top. Pepper. Rest of the Parmesan. 5. Bake 12–16 minutes, until whites are set and yolks still soft. 6. While that bakes: cook bacon or sausage in a pan. Eat the ramekin with the meat on the side. No toast needed. Neil: this plate is protein + fat + spinach. That is on the path. Does this serve the Big Three and your current master list? Carb rating (Low): Low-carb ingredients (parmesan, spinach, butter) without flour/sugar staples.

recipes.title: Lime-bright skillet chicken fajitas
recipes.how: Serves 2–3 • 1½ lb boneless chicken thighs, sliced in strips • 2 Tbsp lime juice (the part you liked) + 1 tsp lime zest • 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp salt, ½ tsp smoked paprika, black pepper • 1 Tbsp avocado oil or ghee • 1 onion, sliced • 1 red bell pepper, sliced • 1 jalapeño, sliced (optional) • Extra lime wedges • 2 ripe tomatoes • 1 garlic clove • 1 small chile (jalapeño or serrano; seeds out if you want milder) • Pinch salt • ⅓ cup Mexican crema or sour cream • 1 Tbsp lime juice Toss chicken with lime juice, zest, and spices. Rest 10–20 minutes. Hot skillet, oil, chicken in one layer. Brown, then pull it out. Same pan: onion and peppers until soft-charred. Chicken back in. Hit with another squeeze of lime. Salsa roja con crema (red cream) Char tomato, garlic, and chile in a dry pan or under the broiler until blistered. Blend with salt. Cool a minute. Stir in crema and lime. Do not boil after the cream goes in. Neil: this is meat, peppers, lime, cream. Same direction as the 325 weigh-in. Skip the flour tortillas and it stays on the path. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (flour). Carb swap: swap AP flour for almond flour (psyllium helps bind baked goods). (Chose that over arrowroot: almond flour structure beats arrowroot for baked flour swaps.)

recipes.title: Chicken Guacamato
recipes.how: 2 Chicken Breast 1 Heirloom tomato 1 Avocado Balsamic Vinegar Rosemary Olive oil Preheat the oven to 400 Season the chicken Bake the chicken at 400 for 20 minutes While the chicken is baking, Slice tomato and Avocado Peter last made this 9./14 first made with chicken shish kebabs Carb rating (Low): Meat/fat forward with minimal plant carbs (chicken, chicken, avocado) — low-carb band. recipes.title: Dolly Parton’s Favorite Pimento Cheese Sandwich
recipes.how: For the spread: - 2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese - 8 oz cream cheese, softened and cubed - 3 Tbsp diced dill pickles - 2 Tbsp diced pimentos, drained - 2 heaping Tbsp mayonnaise (avocado-oil mayo) - 1 hard-boiled egg, peeled and grated - Pinch of salt - Pinch of black pepper For serving: - 12 slices white sandwich bread (or lettuce cups / toasted almond-flour bread for lower carb) 1. Let the cream cheese sit out until soft. 2. In a bowl, beat cream cheese and mayonnaise until smooth. 3. Fold in cheddar, grated egg, pickles, and pimentos. Season with salt and pepper. 4. Taste. Add another pinch of pickle brine if it needs brightness. 5. Spread on bread for 6 sandwiches, or chill the spread and use as a dip. 6. If making sandwiches ahead, wrap and refrigerate. Best the same day. Sharp cheddar, cream cheese, dill pickles, pimentos, and a grated hard-boiled egg. The egg and pickle are what make this version hers. - Carb level: High-carb as a white-bread sandwich. Low-carb as a spread, lettuce cup, or almond-flour bread sandwich. - Mayo: avocado-oil mayo preferred; do not swap in sour cream. - Bread optional for Recipe Box — the spread is the recipe. Source: Dolly Parton / Downloads import Sep 19 2026. Carb rating (High): Notes already flag this as high-carb / indulgent.

recipes.title: Dolly Parton’s 5-Ingredient Chicken Casserole
recipes.how: - 3 cups cooked, shredded chicken (rotisserie is the usual shortcut) - 1 (10.5 oz) can cream of chicken soup (or homemade cream-of-chicken sauce, see Notes) - 1 cup sour cream - 1½ cups shredded cheddar cheese - 1 sleeve Ritz crackers, crushed (or 1–1½ cups crushed pork rinds, or 1 cup almond flour tossed with 3 Tbsp melted butter, for lower carb / no seed oil) 1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9-inch square baking dish with butter. 2. Mix the chicken, cream of chicken soup, and sour cream until combined. 3. Spread half the chicken mixture into the dish and top with half the cheese. 4. Add the remaining chicken mixture, then the rest of the cheese. 5. Top with the crushed crackers (or pork-rind / almond-flour topping). 6. Bake about 30 minutes, until hot and bubbly and the top is golden brown. 7. Let it sit about 5 minutes before serving. Day 2 of Dolly for Guilty Pleasures Week — five ingredients, one baking dish. - Carb level: Moderate with Ritz + canned soup; lower with pork-rind or almond-flour topping and homemade sauce. - Grease dish with butter. Homemade cream-of-chicken: melt 2 Tbsp butter, whisk in 2 Tbsp almond flour, cook 1 minute, whisk in 1 cup chicken stock + splash of cream; salt + poultry seasoning. Source: Dolly Parton / Downloads import Sep 19 2026. Carb rating (High): High-carb ingredients drive the rating (flour).

recipes.title: Peter's Work Bento Chicken Salad
recipes.how: For the chicken salad: 2 cups cooked chicken, chopped or shredded (rotisserie or leftover roast) 1/3–1/2 cup mayonnaise (avocado-oil mayo preferred) 1/3 cup roasted cashews, roughly chopped 1–2 tsp very finely minced onion or a pinch of onion powder (optional; skip if you want none) Salt and black pepper to taste Optional: 1 tsp Dijon mustard, squeeze of lemon, or a little celery For the bento base: 2 slices tomato 1–2 tsp extra-virgin olive oil 1 tsp balsamic vinegar Pinch of salt 1/2 avocado, sliced 1. Mix chicken, mayonnaise, cashews, and the tiny bit of onion (if using). Season with salt and pepper. Taste and stop. Do not load it with onion. 2. In the bottom of the bento box, lay the two tomato slices. 3. Drizzle olive oil and balsamic over the tomato. Pinch of salt. 4. Lay avocado slices on the tomato. 5. Spoon the chicken salad with cashews on top. Close the box. 6. Keep cold until lunch. Eat with a fork straight from the box. Weekly lunch Peter packs for work. Layers stay separate so tomatoes and avocado do not water the salad. Carb rating (Low): chicken + avocado-oil mayo base; cashews, tomato, and a little balsamic only — no bread. Fat rule: avocado-oil mayonnaise. Tomato drizzle is extra-virgin olive oil, not seed oil. Onion stays a whisper or skip it — house version. Pack order matters: tomato + oil + vinegar first, avocado next, salad last. Extra salad keeps 3 days refrigerated. Slice avocado the morning you pack. Double the chicken salad only for another lunch; build each bento fresh.

recipes.title: Circassian Chicken
recipes.how: For the chicken: 3 quarts water 1 medium onion 1 carrot 1 stalk celery with leaves ½ cup parsley clusters 1 teaspoon salt ½ teaspoon pepper 1 (4-pound) chicken For the walnut paste: 3 slices bread (or low-carb bread) 1 cup of the chicken cooking liquid 2 cups walnut meats For serving: Paprika Parsley 1. In a large saucepan put the water, onion, carrot, celery, parsley, salt, pepper, and chicken. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 1½ hours, or until the chicken is tender. 2. Remove 1 cup of the cooking liquid. Let the chicken cool in the remaining liquid. 3. Tear the bread into the blender container. Add the 1 cup cooking liquid, cover, and turn the motor on high. Gradually add the walnuts and blend to a smooth paste, stopping to stir down if necessary. 4. Slice the chicken and spread with the walnut paste. Arrange on a serving platter, sprinkle with paprika, garnish with parsley, and chill. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 141 (The Near East). Poached chicken served cold under a smooth walnut paste. - Carb level: Low-carb (chicken and walnuts; 3 slices of bread thicken the paste for 6 servings, about ½ slice each) - Cook time: 105 minutes - Fats: none added; the richness comes from the walnuts. - Keep the leftover poaching broth; it is a good light stock. - Bread: pick one without soybean or canola oil. Low-carb bread works; it may need a splash more broth. - Science: walnut oil and bread starch bind with the warm broth into a smooth emulsion; chilling firms the paste so it clings to the chicken.

recipes.title: Baked Lamb
recipes.how: For the wheat layers: 1½ cups cracked wheat (bulgur) 2 medium onions, quartered 1 egg ½ teaspoon dry basil 1½ teaspoons salt ¼ teaspoon pepper 1 pound lean ground lamb For the filling: 1 pound lean ground lamb ½ cup pine nuts 1 teaspoon salt Butter, for the pan 1. Put the cracked wheat into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 25 seconds, or until ground. Empty into a large bowl. 2. Put the onions into the container and add water just to cover. Cover and blend on high speed for 3 or 4 seconds, or until finely chopped. Drain. 3. Return half the chopped onions to the container and add the egg, basil, 1½ teaspoons salt, and pepper. Cover and blend on high speed for 10 seconds. Pour into the bowl with the wheat, add 1 pound lamb, and mix well. 4. Spread half the wheat mixture in the bottom of a buttered 9-inch square pan. 5. In another bowl mix the remaining chopped onion, the second pound of lamb, the pine nuts, and 1 teaspoon salt. Spread over the wheat layer. 6. Top with the remaining wheat mixture and smooth it flat with a knife. Run the knife around the edges and cut into 6 pieces. 7. Bake in a preheated 375°F oven for 1 hour. Serve hot, with Leeks and Olives if you like. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 142 (The Near East). A layered kibbeh-style bake of seasoned cracked wheat and ground lamb with pine nuts. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (1½ cups cracked wheat (bulgur) spread over 6 servings, balanced with 2 pounds lamb and pine nuts) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 75 minutes - Fats: the book says a greased pan; use butter (or avocado oil), not shortening. - Scoring before baking lets the heat reach the center evenly and makes clean portions. - Scan check: part of this recipe comes from a page that only exists as an OCR copy (no photo of the page), so the ½ / ⅓ / ¼ amounts could not be double-checked. recipes.title: Lentil Soup
recipes.how: For the soup: 1 pound (2 cups) lentils 6 cups water 1½ teaspoons salt ½ teaspoon pepper 2 medium onions For the finish: 4 cups spinach 2 tablespoons lemon juice ¼ teaspoon Tabasco 1. Put the lentils, water, salt, pepper, and onions into a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes. 2. Fill the blender container half full of soup. Cover and blend on high speed for 10 seconds, or until smooth. Pour into a clean saucepan. Repeat until all the soup is blended. 3. Put the spinach, lemon juice, and Tabasco into the container and add water just to cover. Cover and blend for 2 to 3 seconds, or until the spinach is finely chopped. 4. Add to the soup, bring to a boil, and simmer for 10 minutes. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 140 (The Near East). recipes.title: Stuffed Veal Birds
recipes.how: For the stuffing: 6 slices bread (3 cups crumbs) ¼ cup hot water 1 medium onion, coarsely sliced 1 teaspoon salt ¼ teaspoon pepper ¼ cup melted butter 2 tablespoons parsley clusters ½ cup coarsely cut celery ¾ teaspoon sage For the veal: 1½ pounds veal, cut into 6 serving pieces and thinly pounded Flour, for dredging (lower-carb option: same amount blanched almond flour) Butter, for browning Stock or bouillon, to cover ½ cup cream For optional thicker gravy: 1 tablespoon flour mixed to a paste with 1 tablespoon soft butter (lower-carb option: 1/8 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1. Tear 2 slices of bread into the blender container, cover, and blend on high speed for 10 seconds. Empty into a bowl. Repeat twice more to make 3 cups crumbs. 2. Put the hot water, onion, salt, pepper, melted butter, parsley, celery, and sage into the container. Cover and blend on high speed for 10 seconds. Add to the crumbs and mix well. 3. Spread the stuffing on the veal pieces, roll up, and tie with string. 4. Dredge the rolls in flour and brown in butter. 5. Transfer to a baking dish, add stock to cover and the cream. Cover and bake in a 325°F oven for 1½ hours. 6. If you like a thicker gravy, stir in the flour-butter paste at the end. From The Blender Cookbook, pp. 133–134 (Italy). Thin veal rolled around a sage-celery bread stuffing, browned, then baked in stock and cream. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (6 slices of bread in the stuffing plus a flour dredge, over 6 servings) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 120 minutes - Fats: the book says 'butter or drippings.' recipes.title: Scrambled Eggs and Peppers Mexicana
recipes.how: ½ medium onion, coarsely cut 1 clove garlic 2 green peppers, seeded and cut into strips ½ cup tomato purée 1 teaspoon salt ¼ teaspoon pepper 6 eggs 3 tablespoons butter Toast or tortillas, for serving (optional) 1. Put the onion, garlic, green peppers, tomato purée, salt, pepper, and eggs into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 3 seconds. 2. In a skillet heat the butter. recipes.title: Chicken Mole
recipes.how: For the chicken: 1 (4-pound) chicken, cut into serving pieces Salted water, to cover 2 tablespoons avocado oil (replaces the book's salad oil) 1 green pepper, seeded and cut into strips 1 red pepper, seeded and cut into strips For the mole: 1 ounce (1 square) unsweetened chocolate, cut into pieces 2 cups chicken broth (from simmering the chicken) 1 medium onion, coarsely cut ½ teaspoon dried hot peppers 1 large clove garlic 3 peppercorns ¼ teaspoon coriander seeds ¼ teaspoon anise seeds 1 teaspoon sesame seeds 3 tablespoons tomato paste 2 tbsp. golden monk fruit blend (in place of 2 tablespoons brown sugar) 1 teaspoon salt 1. Simmer the chicken in salted water to cover until tender. Drain, reserving the broth. 2. Brown the chicken pieces in a large kettle in the avocado oil. 3. Put the chocolate into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 10 seconds. Empty onto waxed paper. 4. Put the green and red peppers into the container, add water just to cover, and blend on high speed for 5 to 6 seconds, or until finely chopped. Drain and add to the chicken. 5. Put 2 cups broth, the onion, hot peppers, garlic, peppercorns, coriander, anise, sesame seeds, tomato paste, brown sugar, salt, and the grated chocolate into the container. Cover and blend on low speed for 30 seconds, then on high for 10 seconds. 6. Pour over the chicken and peppers. Cover, bring to a boil, and simmer for 30 minutes. Serve with rice (or cauliflower rice). From The Blender Cookbook, p. 138 (Mexico). recipes.title: Barbecued Spareribs
recipes.how: For the sauce: 1 medium onion, quartered 1 clove garlic 1 (12-ounce) bottle chili sauce Juice of 1 lemon ¼ cup avocado oil (replaces the book's salad oil) 1 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon dry mustard 1 teaspoon chili powder ½ teaspoon pepper ½ teaspoon paprika 3 dashes Tabasco 2 tablespoons anchovy-free Worcestershire sauce 3 tablespoons honey 1 tablespoon vinegar ½ cup beer For the ribs: Spareribs (about 4 pounds), cut into small pieces 1. Put all the sauce ingredients into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 20 seconds. 2. Pour into a saucepan and bring to a boil. 3. Spread the ribs in a roasting pan and brush generously with the sauce. 4. Bake in a 350°F oven for 1 hour, basting often with the sauce and turning the ribs several times. 5. Simmer the remaining sauce for 1 hour and serve with the ribs. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 125 (The Luau). Oven-barbecued spareribs basted with a beer, honey, and chili-sauce barbecue sauce. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (chili sauce and 3 tablespoons honey in the basting sauce) - Cook time: 70 minutes - Peter: regular Worcestershire sauce is made with anchovies. recipes.title: Laulaus with Curry Sauce
recipes.how: 1 plump roasting chicken Large spinach leaves Salt and pepper A little finely chopped onion Ti leaves or aluminum foil, and string Luau Coconut Curry Sauce, for serving 1. Remove the meat from the chicken and cut it into squares. 2. Lay several large spinach leaves crosswise on the counter and put a piece each of white and dark meat on them. Sprinkle with salt, pepper, and a little chopped onion, and fold the spinach over the filling. 3. Wrap each package in ti leaves or foil and tie with string. 4. Steam in a covered steamer for about 2½ hours (or cook in the luau pit with other foods). 5. Serve with Luau Coconut Curry Sauce. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 126 (The Luau). recipes.title: Sauerbraten
recipes.how: For the roast: 1 (4-pound) pot roast 2 tablespoons flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 1 teaspoon salt ⅛ teaspoon pepper 2 tablespoons beef tallow, lard, or avocado oil (replaces the book's unspecified fat) For the first blend: 1 cup water 2 tablespoons brown sugar 2 slices lemon, peeled 2 medium onions, sliced For the second blend: ½ cup water ½ cup vinegar 3 cloves garlic 2 carrots, coarsely cut 2 stalks celery with leaves, coarsely cut 1 bay leaf To finish: ¼ teaspoon cloves ¼ teaspoon cinnamon ½ cup seedless raisins 5 gingersnaps 1. Rub the pot roast with the flour, salt, and pepper. In a heavy kettle heat the fat and brown the meat on all sides. 2. Put the water, brown sugar, lemon slices, and onions into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 3 seconds. Pour over the meat. 3. Put the water, vinegar, garlic, carrots, celery, and bay leaf into the container. Cover and blend on high speed for 3 seconds. Pour over the meat. 4. Add the cloves and cinnamon. Cover and cook over low heat for about 1½ hours. 5. Add the raisins. Cover and cook for 1½ hours longer, or until the meat is tender. 6. Put 1 cup of sauce from the pot into the container, add the gingersnaps, cover, and blend for 10 seconds. Stir into the liquid in the kettle and heat briefly. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 120 (Germany). A quick-braise sauerbraten: pot roast simmered with vinegar, vegetables, and spices, with a gingersnap gravy. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (a flour rub, brown sugar, raisins, and gingersnaps in the gravy, over 8 servings) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 200 minutes - Fat swap: the book says '2 tablespoons fat.' Use beef tallow or lard for the traditional flavor, or avocado oil. No shortening or seed oil. - Gingersnaps: pick a brand without seed oils or use a low-sugar ginger cookie. - Science: vinegar and a long, low braise break down the roast's connective tissue; the gingersnaps thicken and spice the gravy in one step. - Scan check: part of this recipe comes from a page that only exists as an OCR copy (no photo of the page), so the ½ / ⅓ / ¼ amounts could not be double-checked. Check them against the book if something seems off.

recipes.title: Onion Soup
recipes.how: ½ cup diced Parmesan cheese 4 large onions, quartered 2 (10½-ounce) cans beef bouillon 1½ cups water 1 teaspoon salt ¼ teaspoon pepper 2 cups cubed French bread 1. Put the Parmesan into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 5 seconds, or until grated. Turn out onto waxed paper. 2. Put the onions and bouillon into the container. Cover and blend on high speed for 3 seconds, or until the onions are chopped. 3. Turn into a large saucepan and add the water, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil and simmer for 15 minutes. 4. Pour into a large ovenproof dish or 6 individual casseroles. Top with the bread cubes and sprinkle with the Parmesan. 5. Broil 4 to 5 inches from the heat for 5 minutes, or until golden and crusty. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 115 (France). A quick blender French onion soup topped with bread and broiled Parmesan. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (onions plus 2 cups French bread cubes over 6 servings) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 30 minutes - Different from the Pi's Upgraded Creamy Onion Soup for Two. - Deeper flavor: brown the chopped onions in 2 tablespoons butter for 15 minutes before adding the broth. - Lower carb: skip the bread and broil the Parmesan (plus some Gruyère) right on the soup.

recipes.title: Buck Rabbit
recipes.how: For the rarebit: ⅔ cup warm stale beer or ale 2 tablespoons flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) 2 tablespoons soft butter 2 cups diced Cheddar cheese 1 teaspoon anchovy-free Worcestershire sauce ¼ teaspoon dry mustard ½ teaspoon salt Dash cayenne For serving: 4 slices hot buttered toast (or low-carb bread) 4 poached eggs 1. Put the beer, flour, butter, Cheddar, Worcestershire, mustard, salt, and cayenne into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 30 seconds. 2. Pour into a saucepan (or double boiler) and heat over simmering water, stirring constantly, until hot and smooth. 3. Spoon over the buttered toast and top each with a poached egg. From The Blender Cookbook. A beer-and-Cheddar rarebit made in the blender, served on buttered toast under poached eggs. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (beer, 2 tablespoons flour, and the toast underneath) - Cook time: 20 minutes - Peter: regular Worcestershire sauce is made with anchovies. Use an anchovy-free (vegan) Worcestershire. - Fats: butter, no swap needed. Pick a bread without soybean or canola oil; low-carb bread keeps this near low-carb. - 'Buck' rabbit is Welsh rarebit topped with a poached egg. - Science: flat (stale) beer blends without foaming, and gentle heat keeps the cheese from turning stringy or oily.

recipes.title: Fine Beef Soup
recipes.how: For the stock (day 1): 3 pounds fresh beef shank or foreleg, with bones (substantial, not too fatty) 4½ pints (9 cups) water Pinch salt Pinch pepper For the soup (day 2): 2 carrots, sliced 1 to 2 turnips, sliced 1 onion, sliced 2 stalks celery, sliced 2 tomatoes, peeled and chopped (optional) Other vegetables you like (optional) Salt and pepper, at the table 1. Day 1: Wash the beef. Take the meat off the bones and break or crack the bones. 2. Put the meat and bones into a large pot, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and pepper, and add the water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then keep at a steady, gentle boil, covered, for 8 to 9 hours. Skim off the fat that rises, re-covering the pot each time. Don't add more water, and don't let it boil hard or the meat turns tough and dry. 3. Take the pot off the heat and let it cool for about 15 minutes. Strain into a large crock or bowl (straining makes it clear and removes the meat and bones). Cover and keep in a cool place (the refrigerator) overnight. It should set into a jelly; don't break it up until you are ready to use it. 4. Day 2: Cook the vegetables separately in boiling water until almost tender, carrots first since they take longest. Cook peeled, chopped tomatoes in their own juice until they melt. 5. Scrape any fat or sediment off the jellied stock. Cut the jelly into pieces and put it into a pot about 30 minutes before serving. 6. Add the vegetables, enough to make the soup nicely thick, and simmer gently until hot, no more than about 30 minutes. Overcooking on the second day makes it taste flat. 7. Season lightly; let everyone add salt and pepper at the table. From an old-style recipe card ('FINE BEEF SOUP'). A clear, slow-simmered beef soup made over two days: long-boiled stock the first day, jellied overnight, then reheated with vegetables cooked separately. - Carb level: Low-carb (beef broth and vegetables; carrots and turnips add a little) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 570 minutes - Ingredient list written out from the card's ratio: the card gives no ingredient list, only 'about a pint and a half of water for every pound of meat.' 3 pounds of beef is an example amount (scale at 1½ pints water per pound). The vegetable amounts are estimates; the card says only 'enough to make the soup nice and thick.' - Fats: none added; skim the beef fat as it rises. No seed oils. - Cook time: about 9 hours on day 1 plus 30 minutes on day 2, with an overnight chill in between. - The card warns against over-seasoning: keep salt and pepper light and let people season at the table. - Science: long, gentle simmering pulls gelatin from the bones (that's why it jellies), and cooking the vegetables separately keeps the broth clear and bright.

recipes.title: Wild Rice and Mushroom Soup
recipes.how: For the rice: 4 cups water 1 sprig fresh thyme 1 bay leaf 1 garlic clove, peeled ¾ teaspoon salt ¼ teaspoon baking soda 1 cup wild rice For the soup: ¼ ounce dried shiitake mushrooms, rinsed 4 tablespoons unsalted butter 1 pound cremini mushrooms, trimmed and sliced ¼ inch thick 1 onion, chopped fine 4 garlic cloves, minced 1 teaspoon tomato paste ¾ teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon pepper ⅔ cup dry sherry 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth 1 tablespoon soy sauce ¼ cup water ¼ cup cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) ½ cup heavy cream ¼ cup minced fresh chives ¼ teaspoon finely grated lemon zest Salt and pepper, to taste 1. Adjust an oven rack to the middle position and heat the oven to 375°F. Grind the shiitake mushrooms in a spice grinder (or blender) until finely ground; you should have about 3 tablespoons. 2. Bring 4 cups water, the thyme, bay leaf, peeled garlic clove, ¾ teaspoon salt, and baking soda to a boil in a medium saucepan over high heat. Add the rice and return to a boil. Cover, transfer to the oven, and bake until the rice is tender, 35 to 50 minutes. 3. Strain the rice through a fine-mesh strainer set over a 4-cup liquid measuring cup. Discard the thyme, bay leaf, and garlic. Add enough water to the reserved cooking liquid to measure 3 cups. 4. Melt the butter in a Dutch oven over high heat. Add the cremini, onion, minced garlic, tomato paste, ¾ teaspoon salt, and 1 teaspoon pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are browned and a dark fond forms on the bottom of the pot, about 15 minutes. 5. Add the sherry, scraping up the browned bits, and cook until reduced and the pot is almost dry, about 2 minutes. 6. Add the ground shiitakes, the reserved rice liquid, broth, and soy sauce, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the onion and mushrooms are tender, about 20 minutes. 7. Whisk the cornstarch and ¼ cup water in a small bowl. Stir the slurry into the soup, return to a simmer, and cook until thickened, about 2 minutes. 8. Remove from the heat and stir in the cooked rice, cream, chives, and lemon zest. Cover and let stand for 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper and serve. From Cook's Illustrated (Wild Rice and Mushroom Soup). Oven-cooked wild rice in a deep cremini, shiitake, and sherry soup finished with cream, chives, and lemon zest. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (1 cup wild rice and ¼ cup cornstarch over 6 to 8 servings) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 110 minutes - Fats: butter, no swap needed. No seed oils. - White mushrooms can stand in for the cremini (recipe note). - Science: baking soda in the rice water softens the wild rice's tough outer layer so it cooks evenly, and the 20-minute rest lets the rice absorb some broth without going mushy. - For lower carb, cut the wild rice to ½ cup.

recipes.title: Italian Wedding Soup
recipes.how: For the broth: 1 onion, chopped 1 fennel bulb, stalks discarded, bulb halved, cored, and chopped 4 garlic cloves, peeled and smashed ¼ ounce dried porcini mushrooms, rinsed 4 ounces ground pork 4 ounces 85 percent lean ground beef 1 bay leaf ½ cup dry white wine 1 tablespoon anchovy-free Worcestershire sauce 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth 2 cups beef broth 2 cups water For the meatballs: 1 slice hearty white sandwich bread, crusts removed, torn into 1-inch pieces 5 tablespoons heavy cream ¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese 4 teaspoons finely grated onion ½ teaspoon finely grated garlic Salt and pepper 6 ounces ground pork 1 teaspoon baking powder 6 ounces 85 percent lean ground beef 2 teaspoons minced fresh oregano For the soup: 1 cup ditalini pasta 12 ounces kale, stemmed and cut into ½-inch pieces (6 cups) 1. For the broth: Heat the onion, fennel, garlic, porcini, pork, beef, and bay leaf in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat; cook, stirring frequently, until the meats are no longer pink, about 5 minutes. Add the wine and Worcestershire; cook for 1 minute. Add the chicken broth, beef broth, and water; bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes. 2. For the meatballs: While the broth simmers, combine the bread, cream, Parmesan, onion, garlic, and pepper to taste in a bowl; mash with a fork to a uniform paste. Using a stand mixer fitted with the paddle, beat the pork, baking powder, and ½ teaspoon salt on high speed until smooth and pale, 1 to 2 minutes, scraping down the bowl as needed. Add the bread mixture, beef, and oregano; mix on medium-low speed until just incorporated, 1 to 2 minutes. With moistened hands, form heaping teaspoons of the mixture into smooth, round meatballs; you should have 30 to 35. Cover and refrigerate for up to 1 day. 3. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh strainer set over a large bowl or container, pressing on the solids to extract as much liquid as possible. Wipe out the Dutch oven and return the broth to the pot. (The broth can be refrigerated for up to 3 days. Skim off the fat before reheating.) 4. Return the broth to a simmer over medium-high heat. Add the pasta and kale; cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes. Add the meatballs; return to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until the meatballs are cooked through and the pasta is tender, 3 to 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper and serve. From Cook's Illustrated, March & April 2012. A quick, deeply flavored broth of fennel, porcini, pork, and beef, with tender baking-powder meatballs, ditalini, and kale. Use a rasp-style grater for the meatball onion and garlic. Tubettini or orzo can stand in for the ditalini. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (1 cup ditalini and a slice of bread over 6 to 8 servings) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 75 minutes - Peter: the recipe's 1 tablespoon Worcestershire is written here as anchovy-free. ALLERGY CHECK FOR PETER: traditional Worcestershire (Lea & Perrins, most store brands) is made WITH anchovies. Read the label and use an anchovy-free or vegan Worcestershire. - No egg in the meatballs: the cream-and-bread paste plus baking powder keeps them tender. - Alcohol: ½ cup dry white wine, simmered in the broth. - Science: beating the pork with salt and baking powder until pale builds a springy protein network, so the meatballs hold together without egg and stay light.

recipes.title: Red Wine-Braised Pork Chops
recipes.how: Salt and pepper 4 (10- to 12-ounce) bone-in pork blade chops, 1 inch thick 2 teaspoons avocado oil (replaces the recipe's vegetable oil) 2 onions, halved and sliced thin 5 sprigs fresh thyme plus ¼ teaspoon minced 2 garlic cloves, peeled 2 bay leaves 1 (½-inch) piece ginger, peeled and crushed ⅛ teaspoon ground allspice ½ cup red wine ¼ cup ruby port 2 tablespoons plus ½ teaspoon red wine vinegar 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth 2 tablespoons unsalted butter 1 tablespoon minced fresh parsley 1. Dissolve 3 tablespoons salt in 1½ quarts cold water in a large container. Submerge the chops in the brine, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 1 hour. 2. Adjust an oven rack to the lower-middle position and heat the oven to 275 degrees. Remove the chops from the brine and pat dry with paper towels. Trim off the meat cap and any fat and cartilage opposite the rib bones. Cut the trimmings into 1-inch pieces. Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the trimmings and brown on all sides, 6 to 9 minutes. 3. Reduce the heat to medium and add the onions, thyme sprigs, garlic, bay leaves, ginger, and allspice. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions are golden brown, 5 to 10 minutes. Stir in the wine, port, and 2 tablespoons vinegar and cook until reduced to a thin syrup, 5 to 7 minutes. Add the chicken broth, spread the onions and pork scraps into an even layer, and bring to a simmer. Arrange the pork chops on top of the pork scraps and onions. 4. Cover, transfer to the oven, and cook until the meat is tender, 1¼ to 1½ hours. Remove from the oven and let the chops rest in the pot, covered, 30 minutes. Transfer the chops to a serving platter and tent with aluminum foil. Pour the braising liquid through a fine-mesh strainer set over a large bowl; discard the solids. Transfer the braising liquid to a fat separator and let stand for 5 minutes. 5. Wipe out the now-empty pot with a wad of paper towels. Return the defatted braising liquid to the pot and cook over medium-high heat until reduced to 1 cup, 3 to 7 minutes. Off the heat, whisk in the butter, minced thyme, and remaining ½ teaspoon vinegar. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Pour the sauce over the chops, sprinkle with parsley, and serve. From Cook's Illustrated, January & February 2012. Brined blade chops braised low and slow on a bed of browned pork trimmings and onions, with red wine, ruby port, ginger, and allspice. Look for chops with a small eye and a lot of marbling; they braise best. The pork scraps can be removed when straining the sauce and served alongside the chops. - Carb level: Low-carb (pork, onions, and a reduced wine sauce) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 200 minutes - Oil: avocado oil replaces the 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (no seed oils). Tallow or lard also works for browning the trimmings. - Red wine and ruby port kept as written. Cory confirmed the pencil X's on the page are not removals. - Alcohol: red wine and port, reduced to a syrup and braised. - Cook time includes the brine, the braise, and the 30-minute rest. - Science: braising at 275 degrees holds the meat in the range where collagen melts to gelatin without the muscle fibers drying out, and the 30-minute rest lets the chops reabsorb juices.

recipes.title: Catalan-Style Beef Stew with Mushrooms
recipes.how: For the stew: 2 tablespoons olive oil 2 large onions, chopped fine ½ teaspoon monk fruit baking blend (in place of sugar) Kosher salt and pepper 2 plum tomatoes, halved lengthwise, pulp grated on large holes of box grater, and skins discarded 1 teaspoon smoked paprika 1 bay leaf 1½ cups dry white wine 1½ cups water 1 large sprig fresh thyme ¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon 2½ pounds boneless beef short ribs, trimmed and cut into 2-inch cubes For the picada: ¼ cup whole blanched almonds 2 tablespoons olive oil 1 slice hearty white sandwich bread, crust removed, torn into 1-inch pieces 2 garlic cloves, peeled 3 tablespoons minced fresh parsley To finish: ½ pound oyster mushrooms, trimmed 1 teaspoon sherry vinegar 1. For the stew: Adjust an oven rack to the middle position and heat the oven to 300 degrees. Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-low heat until shimmering. Add the onions, monk fruit, and ½ teaspoon salt; cook, stirring often, until the onions are deeply caramelized, 30 to 40 minutes. Add the tomatoes, smoked paprika, and bay leaf; cook, stirring often, until darkened and thick, 5 to 10 minutes. 2. Add the wine, water, thyme, and cinnamon to the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Season the beef with 1½ teaspoons salt and ½ teaspoon pepper and add to the pot. Increase the heat to high and bring to a simmer. Transfer to the oven and cook, uncovered. After 1 hour, stir the stew to redistribute the meat, return to the oven, and continue to cook uncovered until the meat is tender, 1½ to 2 hours longer. 3. For the picada: While the stew is in the oven, heat the almonds and 1 tablespoon oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat; cook, stirring often, until the almonds are golden brown, 3 to 6 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the almonds to a food processor. Return the now-empty skillet to medium heat, add the bread, and cook, stirring often, until toasted, 2 to 4 minutes; transfer to the food processor with the almonds. Add the garlic and process until finely ground, about 20 seconds, scraping the bowl as needed. Transfer to a bowl, stir in the parsley, and set aside. 4. Return the now-empty skillet to medium heat. Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil until shimmering. Add the mushrooms and ½ teaspoon salt; cook, stirring often, until tender, 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and set aside. 5. Remove the bay leaf. Stir the picada, mushrooms, and vinegar into the stew. Season with salt and pepper and serve. From Cook's Illustrated, January & February 2012. A Spanish beef stew of boneless short ribs braised with a slow-cooked sofrito of onions and tomato, white wine, smoked paprika, and cinnamon, finished with an almond-garlic picada, oyster mushrooms, and sherry vinegar. Remove the woody base of the oyster mushroom stems before cooking; an equal amount of quartered button mushrooms can stand in. Serve with boiled or mashed potatoes or rice. - Carb level: Low-carb (onions, tomatoes, and a slice of bread in the picada over 4 to 6 servings) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 210 minutes - Sugar swap: ½ teaspoon 1:1 granulated monk fruit blend replaces the ½ teaspoon sugar. The onions still caramelize on their own natural sugars; it just takes the full 30 to 40 minutes. - Fats: olive oil as written. - Alcohol: 1½ cups dry white wine, braised for hours. - Make ahead: follow the recipe through step 2 and refrigerate for up to 3 days. To serve, add 1 cup water and reheat over medium heat, then continue with step 3. - Science: cooking the stew uncovered in a 300-degree oven browns the exposed meat, so there's no need to sear first. The picada's ground almonds and bread thicken the broth at the end.

recipes.title: Onion-and-Cheese Pie
recipes.how: Pastry for a 9-inch pie plate (all-butter; see notes) 2 tablespoons butter 2 small onions, diced ½ pound Swiss cheese, cubed 3 eggs ½ teaspoon salt ⅛ teaspoon nutmeg 1 cup hot cream 1. Line a 9-inch pie plate with pastry. Prick the pastry to prevent puffing, insert another unlined 9-inch pie plate into the pastry, and bake in a hot (400° F.) oven for 8 minutes. Remove from the oven, take off the top pie plate, and let the pastry cool. 2. Sauté the onions in the butter until tender and golden. Sprinkle the onions over the bottom of the pastry. 3. Put the cheese, eggs, salt, and nutmeg into the blender container. Cover and blend for 5 seconds. 4. Remove the cover and, with the motor on, pour in the hot cream. 5. Pour the egg and cheese mixture over the onions and bake the pie in a preheated 350° F. oven for 35 minutes, or until the custard is set. Serve warm. From The Blender Cookbook, pp. 53–54 (Cheese and Egg Dishes). A Swiss cheese and onion custard pie in a pre-baked pastry shell. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (pastry crust; Swiss cheese, eggs, and cream) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 60 minutes - Crust: use an all-butter crust, no shortening or seed oils. Instead of store-bought, use a Recipe Box crust: "Cheddar Pie Crust" (all butter; makes two crusts, use half) or "Low-Carb Flaky Pie Crust" (omit its monk fruit for this savory pie). - Science: pre-baking the shell with a second pie plate on top keeps it flat and crisp under the wet custard.

recipes.title: Puffy Cheese Omelet
recipes.how: ⅓ cup milk 1 cup diced Cheddar or Swiss cheese 1 teaspoon salt ¼ teaspoon pepper 6 egg yolks ¼ cup parsley leaves 6 egg whites, stiffly beaten Butter, for the skillet 1. Put the milk, cheese, salt, pepper, egg yolks, and parsley into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 10 seconds. 2. Fold into the stiffly beaten egg whites. 3. Pour the mixture into a skillet or omelet pan greased with butter, spread evenly, and cook over low heat until puffed and lightly browned underneath. 4. Transfer to a preheated 375° F. oven and brown the top. Turn out onto a heated serving plate. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 49 (Cheese and Egg Dishes, Omelets). A soufflé-style omelet: a cheese and yolk base folded into stiff egg whites, browned on the stove and finished in the oven. - Carb level: Low-carb (eggs, cheese, and milk) - Cook time: 20 minutes - As written, with the skillet greased with butter (no seed oils). Use an ovenproof skillet. - Science: the beaten whites trap air that expands in the oven, so the omelet puffs like a soufflé.

recipes.title: Plain Scrambled Eggs for Two
recipes.how: ¼ cup milk or cream ½ teaspoon salt ⅛ teaspoon pepper 4 eggs 1 tablespoon butter 1. Put the milk or cream, salt, pepper, and eggs into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 3 seconds. 2. To cook scrambled eggs: Melt the butter in a frying pan. When the butter is hot, and before it begins to brown, add the egg mixture and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the eggs are thick and creamy. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 49 (Cheese and Egg Dishes, Scrambled Eggs). Blender-beaten eggs scrambled low and slow in butter until thick and creamy. - Carb level: Low-carb (eggs, milk, and butter) - Cook time: 10 minutes - As written. - Science: low heat and constant stirring make small, soft curds; high heat squeezes water out and makes them rubbery.

recipes.title: Creamy Scrambled Eggs for Three
recipes.how: 6 eggs ½ cup light cream 1 teaspoon salt Dash pepper 3 ounces cream cheese, quartered 3 tablespoons butter 1. Put the eggs, light cream, salt, pepper, and cream cheese into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 6 seconds. 2. Cook as for scrambled eggs, in 3 tablespoons hot butter: when the butter is hot, and before it begins to brown, add the egg mixture and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and creamy. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 50 (Cheese and Egg Dishes, Scrambled Eggs). Extra-creamy scrambled eggs blended with light cream and cream cheese. - Carb level: Low-carb (eggs, light cream, and cream cheese) - Cook time: 10 minutes - Variation, Chili Scrambled Eggs: Use tomato juice in place of the cream, and add ¼ teaspoon chili powder before blending. Blend and cook as for scrambled eggs. - Science: the cream cheese melts into the curds and keeps them soft even if they sit a minute.

recipes.title: Best Chicken Parmesan
recipes.how: For the sauce: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil 2 garlic cloves, minced Kosher salt and pepper ¼ teaspoon dried oregano Pinch red pepper flakes 1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes ¼ teaspoon sugar 2 tablespoons coarsely chopped fresh basil For the chicken: 2 (6- to 8-ounce) boneless, skinless chicken breasts, trimmed, halved horizontally, and pounded ½ inch thick 1 teaspoon kosher salt 2 ounces whole-milk mozzarella cheese, shredded (½ cup) 2 ounces fontina cheese, shredded (½ cup) 1 large egg 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour (lower-carb option: 1 tbsp. blanched almond flour) 1½ ounces Parmesan cheese, grated (¾ cup) ½ cup panko bread crumbs (lower-carb option: 1/2 cup crushed pork rinds) ½ teaspoon garlic powder ¼ teaspoon dried oregano ¼ teaspoon pepper ⅓ cup avocado oil (replaces the recipe's vegetable oil) ¼ cup torn fresh basil 1. For the sauce: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat until just shimmering. Add the garlic, ¾ teaspoon salt, oregano, and pepper flakes; cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in the tomatoes and sugar; increase the heat to high and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer until thickened, about 20 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the basil and remaining 1 tablespoon oil; season with salt and pepper to taste. Cover and keep warm. 2. For the chicken: Sprinkle each side of each cutlet with ⅛ teaspoon salt and let stand at room temperature for 20 minutes. Combine the mozzarella and fontina in a bowl; set aside. 3. Adjust an oven rack 4 inches from the broiler element and heat the broiler. Whisk the egg and flour together in a shallow dish or pie plate until smooth. Combine the Parmesan, panko, garlic powder, oregano, and pepper in a second shallow dish or pie plate. Pat the chicken dry with paper towels. Working with 1 cutlet at a time, dredge the cutlet in the egg mixture, allowing excess to drip off. Coat all sides in the Parmesan mixture, pressing gently so the crumbs adhere. Transfer the cutlet to a large plate and repeat with the remaining cutlets. 4. Heat the avocado oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place 2 cutlets in the skillet and cook without moving them until the bottoms are crispy and deep golden brown, 1½ to 2 minutes. Using tongs, carefully flip the cutlets and cook on the second side until deep golden brown, 1½ to 2 minutes. Transfer the cutlets to a paper towel-lined plate and repeat with the remaining cutlets. 5. Place the cutlets on a rimmed baking sheet and sprinkle the cheese mixture evenly over the cutlets, covering as much surface area as possible. Broil until the cheese is melted and beginning to brown, 2 to 4 minutes. Transfer the chicken to a serving platter and top each cutlet with 2 tablespoons sauce. Sprinkle with the basil and serve immediately, passing the remaining sauce separately. From Cook's Illustrated, March & April 2013. Thin chicken cutlets with a Parmesan-panko crust, pan-fried, topped with mozzarella and fontina, and broiled, with a quick tomato-basil sauce. Our preferred brands of crushed tomatoes are Tuttorosso and Muir Glen. This recipe makes enough sauce to top the cutlets as well as four servings of pasta. Serve with pasta and a simple green salad. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (panko and a tablespoon of flour in the crust; tomato sauce) - Cook time: 60 minutes - Oil swap: ⅓ cup avocado oil replaces the recipe's ⅓ cup vegetable oil for frying (no seed oils). Olive oil is as written. - Sugar: the ¼ teaspoon sugar in the sauce is as written; it can be reduced or swapped for monk fruit if desired. - Thin, even cutlets: rather than pounding whole breasts thin, slice them horizontally (freeze them first for 15 minutes to help with slicing), then pound only the fat ends to an even thickness. - When Parm goes wrong: for a soggy crust, reduce the sauce so it's less watery and replace some of the moisture-absorbing bread crumbs with grated Parmesan. For chewy cheese, supplement the mozzarella (a must for flavor) with creamy, tender fontina. For dry, chewy chicken, turn thick breasts into tender cutlets and briefly salt them, which seasons them and helps them retain moisture. - Science: the short salt rest seasons the thin cutlets through and helps them hold moisture, and Parmesan in the crust browns fast and stays crisp under the sauce. Flour swap: crushed pork rinds work better here: they are pure protein and fat, so they bake and fry up crisper than bread crumbs and stay crunchy under sauce or cheese.

recipes.title: Sweet-and-Sour Pork
recipes.how: 1 (13½-ounce) can pineapple chunks For the batter: 1 egg 3 tablespoons pineapple syrup (from the can) ½ teaspoon salt ½ cup flour For the pork: 1½ pounds boned leg or shoulder of pork, cut into 1-inch cubes Avocado oil, for deep-frying (replaces the book's "hot deep fat") For the sauce: The remaining pineapple syrup 1 medium green pepper, seeded and cut into strips ½ cup vinegar 1/4 cup golden monk fruit blend (in place of ¼ cup firmly packed brown sugar) 1 tomato, quartered 1 tablespoon molasses 2 tablespoons cornstarch (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) Rice, for serving 1. Drain and reserve the syrup from the pineapple chunks. 2. Put the egg, 3 tablespoons pineapple syrup, salt, and flour into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 10 seconds, stopping to stir down if necessary. 3. Pour into a mixing bowl and add the pork cubes. Toss until all are coated with the batter. 4. Fry the pork cubes in avocado oil heated to 365° F. for 6 to 7 minutes, or until well browned. Drain on absorbent paper. 5. Put the remaining pineapple syrup, green pepper, vinegar, sweetener, tomato, molasses, and cornstarch into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 15 seconds. 6. Pour into a saucepan and bring to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. 7. Add the pork and pineapple chunks and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the pork is tender, stirring occasionally. Serve with rice. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 151 (International Specialties, The Orient). Battered pork cubes deep-fried until brown, then simmered in a sweet-and-sour sauce with pineapple, green pepper, and tomato. - Carb level: High-carb (flour batter, pineapple syrup, brown sugar, and molasses; served with rice) - Cook time: 45 minutes - Oil swap: deep-fry in avocado oil at 365° F. (the book says "hot deep fat"). No seed oils; tallow or lard also work. - Kept original: the ¼ cup firmly packed brown sugar is as written. - Science: the egg-and-flour batter fries into a crisp shell that soaks up the sauce without the pork drying out. Sugar swap: The molasses and pineapple syrup stay, and they give the color and the sweet-sour depth. The brown sugar only adds sweetness. Flour is the best for this recipe because: a frying batter turns crisp because wheat starch gelatinizes and dries out in the oil; almond-flour batter soaks up oil, browns before it crisps, and slides off.

recipes.title: Spanish Pork Chops
recipes.how: 4 pork chops ¼ cup flour (lower-carb option: 1/4 cup blanched almond flour) ½ teaspoon salt ¼ teaspoon coarsely ground pepper 2 tablespoons lard (replaces the book's melted fat or shortening) 1 medium onion, quartered ½ cup coarsely cut celery ½ green pepper, seeded and cut into strips ½ teaspoon orégano ½ teaspoon paprika ¼ cup parsley clusters ¼ teaspoon thyme ½ bay leaf 1 No. 2 can tomatoes (about 20 ounces, 2½ cups) 1. Coat the pork chops with a mixture of the flour, salt, and pepper. 2. Brown the chops slowly in a skillet in the lard. 3. Put the onion, celery, green pepper, orégano, paprika, parsley, thyme, bay leaf, and tomatoes into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 10 seconds. 4. Pour off excess fat from the skillet, add the tomato mixture, cover, and cook over low heat for 45 minutes. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 153 (International Specialties, Spain). Floured pork chops browned, then braised in a blended tomato sauce with onion, celery, green pepper, and herbs. - Carb level: Moderate-carb (flour coating and tomatoes) - Weather: Cold + rainy - Cook time: 60 minutes - Fat swap: 2 tablespoons lard for browning replaces the book's "melted fat or shortening" (Cory's choice; no seed oils). - A No. 2 can of tomatoes is about 20 ounces (2½ cups). - Serve with cooked rice, as the book's Spain menu does.

recipes.title: Ham Soufflé
recipes.how: 4 tablespoons soft butter 4 tablespoons flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) ½ teaspoon salt 5 egg yolks 1 (4½-ounce) can deviled ham 1 cup hot milk 5 egg whites, stiffly beaten 1. Put the butter, flour, salt, egg yolks, deviled ham, and hot milk into the blender container. Cover and blend on high speed for 30 seconds. 2. Pour into a saucepan and cook over low heat until thickened, stirring frequently. 3. Fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites. 4. Pour into a 1½-quart soufflé dish and bake in a preheated 375° F. oven for 30 minutes. Serve at once. From The Blender Cookbook, p. 60. A quick blender soufflé: a deviled-ham white-sauce base cooked until thick, then lightened with stiffly beaten egg whites and baked. - Carb level: Low-carb (eggs, deviled ham, and milk; only 4 tablespoons flour) - Cook time: 50 minutes - As written: butter is already the fat. No seed oils. - Peter: safe as written. Canned deviled ham is normally just ham and spices, but check the label. - Science: the thickened base holds the beaten whites' air bubbles, which expand in the oven. Serve right away, because it starts to fall as it cools.

recipes.title: Traditional Ukrainian Borscht
recipes.how: 3 cup of diced celery 3 cup diced onions 3 cup of chopped cabbage 6 cloves of garlic, grated or pressed 3 tbsp of butter (for sautéing onions and celery) 24 cups water, beef broth or chicken broth 3 can diced tomatoes (home or commercially canned) 6 or 3 medium to large sized peeled beets (half grated and half diced) 3 or 6 medium carrots, grated 3 medium potato, diced 1 1/2 cup of fresh dill weed Salt and pepper to taste Optional ingredients: Bay leaf, green beans, peas, beet greens and shredded pork or pork sausage 1. Sauté the onions, celery and cabbage with the butter until soft and translucent. 2. Add the can of diced tomatoes and the garlic, as well as all of the water or broth. 3. Bring to a boil over medium high heat, then reduce to medium heat and let simmer. 4. Peel the beets, carrots and potato. 5. Dice half the beets and grate the other half. 6. Grate all the carrots. 7. Dice the potato. 8. Add the beets, carrots and potato to the broth. If you would like to add any other optional vegetables (ie. beans, peas, beet greens, etc.) do so now. 9. Allow soup to simmer on medium until diced beets and potatoes are soft (test them with a fork or by biting into them!), about 15 minutes. Remove soup from heat. 10. Stir in chopped fresh dill weed and salt and black pepper. 11. Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream and a slice of bread and butter (rye bread is best!) Author: Anastasia Sakawsky Prep Time: 15 minutes Cook Time: 20 minutes Total Time: 35 minutes Yield: 18 servings Category: Soup Cuisine: Ukrainian This traditional Ukrainian borscht combines the earthiness of beets with the freshness of dill and other vegetables. A hearty, healthy and frugal way to use up your garden vegetables and stretch your food budget while filling your family's bellies this fall! Serving Size 8 oz Serves 6 From Cory's Apple Notes ("Traditional Ukrainian Borscht Recipe", 2020). Added as is.
