recipes.title: Ukrainian Borshch from Kiev
recipes.how: ½ pint beer (ideally kvass brewed from black bread; ordinary beer works fine) ½ lb beef, cut into small cubes 2 oz bacon, cut into small cubes 1 raw beetroot (size of a tennis ball), peeled and grated 1 small cauliflower, chopped very small 1 large potato, peeled and diced 1 small carrot, chopped 1 stick celery, chopped 1 small onion, peeled, layers pulled apart and broken up (not finely chopped) 1 large tomato, quartered 1 small apple, peeled, cored and sliced 1 tablespoon sugar 1 dessertspoon salt 1 teaspoon pepper 1 cup cooked butter beans (tinned or pre-cooked) Chopped fresh parsley Sour cream (or ordinary cream) to serve 1. Put the beer into a large saucepan. Add the cubed beef and bacon. 2. Add the grated beetroot, chopped cauliflower, potato, carrot, celery, broken-up onion, quartered tomato, sliced apple, sugar, salt and pepper. 3. Add enough water to cover everything generously. Bring to the boil, then simmer gently until all the vegetables and meat are completely tender (about 1½–2 hours). 4. Taste and adjust the liquid if you like it thinner. Just before serving stir in the cooked butter beans and heat through. 5. Ladle into bowls, scatter with chopped parsley, and pour a generous spoonful of cream (preferably sour cream) into each plateful at the table. (Serves 6) "Borshch". Serve hot or cold—top with peanuts for crunch, cilantro for fresh. Senegalese-style soup, turmeric-only for that golden kick. No curry powder needed. Serves four, thirty minutes. recipes.title: Creamy Pumpkin Pasta with Roasted Brussels and Pork Sausage
recipes.how: 1 LB. brussels sprouts, rinsed and dried 1 Tbls avocado oil, separated 10 Oz whole wheat penne 6 0z Pork sausage 1 clove garlic, minced 1 shallot, minced 15 Oz can pumpkin puree, (not pumpkin pie filling) 1/4 heavy cream, Added to pumpkin 1/8 Tsp ground nutmeg 3/4 cup chicken broth 1/4 cup plus 3 tablespoons Pecorino Romano Cheese grated and separated 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella 1/2 Tsp salt, or more to taste 1/4 Tsp black pepper, or more to taste Prepare sprouts by cutting off the bottoms and removing the outer leaves. While sprouts are roasting, bring a large pot of water to a boil. While waiting for water to boil, place a medium saucepan over medium heat and add oil, garlic, and shallots. Sauté until golden and fragrant, about 3 minutes. [Add in pumpkin, heavy cream, chicken broth, nutmeg, 3 tablespoons Pecorino Romano Cheese. Stir well then add salt and pepper to taste. Simmer for 8-10 minutes.]. *Instead I added the roasted pumpkin, broth, cream and nutmeg and blended mixed it with all the rest and baked.* Once boiling, follow package directions on pasta for al dente. Once cooked, drain past water and add pasta to pumpkin sauce. Add cooked chicken sausage and brussels sprouts to saucepan and give a quick stir. recipes.title: Neapolitan Spaghetti
recipes.how: 1 lb. dried spaghetti 2 Tbs. butter 4 oz. onion, sliced 4 oz. green pepper, cored and sliced 4 oz. white button mushrooms, trimmed 4 smoked sausages (about 8 oz.), sliced on an angle 1 tsp. paprika 1⁄4 cup sake 1⁄4 cup milk 5 Tbs. ketchup 1⁄4 cup grated Parmesan cheese Tabasco sauce (optional) Cook the pasta in a large pot of salted, boiling water (add 1 tsp. of salt per pint of water). Follow package instructions for cooking, but remove the pasta from the water 1 minute earlier than specified, so the pasta is al dente. While the pasta is cooking, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, green pepper, and mushrooms, and cook, stirring constantly, for about 2 minutes. Add the sausage and cook for 2 minutes more, stirring frequently, to brown the sausage. Reduce the heat to low and add the paprika, sake, milk, and ketchup. Cook for about 5 minutes, mixing occasionally. When the spaghetti is ready, drain in a colander. Add to the saucepan and toss for 30 seconds, so the pasta absorbs the flavors of the sauce. Turn off the heat and divide the pasta and sauce among 4 plates. Top with the Parmesan cheese and season with the Tabasco, to taste, and serve. When the Americans arrived in Japan after World War II, they set up headquarters in the New Grand Hotel in Yokohama. A crowd of hungry GIs had to be fed, so the Americans arrived with truckloads of spaghetti at the ready, which they dished out liberally. The Japanese cooks at the hotel took notice. When the GIs eventually departed, they left behind cases of spaghetti and ketchup in the hotel stockrooms. What to do? An inventive hotel chef created a dish with spaghetti, sausage, and ketchup (tomatoes were too expensive at the time), and dubbed it “Napolitan.” The people of Naples might not recognize this dish as their own, but, inexpensive and filling, it soon became a standard of school lunch menus across Japan. And what you eat as a kid, of course, is what you crave as an adult, and thus Napolitan happily entered the cuisine. If you’d like, you can substitute ham, bacon, or chicken for the sausage. This recipe is excerpted from Japanese Soul Cooking: Ramen, Tonkatsu, Tempura, and More from The Streets and Kitchens of Tokyo and Beyond. From Cory's Apple Notes ("Neapolitan spaghetti", 2020). recipes.title: Pirozhki with Chicken Broth
recipes.how: For the Chicken Broth 1 large boiling fowl (whole chicken) 1 onion, roughly chopped 1 carrot, roughly chopped 1 bay leaf Mixed herbs (a few sprigs of parsley, thyme, etc.) Water (enough to cover) Salt & pepper to taste For the Pirozhki (makes about 8–10 pasties — you’ll have filling left over for tomorrow) Breasts from the chicken above 1 hard-boiled egg Pastry: either ready-made puff pastry or shortcrust made with ½ lb butter to 1 lb flour Salt & pepper 1. Remove the two breasts from the chicken and set them aside. Chop the rest of the bird (wings, legs, carcass) into pieces. 2. Put the chopped chicken into a large pot with the onion, carrot, bay leaf and herbs. Cover with cold water, bring to the boil, then simmer very gently for several hours until every bit of flavour is extracted. 3. Strain the liquid, skim off every trace of fat, and adjust with a little water if needed until you have about 1½ pints (enough for 4 people). Season and keep hot. 4. Meanwhile, mince the chicken breasts. Poach the mince gently in a little of the broth until just cooked, then pass it through the mincer again with the hard-boiled egg. Mix well and season generously. 5. Roll out the pastry fairly thinly and cut into 3-inch circles. Put a spoonful of filling on each, moisten the edges, fold over into half-moons, press to seal, and brush with beaten egg. 6. Bake in a hot oven (about 220°C / 425°F) for 10–15 minutes until golden and crisp. Serve immediately, 2–3 pirozhki per person on a side plate with a bowl of the clear chicken broth. (Serves 4 as a first course) (Note: the filling from one chicken breast makes twice as much as you need for the broth, so enjoy extra pirozhki the next day without soup.) What to make first (important timing!) Start the Chicken Broth first — it needs a very long, slow boil to get rich flavour (the author says “boil and boil until you have got every drop of flavour out”). While the broth is simmering, you can start the Borshch in a second pot (they cook at the same time with no problem). Make the Pirozhki pastry and filling during that time, but bake the Pirozhki right at the end, only 10–15 minutes before you sit down, so they come to the table piping hot with the broth. Pressure-cooker version (from the same note): Original: Several hours of open simmering for the broth to get “every drop of flavour out.” With pressure cooker: About 45–60 minutes total cooking time (plus 15–30 minutes to come to pressure and natural release), yielding a richer, more gelatinous broth than stovetop in far less time. Adapted Method: Remove the chicken breasts and set aside (same as original). Chop the rest of the bird into pieces. Add to the pressure cooker pot with the onion, carrot, bay leaf, mixed herbs, and enough cold water to cover (don’t exceed the max fill line—aim for about 1½–2 quarts/1.5–2 liters final broth). Seal the lid. Cook on high pressure for 45–60 minutes (45 for cleaner/lighter broth, 60 for deepest flavor and body—most sources say 45–60 is ideal for excellent results). Allow natural pressure release (best for clear, flavorful stock—takes 20–40 minutes) or quick release if in a rush (but natural is better to avoid cloudiness). Strain, skim fat meticulously, adjust volume with water if needed to ~1½ pints for 4 people, season, and keep hot. For the filling: Mince/poach the breasts in a little broth as original (this step is quick on stovetop or even sauté mode in the pot after broth is done). Mix with minced hard-boiled egg, season. Make pastry, fill, seal, egg-wash, and bake the pirozhki fresh/hot as original (no change—bake just before serving). Result: Broth done in under 2 hours total (vs. several hours), often tasting even more intense. You can poach the breast mince in the finished broth or separately. From Cory's Apple Notes ("What to make first (important timing!)", 2026). Added as is. The same note also holds Ukrainian Borshch from Kiev (already in the Recipe Box). Grok Bot estimated cook time. Flour is the best for this recipe because: the layers puff because gluten sheets hold steam between the butter layers; low-carb flours crumble instead of laminating.

recipes.how: 170 g (1 cup and 2 tbsp) unbleached all-purpose flour 5 ml (1 tsp) sugar 5 ml (1 tsp) instant yeast 2.5 ml (1/2 teaspoon) salt 125 ml (1/2 cup) lukewarm water 45 ml (3 tbsp) olive oil Tomato sauce 2 garlic cloves, chopped 30 ml (2 tbsp) olive oil 1 398 ml (14 oz) can of diced Italian tomatoes Trim 90 g (1/2 cup) small salami, cut into thin slices 100 g (1 cup) grated mozzarella cheese 1/4 red pepper, seeded and diced 1/4 green pepper, seeded and diced Dough In a large bowl, using a wooden spoon, combine flour, sugar, yeast and salt. Using a rolling pin, roll out the dough to a 10-inch (25 cm) disc. Divide half the oil into a large frying pan or 11-inch round baking dish. Place the dough in it. Brush the surface of the dough with the rest of the oil. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm, moist place for 1 hour and 30 hours or until the dough doubles in volume. Tomato sauce Meanwhile, in a small saucepan over medium-high heat, brown the garlic in the oil. Add tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Off the heat, using a potato pestle, mash the tomatoes to have a smooth sauce. Leave to cool. Trim Place the grill in the centre of the oven. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit. With your fingers, press the center of the dough to have a flat center and a still swollen border. Spread the tomato sauce in the centre of the dough while keeping the border intact. Divide half of the salami. Cover with cheese. Divide the peppers and the rest of the salami. Bake for 20 minutes or until crust is golden and cheese is melted. Unmould the pizza on a cutting board by dragging it out of the pan. Cutting into a wedge From Cory's Apple Notes ("Pizza crust", 2020). Added as is. Grok Bot estimated servings/cook time. recipes.title: Stout Potpie
recipes.how: 7 Tbs. olive oil 1 lb. white button mushrooms, quartered 2 cups frozen pearl onions, thawed Salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste 3 1/2 lb. beef chuck roast, cut into 1-inch cubes 1 cup all-purpose flour (lower-carb option: 1 cup blanched almond flour) 3 garlic cloves, minced 2 Tbs. tomato paste 2 1/2 cups Irish stout 1 cup beef broth 1 lb. carrots, cut into chunks 1 lb. red potatoes, cut into chunks 1 Tbs. finely chopped fresh thyme One 16-inch round Stilton Pastry 1 egg, beaten with 1 tsp. water In a 5 1/2-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat, warm 1 Tbs. of the olive oil. Add the mushrooms, onions, salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, about 12 minutes. Transfer to a bowl. Season the beef with salt and pepper. Dredge the beef in the flour, shaking off the excess. In the Dutch oven over medium-high heat, warm 2 Tbs. of the olive oil. Add one-third of the beef and brown on all sides, about 7 minutes total. Transfer to a separate bowl. Add 1/2 cup water to the pot, stirring to scrape up the browned bits. Pour the liquid into a separate bowl. Repeat the process 2 more times, using 2 Tbs. oil to brown each batch of beef and deglazing the pot with 1/2 cup water after each batch. Return the pot to medium-high heat. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, for 30 seconds. Add the beef, stout, broth and reserved liquid, stirring to scrape up the browned bits. Add the mushrooms, onions, carrots, potatoes and thyme and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the beef and vegetables are tender, about 3 hours. Preheat an oven to 400°F. Brush the rim of the pot with water. Lay the pastry round on top, allowing it to droop onto the filling. Trim the dough, leaving a 1-inch overhang, and crimp to seal. Brush the pastry with the egg mixture, then cut 4 slits in the top of the dough. Bake for 30 minutes. Let the potpie rest for 15 minutes before serving. Calls for a 16-inch round Stilton Pastry; that recipe was not in the original note, so one was created. See "Stilton Pastry (for Stout Potpie)" under Pastries. Cook Time: 240 minutes Prep Time: 35 minutes Serves 8 to 10. Source: Williams-Sonoma Kitchen. Dry Stout is black beer with a dry-roasted character thanks to the use of roasted barley. The emphasis on coffee-like roasted barley and a moderate degree of roasted malt aromas define much of the character. Hop bitterness is medium to medium high. This beer is often dispensed via nitrogen gas taps that lend a smooth, creamy body to the palate. From Cory's Apple Notes ("Stout Potpie", 2021). Added as is. The note repeated the ingredients block; one copy kept.

recipes.title: Leftover Turkey Cranberry Brie Bake
recipes.how: leftover turkey butter Kinders buttery seasoning cranberry sauce brie cheese basil Preheat oven to 350 degrees In a sauce pan melt the butter and mix with Kinders buttery seasoning make enough for the two dishes and pour into the individual casserole dishes just enough to cover the bottom. Now, You will build the dish starting with the turkey placed in the dish. Over your leftover turkey. Layer first the cranberry sauce. Cut brie cheese in thin slices and place over the top of the cranberry sauce Sprinkle over the top the basil 12. Place in the oven for 15 minutes or until all the cheese is gooey 13. Pull out of the oven and enjoy From Cory's Apple Notes ("leftover turkey.", 2023). Added as is. The note gives no ingredient amounts; the ingredients are listed as they are named in the steps.

recipes.title: Taco Soup with Beef
recipes.how: 1 lb. ground beef 1 red onion (chopped) 1 bell pepper (chopped) 1 block (8 oz) cream cheese 1 packet taco seasoning (or 2 Tablespoons homemade taco seasoning) 1 can (14 oz) diced tomatoes (undrained) 1 can (4 oz) green chilies 1 1/2-2 cups beef broth 1/2 cup Mexican blend cheese (plus more for serving) 1/4 cup chopped cilantro 1 lime (quartered) Optional toppings: 1 avocado; 4 radishes (sliced); 2 cups tortilla strips; additional cheese; 1/2 cup sour cream 1. Set a Dutch oven or other heavy-bottomed soup pot over medium heat. Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up with a spatula, until browned, about 6 minutes. 2. Add the onion and bell pepper and saute until softened, another 5 or so minutes. If there is a lot of excess grease, drain all but one tablespoon off. Otherwise, continue on with the recipe. 3. Stir in the cream cheese until melted, then season with the taco seasoning. 4. Stir in the diced tomatoes, green chilies, and beef broth. Bring to a low simmer and simmer for 5 or so minutes or until heated through. 5. Stir in the cheese until just melted, then turn off the heat. Sprinkle with cilantro and a squeeze of lime juice, reserving some of each for toppings. 6. Serve with avocado, radish, tortilla strips, cheese, more cilantro and lime, and a dollop of sour cream, if desired. Creamy Beef Taco Soup. Prep 5 mins, cook 25 mins, total 30 mins; 452 kcal per serving. For a spicier version, saute a seeded jalapeno with the bell pepper and onion, or top with fresh sliced jalapeno. Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Use gluten-free beef broth if needed. Soup thickens as it sets: 1 1/2 cups broth for thick, almost queso-like; 2 to 2 1/2 cups for thinner. For Peter: check the taco seasoning label.

recipes.title: Chicken Soup with Vegetables
recipes.how: 8 cups chicken stock (page 4) or canned chicken broth 1 imported bay leaf ½ cup dry white wine or dry white French vermouth 1 cup each julienne or fine dice of onion, celery, white of leek, and carrot 2 boned and skinned chicken-breast halves Salt and pepper Bring stock or broth to the simmer with the bay leaf, wine, and vegetables; simmer 5 to 6 minutes, or until the vegetables are just tender. Meanwhile, cut the chicken into thin slices, and the slices into julienne matchsticks 1½ inches long. Fold them into the soup and let simmer just a minute or two, until cooked through. Correct seasoning, then let sit for I5 to 20 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb flavors. Serve hot with melba toast or buttered toast points. SOUPS MADE FROM STOCK OR CANNED BROTH, Master Recipe. For about 2½ quarts, serving 6 to 8. COOKING WITH OR WITHOUT WINE. For red wine, use a young, full wine such as a zinfandel or a Chianti. White wines should be dry and full-bodied, such as a sauvignon, but because many of the whites are too acid, I prefer to use a dry white French vermouth. In addition to its strength and quality, it keeps nicely. Port, Madeiras, and sherries must be dry. If you do not wish to cook with wine, simply omit it, or add stock or more herbs. From Cory's Apple Notes ("SOUPS MADE FROM STOCK", 2021). Added as is. A second note (p11158) has the same ingredient list without the steps; this more complete version was used. Grok Bot estimated cook time.

recipes.title: Flourless Peanut Butter, Oat, and Banana Pancakes
recipes.how: 2 ripe bananas 3 eggs 2 tablespoons creamy peanut butter ¾ cup quick-cooking oats (make sure they’re gluten-free) ¼ cup chocolate chips Pinch of salt ADDITIONAL TOPPINGS *Optional: Chocolate chips, Sliced bananas, Maple syrup 1. In a medium bowl, mash bananas until puréed. Add eggs, peanut butter, oats, chocolate chips, and salt. Stir until the ingredients are fully mixed and batter is formed. 2. Heat a lightly oiled pan over medium-high heat. Pour ½ cup of batter into the pan and brown on both sides. 3. Top with chocolate chips, sliced bananas, and maple syrup. Serve hot. Makes 4–6 Pancakes. Recipe by Robert Broadfoot, via BuzzFeed Tasty (youtube.com). From Cory's Apple Notes ("1. Flourless Peanut Butter, Oat, and Banana Pancakes", 2023). Added as is. The note ends with the title of a second recipe (Coconut Flour German Chocolate Pancakes) but no recipe for it. Grok Bot estimated servings/cook time.

recipes.title: Turkey Soup
recipes.how: 1 box chicken stock Frozen peas and carrots 1 1/2 carrots quartered and sliced 1/2 onion 1 cup turkey gravy Minute rice Lots of pepper Boil carcass 4 hours, remove bones Add onion late, with catsup for color and tanginess From Cory's Apple Notes ("Turkey Soup", 2015). Added as is. Grok Bot estimated servings.

recipes.title: Green Pea Soup
recipes.how: Dried pea soup: 1 quart split peas, or Lima beans, which are better 3 quarts very soft water 3 onions, chopped up Pepper and salt A large piece of butter and flour (lower-carb option: xanthan gum, about 1/8 tsp. per tablespoon of flour, whisked into the liquid) Some slices of nice salt pork 1 large tea-spoonful celery seed, pounded Toasted bread cut into dice and fried in butter Green pea soup (in place of the celery seed): A handful of mint, chopped small 1 pint young peas A quarter of a pound of butter 2 spoonsful of flour (lower-carb option: xanthan gum, about 1/8 tsp. per tablespoon of flour, whisked into the liquid) Make it exactly as you do the dried pea soup, only in place of the celery seed, put a handful of mint chopped small, and a pint of young peas, which must be boiled in the soup till tender; thicken it with a quarter of a pound of butter, and two spoonsful of flour. Take one quart of split peas, or Lima beans, which are better; put them in three quarts of very soft water with three onions chopped up, pepper and salt; boil them two hours; mash them well and pass them through a sieve; return the liquid into the pot, thicken it with a large piece of butter and flour, put in some slices of nice salt pork, and a large tea-spoonful of celery seed pounded; boil it till the pork is done, and serve it up; have some toasted bread cut into dice and fried in butter, which must be put in the tureen before you pour in the soup. From Cory's Apple Notes ("GREEN PEA SOUP.", 2022). Added as is. The note holds both the green pea soup and the dried pea soup it builds on (the second paragraph); the ingredient list is the items named in the text. See also "Green Pea Soup with Mint". Grok Bot estimated servings/cook time.

recipes.title: Coconut Flour German Chocolate Cake Pancakes
recipes.how: Coconut Flour Chocolate Pancakes: ¼ cup coconut flour ⅛ cup tapioca flour (lower-carb option: 1/2 tsp. xanthan gum, whisked into the liquid) ½ teaspoon baking soda pinch of salt 2 tablespoon Green & Black's Organic cocoa powder 2 eggs ⅛ - ¼ cup coconut milk 2 tablespoon melted coconut oil 2 tbsp. sugar-free monk fruit maple syrup (in place of 2 tablespoon maple syrup) ¼ cup Green & Black's Organic chocolate chunks optional Coconut Pecan Topping: 3/4 cup monk fruit allulose blend (in place of ¾ cup coconut sugar or unrefined cane sugar) ⅔ cup coconut milk ¼ cup butter or coconut oil 2 egg yolks 1 pinch of salt 1-½ cups coconut flakes unsweetened ¾ cup chopped pecans toasted 1. To prepare the Coconut Pecan Topping whisk together sweetener, coconut milk, butter, egg yolks and salt in a saucepan. Heat on medium-low while stirring almost constantly until mixture starts to thicken; 5-8 minutes (it will thicken more as mixture cool). Stir in coconut flakes and pecans and set topping aside. If it thickens too much, you can reheat it to make more pourable/spreadable. 2. For the Coconut Flour Chocolate Pancakes whisk together coconut and tapioca flour, baking soda, salt, and Green & Black's Organic cocoa powder in a small bowl until combined. 3. In a medium bowl, mix together eggs, ⅛ cup coconut milk, coconut oil, sweetener. Add the dry ingredients and whisk until fully combined. 4. Let the batter sit for 3-5 minutes. It should be quite thick (like brownie batter). If it gets too dry and clumpy, add more coconut milk (1 tablespoon at a time) until a thick batter forms. 5. Heat a lightly greased pan or griddle to medium-low. Drop 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake onto the griddle or pan and spread out a little. If desired you can sprinkle a few chocolate chunks between the 2 tablespoons of batter. 6. Cook pancakes for about 3 minutes on one side, then flip carefully. Cook the other side for 2 more minutes. Keep a close eye on the pancakes, as they burn easily. 7. Serve the pancakes while hot topped with the coconut-pecan topping. Sprinkle with chocolate chunks & coconut flakes and drizzle with melted chocolate, if desired. Source: LeelaLicious, by Regina (leelalicious.com/coconut-flour-german-chocolate-cake-pancakes/). Linked from Cory's note "1. Flourless Peanut Butter, Oat, and Banana Pancakes" (BuzzFeed list). Prep Time 10 minutes, Cook Time 30 minutes, Total Time 40 minutes. Servings: 8 pancakes. Sugar swap: The coconut pecan topping is a stirred egg custard. Allulose thickens it the same way and gives caramel notes as it heats, and it stays soft and spreadable when cool.

recipes.title: Chef's Chuck Roast
recipes.how: Marinade: 2 cloves garlic, minced 2 tablespoons olive oil 1/2 teaspoon curry mustard 1 1/2 teaspoons soy sauce 1/2 teaspoon crushed rosemary 2 tablespoons wine vinegar 1/4 cup Sauternes (sweet white wine) Basting Sauce (added after marinating): 2 tablespoons ketchup 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce 1 1/2 teaspoons A.1. steak sauce Meat: 1 chuck roast, 2 1/2 to 3 inches thick 1. Sauté the garlic in the olive oil until fragrant, about 1 minute. Do not brown. 2. Remove from heat. Stir in curry mustard, soy sauce, rosemary, wine vinegar, and Sauternes. 3. Place the roast in a large resealable bag or dish, pour the marinade over, and refrigerate for 24 hours, turning the meat several times. 4. Remove the roast from the marinade and set the marinade aside. 5. Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, and A.1. into the reserved marinade to make the basting sauce. 6. Sear over direct medium-high heat, basting with the sauce, 6 to 8 minutes per side. Then move the roast to indirect heat and cook 30 to 50 minutes total, basting occasionally. 7. For medium doneness, pull the roast when the internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C). For medium-rare, pull at 135°F (57°C). 8. Rest the roast 10 minutes before slicing against the grain. (Adjusted from a 1980s church cookbook recipe) Original recipe called for 40 minutes per side. Adjusted to a 6-8 minute sear per side, then 30-50 minutes over indirect heat, pulling by internal temperature. The Sauternes adds sweetness that balances the tangy basting sauce. Leftover basting sauce can be simmered briefly and served alongside. Added at Cory's request (2026-10-01), as written. Grok Bot estimated servings.

recipes.title: Pork Chops in Mushroom Sauce
recipes.how: Pork chops 1 can cream of mushroom soup or cream of chicken soup (or about 1¼ cups homemade from the box) About ½ can water or milk, to dilute the soup by half 1. Brown the pork chops in a skillet. 2. Add the cream of mushroom or cream of chicken soup, diluted by half with water or milk. 3. Cover and simmer for 1 hour. Added 2026-10-03. Instead of canned soup, use the box's homemade Cream of Mushroom Soup, the Mushroom Sauce recipe, or Blender Mushroom Soup (or Cream of Chicken Soup).

recipes.title: Old-Fashioned Roast Pork
recipes.how: 1 boneless pork shoulder roast (Boston butt, about 6 pounds) 3 cloves garlic, minced 2 teaspoons ground black pepper 1 1/2 teaspoons table salt 1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary 1 tablespoon chopped fresh sage leaf 1 tablespoon fennel seeds, roughly chopped 2 large red onions, cut into 1-inch wedges 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (if necessary) 1 cup apple cider 1/4 cup apple jelly 2 tablespoons cider vinegar 1. Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and heat oven to 300 degrees. Trim outer fat from pork, leaving 1/8-inch-thick layer. Combine garlic, pepper, salt, rosemary, sage, and fennel seeds in small bowl. Tie pork roast tightly into uniform shape. Rub with herb mixture. 2. Transfer to roasting pan and cook 3 hours. Scatter onion wedges around meat, tossing onions in pan drippings to coat. (If roast has not produced any juices, toss onions with oil.) Continue roasting until meat is extremely tender and skewer inserted in center meets no resistance, 3 1/2 to 4 hours. (Check pan juices every hour to make sure they have not evaporated. If necessary, add 2 cups water and stir browned bits into water.) 3. Transfer roast to large baking dish, place onions in medium bowl, and pour pan drippings into liquid measuring cup, adding enough water to measure 1 1/2 cups. Allow all to cool 30 minutes, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate overnight. 4. One hour before serving, adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 300 degrees. Cut cold meat into 1/4-inch slices and overlap in large baking dish. Spoon fat layer off drippings (discard fat) and transfer drippings and reserved onions to medium saucepan. Add cider, jelly, and vinegar and bring to boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to simmer. Spoon 1/2 cup simmering sauce over pork slices and cover baking dish with foil. Place in oven and heat until very hot, 30 to 40 minutes. Meanwhile, continue reducing sauce until dark and thickened, 10 to 15 minutes (reheat mixture just before serving pork). Serve pork, spooning onion mixture over meat or passing at table. Source: America's Test Kitchen. Serves 6 to 8, about 7 hours plus overnight chill. NOT paleo as written — the sauce uses apple jelly (sugar). The roast itself (herb rub, onions, pan drippings) is fully paleo. Swap options: 2 tablespoons apple butter (in place of apple jelly), or reduce the cider further to concentrate sweetness, or serve with just the onions and pan drippings and skip the sauce. No monk fruit/allulose swap — the jelly is what gives the reduced sauce its glaze and body. Cut check: a ~6 lb boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt). For a 2-3 lb roast, scale the rub (about 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper per pound, one small garlic clove, and about 1/2 tablespoon each rosemary, sage and fennel per 2 pounds) and start checking tenderness earlier. Timing at 300°F: about 1 hour 5 minutes per pound plus a 1.5-hour base (2 lb ~3 1/4 hrs; 3 lb ~4 1/4; 4 lb ~5; 5 lb ~6; 6 lb ~7; 7 lb ~7 3/4). Dry roast ~3 hrs, then add onions. The skewer test is the real test: 190-200°F for shreddable, 170-180°F for slicing. Check pan juices every hour — if they've evaporated, add 2 cups water and scrape the browned bits back in. Burnt drippings make the sauce bitter. Don't rush the low 300°F roast — that's what renders the fat and melts the connective tissue. The overnight chill is for clean 1/4-inch slices. A heavy, deep-sided (3-inch) roasting pan is best; a shallow broiler pan also works. Carb rating (Low): Pork shoulder with herbs and onions is low-carb; the cider/apple jelly sauce pushes it to moderate as written — skip or swap the jelly to keep it low.

recipes.title: Pork Roast with Mushroom Gravy
recipes.how: 1 (4- to 5-pound) boneless pork shoulder roast, fat trimmed to 1/8 inch thick 1 1/2 teaspoons dried thyme 1 1/2 teaspoons dried sage 2 teaspoons salt 1 teaspoon pepper 1 onion, peeled and halved 20 ounces cremini or white mushrooms, quartered 1 cup low-sodium chicken broth Water 1 bay leaf 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour 1. Prep pork: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and heat oven to 300 degrees. Pat pork dry with paper towels and rub all over with 1 teaspoon thyme, 1 teaspoon sage, salt, and pepper. Tie roast at 1-inch intervals with kitchen twine. 2. Roast pork: Arrange roast, fat side up, in roasting pan and cook until beginning to brown, about 3 hours. Add onion, mushrooms, broth, 1 cup water, bay leaf, remaining thyme, and remaining sage to pan and continue to roast until meat is well browned and skewer inserted in center meets no resistance, about 3 hours. Transfer roast to cutting board, tent with foil, and let rest 30 minutes. 3. Strain juices: Discard onion and bay leaf. Strain contents of roasting pan through fine-mesh strainer into fat separator; reserve mushrooms. Let liquid settle, then pour defatted pan juices (you should have about 1 cup) into measuring cup and add water to yield 1 1/2 cups. 4. Make gravy: Transfer 2 tablespoons of fat from separator to large saucepan and heat over medium-high heat until shimmering. Stir in flour and cook until golden, stirring constantly, 1 to 2 minutes. Slowly whisk in pan juices and bring to boil. Add reserved mushrooms and simmer over medium-low heat until gravy is slightly thickened, about 5 minutes. Remove twine from pork. Cut pork into 1-inch slices. Serve with gravy. Source: America's Test Kitchen. Serves 6 to 8, about 7 hours. NOT paleo as written — the gravy uses flour. The roast itself is fully paleo. Paleo option: 1 tablespoon arrowroot or tapioca starch whisked into 2 tablespoons cold water (in place of flour), or serve with the mushrooms and pan juices and skip the gravy. Cut check: 4- to 5-pound boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt), fat trimmed to 1/8 inch. If smaller, scale the rub and start checking at 2 hours. Remove any netting. Use a regular metal roasting pan, not nonstick (dark nonstick can overbrown the outside). Two-stage roast: 3 hours dry with the rub, then onion, mushrooms, broth and bay leaf for the second 3 hours — the mushrooms caramelize in the pan for gravy depth. Half broth, half water — full broth gives an off-putting poultry flavor. Skewer test: tenderness beats temperature for this cut. Use 2 tablespoons of the separated pan fat for the roux; don't skip the fat separator or the gravy will be greasy. The rubbed roast can be wrapped and refrigerated overnight — it seasons deeper. Tent 30 minutes before slicing. Leftover gravy keeps 3 days and reheats with a splash of water. Shopping: pork shoulder 4-5 lb, dried thyme and sage, onion, 20 oz mushrooms, low-sodium chicken broth, bay leaf, flour (or arrowroot/tapioca), kitchen twine, fat separator. Weekend project — the 7-hour cook isn't a weeknight dish. Carb rating (Low): Pork shoulder, mushrooms and broth with just 2 tablespoons of flour in the gravy across 6 to 8 servings — low-carb band.

recipes.title: Skillet-Roasted Chicken in Lemon Sauce
recipes.how: 1/2 cup table salt 2 quarts cold water 3 pounds bone-in chicken pieces (2 split breasts cut in half crosswise, 2 drumsticks, and 2 thighs), trimmed 1 teaspoon vegetable oil 2 tablespoons unsalted butter 1 large shallot, minced 1 garlic clove, minced 4 teaspoons all-purpose flour 1 cup chicken broth 4 teaspoons grated lemon zest plus 1/4 cup juice (2 lemons) 1 tablespoon fresh parsley leaves 1 teaspoon fresh oregano leaves 1. Dissolve 1/2 cup table salt in 2 quarts cold water in large container. Submerge 2 split chicken breasts cut in half crosswise, 2 thighs, and 2 drumsticks in brine, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 1 hour. 2. Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and heat oven to 475 degrees. Remove chicken from brine and pat dry with paper towels. Heat 1 teaspoon vegetable oil in ovensafe 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until just smoking. Place chicken skin side down in skillet and cook until skin is well browned and crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer breasts to large plate. Flip thighs and drumsticks and continue to cook until browned on second side, 3 to 5 minutes longer. Transfer thighs and legs to plate with breasts. 3. Pour off and discard fat in skillet. Return skillet to medium heat; add 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1 large minced shallot, and 1 minced garlic clove and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. Sprinkle 4 teaspoons all-purpose flour evenly over shallot-garlic mixture and cook, stirring constantly, until flour is lightly browned, about 1 minute. Slowly stir in 1 cup chicken broth and 1/4 cup lemon juice, scraping up any browned bits, and bring to simmer. Cook until sauce is slightly reduced and thickened, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 1 tablespoon grated lemon zest and remove skillet from heat. Return chicken, skin side up (skin should be above surface of liquid), and any accumulated juices to skillet and transfer to oven. Cook, uncovered, until breasts register 160 degrees and thighs and legs register 175 degrees, 10 to 12 minutes. 4. While chicken cooks, chop 1 tablespoon parsley leaves, 1 teaspoon oregano leaves, and remaining 1 teaspoon lemon zest together until finely minced and well combined. 5. Remove skillet from oven and let chicken stand for 5 minutes. Transfer chicken to serving platter. Whisk sauce, incorporating any browned bits from sides of pan, until smooth and homogeneous, about 30 seconds. Whisk half of herb-zest mixture into sauce and sprinkle remaining half over chicken. Pour some sauce around chicken. Serve, passing remaining sauce separately. Source: America's Test Kitchen. Inspired by Rao's lemon chicken in New York. Serves 4; 1 1/4 hours plus 30 minutes brining. NOT paleo as written — the sauce uses 4 teaspoons flour. Paleo option: 1 tablespoon arrowroot or tapioca starch whisked into 2 tablespoons cold water (in place of flour), added at the same point in step 3 — or skip the thickener and reduce the sauce a few extra minutes. Cut check: 3 lb bone-in pieces = 2 split breasts halved crosswise + 2 thighs + 2 drumsticks. Brine 30 minutes to 1 hour — no longer or the meat gets too salty. Pat the chicken VERY dry after brining — the single biggest factor in crisp skin. Oil until just smoking, chicken skin side down and don't move it for 8 to 10 minutes. Flip only the dark meat for 3 to 5 minutes so everything finishes together. Pour off the fat before the sauce; keep the fond. Only 1/4 cup lemon juice — the Rao's trick; zest adds lemon flavor without extra acidity. Return chicken skin side up above the liquid; pour sauce around, not on, the chicken. Serve with crusty bread, rice, potatoes or egg noodles (or a green veg for low-carb). Carb rating (Low): Bone-in chicken with a butter-lemon pan sauce thickened by only 4 teaspoons of flour — low-carb band.

recipes.title: Tuscan-Style Roast Pork with Garlic and Rosemary (Arista)
recipes.how: 1 lemon 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil 8 garlic cloves, minced 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes 1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary 2 ounces pancetta, cut into 1/2-inch pieces 1 (2 1/2-pound) boneless center-cut pork loin roast, trimmed Kosher salt 1. Finely grate 1 teaspoon zest from lemon. Cut lemon in half and reserve. 2. Combine lemon zest, oil, garlic, and pepper flakes in 10-inch nonstick skillet. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until garlic is sizzling, about 3 minutes. 3. Add rosemary and cook, 30 seconds. 4. Strain mixture through fine-mesh strainer set over bowl, pushing on garlic-rosemary mixture to extract oil. Set oil aside and let garlic-rosemary mixture cool. Using paper towels, wipe out skillet. 5. Process pancetta in food processor until smooth paste forms, 20 to 30 seconds, scraping down sides of bowl as needed. Add garlic-rosemary mixture and continue to process until mixture is homogeneous, 20 to 30 seconds longer, scraping down sides of bowl as needed. 6. Position roast fat side up. Insert knife one-third of way up from bottom of roast along 1 long side and cut horizontally, stopping 1/2 inch before edge. Open up flap. Keeping knife parallel to cutting board, cut through thicker portion of roast about 1/2 inch from bottom of roast, keeping knife level with first cut and stopping about 1/2 inch before edge. Open up this flap. If uneven, cover with plastic wrap and use meat pounder to even out. 7. Sprinkle 1 tablespoon kosher salt over both sides of roast (1/2 tablespoon per side) and rub into meat to adhere. 8. Spread inside of roast evenly with pancetta-garlic paste, leaving about 1/4-inch border on all sides. 9. Starting from short side, roll roast (keeping fat on outside) and tie with twine at 1-inch intervals. 10. Set wire rack in rimmed baking sheet and spray with vegetable oil spray. Set roast fat side up on prepared rack and refrigerate for 1 hour. 11. Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 275 degrees. Transfer roast to oven and cook until meat registers 135 degrees, 1 1/2 to 2 hours. 12. Remove roast from oven, tent with aluminum foil, and let rest for 20 minutes. 13. Heat 1 teaspoon reserved oil in now-empty skillet over high heat until just smoking. Add reserved lemon halves, cut side down, and cook until softened and cut surfaces are browned, 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer lemon halves to small plate. 14. Pat roast dry with paper towels. Heat 2 tablespoons reserved oil in now-empty skillet over high heat until just smoking. Brown roast on fat side and sides (do not brown bottom of roast), 4 to 6 minutes. Transfer roast to carving board and remove twine. 15. Once lemon halves are cool enough to handle, squeeze into fine-mesh strainer set over bowl. Press on solids to extract all pulp; discard solids. Whisk 2 tablespoons strained lemon juice into bowl with remaining reserved oil. 16. Slice roast into 1/4-inch-thick slices and serve, passing vinaigrette separately. Source: America's Test Kitchen (Annie Petito, November 2015). Serves 4 to 6; 2 1/2 to 3 hours plus 1 hour chilling and 20 minutes resting. Fully paleo as written — no flour, dairy or grain. The reserved garlic oil becomes the lemon vinaigrette base. Cut check: needs a 2 1/2-lb boneless center-cut pork LOIN. The vacuum-sealed roast in the fridge is pork SHOULDER — it won't butterfly and roll this way and the timing won't match; save the shoulder for a low-and-slow roast. If using enhanced (salt-injected) pork, reduce the salt to 2 teaspoons (1 teaspoon per side). Start the garlic in a COLD pan with cold oil so it infuses without burning; cooking tames garlic's harshness. The double-butterfly is what lets you salt both sides and spread the paste inside — don't skip it. Reverse sear: roast at 275, rest 20 minutes, THEN sear — keeps the crust crisp. Pull at 135 degrees; it climbs another 5 to 10 while resting. Carb rating (Low): Pork loin, pancetta, garlic, olive oil and lemon — essentially no carbs, low-carb band.

recipes.title: Pork Saltimbocca
recipes.how: 2 (1-pound) pork tenderloins, trimmed Salt and pepper 8 thin slices prosciutto (3 ounces) 8 large fresh sage leaves, plus 1 teaspoon minced 1 large egg white, lightly beaten 3 tablespoons olive oil 2 garlic cloves, sliced thin 1 cup chicken broth 1/4 cup dry white wine 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into 4 pieces and chilled 2 teaspoons lemon juice 1. Cut each tenderloin crosswise into 4 equal pieces. 2. Working with 1 piece at a time, place pork, cut side down, between 2 pieces of plastic wrap. Using meat pounder, gently pound to even 1/4-inch thickness. (Pieces should be about 5 inches long.) 3. Pat pork dry with paper towels and season with pepper. 4. Place 1 prosciutto slice on top of each cutlet, folding as needed to prevent overhang. 5. Dip 1 side of each sage leaf in egg white and place 1 leaf, egg side down, in center of each prosciutto slice. Cover with plastic and pound lightly until prosciutto and sage adhere to pork. 6. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. 7. Add half of pork to skillet, prosciutto side down, and cook until lightly browned, about 2 minutes. 8. Using tongs, carefully flip pork and cook until second side is light golden brown, about 1 minute. 9. Transfer to platter and tent with aluminum foil. 10. Repeat with remaining pork. 11. Add remaining 1 tablespoon oil to now-empty skillet and heat over medium-high heat until shimmering. 12. Add garlic and minced sage and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. 13. Stir in broth and wine and simmer until reduced to 1/2 cup, 5 to 7 minutes, scraping up any browned bits. 14. Reduce heat to low and whisk in butter, 1 piece at a time. 15. Stir in lemon juice and any accumulated meat juices from platter. 16. Season with salt and pepper to taste. 17. Spoon sauce over pork and serve. Source: America's Test Kitchen (Ashley Moore, October 2015). Serves 4; 50 minutes. Paleo as written (butter is the only dairy). The egg white just glues the sage to the prosciutto. The egg-white trick is the whole dish — the sage bonds to the prosciutto on top and crisps instead of wilting. Pound gently to an even 1/4 inch; cutlets longer than 5 inches crowd the skillet, so trim as needed. Press the prosciutto flat with your palm before the second pound. Prosciutto side down first: 2 minutes, then 1 minute on the second side — tenderloin cooks fast. Sauce reduces to only 1/2 cup; spoon, don't drown. Butter goes in one chilled piece at a time over low heat so it stays glossy. If a sage leaf tears, use another. Tent the first batch while the second cooks. Shopping: 2 pork tenderloins, 8 paper-thin prosciutto slices, 8 large FRESH sage leaves, 1 egg, dry white wine (sauvignon blanc or pinot grigio), chicken broth, garlic, butter, lemon. Pair with something green and simple — sautéed spinach or roasted broccoli. Carb rating (Low): Pork tenderloin, prosciutto and a butter-wine pan sauce — no flour or starch, low-carb band.
